- **Changing model no longer demands signing in to Claude again.** Before, one time Jarvis 007's query did not return in time and the Claude card showed "not signed in" with a sign-in button, even though the account lost nothing. Now it clearly says "could not check, you were not signed out", and it remembers the state so it asks less often.
- **The Antigravity CLI brain works again.** Jarvis 007 misread the model list of the new `agy` build so it sent the wrong model name and every chat turn failed; and when it did run, the reply bubble came back empty. Both are fixed, and the line "Fetching available models..." no longer shows up as a model in the picker.
- **Older Linux kernel machines (NAS, old VPS) can chat with Claude Code.** Before, every turn died at once because Jarvis 007 ran the wrong prepackaged Claude build; now it uses the build actually installed on the machine.
- On Windows, a conversation too long for Antigravity now reports clearly and suggests two ways forward, replacing a confusing error about a "file name too long".

Thanks to the user who sent a very detailed report with logs and a patch for the four bugs above.

## [0.30.3] - 2026-08-13
### Fixed
- **Antigravity CLI sign-in really works now.** The previous version stood still because `agy` asks "choose a sign-in method" before giving the link, while Jarvis 007 sat waiting for the link. Now Jarvis 007 picks the **Google OAuth** entry for you and then brings out the link for you.
- The **Check again** button when not signed in also says the right thing to do, instead of saying "did not answer in time" and leaving you to guess.

## [0.30.2] - 2026-08-13
### Fixed
- **Clicking a file link in chat now opens it straight to edit, no longer sometimes yes and sometimes no.** The .html file Jarvis 007 just exported, .md, .css, .json files... one click and you are in the editor; before, sometimes it threw you to the folder on the Files page.
- Old reason: the same link had two paths (a normal click, and opening in a new tab or F5) and the two paths handled it differently. Now both follow one rule.
- The hover text also says the right thing: **Open to edit** for a file, **Open location in Files** for a folder. Images, PDFs and archives still download as before.

## [0.30.1] - 2026-08-13
### Fixed
- **The conversation marker list is readable again when a chat is long.** From about 60 questions, the rows in the list were squashed into a mess of faint streaks; now each row keeps its height and the list scrolls normally.

## [0.30.0] - 2026-08-13
### Added
- **Google sign-in for Antigravity CLI right on the Models page, no need to open a terminal.** Press **Sign in with Google**, open the link, sign in, paste the code Google gives back and you are done - exactly like the Claude Code and ChatGPT sign-in you already have.
- Works even when Jarvis 007 is on a VPS: Jarvis 007 handles the terminal part itself. It also fixes a CLI bug that broke the link into pieces when signing in over SSH, so that pasting it into a browser gave an error.
- On Windows the card plainly says you must type `agy` once in PowerShell, instead of showing a button that does not work when pressed.

### Improved
- The **Runs on** box on the Claude Code card is clearer: it only changes **who pays**, while machine commands and MCP stay the same in both choices - unlike the "Anthropic (API)" card below. Before, the two places looked like duplicates.

## [0.29.1] - 2026-08-13
### Improved
- **The Google Gemini CLI card hides itself if your machine does not have it**, so no one stumbles into a Google option that has been cut off and struggles to sign in. Anyone who set it as the main brain still sees the card so they can switch to another.
- **Jarvis 007 no longer auto-installs Gemini CLI during setup.** The install is lighter and a little faster. It still works if you have an enterprise license or run with an API key: install `npm i -g @google/gemini-cli` yourself and the card reappears.
- The Google brain for personal accounts is now **Antigravity CLI** (version 0.29.0).

## [0.29.0] - 2026-08-13
### Added
- **The 10th brain: Antigravity CLI - uses your Google plan, and you can pick the exact model lineup as in the Antigravity IDE**, including non-Google models. This is the path Google designated after cutting off Gemini CLI for personal accounts.
- Install once on the machine running Jarvis 007 then type `agy` to sign in to Google, go to the **Models** page and press **Check again** and you are done. It also works on a VPS: it prints a link by itself for you to open on your own machine.
- The model list **asks the CLI directly** and Jarvis 007 keeps no hand-copied table, so whichever models your account is granted are exactly what you see.
- On par with Claude Code and ChatGPT: runs machine commands, calls every connection you have connected, uses skills, takes background work and replies through Telegram.

## [0.28.9] - 2026-08-13
### Fixed
- **Google cut off Gemini CLI for all personal accounts from 18/06/2026** - the free plan, AI Pro and Ultra alike. Before this version chatting with it produced a confusing blank line; now Jarvis 007 says plainly what happened and points to the path that still works. This is a block from Google's side, not a fault on your machine.
- The **Google Gemini CLI** card on the Models page no longer invites you to sign in as if it were still usable. For Gemini models use **OpenRouter** (many models in one place, both Gemini and Claude) or **Google Gemini (API)**.

## [0.28.8] - 2026-08-12
### Fixed
- **The code paste box in Google sign-in can be typed in again.** The "Done" button stretched to take the whole row, shrinking the input to a few dozen pixels so no code could be pasted. On a narrow screen the button now drops to the next line so the input is wide enough.

### Improved
- **Installing Jarvis 007 gives you all three sign-in-plan brains out of the box: Claude Code, ChatGPT (Codex) and Gemini CLI.** No more opening a terminal and typing `npm i -g` for each one; open the Models page and all that is left is signing in.
- It applies to all three install paths: Docker, `install.sh` on a VPS, and `setup.bat` on Windows (before, this file installed no brain at all).
- A running install gets it with one **Jarvis 007 update**. A failed install of any one is fine: the other brains still run as normal, and the card on the Models page just shows how to install by hand.

## [0.28.7] - 2026-08-12
### Fixed
- **Reopening an old conversation no longer shows a pile of machine text in your question bubble.** When you have a file open in the editor, Jarvis 007 attaches an instruction block to the message so it knows which file it is working on. That block was meant for machines only, but on page reload it showed up in place of the sentence you typed.
- **The conversation marker bar is readable again.** Before, the longer the conversation the more the list was full of identical rows, because every row was that instruction block - you could not tell one sentence from another.
- **Conversation names in History are no longer set from that block either.** The resend and edit-question buttons now use exactly the sentence you typed, without the junk.

## [0.28.6] - 2026-08-12
### Added
- **Google sign-in for Gemini CLI right on the Models page, no need to open a terminal.** Press **Sign in with Google**, sign in, Google shows a code, paste that code back and you are done - exactly like the Claude Code and ChatGPT sign-in you already have.
- Works even when Jarvis 007 is on a VPS and the browser is on your machine, because there is no localhost in between. Google's consent screen shows the correct name **Gemini CLI**.
- There is a **Disconnect** button to remove the Google account from Jarvis 007. Anyone who prefers signing in by terminal can still do so as before.

## [0.28.5] - 2026-08-12
### Added
- **The 9th brain: Gemini CLI, running on your Google account - no API key purchase needed.** On par with Claude Code and ChatGPT: runs machine commands, calls every connection you have connected, uses skills, takes background work. Install `npm install -g @google/gemini-cli`, run `gemini` once to sign in to Google, then go to the Models page and press **Check again**.
- The new card stands separately, not mixed with the old **Google Gemini (API)**: the old card pays per call, the new one uses the free plan tied to the Google account.
- Background work can be assigned to it too, and Jarvis 007's three permission levels map straight to the CLI's approval mode - the **Read-only** level is blocked by Gemini CLI itself, not by a line of advice in the prompt.

### Improved
- Running out of the Google plan quota now reports in Vietnamese with the time it can be used again, replacing Google's English sentence.

## [0.28.4] - 2026-08-12
### Fixed
- **Connecting ChatGPT no longer stops at "0 models".** The model list of the ChatGPT plan is supplied by Codex, and before, nobody asked for it until you opened the model picker yourself. Now after sign-in the Models page asks by itself and fills in the real number. A freshly installed machine (or a Mac just set up) shows it most, since it has no old list to show temporarily.
- **When models cannot be fetched it says exactly why.** Replacing the vague sentence "provider not connected or has no models", it is now a sentence naming the right thing to do: not signed in, Codex CLI not installed, or missing API key.
- **On Mac, Jarvis 007 finds `claude` and `codex` installed through Homebrew or nvm by itself.** In background mode the operating system gives Jarvis 007 only a very short list of folders, so these two commands ran when typed in Terminal while Jarvis 007 reported them as not installed.

### Improved
- **Typing `/` in Telegram opens a more trustworthy command list.** Jarvis 007 sets the menu for both private chats and groups, and if Telegram refuses it reports the reason on the Settings page instead of staying silent as before.
