## [0.26.23] - 2026-08-12
### Fixed
- **The two-factor authentication QR code could not be scanned.** The repo owner turned on 2FA, the QR showed up fine, and the phone refused to read it. Three bugs stacked up, and all three were INVISIBLE to the eye because the QR looked normal.
- **The white margin was only 2 cells, the QR standard demands 4.** Without that margin the scanner cannot separate the code from the surrounding background.
- **The otpauth string carried an extra `algorithm=SHA1&digits=6&period=30`** - all three are DEFAULT values every Authenticator app understands on its own. 34 extra characters pushed the QR from version 6 (41x41 cells) to version 8 (49x49 cells) in the same frame. Now it declares them only when the constant really differs from the default.
- **CSS squeezed the QR image down to 200px while the source image is 265px**, leaving each cell 3.77 pixels. This was the worst culprit: users point the phone at the computer SCREEN, not a sheet of paper, so the size of each cell decides everything. Now the image appears at the exact size the server computed (8 pixels per cell, more than double).
- **A long workspace name bloated the QR.** The name sits in TWO places in the otpauth string so each character costs double; measured, a 48-character name pushed the QR to version 11 (69 cells). Now the name is cut at 24 characters, so however it is named the QR keeps 8 pixels per cell.
- **The QR background is now truly white**, no longer transparent and relying on the wrapper card's background - anyone on a dark theme used to see a black code on a dark background.
- **The name in the Authenticator app follows the workspace and the PERSON.** Before it showed "Jarvis 007: admin" - technically right but meaningless among a dozen 2FA accounts on a phone. Now it takes the real workspace name plus the user name (`USER_NAME`), falling back to the login name when unset: "Jarvis 007: Minh Quý".
- **The label KEEPS Vietnamese accents.** The first version stripped accents ("Minh Quý" became "Minh Quy") for fear apps would show a broken string; that fear is outdated - the Key Uri Format allows percent-encoded UTF-8 labels and popular apps have read them correctly for a long time. Only control characters and the ':' sign are removed (it is the separator between workspace name and account name, and getting in would break the label). Measured: even with a maximum-length accented name the QR keeps 8 pixels per cell.
- Added a canary that measures by NUMBERS rather than reading text: each cell must be >= 7 pixels at natural size, the margin must be 4 cells, the background must not be transparent, and CSS must not force the image to a fixed pixel size. The last one is the quietest way to undo everything above - the server returns the right size, the browser shrinks it, and no server-side test can see it.

## [0.26.22] - 2026-08-12
### Added
- **Install MULTIPLE Jarvis 007 instances on one VPS, each with its own link.** Before this version you could not: the second instance died as soon as it came up. The app itself has been multi-instance capable for a long time (`JAVIS_PORT` and `JAVIS_STATE_DIR` are both read from environment variables); the blockers were all in the install files, and all the same kind of bug - a name hard-coded where Docker/Traefik/systemd identify by MACHINE-WIDE scope. Five such names: `container_name: javis`, host port `7777`, Traefik router/service name `javis`, `/etc/systemd/system/javis.service`, and `~/.codex/javis.config.toml`.
- **Three variables are enough to separate an instance:** `JAVIS_NAME` (container name + Traefik router name + systemd service name), `JAVIS_HOST_PORT` (host port), `DOMAIN_NAME` (the link). Leave all three blank = `javis` + port `7777`, which is **identical to the old install** - anyone running one instance has nothing to change.
- **A shared proxy for self-managed VPS** (`docker-compose.proxy.yml` + `docker-compose.multi.yml`). A machine has only one port 443, so Caddy must sit OUTSIDE every instance: run the proxy once for the whole machine, then give each instance its own folder. The proxy detects new instances through Docker labels and requests Let's Encrypt on its own, so adding or removing an instance needs NO change to the proxy and no restart of it. Exactly how Hostinger's Traefik works. The Docker socket is mounted `:ro` only.
- **Hostinger:** deploy `docker-compose.hostinger.yml` as a second stack and fill in those three fields. The Environment box therefore gets two more fields `JAVIS_NAME` + `JAVIS_HOST_PORT`; both have defaults so whoever installs the first instance still leaves them blank. There is no way to derive them from the three old fields because Traefik and Docker both identify by machine-wide scope.
- **Native:** `JAVIS_NAME=javis-shop JAVIS_PORT=7778 ./install.sh` produces `javis-shop.service` instead of overwriting the previous instance's `javis.service`. `install.sh` rejects names with odd characters before writing to `/etc/systemd`.

### Fixed
- **Two native Jarvis 007 instances under the same user overwrote each other's Codex profile.** `~/.codex/javis.config.toml` is a fixed name, and that file holds the hub URL + token, so the instance that started later overwrote the earlier and instance A's Codex turned to call instance B's hub - a silent wrong, with no error showing anywhere. Now the profile name carries the port when the port differs from the default (`javis-7778.config.toml`); port 7777 keeps the name `javis` so running machines do not generate a new file. The two places that write the profile (hub on / hub off) now share one naming function.
- **`update.sh` of one instance restarted another.** The script looked up containers and services by the hard-coded name `javis`. Now it reads `JAVIS_NAME` from the `.env` of the very folder it is in, and keeps the `docker-compose.multi.yml` override when it detects a shared proxy - without this, one update strips the Caddy labels and that instance falls off the proxy.
- **Watchtower watches the right container of your instance** instead of always aiming at the container named `javis`.

### Improved
- `JAVIS_BIND` lets you pull the port back to `127.0.0.1` when a proxy already stands in front. Done with a variable rather than a `ports` line in the override file, because compose APPENDS the `ports` list across `-f` files instead of replacing it - redeclaring gives two bindings on the same port and Docker reports `port is already allocated`.
- Added `test_nhieu_ban_mot_vps.py` locking all five global names, and locking the most important condition: with every variable blank, every file must render identically to before. The test expands `${VAR:-default}` itself the way compose does so it runs in CI without Docker.
- DEPLOY.md has its own section on this, with a table saying which variable clash breaks things and how, and stating plainly what is shared and what is separate (nothing is shared - each instance must sign in to Claude once).

## [0.26.21] - 2026-08-11
### Fixed
- **Two-factor authentication could not be found from the Settings page.** Jarvis 007 has TWO account-settings surfaces - the **Account** page (everything, including the 2FA enable flow with the QR) and the old "Sign-in account" block embedded in the **Settings** page (password change only). 0.26.20 added 2FA to the first and forgot the second. The result was not "a missing button": users opened the Settings page, saw an account block that said nothing about 2FA, and concluded Jarvis 007 did not have the feature - while it had been running all day. A security feature people cannot find equals nothing.
- Now that block has one more status line: if not enabled it invites you to enable it, if enabled it shows how many recovery codes remain (with a warning when running low), and if no password is set it says plainly to set a password first instead of showing a button that does nothing.
- **Deliberately only a pathway, not a duplicated enable flow.** The QR scan screen stays in exactly one place on the Account page; the button here reuses the existing page-switch route. Two copies of a security flow are two places to fix on every change, and wherever one is forgotten becomes a hole - `test_2fa_loi_vao.js` has a canary forbidding duplication.

## [0.26.20] - 2026-08-11
### Added
- **Two-factor authentication (2FA) with an Authenticator app.** Turn it on at Dashboard → Account: scan the QR with Google Authenticator / Microsoft Authenticator / 1Password / Bitwarden (any works), enter a 6-digit code to confirm, done. From then on every sign-in asks for an extra code. Jarvis 007 runs with full access and has Bash, so a leaked password that still gets someone in is a risk not to accept.
- **10 recovery codes, shown exactly once when enabling.** Without them enabling 2FA sets a trap for yourself: lose the phone and you lose the way in, and the only exit is SSH into the server to hand-edit `settings.json` - exactly what people enable 2FA to avoid. Each code is used once and spent; a new set can be generated (the old set stops working at once).
- **`install.sh` asks whether to enable 2FA.** Deliberately NOT completed fully in the terminal: drawing the QR in a terminal shows wrong on half of machines and makes users point the phone at the SSH window, when in a few seconds they will open a browser - the right place to show a QR. So this step only records the intent in `.env`, and the Dashboard opens the QR scan screen on the Account page ready.

### Security
- **Code reuse protection.** A TOTP code lives 30 seconds, plus the clock-drift window it reaches 90. Jarvis 007 records the time step of the most recent successful sign-in and rejects every step less than or equal to it, so a code peeked over the shoulder cannot be reused. This is a hole most hand-written TOTP versions have, because it does not show up during trial use.
- **Enabled only AFTER the user proves the app generates the right code.** The new secret stays in RAM until confirmation and is not written to config. Enabling first would lock the owner out when the app's clock is off or the scan missed.
- **Password checked FIRST, code checked SECOND.** Reversing it turns the code box into a detector of which accounts have 2FA enabled, for someone who does not yet know the password. A wrong password gives a response that never mentions 2FA.
- **The TOTP secret and recovery codes are not on disk in plain text.** The secret goes into the list of fields encrypted at rest like API keys; recovery codes are stored as PBKDF2 hashes like passwords, so there is no path to read them back.
- **Disabling 2FA demands BOTH the password and a valid code.** If someone who borrowed a machine with the dashboard already open could turn off the second layer with one tap, that layer would count as absent. Every 2FA endpoint demands a browser session and does not accept API tokens.
- TOTP (RFC 6238) is hand-written instead of adding a library: it is HMAC-SHA1 over a 30-second counter, genuinely 20 lines, and unchanged since 2011. Adding a dependency for that much code trades something fully readable for something uncontrolled, right at the sign-in gate. Only `segno` is added to draw the QR (pure Python, pulls in nothing); without it the enable screen falls back to typing the key by hand.

## [0.26.19] - 2026-08-11
### Improved
- **After install you can sign in at once, no more hunting for the SETUP CODE in the log.** Before this version, opening Jarvis 007 publicly with no account made the server generate a random string and print it only to the log at startup; users had to SSH into the machine, `docker compose logs javis`, copy the code and paste it into the browser. That code stops a stranger with only the URL from seizing admin before the owner, so it has a reason to exist, but making people read logs is a bad experience, and bad exactly when they have just installed and know nothing yet. Now `install.sh` asks for the username and password directly and writes them to `.env`: the person running the script is already at the server, so one question adds NO step, and the server boots with an admin already so the setup code never shows.
- **One Enter gives a strong password.** Leave the password box blank and the script generates 20 letters and digits and prints them EXACTLY ONCE at the end of the install screen. Running without a keyboard (`curl | bash`, CI) also generates one rather than leaving it blank, since blank pushes users back to the very read-the-log screen just removed.
- **Re-running `install.sh` does not change the password in use.** If it is already in `.env` it is kept, and the script says so plainly. Reinstalling or re-running the script is common and must not turn into an unintended password change.
- **`docker-compose.yml` accepts `JAVIS_ADMIN_USER` / `JAVIS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`.** The Hostinger build has had these two fields for a long time, but plain compose did not, so anyone deploying with it ALWAYS had to read the log - there was no other way. Now filling two lines in the `.env` beside compose is enough.
- The password is written to `.env` with Python rather than `sed`: a password people type themselves can contain `|`, `&`, `\`, `"`, `'` and all of those break a `sed` command written the usual way. There is a test that writes and reads back a password containing all six characters.

### Security
- **The SETUP CODE mechanism is NOT removed**, it just stops being the main path. It remains the safety net for people deploying another way (hand-written compose, bare image). Removing it entirely would open `/auth/setup` wide to anyone who hits the URL before the owner, and what they would seize is a machine with Bash, running full access, plugged into the owner's POS/ads/email. There is a canary in `test_install_admin.py` keeping this mechanism from being removed by mistake later.

## [0.26.18] - 2026-08-11
### Fixed
- **Chat ran very long then died with `Control request timeout: initialize`.** The repo owner typed one sentence asking to create 2 checkout pages on Webcake, waited, then received exactly two lines: a bare English error string and "(không có nội dung trả về)" (no content returned). The cause sat where no one thought to look - the MCP tool list is on the CRITICAL PATH of every chat turn. At startup, `claude` must finish connecting every MCP server before it takes work; it connects to the Jarvis 007 hub; the hub returns tools by **probing each source one at a time**, and each source may wait up to its own transport cap (http 60s, stdio 90s at init). On a machine with a dozen connectors and one dead source the total is in minutes, while the Agent SDK waits exactly 60 seconds and gives up. The whole chat turn was lost over one unrelated source.
- **MCP probing now runs in parallel, with a 20-second cap per source.** The total time is about the slowest source rather than the sum of all sources, and a hung source is skipped for that round instead of dragging the whole turn along (the hub cache expires after 60s and probes again, so nothing is lost long-term). A session cut midway is discarded, not reused - cutting through an NDJSON request leaves the stdio pipe permanently out of sync. Adjust with `JAVIS_MCP_DISCOVER_TIMEOUT=<seconds>`, set 0 to remove the cap.
- **The cap for waiting on `claude` to start is raised from 60 to 300 seconds.** The Agent SDK only accepts this cap through the environment variable `CLAUDE_CODE_STREAM_CLOSE_TIMEOUT` and has no parameter in options, so Jarvis 007 sets it for you; if you already set that variable Jarvis 007 does not override it. Adjust with `JAVIS_CLAUDE_INIT_TIMEOUT=<seconds>` (the hard floor of 60s belongs to the SDK).
- **The startup timeout error now says what to do.** Instead of `SDK engine: Exception: Control request timeout: initialize`, users read that the culprit is almost always a dead data source, and to open the Connections page and press Check to find it. An error that does not match the pattern keeps the original string - guessing the cause is worse than bare English.
- Added `test_khoi_dong_cham.py` locking all three: parallel probing with a per-source cap, the raised startup cap, and the error message pointing to the place to click.

## [0.26.17] - 2026-08-11
### Security
- **Jarvis 007 no longer reads your Claude Code sign-in token by itself.** From 0.18.2 until this version, Jarvis 007 opened `~/.claude/.credentials.json` (or the Keychain on macOS), took out the OAuth access token and sent `Authorization: Bearer <token>` straight to `api.anthropic.com/v1/messages`. Anthropic forbids exactly that: Free/Pro/Max plan tokens may only be used in Claude Code and Claude.ai, as they state in the Legal & compliance docs since February 2026, and they fully blocked third-party tools from 04/04/2026. They detect it by inspecting the request fingerprint - missing the telemetry and heartbeat that only the official CLI emits - and the requests Jarvis 007 built itself had none of those. Some Jarvis 007 users had their accounts locked.
- **All three places that extracted the token are removed**, and each has a regression canary: the saving chat path (`main._api_stream_goc`), the tool-call loop of the specialist bot (`main._bot_stream_co_tool`), and the live model list (`claude_models`). The two `oauth_token` parameters in `engine.py` are removed too. The `claude_models` module now has only two functions and touches none of the user's files.
- **No feature is lost.** All three paths run through the real `claude` binary again, letting Anthropic's own product handle sign-in. The Ultra-saving level keeps its savings by sending a bare system prompt instead of the Claude Code preset - putting the preset in makes it stuff the full prompt back in and eats all the savings. The live model list now asks with an API key if the machine has one; without a key it keeps the four aliases `opus/sonnet/haiku/fable`, and aliases always point to the latest version so they do not go stale.

### Added
- **The Models page has a "Runs on" box for Claude Code**: keep the signed-in plan, or use an Anthropic API key. Both choices keep the SAME capabilities - Bash, WebFetch, MCP, resuming old sessions - and differ only in who pays and who bears the risk. Choose the API key and Jarvis 007 passes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` down to the `claude` process; choose the API key but leave the key box blank and it falls back to the existing sign-in session rather than killing the chat turn.
- **The warning shows exactly when it is worrying**, not flashing all the time: only when the machine has the subscription plan carrying background work (the background-work model points at Claude Code) does the Claude Code card show a yellow strip stating the risk and the two ways out. The server combines those two conditions itself and returns them with the data; the dashboard does not guess.
- **Background work on a subscription plan is still a CHOICE, not hard-disabled.** The machine owner weighs the risk, and Jarvis 007 only ensures they weigh it knowing. The README, the website and the system prompt all say this plainly instead of just advertising "0 dong API cost".

### Fixed
- **The Full access level of Kanban jobs was never full access.** `_lane_tools` read `execution_mode` and threw it away: every job was fenced by the allowlist, even a job the owner deliberately set to Full access. The result was not "slightly stricter" but a whole layer of tools missing. Gmail, Google Drive and Google Calendar plug into the Claude ACCOUNT and are not in Jarvis 007's MCP registry, so they can only be called with the native tool `mcp__<name>__*` - and native tools exist only when the session runs WITHOUT an allowlist. Now `full` returns a truly empty allowlist, identical to the full branch of loops and reminders. The three lower levels keep the fence.
- **Turning on `mcp.strict` silently locked the back door of Full access.** This flag means "use only Jarvis 007's MCP", and ambient connectors sit outside Jarvis 007's registry, so at full level it opened the allowlist and then blocked exactly the group it just opened. Now `full` ignores this flag. Whoever turns on strict wants to tighten the LOWER levels; anyone who chose Full access for a job needs that job to be truly full access, otherwise "Full access" is a lying label.
- **Full access background work no longer falls back to a backup engine on its own.** The chain *secondary engine → Claude → OpenRouter free* is right for light work, but plainly wrong at full level for three reasons: API engines have no native tools so a job needing Google Drive stops midway; the model does not know it was just switched to another engine so it makes up a plausible but wrong reason; and the earlier link may have done PART of the job (posted 1 of 3 posts) before breaking, and rerunning the whole prompt would repost from the start. Now full level stops outright and reports the real reason. Auto/suggest levels keep the fallback chain.
- **The API engine states honestly which tools it lacks.** Without this statement the model only sees "tool call failed" and blames permissions - exactly what happened: a Fanpage posting reminder reported to Telegram "this session is permission-blocked" while the owner had turned on Full access, sending people to fix the wrong place all morning. Now the API engine's system prompt says plainly that it has no Bash, no WebFetch, no Claude account connectors, and directly forbids describing that as lacking permission.

### Improved
- **Specialist bots running on the Claude Code plan now build an explicit safety fence.** Up to the previous version, "bots never have native tools" was a free consequence of an architectural fact: no bot engine opened the CLI. This version had to drop that fact, so the support is rebuilt in four layers and all four have canaries: an allowlist containing only the hub (the `can_use_tool` gate rejects every other tool on each call), a denylist directly blocking the native group, a hub config carrying the BOT's brain so file tools are locked by `_safe_path` to exactly that brain, and `mcp_strict` so the bot does not see the owner's connectors.
- `mcp_hub.claude_config_path` takes an extra `vault_root`. Needed for exactly the case above: the normal Claude engine has native Read/Write so the hub deliberately does not grant the file tool group, but the bot has native blocked so without it the bot loses the ability to write entirely. The config file is split per brain so two bots on two brains running in parallel do not overwrite each other's headers.
- Added `test_full_quyen_ungated.py` guarding the rule **"full => ungated"** on all four background paths. The four paths deliberately do not share one engine-building function (their fences really differ), so this rule must be guarded on each path one by one - which is exactly why `tasks.py` drifted for many versions without anyone seeing.

## [0.26.16] - 2026-08-10
### Added
- **Back / Forward buttons between notes in the editor.** Reading a wiki means following a chain of `[[wikilink]]`: one click leaves the note you are reading, and before this version there was NO way back - you had to find the old file again in the tree. That means every link click is a one-way decision, exactly what makes people shy of clicking links in their own vault.
- **Designed to be familiar rather than clever.** Two arrows `‹ ›` sit to the LEFT of the file name, exactly where every browser puts them, so there is nothing to learn. `Alt` + `←` / `→` keys work like a browser. A mouse with side back/forward buttons works too (caught at `mousedown` so it does not go back a whole dashboard page and lose the conversation that is open).
- **The tooltip names the destination FILE**, not just the word "Back": "Back to: Bát Giác Offer.md". After going four or five link levels deep, remembering where you came from is not easy, so the button says it before you press.
- **When there is nowhere to go the button FADES instead of disappearing.** A button that shows and hides makes the title bar jump, and users never learn the button exists. A faded button can still explain why pressing does nothing.
- The trail survives closing the editor (closing to go to chat and returning to the same note and reopening is the most common flow), clears itself when the brain changes, fixes itself when a file is renamed and trims itself when a file is deleted - all three cases lead to "press Back and land on a path that no longer exists". Standing mid-trail and opening a new note cuts the forward branch, just like a browser.

### Fixed
- **Leaving a half-edited file no longer loses text.** Click a `[[wikilink]]`, click another file in the tree, or press Back/Forward: if there are edits not yet saved, Jarvis 007 saves first and then goes. This bug existed before, but the Back/Forward buttons make leaving a file much more frequent so unfixed it would become a trap.
- **If saving fails it STAYS**, does not move on, and the error shows right on the Save button. Moving on then would throw away what people just wrote without saying a word.
- **Only READING and then leaving writes nothing.** The "was anything edited" baseline comes from the editor frame itself right after opening, not the raw text read from disk: the WYSIWYG render converted back to markdown always drifts a little from the original file (normalized punctuation, line breaks), so compared to the original file, opening it just to read would count as an edit and Jarvis 007 would silently overwrite that file's formatting.

### Improved
- Docs: [File management](docs/05-quan-ly-tep-tin.md) adds a section "Back / Forward between notes".

## [0.26.15] - 2026-08-10
### Added
- **Give commands by voice recording on Zalo**, just like Telegram in the previous version. Hold the microphone and say one sentence, Jarvis 007 transcribes it and acts as if you had typed it. **It shares one Groq key**: if you connected it for Telegram, Zalo works at once with nothing extra to do.
- Work with outside effects (sending messages, posting, scheduling, spending money, editing files) still reads back "Em nghe: ..." (the bot's "I heard: ...") and asks for confirmation. The recording file is not saved to `inbox/`.
- The listening part has been in `server/stt.py` since the previous version and knows nothing of Telegram or Zalo, so this version only wires it up and does not write a second copy. The instruction line for the engine also moved there so the two channels do not drift in wording.

### Fixed
- **Differs from Telegram in exactly one step, and it is the riskiest: Zalo has NO `getFile`.** The whole set of methods Zalo publishes has none that downloads a file, so the only path to the recording is a URL already in the message data - and Zalo leaves the data shape of `message.voice.received` blank in its docs. So Jarvis 007 tries a series of field names (`voice_url`, `voice`, `audio_url`, `audio`, `file_url`, `url`, including the nested form `{"url": ...}`) instead of betting on one and silently dropping all voice messages when the bet is wrong.
- **If all miss it speaks up, not silent.** The bot tells the sender plainly that it could not download the recording, and the server writes ONE line `[zalo voice] không tìm ra đường dẫn file thoại trong payload` (cannot find the voice file path in the payload) with a sample of the real data - the first run tells you by itself what the field is called. It speaks once per bot session, not spamming the log with every message.
- This URL-extracting function is shared with the image part (before, written nested inside the image branch), so the two kinds of file no longer have two drifting copies of logic.

### Improved
- Docs: [Zalo Bot channel](docs/26-kenh-zalo-bot.md) adds a section "Give commands by voice recording" with a warning about the unpublished data shape; [Telegram](docs/11-telegram.md) and [Models & engine](docs/10-models-va-engine.md) are updated to match.

## [0.26.14] - 2026-08-10
### Added
- **Give commands by voice recording on Telegram.** Hold the microphone and say one sentence, Jarvis 007 transcribes it and acts exactly as if you had typed it. Before, sending a voice message only got back the sentence "Jarvis 007 chưa đọc được loại này, nhờ anh gõ chữ" ("Jarvis 007 cannot read this type yet, please type text") - meaning the biggest button in Telegram, the microphone, was unusable, exactly when people need it most (driving, hands busy).
- **Runs on Groq's Whisper, using a key you already have.** Groq is already one of Jarvis 007's eight brains and serves Whisper on the same endpoint as the chat model, so anyone who connected Groq for chat gets voice messages at once, with no extra provider to sign up for. Conversely, connecting a key just for listening also works - you need not switch the main model to Groq.
- **If no key is connected it says clearly what to do**, not silent and not a vague "cannot read yet": the bot points straight to the Models page, the Groq (API) section, to paste a key from console.groq.com. The key is read AT THE MOMENT OF LISTENING so after pasting the next voice message works at once, with no need to restart the bot.
- **Work with outside effects asks again first.** Sending messages, posting, scheduling, spending money, editing files: Jarvis 007 opens with one line "Em nghe: ..." (the bot's "I heard: ...") and waits for confirmation. Machines can still mishear, and those actions cannot be taken back once done. Asking for figures, lookups and summaries is done directly.
- **Every failure path comes back as a spoken sentence**: file too long, no words recognized, Groq returns an error, the listening function throws an exception. A voice message is the kind where "broken" and "working" look identical on the sender's side (hold, release, see it sent), so silence here is the worst kind of failure.
- The recording file is NOT saved to `inbox/`: once heard and turned into text it is done, people record to give commands and not to send Jarvis 007 an `.ogg` file.
- Sending a voice message with the caption `/notes` still runs the right command with the spoken sentence as content (a multi-line voice block goes through intact, not cut like an attached-file marker).
- Video and video notes still cannot be viewed, but the refusal sentence is no longer lumped together with voice.
- The Zalo channel cannot hear voice messages yet. The listening part is in `server/stt.py` and knows nothing about Telegram, so plugging Zalo in later is wiring, not a rewrite.
- Docs: [Telegram](docs/11-telegram.md) adds a section "Give commands by voice recording (voice messages)" + two troubleshooting sections; [Models & engine](docs/10-models-va-engine.md) states plainly that the Groq key is also used for listening.

## [0.26.13] - 2026-08-10
### Improved
- **The "open file" card under the chat box is now clickable: click it to go back to editing that very file.** Before, the card was only to look at. Open a note to edit, close the editor and chat a few turns, and to keep editing you had to find the file again in the vault tree - exactly the chore the pinned card exists to spare. Now click the card (or select it with the Tab key and Enter) and the file reopens in the editor, with the vault tree expanding to the exact branch holding it.
- **If the file is already open it only brings your eyes back, it does NOT reload.** This is the part easiest to get wrong: reopening an already-open file means rereading the content from disk, so the text just typed and not yet saved would be wiped. So the editor remembers which file is open, and on a match only scrolls back and puts the cursor where you were composing.
- **The ✕ button on the card is still only unpin**, and does not catch the click that opens the file. On phones (screens under 860px, where the pinned editor is off) the card opens the file in the edit frame popping up in the middle of the screen.
- The card now has a pen on the right and changes its border on hover - a feature with no visible sign counts as nonexistent. The sub-line changes from "open - Jarvis 007 works on this file" to "open - click to keep editing"; the "Jarvis 007 is working on this file" meaning moves into the tooltip along with the full path.
- Docs: updated [File management](docs/05-quan-ly-tep-tin.md) and [Chat & voice](docs/02-tro-chuyen-va-giong-noi.md).

## [0.26.12] - 2026-08-09
### Fixed
- **"Start with Windows" showed On while nothing ran at boot.** The whole feature fits in one registry line `HKCU\...\Run`, and the dashboard read exactly that line and concluded "On". But that line **remains intact** in at least three situations where nothing runs at sign-in, and none leaves an error anywhere to trace. Users only saw `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` and a lying card.
- **The quietest situation: Task Manager turned it off.** The **Startup** tab does not delete the entry in the Run key when you press Disable; it writes a 12-byte flag into `Explorer\StartupApproved\Run` and Explorer then ignores that entry. "Clean-up, boost startup" software also turns things off with exactly this flag, often without asking. Jarvis 007 now reads that flag, and **pressing Turn on autostart removes the real flag** rather than just rewriting the Run key (rewriting the Run key does not touch the flag, so before, that button did nothing in exactly this case).
- **The second situation: the install folder moved.** The `stale` flag had been computed for a long time but **the Settings page ignored it entirely**, only the Overview page showed it. On the same broken machine two pages gave two different answers. Now the reason is computed once by the server and both pages show it, so there is no room for two drifting copies.
- **The third situation: a piece of the chain vanished** (`start-javis.vbs` or `.venv\Scripts\python.exe`). `wscript` is completely silent when it cannot see the .vbs file, while `cmd` writes the error to `javis.log`, a file no one ever opens. Now Jarvis 007 checks when reading the status and names exactly which file is missing.
- **The label on the card tells the truth:** if on but there is a problem it says "On but not running" with a sentence pointing to what to fix, instead of a plain "On". The status also returns the path `server\javis.log` so there is somewhere to look when the server runs but dies midway.
- Docs: added a section "When the card says On but it is not running" to [Getting started & setup](docs/01-bat-dau-thiet-lap.md).
## [0.26.11] - 2026-08-09
### Fixed
- **The Zalo bot card no longer turns red over a single failed poll.** Version 0.26.10 fixed the idle "Request timeout" case, but it rested on an UNVERIFIED GUESS: that Zalo's wait-timeout beat carries no `error_code`. Zalo's docs say nothing about it. If the guess went wrong that way, the fix would silently not run, and users would see the same old red card without knowing why. It now accepts both shapes: a timeout code (408, 504) together with the word timeout is still an idle beat.
- **An unknown error only turns the card red after 3 CONSECUTIVE failed polls.** One failed poll is a transport problem, not something the owner has to act on, and a card that goes red for it loses its value just as it did when it went red on every idle poll. A poll that works or an idle poll clears the counter, so two failures an hour apart do not add up to "broken".
- **Errors that NEED A PERSON still turn the card red immediately** (401 wrong token, 403 blocked, 404 bot deleted, 429 too many calls). Only this group can tell the owner one concrete thing to do, so it is not delayed by the 3-poll threshold.
- Why both problems tend to show up when you ask a HARD question: while Jarvis 007 thinks for a long time, the poll loop runs empty with no messages, so every poll in that stretch lands in exactly this branch. In quick back-and-forth chat every poll has messages and the card stays clean, so the bug only shows when someone is waiting on a long answer.

## [0.26.10] - 2026-08-09
### Fixed
- **An IDLE Zalo bot is no longer reported as BROKEN.** The bot card on the Chatbot page showed a red "Error" dot with "Request timeout" while the bot was alive and still answering. Cause: Zalo's `getUpdates` does not behave like Telegram's. When the wait times out, Telegram returns `ok: true` with an empty list, while Zalo returns `ok: false` with `description: "Request timeout"`. That is the normal rhythm of long polling: 25 seconds with nobody writing means there is simply nothing to return.
- **And the bot no longer goes DEAF for 10 seconds every idle poll.** This is the heavier part, but it hid behind the one above so nobody saw it: the error branch slept 10 seconds before polling again, so on every poll with no messages the bot heard nothing for 10 seconds. Messages arriving in that gap were not lost, they just had to wait for the next poll to be read. Now an idle poll polls again immediately, and only holds back a short beat if Zalo answers almost instantly (ignoring the `timeout` parameter), so the loop does not hammer the API several times a second and then hit a real 429.
- **A permanently red card is a worse failure than it looks:** idle is the normal state of a customer-care bot, so the card would be red nearly all the time, and when the bot breaks FOR REAL nobody would notice any more.
- **The line of the fix is drawn at who is speaking, not at the word "timeout".** A Jarvis 007 server losing its network also produces a string containing timeout, and that is a real failure. Now `_api` tags dicts built from exceptions with a `loi_mang` marker, while an idle beat must come from Zalo itself as a JSON body carrying no error code. Real errors (401, 429, network loss) keep the old behavior: red card, reason recorded, long pause, then retry.

### Improved
- **Anthropic's 429 is now waited out at the pace of the rate limit, not the pace of a network hiccup.** The previous version retried at 1 second, 2 seconds, 4 seconds, so all three retries fit inside seven seconds, while the rate-limit window is measured in minutes. Three tries in seven seconds just hit the same 429 three times, then report "retried 3 times" and give up. Now a 429 waits at its own pace, long enough for a short congestion spike to pass.
- **It also reads the window reopening times that Anthropic already sends** (`anthropic-ratelimit-*-reset`). Anthropic does not always send `Retry-After`, and when it is missing these headers are the ONLY source that says how long to wait. Ignoring them means blinding yourself and guessing. It takes the earliest window to open: waiting too little still leaves a retry to wait again, while waiting too long makes people sit idle for nothing.
- **The error line on the bot card now says what to do next.** Before, it pasted a raw blob of the provider's JSON, which does not answer the only question the owner has when looking at a red card. Now it says plainly that this is a rate limit, how long until the window reopens (when known), and that the bot's brain can be changed on the Models page. The original error is still kept next to it so it can be looked up.

## [0.26.9] - 2026-08-09
### Improved
- **Jarvis 007 stops answering with walls of prose in the web chat box.** Long answers now have shapes for the eye to hold on to: paragraphs of 2-4 sentences, bullets when listing 3 or more points, bold for numbers and conclusions, `###` headings when an answer has clearly separate parts, and tables when comparing the same set of fields across several items.
- **Why it wrote that way before: it was a real rule, written for the era of using it by VOICE.** CLAUDE.md flatly banned "markdown tables, thick dashes, or headers when reporting in chat". That rule was right for the listening era, but it banned the whole presentation toolkit on a channel that can draw full markdown. Once use moved to mostly reading by eye, the same rule became the chat box's worst display bug.
- **The worry about breaking the voice reading is gone.** The dashboard speaker button already strips markdown (headings, bold, bullets, links, code blocks) before reading aloud, so formatting that looks good to the eye does not hurt the audio at all. Jarvis 007 is now told this plainly so it stops holding itself to prose.
- **Structure serves length, not the other way round.** A question answerable in one sentence still gets one sentence. Splitting a small point into three bullets to look like a report is harder to read than prose, so the new rule blocks that opposite direction too.
- **Plain-text channels are NOT loosened.** Telegram and Zalo still ban tables, and the terminal still bans tables, embedded images and markdown links. These three channels only gain the one thing that reads clearly everywhere: bullets when listing.
- Fixed in all three layers, because missing one layer sends behavior back to the old way on exactly that path: the root rule in `CLAUDE.md`, the channel block in `channel_context.py` (it sits at the end of the system prompt so it is the loudest voice), and the capsule in `context_compiler.py` (the token-saving path does not read CLAUDE.md, and forgetting it means turning on "Super saver" brings the prose back with nobody able to guess why). `tests/python/test_chat_de_doc.py` guards all three, with canaries for the old ban sentence and for the plain-text channel boundary.

### Good to know
- If the brain's long-term memory still holds an old memory like "dislikes markdown tables, prefers short spoken prose", that memory is loaded into every turn and will pull behavior back to the old way. Jarvis 007 is now told the new rule beats that memory, but cleaning the memory out of `Memory/facts/` is still cleaner.

## [0.26.8] - 2026-08-08
### Added
- **A Zalo channel for the OWNER: ask Jarvis 007 right on Zalo, no Telegram install needed.** A new Zalo card on the **Channels** page (Connections group). It uses Zalo's official API, so there is no risk of an account lock. See [Zalo Bot channel](docs/26-kenh-zalo-bot.md).
- **Pairing with ONE click, no id lookup.** Zalo has no tool for you to look up your own Zalo id, and that id is a hex string like `6ede9afa66b88fe6d6a9`, not an easy number. So Jarvis 007 flips the flow: turn the bot on with the Chat ID box left EMPTY, send the bot one message, the bot replies with a 4-digit pairing code, then you click **Allow** right on the dashboard. The waiting person shows up with their **real Zalo name** so you do not click the wrong one.
- **Work assigned from Zalo reports results BACK to Zalo.** Loops, Kanban tasks and reminders set through Zalo carry the `zalo:` prefix, so results land in that very chat box, not in the owner's Telegram.
- **The "preconditions before creating a schedule" gate now accepts Zalo.** Before, if you only connected Zalo and created a reminder, it was blocked with the reason "Telegram bot not enabled" - a sentence that was both wrong and unfixable, and it pushed users to install an app they did not need.

### Security
- **An empty Chat ID box on the Zalo channel means NO ONE is allowed yet**, deliberately different from Telegram. On Telegram an empty box opens it to everyone, and the docs have to warn against leaving it empty - because there users can look up their own id before turning it on. Zalo has no such path, so the right flow is to turn it on empty and then message the bot yourself. Keeping Telegram's behavior here would make that very guided flow create a bot anyone can use to reach the brain, in the gap between turning it on and clicking Allow. Fail-closed.
- A stranger who writes in gets **one** refusal per 10 minutes, the waiting queue holds at most 20 people, and entries older than 30 minutes drop off on their own. This is a mailbox open to strangers, so it must not grow without limit.

### Good to know
- Zalo cannot edit or delete messages, so this channel has **no status message**: while waiting there is only the "typing" dot, and the tool trace line attached at the end of the answer.
- Zalo Bot **has no document-sending API yet**, so PDFs and spreadsheets cannot be sent through this channel. Jarvis 007 says so plainly and gives the path inside the brain instead of silently swallowing the file.
- The ceiling for one message is **2000 characters**, and Zalo **shows no command menu**, so `/...` commands must be typed by hand.

## [0.26.7] - 2026-08-08
### Fixed
- **Internal connectors (Substack, Botcake) were swept out of the tool discovery pass, so no brain could call them.** The connection was on, permission full, token alive, and the Connections page showed "Connected", yet all 16 tools of these two connectors were invisible to every engine - with no error line anywhere. This is the worst kind of failure: every light is green while nothing runs.
- **Cause: three places asked the same question and all gave the same wrong answer.** "Does this connection have a server to dial" was asked in the tool discovery pass, in the Test button, and in the health check; all three hand-wrote `not (url or command)`. The `internal` transport calls a Python module in the repo directly, so it has neither url nor command, and fell straight into the "no server" branch meant for connections that only hold an OAuth token.
- **The last two also hid the first.** The Test button and the health light returned "OK" without ever making a call, counting tools from the catalog description instead of calling for real. So there was no way to notice the discovery pass was broken. Now both really dial like every other connector.
- The fix: one shared function `mcp_client.co_server_de_dial`, and `tests/python/test_mcp_connector_internal.py` guards both the behavior and that all three places really call the shared function - because the root disease was three hand-copied versions drifting apart.

## [0.26.6] - 2026-08-08
### Fixed
- **Opening the bot Edit form and clicking Save no longer wipes the name of a running bot.** The bug came in with 0.26.5: the function that applies the channel choice also ran ONCE when the form opened to build the initial state, and it dropped the verified token unconditionally. As a result, editing any field and saving made the card report "no token yet" for a bot that was still alive. Now it only drops when the channel REALLY changes, and the "Using ..." line stays as is when nothing changed.

## [0.26.5] - 2026-08-08
### Added
- **Specialist bots run on Zalo, through the OFFICIAL API.** This is the biggest business-value change in this release: no Vietnamese customer installs Telegram, while Zalo is already on their phone. Create the bot on the **Chatbot** page, pick the Zalo channel, and paste the token from the "Zalo Bot Manager" Official Account in the Zalo app. There is no account-lock risk like the personal Zalo route.
- **Zalo Bot does NOT replace Zalo Agent MCP**, they are different in nature and coexist. The bot is its own official identity and only sees what people message straight to it; `zalo-agent-cli` logs in as your own account, reads real conversations and can message anyone, at the price of a lock risk. The first is for **customers to talk to Jarvis 007**, the second is for **Jarvis 007 to act for you**.
- **Choosing the channel is the FIRST field in the bot creation form**, as two tappable cards with logos rather than a plain dropdown. It goes first because it changes everything after it: where the token comes from, whether groups work, whether documents can be sent. Each card states its pros and cons right on the button.
- **A channel mark for each bot**, hand-drawn to the repo owner's description: Telegram is a white paper plane on blue, Zalo is a white Z in a blue chat bubble. It appears in two places for two viewing distances: a small badge over the corner of the bot icon (know it at a glance), and a chip with the logo in the info section (for skimming). Two bots on different platforms sitting side by side and differing by one small word would one day lead to editing the one that is talking to customers.
- **An All / Telegram / Zalo filter row** at the top of the Chatbot page, shown only when there really are two or more channels. A new user who only has a Telegram bot and already faces a row of filter buttons is being answered a question they never asked.

### Improved
- **The UI hides what Zalo cannot do**, instead of showing it and letting it do nothing. Choosing Zalo makes the whole group block disappear with one line saying why (Zalo's basic bot plan does not let bots join groups), and group ids already typed are not sent to the server. The "Telegram privacy mode" warning also stops appearing on Zalo bot cards, since it taught people to look for a setting that does not exist.
- **The Check token button asks the platform you ACTUALLY chose.** Pasting a Zalo token into the Telegram route only gives a 401 error, and "invalid token" when the token is perfectly valid is where users stay stuck longest. Duplicate-token blocking is also per channel, because account names are each platform's own namespace.
- **The channel can NOT be changed after the bot is created**, and the Edit form says so plainly instead of letting you click and then reporting a token error at a later step. Changing channel means switching to a completely different bot: different token, different identity, different customers, and every saved group id instantly becomes meaningless.
- **The part shared by every bot gateway is split out into `server/bot_gateway.py`**: turn queue, `/stop` rule, the gate before spending a turn, tool trace line. These are Jarvis 007's behavior rules, not one provider's details, so both channels share one copy. Copying to a second copy guarantees two copies drift apart, and the drift would sit in the place least looked at: a bot talking to strangers.

### Good to know
- Zalo Bot **has no document-sending API yet** (only image sending), so files Jarvis 007 creates cannot be sent through this channel. Jarvis 007 states the reason plainly instead of silently swallowing the file.
- Zalo **cannot edit or delete sent messages**, so the Zalo bot has no status message at all: only the "typing" dot while waiting, and the tool trace line attached right in the answer.
- The ceiling for one Zalo message is **2000 characters** (Telegram is 4096), and long answers split automatically.
- Zalo has not published API rate limits. On a 429 Jarvis 007 pauses and retries on its own, and shows the error on the status line instead of swallowing it.

## [0.26.4] - 2026-08-08
### Improved
- **The Telegram bot no longer sends a message and then deletes it.** Before, on every turn the bot sent "🤔 Jarvis 007 is processing...", updated it with progress, then **deleted it entirely** and sent the answer. Users saw a message flash and vanish, which read like an error, and anyone mid-read lost text. Now that message **stays**: the last update turns it into a compact trace line, and the answer is a new message below. No message disappears any more.
- **The phone vibrates once per turn, and at the right moment.** The status message is now sent silently (`disable_notification`), so the only notification is when the real answer arrives, showing the actual answer content. Before, it vibrated twice and the first only said "processing", which called people over to read a sentence with no information in it.
- **The trace line says what that turn touched**, for example `⚙ pos_statistics · Read · 8s`. A turn that called no tool reads `✓ Answered directly · 3s`. This is not decoration: it is how to tell a number just fetched from the real POS apart from a bare answer, and it stays in the chat history so it can be looked up.
- **Typing `/stop` midway turns the status message into "⏹ Stopped"** instead of vanishing without trace, so the cut-off question still has a place in the chat thread.
- Checked against the Telegram API: **there is no way to show arbitrary status text without sending a message** (`sendChatAction` only takes a fixed set of actions like "typing", "sending photo", and takes no text). So what could be fixed is not letting any message vanish and not firing extra notifications, rather than dropping the status message altogether.
- Specialist bots talking to customers **keep their old behavior**: still not exposing a single status line, only the "typing..." dot.

## [0.26.3] - 2026-08-08
### Added
- **Saver mode says HOW MUCH it saves, not just what percent.** The Usage page gains three numbers: real tokens saved in the window just measured, a projection to one month at that same pace, and the conversion to money. "38% less" means nothing to someone paying; "about 40 thousand a month" does.
- **The three confidence levels are named exactly**, because the biggest number is easily read as an invoice: tokens in the window just measured are **measured**, tokens per month are a **projection**, money is an **estimate**.
- **Price follows the model that is actually running** rather than a fixed number (Opus differs from Sonnet differs from Haiku differs from Groq). This reference price table will go stale because providers change prices every few months, so setting `gia_input_1m` in the `model` section of `settings.json` overrides it with your real unit price.
- **Honest to subscription-plan users.** A subscription plan does not pay per token, so for them the money figure is the saving converted at API prices, and in practice it shows up as hitting the plan cap later. The UI states this when it detects the engine is a subscription plan; being vague here would cost the whole page its credibility, and this page exists precisely so the numbers can be trusted.
### Fixed
- The **repo URL** box in GitHub Sync no longer uses the repo owner's account as its example.
### Tests
- `test_trang_tiet_kiem.py` adds 20 checks for this part: how saved tokens are computed, the projection scaling correctly with the measurement window length, price changing by model, a custom unit price overriding the table, a junk unit price not crashing the page, not inventing money when there is not enough data, and the UI having to name the three confidence levels exactly.

## [0.26.2] - 2026-08-08
Git keeps only TEXT, not media. Chat box font size goes up to 16px.
### Changed
- **GitHub Sync only puts text files into the repo.** Notes, Wiki, memories, skills, recurring-job configs, scripts (`.md .txt .html .csv .json .yaml .canvas .py .svg`...). Images, video, audio, PDF and every other binary file **do not go up** - they stay on your machine and work as usual, they just do not enter git history. The list is an ALLOW list, not a block list, so newly invented media formats are automatically left out, with no need to chase them with patches.
- Why a hard rule and not an option: git is designed to remember forever. The content of every committed file becomes a blob that lives permanently in `.git/objects`; deleting the file later only records one more line saying "from here this file is gone", while the blob must be kept so older commits can be restored, and `git gc` cannot clean it because it still has an owner. For text that is an advantage (git compresses and stores deltas, so hundreds of edits stay light). For media it is the opposite: mp4/jpg are already compressed by a codec so git cannot compress them further, and two renders of the same clip are two entirely different files, not one lightly edited file. A few hundred MB of media plus a habit of re-rendering a few times will push the repo to several GB within months, and the only way to shrink it is to rewrite the whole history - which makes every copy on other machines incompatible.
- **The Sync page says this plainly**, with the reason and where media should live instead (Drive, an external drive: stored by current state, delete it and you get the real space back). After each sync, if any media was skipped, Jarvis 007 states how many files and how many MB. Skipping silently would one day lead a user to think their photos were backed up too.
### Fixed
- **`.gitignore` rules are now written as a BLOCK, not appended at the end.** An allowlist rule is only right in the right order (block everything → open for text → block the forbidden folders again). The previous version only appended missing lines at the end of the file, so on an old brain the "block again" lines sat before the "open for text" line and git read it backwards: `Javis/learn-log/*.json` was opened again. Raw logs may contain secrets, so that was not a cosmetic bug. Users' own added rules are still kept and still sit after Jarvis 007's block so they can override it.
- **Other machines no longer lose real media.** The machine that updates first cleans media out of its copy and pushes that deletion to the repo; if the second machine pulled and simply applied it, it would lose files on disk. Both directions now go through exactly one filter function, so media deletions coming from the remote are ignored instead of executed.
### Improved
- **Chat box font size 15px up to 16px** (both Jarvis 007's messages and the user's). The line length cap is measured in `ch` so it widens along with it, keeping the same number of characters per line.
### Tests
- Added `tests/python/test_git_chi_giu_chu.py`: 45 checks, including **building a REAL git repo** and asking git what it would commit - the only way to be sure of rule order, since reasoning over a `.gitignore` string is very easy to get wrong. It also covers upgrading an old brain that has the user's own rules.
- **Fixed a false positive in the `test_bien_chua_gan.py` scanner**: it walked into comprehensions to pick up assigned names, so a module-level line `X = [f(n) for n in ...]` was treated as "the module has a variable `n`", and then every function counting with `n += 1` was reported as forgetting `nonlocal`. In Python 3 the comprehension loop variable does not leak out. Locked with its own check.

## [0.26.1] - 2026-08-07
The repo owner sent a screenshot of a long answer: *"I want to improve how Jarvis 007 displays so it is easier to read, more line breaks, it is too hard to read."* Three different causes piled into one wall of text, and fixing any less than all three is still hard to read.
### Improved
- **Line spacing 1.6 up to 1.75.** This is the easiest one to name, and for Vietnamese it matters even more: diacritics stack on top of the letters, so tight lines make the marks almost touch.
- **Spacing between two paragraphs from 6px up to 14px.** This is the quieter cause: 6px is close to the gap between two LINES inside the same paragraph, so the eye cannot tell where a paragraph ends and the whole block sticks into one patch. Lists, headings and quotes were loosened by the same principle; nested lists alone are tightened because they belong to their parent item, and spacing them like paragraphs breaks the reading flow.
- **Line length capped at 76 characters.** This is the main culprit on wide screens: when a line runs past 120 characters, after reading it the eye has to sweep back across the whole screen to find the start of the next line, and every few lines it misreads into a line already read. People feel that as "tiring" and rarely can point to it, so it is also the thing most easily tuned back to the old way. The cap is set on the whole bubble, not on each text paragraph: capping each paragraph leaves the bubble background full width with an empty strip on the right that looks like a display bug. Code blocks and dataview tables are not squeezed because they already have their own horizontal scroll; in narrow chat frames (brain pane, phone) the cap touches nothing.
### Tests
- Added `tests/js/test_de_doc_bong_bong.js`: 15 checks that lock the numbers by **relationship** rather than absolute value. Changing font size or tweaking a few pixels stays green; it only goes red when a relationship breaks, e.g. paragraph spacing dropping below line spacing inside a paragraph (paragraphs stick together), the line length cap being removed, or a heading sitting closer to the paragraph before it than to the one after.

## [0.26.0] - 2026-08-07
"Do it yourself then report" reminders now **do exactly the job you scheduled**, including jobs that have to reach outside. Before this release their permission level was hard-pinned to read-only, so every reminder like "send this for me at 10am tomorrow" woke up on time, ran, then reported it could not do it, and the job was still undone.
### Added
- **Three permission levels for reminders**, same vocabulary as repeating work: **Read only** (read MCP and files then report back), **Write files** (adds permission to write drafts inside the brain), **Full access** (uses every connected tool, including outside actions). Changeable in the form on the Recurring work page, and shown as a label right on the job card.
- **The default is Full access, and this is a deliberate decision.** A reminder differs from repeating work in a basic way: repeating work thinks up the work to do each round, while a reminder does EXACTLY one job you wrote out and scheduled, i.e. a chat instruction moved to another time. Tying it down tighter than when you were sitting in chat is self-contradictory.
- **A warning appears at the moment you are looking.** Choosing Full access on the form shows a red warning box; creating through chat makes the `javis_schedule` tool return a warning sentence that Jarvis 007 must read back verbatim. The content says three things: the job runs alone, with no one reviewing, and most outside actions cannot be taken back.
### Fixed
- **Old reminders (created before this release) automatically run at the new default** instead of falling into read-only, so reminders already waiting in the queue can do the job immediately without being recreated.
- The reminder prompt now states its own permission level correctly. The old version hard-pasted the sentence "absolutely do not send messages outside" into every reminder, so even when permission was opened at the tool layer the model refused on its own. Full access also gets told one thing it cannot infer by itself: at that time nobody is sitting beside it, so asking back is asking into the void - if it can do it, do it and narrate, if it cannot, say so plainly.
### Tests
- Added `tests/python/test_nhac_hen_muc_quyen.py`: 39 checks, the most worthwhile part being that **the three levels build REALLY different engines** (allowlist, hub level, the brain passed down, and the constraint sentence in the prompt) rather than only changing the label. It includes old records missing a field and junk values.
- Also locks the requirement that **the warning must be neutral**: the test rejects it if the warning sentence contains the name of a specific channel or industry. Jarvis 007 is a tool for many people, each connecting a different set of tools.

## [0.25.9] - 2026-08-07
The repo owner sent a Telegram screenshot: the loop "[CK] Tin Hot Chứng Khoán" ran on ChatGPT instead of Claude, every file read/write command returned `bwrap: Failed to make / slave: Permission denied`, and the report that came back was a long essay of the model narrating its own confusion.
### Fixed
- **Background work running on ChatGPT could not read a single file in Docker.** Codex wraps all its file read/write commands in bubblewrap, and bubblewrap needs to create a user namespace and change the propagation of `/`. The Jarvis 007 container runs as a normal user without `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, and Ubuntu 24.04 also blocks unprivileged user namespaces with AppArmor. So in Docker, both Codex sandbox levels `read-only` (suggest mode) and `workspace-write` (auto mode) **can never start** - the fence is not stricter, it is simply dead. Loops created from chat default to `suggest`, so all background work running on ChatGPT in Docker went mute in exactly this way. Running on Claude is fine because Jarvis 007 blocks per tool through the SDK itself, with no bubblewrap needed.
- **The Docker image now presets `JAVIS_CODEX_SANDBOX=off`**, so the container itself is the fence. Updating to this version makes ChatGPT background work run right away, with nothing to touch on the VPS. The trade-off is written straight into the Dockerfile rather than hidden: Codex has no per-call allowlist like Claude, so with this flag a `suggest`-level loop loses the thing that stopped it writing files inside the container. The fences for money, orders, posting and sending messages are NOT affected because they live in the MCP Hub, not in the sandbox. Anyone who wants to keep the fence sets `JAVIS_CODEX_SANDBOX=auto` and then grants the container permission (e.g. `security_opt: [apparmor:unconfined]`).
- **Jarvis 007 recognizes the `bwrap` trace and explains itself inside the report.** Before, what reached the owner was a model telling a story, and after reading it nobody knew the fix belonged at the container layer. Now the end of the run has one line naming the culprit, stating this is not a fault of the run, and pointing at exactly two ways out. Needed too by people running their own container.
### Tests
- Added `tests/python/test_codex_sandbox_docker.py`: 24 checks covering the map from permission level to sandbox flag (including odd values and odd levels), the real wiring through `aux_engine._build_codex` down to argv, whether the Docker image sets the flag and records both the reason and the trade-off, and that recognizing the `bwrap` trace does not catch normal runs by mistake.
- Also locks an image-build trap: a comment must not be wedged into the middle of an `ENV` block continued with `\`, because a broken Dockerfile means the VPS can no longer update.

## [0.25.8] - 2026-08-07
Two intermittently red tests were the background of every run, forcing everyone to guess "is this a bug I just caused?". Both are now fixed for good, and one of them turned out to be a real product bug, not a test bug.
### Fixed
- **The representative sentence in the "missing documentation" list was chosen wrongly when two turns had the same timestamp.** `chatbot_log.lo_hong` groups duplicate questions and keeps the NEWEST one as the representative, but it compared with `>`, so when two turns had equal `ts` it kept the OLD one. The Windows system clock jumps in steps of ~15ms, so two customers asking close together having the same `ts` is common. Now it compares with `>=`: `_nap` reads in the order written, so the one later in the file is the newer one. This is a product bug, only coincidentally exposed by a randomly red test about 1 run in 6.
### Tests
- `test_chatbot_grounding.py` locks the same-`ts` case with a STANDING-STILL clock instead of relying on luck: changing `>=` back to `>` makes the test red for certain. Run 25 times in a row, green all 25.
- **`test_readonly_orchestrator_phase7.py` was red on a machine that had run the real app, green on CI** - the hardest kind of "red on my machine" to trace because the fault lives in data outside the repo. `ObserveRuntime.start_turn` pins the revision from the GLOBAL registry, while `resume` checks against a registry built separately for the test. The fixture pinned `registry_revision` but missed `model_profile_revision`, so any machine with data in the `model_profiles` table had 3 resume checks go red. Now both are pinned, and the test no longer depends on the runner's state dir.

## [0.25.7] - 2026-08-07
The repo owner sent a screenshot of the "Cười Sóng AI" group: *"chat anything in the group once the bot is added and it always shows typing, how do we make typing show only when the bot actually answers."* Two people in the group talk to each other, and on every message the bot shows "typing..." then quietly says nothing.
### Fixed
- **The `precheck` gate never could block the silent case.** A specialist bot says "block, say nothing" by returning `{}`, but the gate in `_dispatch` was written as `if chan:` - an empty dict is falsy so the block branch was skipped and the turn kept running. What was visible was the "typing..." dot on every message in the group. What was NOT visible costs much more: **every message in the group cost a real engine turn**, run to the end and only then returned as `im_lang` by a second layer in `answer_fn` and thrown away. In a busy group that is a token bill for sentences nobody asked the bot. The gate now compares with `is not None`, exactly as the contract in the docstring says.
- This bug sat quiet from the day `precheck` existed and only showed up in 0.25.5, when the "typing..." dot changed from one 5-second blink to lit continuously through the turn. It turned an invisible bug into a visible one.
### Tests
- `test_bot_noi_nhu_nguoi.py` adds 7 checks for the precheck gate: `{}` means no engine call, no "typing...", nothing sent; `{"reply": ...}` says exactly one sentence and still does not call the engine; `None` is the only case allowed to run the turn; and if precheck blows up it still answers instead of swallowing the customer's message.

## [0.25.6] - 2026-08-07
The repo owner told Jarvis 007 *"design a .md file for me"*, Jarvis 007 answered *"there is a clash between your choice and the strategy document, I will handle it directly in the file. Writing the file now."* and then the turn died at second 180 with the line *"Claude was answering then went silent for 180s - stopped to avoid hanging the server."* An unjust death: the engine was composing the file content to pass to the Write tool, everything was running correctly, there was just nothing to emit.
### Fixed
- **The 180s cap and the 600s cap are gone entirely.** The problem is not the numbers but the MEASUREMENT: the watchdog counted "how long since a message was received from the SDK" and treated that as hung, while the SDK only emits a message when the model finishes a block. A model thinking at high effort, or composing a long file's content to hand to the write tool, both make the channel silent for minutes with nothing broken. Now the two silence-measuring caps (`JAVIS_CLAUDE_IDLE_TIMEOUT`, `JAVIS_CLAUDE_FIRST_TIMEOUT`) default to **no limit**. Cutting a turn that is running fine loses all the effort and tokens, which is far worse than letting it run long.
- **The TOOL wait cap stays at 1 hour.** This cap measures something real: a tool has started but not returned a result, meaning a child process is alive out there and it really can hang (waiting for input, stuck on a file lock). This is a fundamental difference from the two caps above.
- **Background work still cannot hang forever.** Loops, Kanban tasks, reminders and self-learning all already have their own wall-clock cap (`max_wall_s`, from 240 to 600 seconds depending on kind), so removing the silence cap does not open the way for background work to run forever. Dashboard chat can always be stopped with the Stop button.
- **`0` hours means "no limit" for all three variables**, for both the Claude engine and the Codex engine. A junk value in the environment variable falls back to the default instead of blowing up the chat turn.
- **The timeout message no longer infers the reason backwards.** The cap and the reason are fixed together when the cap is chosen; inferring backwards after the timeout both produced a wrong message (saying "tool ran too long" when it actually hit the wall-clock cap) and had a path to `int(None)` blowing up mid-chat when one cap is turned off.
### Tests
- `test_sdk_engine.py` adds 4 checks running FOR REAL through the engine: with `IDLE=0` it is not cut however long it is silent, `FIRST=0` likewise, the tool wait cap can still interrupt when the other two are off, and background work is still stopped by the wall-clock cap.
- `test_watchdog_treo.py` locks the behavior of `tran_watchdog` (0/negative/junk/positive) and also locks that the cap is fixed together with its reason in both engines.

## [0.25.5] - 2026-08-07
The repo owner sent a screenshot of a Telegram group: a specialist bot was talking like a person, then in the middle *"⏳ Still processing the previous message. Send /stop to stop then ask again."* appeared in front of the whole group. A sentence like that instantly admits it is a machine, and also teaches strangers an admin command. The request: *"I do not want Jarvis 007's status parts exposed like that, I want them hidden so it feels like a real person talking, not a bot."* Root cause: specialist bots and the owner's Jarvis 007 bot share the `TelegramBot` class, and that class speaks status outward as if talking to a machine operator.
### Fixed

Four leaks were plugged: the "🤔 Jarvis 007 is processing..." message with its "⏳ ⚙ Calling tool..." updates, the sentence "Processing the previous message, send /stop", the line "⚠ Error: ExceptionClassName: ..." when a turn breaks, and the text "(no content)" when a turn returns empty. The OWNER's Jarvis 007 bot keeps all of them: a machine operator needs to see how far Jarvis 007 has run.
- **Status messages are replaced by Telegram's own "typing..." dot**, kept lit steadily through the answer. This is exactly what a real person leaves behind while typing, and it is not a message so it does not stay in the group history.

### Improved
- **Extra messages sent while the bot is answering are no longer blocked, they are queued.** Hiding the busy notice while still dropping the message is worse than exposing it: the customer asks and nobody answers. Now the bot gathers the messages arriving while busy and, once the previous one is answered, answers them all in one go, like a person finishing reading before replying. The cap is 5 messages or 4000 characters per conversation so strangers spamming cannot bloat memory; typing `/stop` also drops what is waiting.
### Tests
- Added `tests/python/test_bot_noi_nhu_nguoi.py`: builds a simulated Telegram and inspects exactly what the bot INTENDS to send. 24 checks cover all four leaks, the queue rule and its cap, the `/stop` interrupt case, and a control showing the owner's bot keeps its old behavior case by case.

### Fixed

With nothing to show the strip hides completely. Work assigned from this very conversation gets its own outline and its own count, because "the machine is busy" and "MY work is running" are two different things.

- **One failed getMe makes the bot DEAF in every group, permanently, without a trace.** If the bot does not know its own `@username`, `_co_nhac_ten` returns False for EVERY message - private messages still work perfectly (no need to recognize the name), while in groups it is absolutely silent. One network drop at the exact second of startup is enough.

This reason is kept apart from `last_error` because the loop clears `last_error` after every successful poll, and every poll succeeds.

But it does not count as a bot call: counting them together would make the number "someone called the bot N times" lose all meaning.
### Improved
- **`/id` is now a diagnostic, no longer a bare number.** It is the ONLY place that can reliably speak up when the bot is silent in a group. Now it answers: the group id, whether this group is enabled, whether privacy mode is on or off, whether the bot knows its own identity, and what to do next. In private messages it is still just one id line as before, with no extra lecture.
- **The privacy mode warning shows for EVERY bot that uses groups**, not only bots set to "answer every message" as in 0.25.0. It is the number one cause of "private works, in the group tagging the name gets dead silence", and users have no way to guess because every sign on the page is green.
- **It states BOTH ways to fix it**, not just one: `@BotFather` → `/setprivacy` → **Disable**, **or** make the bot a group **admin** (an admin receives every message, independent of privacy mode). The second can be done right in the group, with no need to go find BotFather.
### Tests
- getMe canary: there must be a retry, the reason must be kept, and that reason must be SEPARATE from `last_error` - the test guards the exact line `self.last_error = ""` in the loop so a later version does not merge them back.
- `/id` in a not-enabled group / an enabled group / a private message: three paths give three different sentences, and the group is read from the STORE not from the snapshot taken when the command was built (clicking Allow takes effect from the very next message, no need to toggle the bot).
- Any message from a group puts the group in the queue but does NOT inflate the call counter.
### Docs
- `docs/25-chatbot.md`: Step 4 switched to using `/id` instead of calling the bot's name, with the reason; added a whole section **Telegram privacy mode** listing exactly what reaches the bot and what does not, along with all three causes of the "private works, group dead silent" symptom.

## [0.25.0] - 2026-08-06
The repo owner sent two screenshots. Screenshot one: a Telegram group, the bot had just answered `/id`, then three messages calling it by name - `@ten_bot em hỗ trợ được gì bọn anh nhé?`, `@ten_bot ALo`, `chốt mịa rồi ném vào nhóm nhỏ méo phản hồi`. No message from the bot after that. Screenshot two: the bot card on the dashboard still said **Starting** while that very bot had just answered in the group.

Three things, and all three are **silent failures**, not broken features.
### Fixed
- **Drop the bot into a group, call its name, nothing happens.** The fence is right: the bot does not take work in a group the owner has not declared. But the WAY OF REFUSING is completely wrong - total silence, no log, no line on the Chatbot page. "Correct behavior" and "bot broken" look identical, and the user can only conclude the second.

  Now refusing is still refusing, but it **speaks**: the bot answers one sentence so the caller knows what to do, and that group **shows up on the bot card** with an **Allow this group** button. One click replaces the old seven-step path (type /id, copy the id, open the dashboard, click Edit, scroll to the bottom of the form, paste, Save) where missing a single step lands you back at the same silence.
- **The "Allowed groups" box existed only in the Edit form, not in the Create form.** That meant the most natural path - create the bot and drop it straight into a group - guaranteed every user's first attempt met a silent bot. Now it can be declared right at creation, and the "in a group, when does the bot speak" selector also reaches the UI (before, it existed only in the store, with no way to change it).
- **When a regular group is upgraded to a supergroup Telegram changes the id** (adds the `-100` prefix), without telling anyone. The id the owner declared yesterday instantly points at a group that no longer exists, and the bot goes silent in the very group it answered yesterday. Now the two id forms match, and Jarvis 007 listens for the upgrade message to update the list by itself.
- **Calling the bot's name when Telegram attaches no `entities` turned the "was called" flag off.** `entities` is something Telegram adds, not a guarantee. Added a raw string comparison branch as a safety net.
- **The bot card stood still at "Starting".** Clicking Enable makes the server return `starting` - the poller has just been created, not yet shaken hands with Telegram - then a few seconds later it becomes `polling`. But the page only reloaded when the user clicked something, so the card stayed at "Starting" until the user left the page and came back, while the bot had been really answering for ages. Now the page refreshes itself every 5 seconds; that beat is also the ONLY thing that can detect a bot that has just died.
- **The Full access level icon drew an empty box.** `shield-alert` is not in the vendored icon set. The icon test did not catch it because it only looks for names written directly in the call, while here it was a ternary expression.
### Improved
- **The permission level shows on the card at ALL THREE levels, including Read only.** The previous version left the label blank for the default level, reasoning "the default needs no label".
