But a blank box reads as two opposite things: is the bot read-only, or does this page not tell? Grey for Read only, yellow for Can write, red for Full access.
- **The card says clearly when the bot speaks in groups** ("3 groups, when called by name") rather than only counting groups.
- **A warning when the configuration asks for something Telegram does not allow.** Setting the bot to "answer every message in the group" while Telegram's privacy mode is still on makes Telegram block from its side, Jarvis 007 never sees those messages, and every sign on the page stays green. Now `getMe` reads `can_read_all_group_messages` and the card says plainly to go to @BotFather and type `/setprivacy` → Disable.
### Security
- **Deliberate silence is now REAL silence.** Before this release, when the bot refused a message in a stranger's group it still went the whole way: sent a "🤔 processing..." message, deleted it, then sent **"(no content)"** in the outsiders' faces. The new gate sits at the channel layer, running BEFORE spending an engine turn and even before the status message. An answer that is empty because the engine broke still shows up as before - those two must not be mixed up.
- `/...` commands deliberately do NOT go through the gate: `/id` is the official way to get a group id, and blocking it leaves the owner no way to declare a group for the bot.
- The fence "the bot does not take work in a stranger's group" is **not loosened**. The queue of groups awaiting approval lives in RAM, has a cap of 20 groups per bot, and the notice in the group speaks only once per group.
### Tests
- `test_chatbot_store.py` adds two items: the reason for silence must be distinguishable (group not enabled ≠ nobody called the name - two things fixed in completely different ways), and a canary for regular group ↔ supergroup ids, with a reverse item so normalization does not wrongly swallow a different group with a matching tail.
- A new canary at the channel layer: the gate must stand before the status message, commands are not blocked, and deliberate silence must be distinguishable from an empty answer.
- `test_trang_chatbot.js` reverses one old item ("read-only level gets NO label") with the reason for the change written in place, and adds an item guarding that the auto-refresh beat must stop when leaving the page.
### Docs
- `docs/25-chatbot.md` rewrote Step 4 along the new path (drop into group → call the name → click allow), added the Telegram privacy mode section, and two frequently asked questions in the repo owner's exact words.

## [0.24.7] - 2026-08-06
The repo owner settled four things at once: *"move the saver button over to Usage, make the new version's default super saver, and remove the numbers that mean nothing to the end user. The saver menu is not needed any more either."*
### Behavior changes
- **This version's default is Super saver**, replacing Off. It applies to long-installed machines too, not only fresh installs - the `_ap_muc_mac_dinh` mechanism built since 0.16.0 is now actually used for the first time.

  Why the change: before, the default was Off and almost nobody turned it on themselves, meaning **most people were paying for the most expensive mode without knowing**. Measured on a sample brain: Off is about 8,900 fixed tokens per turn, Super saver about 460.

  This is a safe default, not a gamble: every path in this level is fail-closed, so when a condition is missing that turn falls back to Full mode instead of answering wrongly. And anyone who **has ever picked a level themselves** is not touched, including someone who deliberately picked Off.
- **The Saver page is merged into the Usage page, and the "Saver" entry disappears from the sidebar.** The three level buttons sit at the TOP of the Usage page, above even the period filter.

  "How much do I spend" and "how do I spend less" are the same question. With two pages, users read the whole bill and never see the switch.
- **Removed from the screen are all the machine operator's numbers**: the canary table measured in ten-thousandths, the umbrella off/observe/shadow/canary/on switch, the quota declaration box, the 60-second token window, the self-learning quota, the registry tool count, the guess accuracy, the "Recent turns" table with task_id and execution_path, the tables counting failure reasons.

  Kept is exactly what an end user can decide: the level name, what percent it saves, how many tokens remain per turn, the "does not apply to the brain in use" mark, and the **measured over the last 24 hours** block.
### Added
- **`GET /runtime/muc`** - a compact endpoint returning exactly the four things the page needs. The Usage page calls it after every level change so it must be cheap; `/runtime/diagnostics` remains intact for anyone inspecting the machine, with every field just removed from the UI.
- Clicking the mode line under each answer, or the "Saver" line in the Usage panel, both go straight to the Usage page. The old page id `runtime` has a redirect table so old bookmarks do not land on a blank screen.
### Fixed
- **The mode name translation table is now just ONE copy** (in the chat box). Before there were two hand-copied versions of the same set of names, and two hand copies are two places to drift apart - when they drift the user cannot connect the line under an answer with the place to adjust the level. The remaining copy was extended with names for the `bot` path.
### Tests
- Three fixtures that hard-pinned "a clean slate is all zeros" were corrected (`test_muc_mac_dinh`, `test_settings_merge`, `test_runtime_preset`): a clean slate is no longer all zeros since the factory level is a real level. This is exactly the trap that bit `test_cauhinh_cu_khong_ket` in 0.24.3, so this time the reason is written straight into the test.
- The invariant "numbers must reach human eyes" changes SCOPE rather than being dropped: it now inspects the four fields of `/runtime/muc` on the Usage page, and separately guards that the diagnostics data path remains for operators.
### Docs
- `docs/23-muc-dung-token.md` adds sections **Token saver mode** and **Why the default is Super saver**; `docs/10` and `docs/17` point to the new place.

## [0.24.6] - 2026-08-06
The repo owner sent a screenshot of a specialist bot on duty: someone messaged in, the bot answered *"Em đang gặp trục trặc kỹ thuật, anh chị nhắn lại giúp em sau ít phút ạ"* ("I am having a technical problem, please message me again in a few minutes"), and the person on duty was woken with the reason `⚠ Anthropic 429: {"type":"rate_limit_error"}`.

429 is a **temporary** error. The right move is to wait a beat and ask again.
### Fixed
- **Seven of eight brains gave up at the very first failure.** `engine.py` has long had the full toolkit for retrying - `_RETRY_STATUS`, `_is_transient_body`, `_parse_retry_after`, `_jittered_backoff` - but **only `openrouter_stream` used them**. The other seven model-calling paths and all four tool loops died the moment the provider sneezed.

  Nobody saw it because on a clean machine the provider never returns 429. It only showed when a bot was really on duty, for real people: a 429 lasting under a second was enough for the person asking to get a technical apology and the person on duty to be called awake mid-shift.
- **Temporary errors are now marked AT THE SOURCE** (`engine.ev_loi_http` / `ev_loi_exc`), because only the HTTP call site still has the real status, real body and the `Retry-After` header. By the upper layers everything has been squashed into one text string, and guessing again by probing text in that string breaks the first time someone edits a label.
- **The retry lives in `_api_stream`**, the ONLY place every non-tool chat path passes through: dashboard, Telegram, specialist bots, background work, the shortcut path. At most three turns, obeying `Retry-After` if the provider sent one. The tool loop is wrapped too.
### Security
- **Two conditions to retry, missing either means stop.** Once text has been released outward, stop (people would read the answer twice), and **once a tool has run, definitely stop** - that turn may have already sent a message, written a file, booked a schedule, and rerunning the whole round does those things a second time. This is the heaviest canary item in the test file.
- **Errors that are NOT temporary are reported immediately on the first try**: wrong key, wrong model name, exceeding the context size, and every error that has read out a real quota. Retrying unchanged only costs one more paid model call to get the exact same error back.
- **The last attempt strips the `tam_thoi` mark.** That mark is an invitation to rerun, and the attempts are used up. Thanks to this, wrapping two layers does not blow up into nine calls, and `openrouter_stream` (which retries on its own inside) does not get retried one more level.
### Improved
- The final error sentence now carries *(retried 3 times)* - so the owner can tell a flash glitch apart from a really exhausted quota, two things fixed in completely different ways.
### Tests
- New `test_thu_lai_tam_thoi.py`, guarding all three layers, and the last item rebuilds EXACTLY the owner's screenshot: the bot hits 429 for one beat and still answers the person asking and does **not** wake the person on duty; with 429 forever it still has to report the failure rather than swallow the error.
- Canary "all eight brains": fixing Anthropic and leaving the other seven is exactly the kind of fault just fixed, so the test runs straight through every provider in `PROVIDER_DEFS`.
### Docs
- `docs/17-khac-phuc-su-co.md` adds a section **When a provider fails for one beat, Jarvis 007 asks again by itself**; `docs/25-chatbot.md` states the third case that calls the person on duty (bot broken) and the retry done before it.

## [0.24.5] - 2026-08-06
Two snags when Jarvis 007 brings an HTML file into chat: clicking the link drops the file onto your machine, and opening it to edit shows code in one grey color that tires the eyes.
### Improved
- **Clicking an `.html` link in chat now opens the editor directly, no more download.** That is the SOURCE file, and forcing one click to drop a file onto the machine is the longest detour: to view it you must open it in another app, to fix one word you must edit outside and upload again. The editor already has both an **Open in new tab** button and a **Download** button, so opening the editor is the shorter path for BOTH intents. Images, video, pdf, docx, zip still download as before.
- **The editor pane expanded to mid-screen gains an "Open in new tab" button** (↗), before it only had a download button. The docked editor already had this pair of buttons, now the two places match.
- **Syntax coloring when editing code**, for both the docked editor and the mid-screen expanded pane: `.html`, `.css`, `.js`, `.json`, `.py`, `.yaml`, `.sh` and other common extensions. Tag names, attribute names, strings, numbers, comments and keywords each get a color, with separate palettes for light and dark themes.

  HTML has its own reader rather than sharing the chat code-block colorer: that one treats everything as a C-style language so it reads HTML very wrongly, coloring `class` as a keyword while tag names and attribute names get no color. The insides of `<style>` and `<script>` are read in their own language. CSS and JSON also have their own; the remaining languages are still handed to the shared one, without copying the logic.
### Notes
- The edit box is still a real `<textarea>`, with the color layer sitting EXACTLY UNDERNEATH. It deliberately does not switch to `contenteditable`: switching loses the browser's undo, loses external Vietnamese input methods, loses every familiar shortcut.
- `.md` gets no coloring: it opens in a WYSIWYG editor whose toolbar inserts text into the edit box without firing the `input` event, so the color layer would drift from the real content.
- Two geometry traps are already plugged, both of the kind that only show when the file is long: the two layers must reserve **the same room for the scrollbar** (`scrollbar-gutter`), otherwise from the moment a vertical scrollbar appears the text width in the edit box shrinks by about 15px while the color layer does not, and the colored text drifts clear off the real text; and the test guards the constraint that **stripping all tags must give back exactly the original string**, because if the colorer swallows or adds a single character, from there on every line is off with no error thrown.
- Files over 300 thousand characters skip coloring (every keystroke rebuilds the whole HTML tree). Editing works as normal, the text is just one color.

## [0.24.4] - 2026-08-06
The repo owner reported: *"when I ask Jarvis 007 to add some mcp, it does not show up in the connections section"*. Right, and the reason is not that the UI forgot to draw it - **Jarvis 007 never had any path to write into its own connections store.**
### Added
- **Bundled plugin `javis-connect`, tool `javis_add_mcp`.** Ask Jarvis 007 to connect an MCP right in chat, and it shows up in the **"Connected"** area of the Connections page like an account you added by hand, shared by every brain through the hub.

  Until now the connections store could only be written through `/connect/add`, and that endpoint sits behind the login layer so only the web page could call it. Jarvis 007 had exactly two ways left, both broken: run `claude mcp add` through Bash - the server falls into Claude Code's own config, the other six brains do not see it, and on the Connections page it does not sit in the "Connected" area but drops into the collapsed area *"Claude Code and Codex built-in connections"* (CLOSED by default, loaded only when opened); or say vaguely "please go to the Connections page and add it yourself". The user looks at the Connections page, sees it unchanged, and concludes Jarvis 007 lied - a fair conclusion.

  `op=find` looks up the Connections store first, `op=add` connects a new source. The tool goes straight into `mcp_store`, the same store that `/connect/catalog` reads.
### Security
- **Three hard fences, no parameter can open them.** The default permission level is **read only** (rule in `CLAUDE.md`: Jarvis 007 does not raise permission itself, the user raises it on the Connections page). A source that runs as a **command on the machine** (stdio) is added in the **off** state and is not trial-dialed, because the trial connection alone is already running that command - letting API engines spawn a self-running stdio would open exactly the Bash back door they do not have. A service already in the Connections store (Gmail, Calendar, POS...) makes the tool point to the right card rather than spawn a parallel self-declared copy, because an empty-token connection left on the Connections page looks exactly like a real account but cannot run.
### Fixed
- **If the trial connection fails the entry still stays on the Connections page** with the verbatim reason, in the off state. Different from `/connect/add` (wipes everything when validation fails) - reasonable for a form because the user is looking right at it, but completely wrong for chat: what they need is to SEE it sitting there and know why it does not run yet.
- **`server/chatbots.json` and `server/chatbot-logs/` go into `.gitignore`.** Two runtime artifacts of the Chatbot page (0.19.0) were neither tracked nor ignored from then until now, so one `git add -A` would commit the **bot token** straight into the repo. `test_ignore_files.py` caught it.
### Notes
- The system prompt (`channel_context`) now says directly: to add an MCP use `javis_add_mcp`, never `claude mcp add` / `codex mcp add`, and after adding it must say clearly that it sits on the Connections page, whether it is on or off, and at which permission level.

## [0.24.3] - 2026-08-06
The repo owner read the source directly and pointed out: **the whole Saver system is only wired into the dashboard's WebSocket handler.** Right, and this is a real architectural hole.
### Fixed
- **The Optimized and Super saver levels had no effect on Telegram.** Three things matched exactly: every `prepare()` call in `websocket_endpoint` hard-passes the string `"dashboard"`, `_tg_answer_engine` has not a single line touching them, and `channels` in the config also only declares `["dashboard"]`.

  Consequence: the user clicks a saver level, the Settings page shows a green "enabled, in effect immediately", then every Telegram turn still sends the whole `CLAUDE.md` + `MEMORY.md`. **No error, no warning - just a token bill that does not drop** on exactly the channel with the most users. Same family as the `provider_kinds` disease in 0.12.4, this time falling on the CHANNEL instead of the brain type.

  Now `_tg_answer_engine` wires in both layers, in order of increasing cost: the shortcut path (Phase 5) then the selective source (Phase 8). Both take `channel` as a **variable**, not a string constant.
- **The shortcut path core is split from WebSocket.** `_execute_fast_path` was tightly bound to `ws.send_text` so other channels could not reuse it. Now the core lives in `_fast_path_core` with two per-channel message-sending hooks; the WebSocket version is just a thin shell wrapping it.
- **`channels` opens up `telegram` and `cli`** for the shortcut path, selective memory and load-on-demand skills. Installed machines are widened too, thanks to `_no_rong_pham_vi_bo_nao` (an old settings.json hard-pins `["dashboard"]`, and fixing only the default would reach only fresh installs).

  `conversation_state_canary` is **deliberately not opened**: a Telegram session already keeps its own conversation thread, and adding a transcript into the system prompt would send the history twice.
### Notes
- The three tool execution paths (`readonly`, `orchestrator`, `write`) still only run on the dashboard. They are already fail-closed (`capability_profiles` empty) so today they affect no one, and each path needs its own message-sending adapter - that work is split from this release.
- **Specialist bots do NOT go through those two layers**, and not by omission: the bot's prompt (~20 tokens) is already more than twenty times smaller than the Super saver capsule (~460 tokens). The test guards exactly that.
- Schedule control commands are still handled by the schedule gateway; the shortcut path is asked AFTER the schedule command has been resolved, so it does not steal the turn.

## [0.24.2] - 2026-08-05
The repo owner turned on the **Can write** level for a bot running on a ChatGPT plan, and the bot died: every message sent in got *"⚠ ChatGPT returned empty (the Codex backend may not support tools yet)"*.

A bug of version 0.24.0, and worth recording because it is a named kind of carelessness: **wiring a real path into a function nobody ever called.**
### Fixed
- **Raising the permission level BROKE a bot that was running fine.** `engine.responses_with_mcp` up to 0.24.0 **had never been called from anywhere** - `git log -S` gives exactly one result, the 0.24.0 commit itself - and its docstring itself says EXPERIMENTAL. Version 0.24.0 wired the ChatGPT plan's Can write/Full access levels into it and shipped with no fallback.

  The consequence was not just "the new feature does not work yet": a bot answering fine at Read only level, the owner raises the level, and it **stops answering completely**.

  Now there is a fallback: when the tool loop returns empty, that turn is rerun **without tools**. The rule drawn out and written as a test - *raising the permission level must not TAKE AWAY an ability that already exists*.
- **But NOT silently lowering the level.** The owner sets Can write while the bot quietly runs as Read only is a worse kind of failure than breaking outright. A turn run with missing permission carries a **warning** up to the bot card (a yellow strip, different from the red strip of a broken turn), saying clearly what level it is running at compared with the level set and what to do: change the engine on the Models page, or lower the level to Read only.

  The warning goes on its OWN path rather than borrowing the `loi` field: `loi` drags in the stuck counter, drags in calling the person on duty, and dirties the "Stuck bots" tab - while this is a normal answered turn.
- **`responses_with_mcp` now matches the non-tool path that really runs.** It was missing exactly the line `openai_responses_stream` has: with no `account_id` it DROPS the `chatgpt-account-id` header entirely instead of sending an empty string. Also added `[DONE]` handling and stripping of internal citation marks.
- **When both paths fail, report the error of the NO-TOOL path, not the error of the tool loop.** The no-tool path is the simplest call left so it names the real disease better (quota out, wrong token, network dead). Reporting the tool loop error first sends the owner looking for whether the engine supports tools, while what broke is something else entirely.
- **Setting an elevated level with no source connected** also gives a similar warning, instead of only writing a stderr line nobody reads.
### Docs
- `docs/25-chatbot.md` adds a section **Which engines can run the elevated levels**: Read only level runs on all eight brains with no exceptions; for the two elevated levels, the ChatGPT plan goes through the not-yet-stable Codex backend path, and in that case the bot still answers and the card shows a yellow strip.

## [0.24.1] - 2026-08-05
The repo owner reread the wording of 0.24.0: *"edit the texts so they do not use money, orders, posting. It is too personalized to me. The guidance should be at the most general level for many cases."*

Right. Jarvis 007 is not tied to any industry, but the text on screen was.
### Changed
- **The permission level warning describes the KIND OF OPERATION, not the named work of one industry.** "create orders, spend ad money, post" became "send out, pay, book/cancel, delete, publish outward" - exactly how `mcp_catalog` classifies, and right for every connected data source.

  Not an aesthetic matter: users who use Jarvis 007 to manage projects, look after health or teach read the old version and **thought the warning did not apply to them**, then turned on Full access thinking they had nothing to lose. A warning that misses its target is worse than no warning.
- **"khách / khách hàng" (customer) became "người nhắn cho bot" (people who message the bot)** in all on-screen text. A specialist bot can be on duty for a class, a community, an internal team; customer care is only ONE use case.
- **"nhân viên" (staff) became "người trực" (person on duty)** in field labels, bot cards, logs and the bot's Telegram command menu (`/nhanvien` keeps its command name - renaming a command breaks the habits of people already using it).
- **`docs/25-chatbot.md` drops the shop framing**: the examples "price list, return policy, product descriptions" are replaced by one principle usable for any work - *if a sentence from this file leaked out and you would be bothered, that file does not belong in the bot's brain*. A line at the top lists different use cases.
- **The sample `description` of a skill is no longer a specific product.** "Convert HTML to a Webcake .pke file." became "Summarize meeting minutes into a to-do list." - changed in all three places teaching this rule (`skill_router`, `learn`, the `javis-builder` skill) and in `docs/06-skills.md`.
### Fixed
- **The "stuck bot" detector missed handoff sentences after the wording change.** `_DAU_BI` matches by string on the very sentence the bot just said, so changing "chuyển cho nhân viên" (hand over to staff) and forgetting to add the new phrasing makes those turns quietly stop counting as stuck, and the "Stuck bots" tab empties out with nobody understanding why. Now it keeps BOTH the old phrasing (Agents users wrote earlier still use that word) and the neutral phrasing.
### Tests
- Canaries in both `test_chatbot_muc_quyen.py` and `test_trang_chatbot.js`: warning text and Chatbot page text **must not contain** "đơn hàng", "tạo đơn", "tiêu tiền", "quảng cáo", "đăng bài", "cửa hàng", "bán hàng", "bảng giá", "POS". The rule is written as a test because this is the kind of text that gets rewritten to fit the use case in front of you.

## [0.24.0] - 2026-08-05
The repo owner opened up the scope of Specialist bots: *"the bot creation feature is read-only now, I want to add write and full access. Because basically I still want to be able to do many tasks, but add a notice for me to understand the risks of using it."*

This release lets the bot **do real work**, and does it under exactly the owner's condition: say clearly what can be lost, before the owner clicks.
### Added
- **Three permission levels for bots** (`muc_quyen`), chosen in the **What the bot can do** field when creating or editing:
  - **Read only** (`suggest`, DEFAULT) - old behavior exactly: no tools, only reads documents then answers.
  - **Can write** (`auto`) - write files inside the bot's own brain + call connected data sources at read/write level. The hub still **hard-blocks** the outward operation group: send, pay, book/cancel, delete, publish.
  - **Full access** (`full`) - can do everything the connected sources allow, including the outward group.

  These three words are EXACTLY the name set of loops and the hub, deliberately: the word chosen in the UI goes straight into `discover_all` and becomes the `X-Javis-Mode` header, through no translation table. A translation table is where mistakes come easiest, and a mistake here means granting the wrong permission to a bot talking to strangers.
- **The risk warning shows right at the place of choice**, and is supplied by the SERVER (`GET /chatbots` returns the label + risk list for each level). The UI keeps no copy of its own: once copied, one day the server tightens another fence while the warning box still promises the old way, and the owner clicks agree based on a sentence that has become wrong.
- **The bot card is labeled with the permission level** - yellow for Can write, red for Full access, nothing for Read only. A Full access bot mixed in among several read-only ones, all looking identical, is exactly the silent kind of failure: the owner mixes up which is which and drops the wrong one into a place anyone can message.
- **The log records the permission level of EACH TURN**, not the level set at the time of rereading. Those two diverge as soon as the owner lowers the level after an incident, and when reviewing "what did the bot do that day" what you need is the level at THAT time.
- **The Claude Code plan can call tools** (`engine.anthropic_chat_with_mcp` takes `oauth_token`). Before, the subscription plan could only chat plainly because this function only accepted `x-api-key`.
### Security
- **Two fences do NOT change with the level**, and both are consequences of the bot never touching the engine's NATIVE tools:
  - **Brain isolation.** File tools go through the hub so they are clamped by `_safe_path(vault_root)` with `vault_root` being the BOT'S brain - even at Full access. Opening the CLI to the bot loses this fence immediately: Claude Code's `Read` accepts absolute paths, exactly the hole 0.21.0 had to patch.
  - **No machine commands.** No Bash, no WebFetch/WebSearch, no Task - they were never in the hub.
- **Raising the level needs conscious confirmation.** The fence is placed in the STORE (`chatbot_store.can_xac_nhan`) and not only in the route, because the route is just one of many ways in. The route returns `can_force` with the exact reason, in the same mold as `POST /reminders` when no reporting channel is connected. **LOWERING** the level demands nothing: lowering permission is always safe, and when the owner is putting out an incident do not make them click more.
- **Fail-closed at the fork.** Only exactly the two declared words open tools; an old record missing the key, a hand-edited file with a typo, `None` - all fall to the no-tool path. Written the other way ("different from `suggest` opens tools") a single typo in an old `chatbots.json` would be enough to grant tools to a bot chatting with strangers.
- **An odd value in a patch KEEPS the old level**, does not fall to the default: a bot at Full access that a mistyped patch quietly lowers would make the owner think the bot is still working while it refuses every tool.
- The UI asks once more for the Full access level, and asks again when **turning on** a bot that has operation rights - the time of creation may have been several days ago.
### Tests
- New `test_chatbot_muc_quyen.py`: runs a REAL bot turn through all eight providers at Full access then checks whether each one called the tool loop. Granting tools to six API engines and leaving the two subscription plans behind is the worst kind of silent failure - the owner sets Full access, the bot still politely answers, and does nothing.
- The same file guards fail-closed with eight odd values (including `1`, `True`, `"readonly"`, and two strings with extra spaces so anyone who removes `strip()` goes red immediately), the hub returning empty, and the hub blowing up midway.
- `test_chatbot_cach_ly.py` adds a canary for the path WITH tools: no `claude_engine`, no `CodexCLI`, no `allowed_tools`, no native tool name. Tool names are inspected in quoted form - inspecting the bare form would make the very comment explaining why there is no Bash turn the test red.

## [0.23.1] - 2026-08-05
The repo owner asked: *"I see the bot has not gone through the saver and super saver features. Can you check for me whether that is so?"* It is true it has not, but the error is not there.
### Fixed
- **The Token saver page put bot turns under "Full" - exactly the OPPOSITE of the truth.** `pin_execution_path` only accepts a fixed list of names, and odd names all fall to `legacy`. Bot turns pin nothing so they were merged into the **most expensive** column, while measurement shows it is the **cheapest** path in the system.

  Now there is a `bot` path, shown in the UI as **"Specialist bot"**.
### Noted (not a bug)
- **The bot does not go through Phase 5 (shortcut path) and Phase 8 (selective memory), and does not need to.** Those two layers live in `websocket_endpoint`, meaning they only run for dashboard chat - the owner's own Telegram path never went through them either.

  More important: they exist to trim CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md and the tool spec table - three things the bot never had. Measured fixed part per turn on a sample brain: **~8,900 tokens** (dashboard at Full level), **~460** (Super saver level), **~20** (bot). Pushing the bot through the other two layers would only make it heavier, since the Super saver capsule alone is five times bigger than the entire bot prompt.

  The test now measures those two numbers directly and requires the bot prompt to be smaller than the capsule - so next time someone "optimizes" the bot by wiring it into Phase 8 there is a place to go red.

## [0.23.0] - 2026-08-05
The concept of a **"bot's own brain"** is removed entirely. The repo owner decided: *"whichever brain is picked, show only that brain's agents and chatbots. There is no need for creating a brain for a bot. That will be easier to manage."*
### Behavior changes
- **The Chatbot page belongs to the open brain**, just like the Agents and Skills pages. Change brain at the top of the page and you see that brain's bots. `GET /chatbots?brain=` filters by brain; left empty it still returns everything because the watcher does not stand in any brain.
- **The bot creation form no longer has a brain picker and the "Create new brain" button.** The bot belongs to the open brain, and Agents come from that same brain.

  Version 0.22.3 required choosing a brain in the form and then remembering which brain the Agent lived in - two layers that must match while **nothing forces them to match**. With that box removed, the page's scope is the answer, and nothing is left to drift. The server also keeps `brain` and `agent_brain` equal at both create and edit time.
- **The bot card drops the brain line**, replaced by one line at the top of the page saying which brain's bots you are viewing. Every bot on the page is in the same brain so repeating it on each card is just noise.

Brain isolation is **unchanged**: the bot can still only read its own brain, locked by source code. Only the way of CHOOSING that brain changed - before, a box in the form, now the brain you are standing in.

Also: the docs change the preparation step to "stand in the right brain first", and say plainly the most worth considering point - a bot that answers strangers should not be created inside your main brain.
## [0.22.3] - 2026-08-05
Cleaned up the bot creation form based on real-world feedback, and fixed a help line that described the wrong behavior.
### Fixed
- **The Agent list came from the brain open on the dashboard, not from the bot's brain.** You picked the brain "My Bullet Journal" for the bot, yet the Agent field still listed Agents from another brain. After saving, the bot pointed to an Agent that is NOT in the brain it reads, and nothing told you.

  Now **the brain is asked first, then the Agent**, and changing the brain reloads the Agent list of that exact brain. `agent_brain` also always equals the bot's brain - Agent and documents live in the same place.
- **The Agent picker overflowed the form sideways** when an Agent name plus its role was too long. Browsers do not allow styling `<option>` tags, so the string is cut in JS (role at most 34 characters, the Agent name is always kept in full) and `min-width:0` + `text-overflow` were added to the `<select>` itself.
- **The help line under the "Staff chat ID" field described behavior that no longer holds**: it said "leave it empty and the bot only says it has no information, then stops". Since 0.21.0 Jarvis 007 no longer injects any rule into the prompt, so with it empty the bot **still answers normally** per its Agent, there is just nobody to hand over to. The old line taught users to fear behavior that does not exist.
- **`/nhanvien` with no recipient set gave the wrong reply.** The old line ("I have no information on that, please wait for a reply") was off-topic - the customer asked for a person, not for information - and it also closed the conversation. Now it says honestly that it cannot connect to a person on duty yet, and invites a follow-up question.
### Added
- **A "New Agent" button** right next to the Agent picker, which jumps straight to the Agents page. Before, the form only said "create it on the Agents page" in words and users had to go find it themselves.
- `console.js` exposes `window.JavisNav.go(id)` so other page modules can switch pages. It exposes `navigateTo` rather than letting modules set `store.active` themselves: `navigateTo` also cleans up the old page, stows `#quickSet` and redraws the graph.

## [0.22.2] - 2026-08-05
The bot still said "can't answer yet" after updating. Three separate bugs stacked on top of each other, and all three left the owner staring at the screen with no idea what was happening.
### Fixed
- **A subscription plan calling the API directly could return 401 on EVERY turn.** 0.22.0 sent the bot through `_api_stream` for all eight brains - the right direction, but for the Claude Code plan that path needs the OAuth token the CLI has saved. If it cannot be read (or Anthropic does not accept it), every turn breaks, and the user only sees one apology repeated over and over.

  Now there is a fallback: if the direct call fails, it falls back to that plan's own CLI, with `allowed_tools` set to a string that **matches no tool** - the `can_use_tool` gate switches on and every tool is denied on each call. The bot's contract still holds: same prompt, same documents, same history, no tools. Only the transport differs.

  (An empty list cannot be used as the allowlist: the engine checks `if self.allowed_tools:`, so `[]` is falsy and it reads that as "no allowlist" and runs `bypassPermissions` - opening full access exactly when we meant to lock it down hardest.)

  Codex has no fallback because it has no per-call approval gate. In return, when ChatGPT is not signed in, the bot says plainly what to do instead of returning an HTTP error code.
- **The `/start` greeting still attached "of the store" to the bot's name.** A bot named "Coach kỷ luật" became "Coach kỷ luật of the store" - the same sales-trade framing rejected in 0.20.1, left over here because the command does not go through the prompt.
- **The message for a BROKEN turn was identical to the one for MISSING DOCUMENTS.** Both were "I can't answer that yet..." so from outside you could not tell whether the bot was broken or just lacked documents - two completely different fixes. Now a broken turn says "I'm having a technical problem", clearly separate.
### Improved
- **The latest turn error now shows right on the bot CARD**, no need to open the Log to see it. Poller status says nothing about this: the poller stays "running" with a green dot while every reply breaks. The owner only opens the Log once they already SUSPECT something, so the warning has to hit the eye first.
- **A broken turn counts as stumped** (the bot truly could not answer, so the counter that calls a person sees it) **but is excluded from the "Bot stumped" tab** - that tab is for missing documents. Mixing them would fill the "write more documents" list with technical error lines and the owner would fix the wrong thing. Broken turns are viewed in the Conversations tab, on their own red line.

## [0.22.1] - 2026-08-05
The bot reported an error and **nobody could read the reason**. The repo owner hit exactly this: asked "hello Coach", the bot answered "I can't answer that yet, please wait for the store to reply." That is the GENERIC apology for a broken turn, not a wrong answer from the bot - but from outside the two look identical.
### Fixed
- **The technical reason for a broken turn was thrown away before reaching anywhere readable.** The core of a turn returns a STRING on error (per convention), and `_make_answer_fn` replaces it with the generic apology so technical errors are not thrown in an outsider's face - but then it **discarded the original**. Result: the customer saw a meaningless line, the owner saw the same line, and nobody knew whether the bot was broken or only missing documents. Those two get fixed completely differently (one means changing the engine, the other means writing more documents), so mixing them sends the owner the wrong way.

  Now the reason is kept in three places: written to the log (field `loi`), printed to stderr, and shown as a red line in the **Recent conversations** tab stating "This turn FAILED, the bot did not answer wrongly" with the original text. The customer still only gets the generic apology.
- **A broken turn now alerts staff IMMEDIATELY from the first time**, without waiting for two stumped questions as before. Stumped means missing documents, broken means the bot cannot run - every minute of silence makes the customer think the store is ignoring them. The alert also says plainly "Bot is BROKEN: ..." instead of "stumped N times in a row".

  But it alerts only **once** until a turn runs successfully: if the engine is broken, every later turn breaks too, and alerting on all of them would turn the staff inbox into an error log.

## [0.22.0] - 2026-08-04
The repo owner rejected the approach in 0.21.0: **"I want the experience of talking to the bot to stay the same whether it is claude or codex or the API. Don't you think about how to swap brains without affecting the quality of the bot's answers?"**

Right, and 0.21.0 broke the core promise of Jarvis 007: swapping the brain does not change capability. Blocking Codex was admitting defeat exactly where defeat is not allowed.

The solution turned out simpler than both earlier patches: **the bot needs no tools at all.**
### Changed
- **A dedicated Bot's turn now goes through ONE single path for all eight brains** (`_bot_tra_loi`), no longer branching into four engine paths. Every engine gets the same system prompt from the Agent, the same pre-retrieved documents, the same conversation history, and none has tools. What remains different is exactly the difference between models, not between pipelines.

  Four paths could never behave the same: Claude Code has Bash, Codex has its own MCP store, API engines are capped at 8 tool-call rounds. Three behaviors for one bot, and the owner swapping models would see the difference right away.
- **Removing tools does NOT make the bot lose the ability to read the brain.** `chatbot_grounding` already looked documents up in Python BEFORE the model ran and put them in the prompt. Removing tools only removes the ability to wander around the brain, not the ability to read it.
- **The bot runs on Codex again**, and on all eight brains. Both subscription plans already have a direct no-tool call path in `_api_stream` (ChatGPT via `openai_responses_stream`, Claude Code via `anthropic_stream` with the OAuth token the CLI itself saved) - the previous version missed this, which is why it had to block.
- **The bot answers faster and cheaper**: no CLI launch, no tool catalog load, no tool-call rounds. The `JAVIS_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` cap no longer applies to the bot either.
- Conversation history with each person is hard-cut at 20 turns instead of compressed. Compression means one more model call, and a bot answering strangers needs to be fast and cheap more than it needs a long memory.
### Security
- **Brain isolation is now a consequence of the architecture, not a fence to guard.** The bot has no tools so there is NO way to touch the disk: no per-call approval gate, no sandbox, no hoping `cwd` holds it in.

  Two patches disappear with it: the `allowed_tools` lock for Claude Code (0.21.0) and the Codex refusal branch (0.21.0). So does the `suggest` permission level for bot turns (0.19.0) - it only filtered hub tools, never touched native tools, so it was never a real fence.
- **A bot turn now leaves `_tg_answer_engine` before even reaching `_schedule_cancel_action`.** Before, a stranger messaging the bot "cancel the schedule" could touch the owner's schedule.
- **The bot's prompt no longer carries the channel block.** That block teaches how to send files over Telegram and states the real folder path of the brain - operating knowledge, not something to hand to a bot talking to strangers.
- The `test_chatbot_cach_ly.py` test now checks with **real behavior**: it runs a bot turn through all eight providers and compares that each payload is identical, instead of just reading the source code.

## [0.21.0] - 2026-08-04
The repo owner settled the scope of the dedicated Bot: **"I already have an Agent and its rules, don't add to its rules yourself. Only do the job of blocking the other brains besides the brain the agent is in."** This version removes every rule Jarvis 007 injected on its own, and re-checks the brain isolation fence - it turned out to really leak.
### Security
- **A bot running on Claude Code had FULL machine access, not just its own brain.** A bot turn built the engine with `cwd=CLAUDE_CWD` (the project root) and no `allowed_tools`, so the engine ran `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"`: NATIVE tools (Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, Write) **do not go through the hub** and are not blocked by `mcp_hub._safe_path`. A stranger messaging the bot could get the contents of every other brain and the server source code.

  The `suggest` permission level set since 0.19.0 did not save it: it filters HUB tools and does not touch the engine's native tools. And `cwd` alone was never a fence - `cat ../other-brain/...` still runs.

  Now a bot turn builds the engine with `cwd` = the bot's brain **and** `allowed_tools = ["mcp__javis"]`. Setting `allowed_tools` is the real blocking layer: it switches on `permission_mode="default"` with the `can_use_tool` gate, so every tool outside the hub is DENIED on each call.
- **The bot is REFUSED to run when the engine is ChatGPT (Codex).** Codex has no per-call allowlist like Claude, and its sandbox blocks WRITES and network but does not confine READS - `cat` into another brain still runs. If it cannot be locked, say so plainly rather than lowering the sandbox and calling it done: a half-working fence is worse than none, because the owner thinks it is protecting them. The bot returns one line stating the reason and the fix (switch the main engine to Claude Code or an API engine).
- **New test `test_chatbot_cach_ly.py` guards exactly this fence**, including the escape routes: `../`, `../../`, absolute paths, and brains sharing a name prefix (`brain-bot` and `brain-bot-khac`) - the case where raw string comparison would let it through.
### Changed
- **Jarvis 007 NO LONGER injects any rule into the bot's prompt.** From 0.19.0 to 0.20.1, the bot prompt always had a block of "mandatory rules, above all other instructions" - telling it how to address people, banning promises, banning role changes, forcing short answers. That block fought the rules the user wrote in the Agent file, and 0.20.1 only made it less tied to the sales trade, without removing it.

  Now the bot's prompt = **exactly the Agent file**, plus pre-retrieved documents given as data, not accompanied by any command. If you want the bot not to talk about prices, not to promise delivery, not to change role when tempted, write it in the Agent - that is where those things belong.
- **"Documents only" mode is the one rule left, and the user must turn it on themselves.** The default mode now adds not a single word when no document is found; the Agent decides.
- The Chatbot page and docs now say what Jarvis 007 really does: it does not write rules for the bot, it locks the brain scope. Promising more than that teaches users to trust a fence that does not exist.

## [0.20.1] - 2026-08-04
The repo owner created the Agent **"Coach kỷ luật"**, asked the bot about discipline, and got back a clueless bot: it introduced itself as a store assistant, quoted an internal Jarvis 007 convention section as its answer, then said "I have no information" for exactly the question within the Agent's expertise. Four bugs stacked, all because the first Chatbot version assumed every bot is a sales bot.
### Fixed
- **The prompt framed EVERY bot as a sales employee, overriding the very Agent the user had just picked.** The old text said outright "assistant answering the store's customers", "do not quote prices outside the price list", "do not promise delivery". Any coach Agent landing there became a sales employee refusing to advise.

  Sales is only ONE use case. The original brief is "each chatbot specializes in 1 field to help answer", and the customer care group is an example, not the definition. Now the frame is neutral: the Agent says who it is, the role instructions are stated as **the most important part**, and the rules keep only three things that do not depend on the trade - do not invent details specific to that place, do not reveal internal systems, do not promise on the owner's behalf.
- **The bot was gagged when the brain had no documents.** Version 0.20.0 forced every bot into answer-only-from-documents mode, so a carefully written coach Agent still answered "I have no information" to a question in its own expertise - that expertise lives in the role instructions, not in any file in the brain.

  Now the bot has **two modes**, chosen on create or edit: *Agent expertise + documents* (default) and *documents only*. The difference lies ONLY in what happens when nothing is found; when something is found, both modes behave identically. Both still REQUIRE documents before talking about prices, policy, stock, schedule, contact. Bots created before this version read as the default mode automatically, no migration needed.
- **The bot quoted Jarvis 007's internal conventions back to customers.** `meta_tools` seeds `CLAUDE.md` + `AGENTS.md` into the ROOT of every brain, and the exclusion list only blocked by folder. Asked "why store discipline", the bot looked up the section "Three disciplines against empty/wrong Wiki" and explained to the customer that this was "the store's internal system operating rules" - both meaningless and a leak of the system's insides, exactly what the prompt rules forbid while the lookup itself handed it over. Now `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `index.md`, `log.md`, `_open-questions.md`, `_session-handoff.md` are all excluded; the user's real Wiki notes still work normally.
- **Calling staff over a casual question.** Version 0.20.0 alerted from the very first stumped turn. Staff woken for a question nobody needs handled will turn notifications off after a few times, and when a real person needs help nobody reads them. Now it calls only when the customer types `/nhanvien`, or the bot is stumped **two turns in a row** with the same person; answering one question resets the count to 0.
### Improved
- **Telling an exact-accent match from a match made by stripping accents.** Stripping accents is a double-edged knife: it lets a customer type "gia si bao nhieu" and still get "giá sỉ" (badly needed), but it also makes words with totally different meanings collide, and Vietnamese collides a lot. A real case: "có bán cà phê không" (do you sell coffee) matched the note "Kỷ luật bản thân" (self discipline) which has the phrase "kể cả khi hết hứng" - "bán" met "bản", "cà" met "cả", two words hit, enough to pass every threshold.

  Now the index keeps both forms. If the asker used accents but the document carries different accents, the weight drops hard (0.3) rather than being excluded, because people do still type accents wrong. If the asker typed without accents they say nothing about accents, no penalty: every form counts as a real match. The reference question set in the test grew to 30, including that accent-trap pair.
- **"Stumped" is measured by what the bot just said**, not by whether documents were found. In Agent-following mode, having no documents is normal and the bot still answers well; counting that as stumped fills the "Bot stumped" list with junk exactly where it must be clean.
- **The bot card shows which mode it is running**, and the mode picker sits right under the brain field in the form with an explanation of when to use which - this is something the user must understand BEFORE pressing create, not something hidden at the bottom.

## [0.20.0] - 2026-08-04
The three remaining phases of the dedicated Bot: **grounded answers**, **really joining groups**, and **stats on the questions the bot could not answer**. Plus a hole from 0.19.0 that had to be patched.
### Fixed
- **The bot stayed SILENT in EVERY group in 0.19.0.** The default rule "only answer when addressed by name" reads two flags `mentioned`/`reply_to_bot`, but `TelegramBot._build_meta` never set them - it only set `chat_type`. So the condition was always false and the bot never opened its mouth in a group. Broken in the worst way: silent, no log, no alert, the owner only saw the bot "as dead".

  Now `_build_meta` reads straight from the message: `entities` of type `mention` (customer types `@bot_name`, the string must be cut by offset/length to compare) and type `text_mention` (customer picks from the member list, no `@` in the text, identity sits in `entity.user.id`), plus `reply_to_message`. `caption_entities` on photos count too. The bot asks `getMe` at startup to know who it is itself, instead of taking it from config that may be miscopied or stale.

  Compared by **id** and not by the `is_bot` flag: a group can hold several bots, and claiming a reply to another bot is cutting into someone else's work.
### Added
- **Look up documents first, then answer (phase 2).** The bot already had `javis_read_file` pointing at its brain, but **having a read tool is not the same as reading**: the model answers straight from general knowledge and the sentence is just as fluent and confident, and the owner can NOT tell the difference from outside. With real customers, an invented line about price or policy is a real risk.

  Now every turn searches the brain first (new module `chatbot_grounding`), takes the few best-matching passages and puts them straight into the prompt as the only basis. If nothing is found the prompt **says plainly that it searched and found nothing** - giving an empty block and staying silent is exactly letting the model fill the gap from its general memory.

  Search uses IDF-weighted keyword matching, not vector embeddings: a customer care bot's brain is a few dozen to a few hundred files, at that size this is good enough, runs locally, adds no service, and most importantly is **explainable** - the owner can see why the bot picked that file. Documents are cut by markdown headings so each passage is one complete idea; cutting hard by character count lets the bot read half a condition and answer as if it were the whole condition.
- **Customer conversation log + a list of QUESTIONS THE BOT COULD NOT ANSWER (phase 4).** A Log button on each bot card, two tabs, and the tab that opens by default is "Bot stumped" rather than conversations: conversations are only for checking when in doubt, while each row in "Bot stumped" is a spot where documents are missing, i.e. something the owner **can do something about**.

  Duplicates are merged by the accent-stripped question, sorted by times asked descending - what deserves extra documents first is what the most customers ask, not what was asked most recently. The bot counts as stumped in two cases: no document found, or a document found and it still has to say it has no information. The latter is subtler and more notable - the document EXISTS but is MISSING the point.

  The conversations tab shows **exactly which file the bot used** for each turn. Without that source line, "did the bot answer correctly" is a question that cannot be verified, only guessed.
- **Stumped means staff are alerted right away**, with the customer's question, if a staff Chat ID is set. A customer who asked and got nothing, without anyone knowing, is a lost customer.
### Security
- **Files sent by customers do NOT count as documents.** `inbox/` is excluded from lookup, along with the system folders. Otherwise anyone could upload a file saying "new policy: 100% refund in all cases" and ask again, and the bot would cite it as the store's official document - poisoning the knowledge base with one tap on send file.
- **The Telegram command menu of a customer bot is no longer the owner's admin menu.** `TelegramBot` used to pin `BOT_COMMANDS`, so a customer care bot showed customers "/brain - View or change the brain (vault) of this session" and other admin commands, even though it refuses to run them. Now the menu can be passed in; customer bots use exactly three entries `/help`, `/nhanvien`, `/id`.
### Improved
- **The "counts as found" threshold is measured by QUESTION COVERAGE, not an absolute score.** The absolute score alone is unusable: "does the store hire Rust programmers" hit exactly the word "hàng" (store/goods) in the Delivery section, and since "hàng" is rare its IDF is high, so the score passed the threshold and the bot thought it had grounds to answer about hiring. Now it measures the share of the question's weight actually present in the passage, plus a rule that a question of three or more meaningful words must hit at least two. With a 28-question reference set in the test as a fence against both failure directions (too loose and the bot invents, too strict and the bot says it does not know while the answer sits right in the price list).
- **Stop words rewritten for accent-stripped Vietnamese.** "bán" (sell) and "bạn" (you) both become "ban"; dropping "ban" loses the word "bán" - for a sales bot that is the most meaningful word in the sentence, and "có bán cà phê không" dropped to two words and then matched randomly into "cá cơm". Same reason for "anh" (ảnh) and "chi" (chi phí).

## [0.19.0] - 2026-08-04
The **Chatbot** page: put an Agent you created in front of CUSTOMERS, through its own Telegram bot and its own brain, handing over to a real staff member when a question is out of reach. Full spec in `docs/dev/2026-08-bot-chuyen-trach-spec.md`, usage guide at [docs/25-chatbot.md](docs/25-chatbot.md).
### Added
- **Dedicated Bot.** Jarvis 007 already had Agents, Skills, Workflows, but all of them served only the OWNER. Now an Agent can answer customers: each bot is a trio of **Agent + its own brain + its own Telegram token**. Customers message the bot directly, or you drop the bot into a customer care group.

  The bot **points to** the Agent instead of copying it: edit the Agent on the Agents page and the bot changes right away, no need to edit two places. If the Agent is deleted the bot keeps running (does not crash) but its card on the Chatbot page raises an alarm, and the prompt tells it to be more careful.

- **The Chatbot page was built for many bots from the first version**: card grid, search by name, add/edit/delete, on/off in place. The repo owner set the brief exactly so ("make 1 bot, but with a scalable UX/UI"), so this version runs one bot and adding a second needs no UI rework.

  A bot card has **four** states, not two: running, starting, **error**, off. A bot that dies silently (token revoked, network down, duplicate token) is something the store owner only finds out about when customers complain, so "error" must be a visible colored tile with a reason, not just the absence of green.

- **Hand over to a real staff member.** Set the staff Chat ID and the bot has two handover paths: automatic when a question is out of scope, and the customer typing `/nhanvien` themselves. Staff receive a message with the bot name, customer id and reason. Left empty, the bot only says it has no information and stops, without guessing further.

- **Check the token before saving.** The Check button asks Telegram directly, returns the exact bot name, and **blocks if another bot in Jarvis 007 already uses that token** (compared by @username from getMe rather than the token string, because the same token pasted twice with different whitespace is still two different strings). A token can run only ONE long-polling process; two pollers on the same token make Telegram return 409 and both die, failing where nobody expects it and nobody reports it.
### Security
- **The bot's fence lives in SOURCE CODE, not in the prompt.** This is the most important design point of the feature, because the person on the other end is a stranger:
  - A bot turn runs at the **suggest** permission level (read-only), lowered by code in `_tg_answer_engine`. No file writes, no creating orders, no spending money, no posting, no assigning work, no calling the data sources the owner connected. A line in the prompt can be talked around with clever wording; a permission level cannot, because the tool is simply not granted to that turn.
  - The bot does **not** use the Jarvis 007 system prompt (that prompt teaches orchestration, vault writes, task assignment, all things a customer bot must not do) but its own prompt: the role of the Agent it points to, plus customer reply rules.
  - Commands are a **WHITE**list: only `/start`, `/help`, `/id`, `/nhanvien`. Every other command gets a generic reply. The owner's bot has `/brain`, `/model`, `/status`; inheriting any one of them would let a customer change the store's brain.
  - **A new bot is ALWAYS off**, even when the create call sends `enabled: true`. Turning on is a deliberate click, not a side effect of creating. Turning on without a token is refused with a reason, rather than turning on and letting it die quietly in the watchdog.
  - The token is encrypted via `secrets_store` and **never** returned to the UI even in encrypted form; the UI only receives the `token_set` flag. UI patches go through a **WHITE**list of editable fields, so `id`, `created_at`, `token_enc`, `channel` cannot be overwritten.
  - **Rate limit** per sliding hour, per person within each bot (default 20 turns/hour). One idle person in a group can burn through the owner's whole model quota in an afternoon, and the owner only finds out when looking at the bill.
  - **In groups it is SILENT by default.** Until the group id is declared the bot does not take work in unknown groups; once declared it answers by default only when someone mentions its name or replies to its message.
- **Deleting a bot does NOT delete its brain and Agent**, and the confirm box says so clearly. Same reason deleting a Project does not delete conversations in 0.18.0: the brain may hold a month of documents the owner wrote, and the Agent may be in use by another bot or workflow.
### Improved
- **The permission level of a chat turn is passed down to the MCP Hub.** `_api_stream_mcp` takes a new `mode` parameter, so `discover_all`/`registry_inventory` filter tools by that turn's exact permission level instead of always at full access. This is what makes the "read-only bot" fence real rather than a promise.
- **The Chatbot item in the sidebar has its own icon** (`headset`), not reusing the Chat icon. Two neighboring items with the same icon cannot be told apart by eye.

## [0.18.2] - 2026-08-04
Three bugs reported by real users: **install dies on Vietnamese Windows**, **the model gave the wrong cause when file writes were blocked**, and **hitting the tool-call round cap then stopping with no way out**.
### Fixed
- **`setup.bat` died right at step [2/3] on Vietnamese Windows.** `pip install -r requirements.txt` blew up with `UnicodeDecodeError` midway and installed nothing.

  Cause: pip reads `requirements.txt` with `auto_decode()`. If it sees no BOM and no PEP-263 style encoding declaration in the FIRST TWO LINES it decodes with `locale.getpreferredencoding()` - on Vietnamese Windows that is cp1252/cp1258, and the file has Vietnamese comments. This is the kind of bug a dev machine never sees: Linux and macOS have a UTF-8 locale so they read it fine. The `chcp 65001` already in `setup.bat` does not save it either, since it changes the console codepage and not the ANSI codepage Python reads.

  Fixed with one `# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-` line at the top of the file, with a comment saying not to delete it. The test runs pip's OWN `auto_decode` function under simulated cp1252 and cp1258 locales.
- **The model gave the wrong cause when file writes were blocked.** A Kanban task running at Read-only level makes `javis_write_file` refuse, as designed. But the old refusal was vague ("the current mode does not allow writing files"), so the model read it and made up a plausible-sounding cause that was completely wrong. A real user got **"the filesystem environment has a sandbox permission error"** and went hunting for a disk fault, when all that was needed was raising the task to Draft writes.

  Now the refusal says plainly this is a PERMISSION limit and not a disk or sandbox error, points to the exact place to change it (Work page, Draft writes level), and tells the model not to retry the write but to put the full content into its answer so the user can save it. Messages meant for MACHINES to read are an interface too: write them vaguely and the machine guesses, and guesses wrong.
### Improved
- **The tool-call round cap is adjustable with `JAVIS_MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS`** (default still 8, clamped to 1-40). Multi-step background tasks often hit the cap and stopped midway with no way to raise it. The number 8 used to be hard-pinned in three different places in `engine.py`; now it is declared in a single place.
- **The cap-reached message says what to do**: it names the exact number in effect, warns that the answer may be unfinished, and points to two fixes (split the request, or raise the environment variable). The old version only stated the number and went quiet.

## [0.18.1] - 2026-08-04
Fixed where the icon goes: moved to the **head of the two tabs** and to **Project**, removed from each conversation.
### Fixed
- **Icon put in the wrong place in 0.18.0.** The intent in the dev notes was to add a fitting icon at the head of the two tabs "Conversations" and "Folders"; the previous version instead built an icon picker for EACH conversation.

  The mistake is one you can deduce by asking "what does this icon separate from what". In a conversation list every row is a conversation, so an icon there separates no group from another - it is just decoration to set by hand one by one, plus one more button in a row that already has four. The two tabs, on the other hand, are two different kinds of thing side by side told apart only by text, so at a glance you must read to know where you are.
### Added
- **The two tabs of the History column have icons.** They use exactly the rail icons already used for those two things so the whole app speaks the same visual language, rather than adding new icons just for this spot.
- **A Project with no icon set borrows the folder icon as default**, and the first two lines of the group picker menu have icons too. When every row has an icon the eye can scan down the icon column, and you can see at a glance that the icon is changeable here. Project is still the ONLY place to change an icon, since each group really is a different thing.
### Improved
- **Per-conversation icons removed completely, leaving no dead UI**: the `sessions.icon` column, `SessionStore.set_icon`, the `POST /sessions/{id}/icon` endpoint, the button and the render code are all gone. The hover button row has four buttons instead of five.

## [0.18.0] - 2026-08-04
Cleared a batch of ideas from the dev notes: **pin and group conversations**, **clickable links in .md files**, **skill picking now that skills are 55+**, **log pagination**, added **NotebookLM** to the connection store and **sending images over Zalo**. Full spec in `docs/dev/2026-08-backlog-spec.md`.
### Added
- **Pin conversations to the top, group them into Projects, attach icons.** The History list was sorted purely by time so a conversation used again and again drifted down, and being all text it was hard to tell one from another at a glance. Now hovering a conversation lets you pin it, tag it with an emoji, move it into a Project.

  The group picker sits right under the New conversation button. With a project open the list filters by it, **and a new conversation you start automatically lands in that project** instead of being tagged by hand - something only possible because the conversation id is generated browser-side the moment you press send, so the label is attached from the FIRST message.

  **Deleting a project does NOT delete conversations**: the ones inside are only removed from the group. The confirm box says so with the number of conversations that will be removed from it, since there is no undo for a mis-click that sweeps away a month of chats.

  Icons come from **Jarvis 007's own icon set**, not emoji: Jarvis 007 icons change color with the light/dark theme and draw identically on every machine, while emoji differ per operating system and have fixed colors so they glare on a dark background. The picker shows every available icon with a filter by name.
- **The connection store has Google NotebookLM.** List notebooks, read sources, ask questions right inside a notebook, add sources, create summaries or audio in Studio.

  The notes called this "write an MCP server wrapper", but digging showed `notebooklm-py` already ships an MCP server, so what Jarvis 007 does is just one entry in the connector store - not a line of Python. Default is **Read-only**; sign in with a browser session (see the Security part below).
- **Send IMAGES and FILES over Zalo** (bundled plugin `zalo-image`, tool `zalo_send_image`). The standard MCP `zalo_send_message` only takes text, so Jarvis 007 could create images yet still could not send them to anyone. Meanwhile the underlying library (`zca-js`) has long been able to, and that very CLI already has the command `msg send-image`.

  Version 1.6.2 is already the newest on npm so waiting for upstream to expose more parameters is waiting forever. The approach: call that same CLI again with `HOME` pointing at the session folder of the currently signed-in Zalo connection - no fork of the Node package, no second QR scan.
### Improved
- **Links in .md files are now clickable.** Open a note to read and click a link to another file, and before it went nowhere; while the `[[wikilink]]` right beside it worked, though the two look identical.

  Cause: the handling EXISTED but sat BEHIND the "when composing in the editor, open nothing" fence - and the editor's rendered view IS the compose area, so every markdown link fell into that fence. Now file links come before the fence, right where wikilinks stand. http links in the rendered view are also opened for you (the browser does not open tabs by itself inside the compose area, it only places the cursor). Images keep the old behavior so they can still be dragged and deleted like a single character.
- **Going to a file by link makes the folder tree auto-expand to the branch holding it.** Before, after opening you still did not know where the file lived, and next time you searched from the start again.
- **Opening a file from chat uses the sticky edit panel instead of a popup.** Opening a file from the Folders tab makes the editor take over the chat panel, while opening the same file by a link in chat popped a popup over the middle of the screen - two paths into one file, two faces. Now it is one path. The popup remains for narrow screens (under 860px there is no room for the sticky panel). File types that cannot be edited (pdf, docx, zip) show a file card with Open in new tab and Download buttons.
- **The skill picker when editing an Agent has search and grouping.** A real brain has 55+ skills and this panel was a flat pile of checkboxes, so ticking the right one meant scanning the whole list by eye. Now there is a search box (accent-insensitive, scanning name, slug, group and description), grouping by the same `group` field the Skills page uses, groups with ticked skills open by default, plus a counter and a Clear selection button.
- **Pagination for the self-learning log, learning commits and the Latest turns table.** The Self-learning page used to show only 10 log lines and 12 commits and then nothing, with no way to look further back. The source was widened too: the learning log reads until it has enough entries instead of hard-cutting at 3 files - the log writes one file per day, so cutting at 3 meant pagination only flipped around 3 days.

  The pagination block was split into one shared function instead of copying a second and third version, the very lesson already learned in the Vault tree (0.15.1) and the Jarvis 007 CLI (0.17.0).
### Security
- **Zalo image sending only sends files INSIDE the brain in use.** The tool takes its path from the chat sentence itself and its output is sending outward, which cannot be recalled; without this fence a clever sentence could smuggle a key file or `/etc/passwd` into any Zalo chat. Absolute paths outside the brain are blocked too, not only the `../` form.
- **With several Zalo accounts connected, Jarvis 007 asks back, it does not guess.** Sending from the wrong account is sending under another person's identity. The tool is also at `full` level like `zalo_send_message`, so suggest mode and limited background tasks cannot send on their own.
- **NotebookLM says plainly this is a Google session cookie, not scope-limited OAuth.** Whoever holds that string gets into the Google account, so the connector defaults to **Read-only** and warns at the very first step of the wizard. The tools that SHARE a notebook outward are classed as dangerous even though the library marks them as non-destructive: sharing can be undone, but someone having read it cannot be taken back. The connector is deliberately NOT placed in the one-stop Google group - that group is for connections that share one OAuth client key, with a very different sign-in and risk.

## [0.17.1] - 2026-08-04
Assigning Kanban work now works from **every brain**, not only the two engines that can run machine commands.
### Added
- **Tool `javis_task`** (bundled plugin `javis-task`, on by default): assigns background work into the Kanban queue (`op=add`) and shows how far running work has got (`op=list`), straight from chat, on any engine.
### Fixed
- **The docs promised something the code could not do, for many versions.** `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/10-models-va-engine.md` both said every brain gets the same toolkit, including "assign Kanban work". In reality the only way to assign work was `POST /kanban/task`, and calling it needs Bash and curl - meaning only Claude Code and Codex. The five API engines were left out.

  Worse than the gap: `CLAUDE.md` also told Jarvis 007 "never say you cannot do tasks, that is factually wrong". So an API engine would CONFIDENTLY accept and then silently do nothing. The user sat waiting for work that never ran, with not a single error line anywhere.

  Fixed by raising the CODE to match the docs, not lowering the docs: assigning work is used for real, and having it run on only two engines would puncture the promise "swap brains freely without losing features" at the most regrettable spot.
- **The line "the ONLY difference is running machine commands" was also wrong, now stated in full.** The two CLI engines also have **WebFetch/WebSearch** (open unknown URLs to read, search the web on their own), **Task** (spawn sub-agents running in parallel), and can resume an old session. API engines have two practical limits never written anywhere: at most **8 tool-call rounds** per turn, and when a turn calls tools the answer appears as one block at the end instead of streaming word by word.
### Security
- **The `javis_task` tool CANNOT create `full`-level work.** Full lets work act for real outside (create orders, spend money, run ads, send messages) and cannot be undone, so it must be set by the user themselves on the Work page. Default is `suggest`; an unknown mode is clamped to `suggest` and does not drift to `auto`.
- **It calls the in-process queue directly, opening no extra HTTP door.** The easier way was to have the plugin POST `/kanban/task` the way `javis-schedule` POSTs `/reminders`, but that route requires login and the only way to open it is adding it to the localhost auth-exempt list - meaning any process on the same server could assign work to Jarvis 007 with no credential. Not worth it, when the plugin already runs inside the server process.
- **No swallowing of omissions.** If the brain is unknown it refuses rather than silently falling back to Brain Default (assigning to the wrong brain means running on someone else's data). A missing recipient warns right in the result, since that is the number one reason users "assign work and see nothing".

## [0.17.0] - 2026-08-04
**Jarvis 007 CLI**: type `javis "how is this week's revenue"` right in the terminal. The third channel, the same Jarvis 007.
### Added
- **`pip install javis-cli` then type the question directly.** No subcommand, no opening a browser. The answer still comes from your own Jarvis 007: same brain, same memory, same connected MCPs, same conversation history on the Sessions page.

  There are also `javis chat` (a continuous Q&A session that keeps the thread), `javis status`, `javis task add`, `javis tasks`, `javis brain ls|cat`, `javis loops`, and `javis up` to start the Jarvis 007 installed on that same machine.
- **The CLI is a THIN CLIENT, not a second Jarvis 007.** It holds no server inside and says so on the first line of the docs and in the error messages. Reason: nearly everything that makes Jarvis 007 demands a long-lived process (periodic loops, reminders waiting for their time, the MCP Hub holding connections, the capability store, the token-saving runtime that learns over time), and a command that exits when done is no place for them.

  So the CLI goes through EXACTLY the core the dashboard and Telegram use (`_tg_answer`, which now takes a channel parameter). In return: a new Jarvis 007 feature is seen by the CLI at once, no editing two places. This is also the 0.15.0 lesson - building a second copy of something that already exists and letting the two drift apart - applied at a much larger scale.
- **Jarvis 007 knows it is talking through a terminal so it answers differently.** The `cli` channel has its own context block and output contract: no markdown tables, no embedded images, no markdown links, file paths printed ABSOLUTE so you can copy and run them directly.
- **Unix rules, so it composes into scripts.** The answer goes to stdout, everything else (progress, tool names, errors) goes to stderr. So `javis "summarize this week" > report.md` gives a clean file. On error it exits non-zero and prints nothing to stdout, so `&&` in scripts behaves correctly. A test guards that exactly ONE place in the whole package writes to stdout.
- **Connect several Jarvis 007 at once**: one profile for the home machine, one for the VPS, switched with `--profile`. Config is in `~/.javis/config.json` with `600` permissions, and four environment variables (`JAVIS_URL`, `JAVIS_TOKEN`, `JAVIS_BRAIN`, `JAVIS_PROFILE`) override the file for CI/Docker.
- **The Account page has an API Tokens section.** Create a token, pick its scope, see each one's last use, revoke. The raw string shows exactly ONCE with a ready `javis login` command to paste on the other machine.
### Security
- **No token exists by default.** Until someone presses create, no token exists, and there is no door in other than the browser. This is the most important point of the whole feature: opening a new port to the Internet must be a DELIBERATE action, not a default.
- **Two scope levels.** `chat` follows a WHITElist (`/chat`, `/version`, `/health`, `/sessions`); `full` equals a browser session. The white direction was chosen over the black one, because a blacklist means every new endpoint added to the server is automatically exposed to the narrow token.
- **A token cannot create a token.** Creating a token requires a browser session. Without this fence a leaked token lets whoever holds it grant themselves permanent new tokens, and revoking the leaked one becomes meaningless. Conversely, REVOKING may use the very token in hand: when a machine is lost you must be able to take down the credential at once, even if you cannot open a browser.
- **Only a SHA-256 hash is on disk**, compared with `compare_digest` rather than string comparison (a plain string comparison exits early at the first differing character, and that timing difference is enough to probe a token character by character). The token travels in the `Authorization` header, never in the query string - query strings sit in the logs of every proxy along the way.
- **More than 10 failures in 5 minutes blocks the IP for 15 minutes**, each failure is written to `auth_audit.jsonl` but only the first 12 characters, because log files are often attached to bug reports. The probe block is checked BEFORE hashing, and the token branch is placed AFTER the cookie branch so the dashboard does not read the token file on every request.

## [0.16.1] - 2026-08-03
Ollama trimmed down to just the **Cloud** version - paste an API key and it runs, like every other provider.
### Improved
- **Removed the run-on-home-machine path, keeping only Ollama Cloud.** Jarvis 007 mostly runs on a VPS in Docker, where "localhost" is the container itself and not the user's machine - so the home path was almost unusable, yet it dragged in a whole special case: a separate address field (`host_field`, the only one in the entire provider layer), a separate branch to compute "connected yet", a separate UI branch, and a pick-path-by-key function.

  Now Ollama has exactly the shape of Groq or Gemini: paste the key, done. The provider card is also back to a single field like the other cards.
