- Fetching the model list still asks two paths (OpenAI-standard `/v1/models` first, Ollama-native `/api/tags` after) because their docs do not say which path is primary for Cloud. Better one extra request than reporting "no model found" for a perfectly correct key.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-08-03
Added the eighth brain: **Ollama** - run models right on your machine, or through Ollama Cloud.
### Added
- **Ollama provider, two run paths in one card.**
  - **Home machine**: leave both fields empty. Free, no token limit, and data never leaves the machine - something no provider in Jarvis 007 could do before. Needs Ollama installed and a model pulled (`ollama pull llama3.1`).
  - **Ollama Cloud**: paste the API key from ollama.com. Runs big models the home machine cannot handle.
  - With the address left empty, Jarvis 007 picks the path itself: with a key it goes to Cloud, with no key it uses this machine. If an address is declared it always follows that address, even another machine on the network.
- **Ollama is a fully equipped agent like every other brain**: it calls connected MCPs, reads/writes the brain, runs skills, takes Kanban work. Not plain chat. The model must know how to call tools (llama3.1 and up, qwen2.5, mistral-nemo, gpt-oss... all do).
- **The Check button asks that machine directly which models it has.** Getting models means the address is right and Ollama is running - so it is both the model list and the connection light, no separate test button needed. If nothing is seen it states clearly what to check, and the hint tells home machine apart from Cloud.
### Fixed
- The test "UI lists exactly the 5 providers with MCP" hard-pinned five names, so adding a provider turned CI red even though everything was right - the fence ended up blocking the fix. Now it reads the real list on the server and guards the invariant that matters: **the UI matches the server**.

## [0.15.2] - 2026-08-03
Opening a file from the Folders tab makes the editor TAKE the place of the chat panel, not cover it.
### Added

On the main screen the editor is a floating layer over the brain visual, an empty spot where covering makes sense; on the Chat page below is a chat with content, and covering it is both cramped and messy.

  Closing the editor (close button or the Esc key) brings the chat panel back intact, with the half-said text still there - it was only hidden, not rebuilt.

## [0.15.1] - 2026-08-03
The Folders tab uses EXACTLY the existing Vault tree, instead of a second tree built in the previous version.

- **Version 0.15.0 built a second folder tree instead of using the existing one.** The repo owner pointed it out at once: "why not just carry the same tree over from Jarvis 007 instead of rebuilding it so complicated, and buggy too". Right - Jarvis 007 already has a Vault tree in the left column of the main screen, with search by name and by content, create file, create folder, refresh, highlighting the open file. Writing a second one is copying all that and letting the two drift apart, and the new one had no real users yet so bugs just sat there.

  Now the Folders tab **borrows that same Vault panel**, the way the Chat page already borrows the main screen's chat panel. The same tree, only changing where it stands. The self-built module is removed entirely.

- **A "Locate" button on Vault tree search results** - on BOTH the main screen and the Folders tab in the chat panel, since there is now only one tree. Clicking it expands the tree to the exact folder holding the file and highlights it, instead of opening the note straight away as before.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-08-03
The chat panel's left column gets a new **Folders** tab: the brain's file tree, right next to the conversation history.
### Added
- **A Folders tab in the Chat panel.** The left column used to hold only conversation history, so to see what files the brain has you had to leave for the Files page - and leaving loses your half-said place. Now that column has two tabs, switching back and forth without leaving the chat panel. The selected tab is remembered for next time.
- **The tree expands and collapses, loading on demand.** A folder is read only when you open it, so a brain with a few thousand files still opens instantly. Clicking a file opens it directly in the dashboard editor, meaning it becomes the conversation's open file right away.

Finding a file without knowing which folder it is in means searching again next time; this button answers exactly that. ## [0.14.8] - 2026-08-03
The Updates page stopped saying "you are on the latest version" while right below it said a new version exists.
### Fixed
- **A machine running v0.14.4 still showed "You are on the latest version" in the top box, and the update button did not appear.** Right below, on the same page, it said "New version: v0.14.7". The two lines contradicted each other because they read two different sources: the top box compared the `VERSION` file on the main branch, while the badge below read `CHANGELOG.md`. Versions 0.14.5, 0.14.6, 0.14.7 were all logged in the changelog but forgot to bump `VERSION`, so to the top box the latest was still 0.14.4 - equal to the running version, and it concluded there was nothing to update.

  The consequence is heavier than it looks: Docker users have no button and see no Redeploy instructions, meaning **no way to reach the new version** unless they SSH in themselves. Three patches in a row sat there that nobody could get.
- **Now there is a fence against exactly this bug.** A test checks that `VERSION` matches the newest entry in `CHANGELOG.md`, so next time a bump is forgotten CI goes red on the spot instead of silently shipping. The same test also checks the version number format and the order of entries in the changelog.

## [0.14.7] - 2026-08-03
The Ultra saving level had never once run on a machine with many MCPs connected. Found and unlocked.
### Fixed
- **The shortcut was blocked on almost every turn, and the more sources connected the more surely it was blocked.** The repo owner reported "not once in chat did I see the word Instant", and checking showed exactly that. The turn gate looked at the number of candidates **matched by words**, counted before scoring and before permission filtering. On a machine with a few hundred MCP tools connected (Gmail, Drive, Calendar, ads...), nearly any Vietnamese sentence matched a few tools through one shared word, so that condition was true for every turn and the shortcut never ran.

  Meaning the Ultra saving level saved less the more sources you connected, the opposite of what it promised. It did not show on a dev machine, because the tool store there is nearly empty and every test is green.

  Now it looks at the **highest match score** after scoring. A near-hit still yields to the normal path to be safe, while matching a stray word is no reason to skip the shortcut. The threshold lives at `context_runtime.canary.min_resolver_score` (default 0.45) so it can be tuned when needed.
- **Many reply branches did not carry the mode label, so some turns showed nothing under the answer.** The "mode + tokens" line is carried by the reply packet, and only three branches attached it. The reminder branch, the lookup branch, the execution branch, and the branch refusing for exceeding the quota all sent a bare reply. Now every reply packet carries the label, and a test scans the entire source so no newly added branch gets missed.
### Added
- **The Saving page says plainly why a chat turn could not take the shortcut**, grouped by reason and sorted by count. The "Latest turns" table already recorded the reason for each row, but a reason covering 18 of 20 turns is a break while one appearing twice is normal, and looking row by row you cannot tell those two cases apart. It was exactly the lack of this number that made the bug above wait for the repo owner to say it in words before it showed up.

## [0.14.6] - 2026-08-03
Jarvis 007 knows the time on every path, and stops making up reasons when it does not know.
### Fixed
- **Asked what time it is, Jarvis 007 said "the MCP server is disconnected".** No server was disconnected. The truth is that turn took the Ultra saving shortcut, and the shortcut sends a packet with NO tools - that is exactly where it saves. The model has no clock in its head, so when asked the time with no tool to call, it did the worst thing: it invented a plausible-sounding reason.

  The question filter did block "now" and "today" and forced those questions down the full path, but blocking by keyword is a game of cat and mouse: "what time is it in Vietnam" slipped right through. Now it is fixed at the root - every packet Jarvis 007 sends, shortcut and full path alike, carries a line with the real time in the Vietnam time zone. About 30 tokens per turn, in exchange for leaving no door to make things up, and with saving on or off Jarvis 007 knows the time just the same.

  The time zone is fixed UTC+7 and does not read the server's time zone, because a VPS almost always runs UTC.
### Improved
- The **Token saving** page was renamed **Saving** for brevity.

## [0.14.5] - 2026-08-03
Cleared the way so the default saving level can be raised later without stepping on anyone who chose their own.
### Fixed
- **Changing the default saving level would never reach machines already installed.** The trap sits in how Jarvis 007 stores config: every write rewrites the WHOLE merged config, so the first time a user presses any button on the Settings page, that day's default values get frozen into settings.json. On read the file then overrides the defaults. Consequence: if a later version raises the default to Optimised or Ultra saving, only fresh installs would see it and running machines would not, with no error reported. This is exactly the disease that bit `provider_kinds` in 0.12.4, this time landing on the thing that decides how many tokens each chat turn costs.

  The specific hard part: a 0 in the file has two opposite meanings, "considered and deliberately chose Off" and "nobody chose anything". If they cannot be told apart you either step on the user's decision or the new default never arrives. Now every self-changed level leaves a signature, and with a signature the update does not touch it. A machine that never chose follows the default of the running version, even one installed long ago.
### Improved
- **The Saving page says clearly whether the running level was chosen by you or is just the default.** The two look identical on screen but mean opposite things: the latter rises with updates, the former does not. If never chosen there is a line saying so, with how to pin it by pressing any level, even the one already shown.
- **Raising the default level only RAISES, never LOWERS.** A machine running a level above the default, even by hand-editing settings.json, stays as is. Nothing the user turned on is turned off by an update.
- The "which level enables which path" table is gathered into one place. Before, it sat in `main.py` while the default-raising code is in `config.py` and could not import it - with two copies, when a path is added to some level the default-raising code would still follow the old table, drifting silently.
### Notes
- This version does not change anyone's default, the factory level is still Off. It only builds the mechanism so the next raise can reach its target. One ambiguity remains, stated for transparency: a machine that deliberately chose Off BEFORE this version left no signature, so when the default is raised it will be raised too. Pressing a level once after updating pins it permanently.

## [0.14.4] - 2026-08-03
The Claude Code plan can use the Ultra saving level. Before, it was the only brain left out.
### Added
- **The shortcut for simple questions now runs on the Claude Code plan too.** Version 0.14.0 hard-blocked it because at that time there was no way to call the model directly without an API key, which a subscription plan does not have. But Jarvis 007 already borrowed Claude Code's own access token to ask for the model list, and the same token can call the answer path. Now all three kinds of brain can use this level.
- **There is a safety net.** The CLI's token can expire or be rejected. When that happens the turn falls back to full Claude Code within the same turn, throwing no error and leaving no empty bubble. A little slower, but you still get an answer.
### Fixed
- **A turn that fell back to the full engine still wore the "Instant" label.** The shortcut pins the label the moment it takes the turn, so when it comes back empty-handed the label is still there: the line under the answer lies, the 24-hour table puts it in the wrong column, and the savings figure is inflated by exactly the turns that saved nothing. Now the pin is returned when that tier cannot deliver, and one tier cannot undo another tier's commitment.
- **Claude Code model aliases are translated to real names.** Claude Code understands "haiku" and picks the latest version itself, but the direct-call path does not: sending "haiku" reports model not found. Now Jarvis 007 looks up the available model list and translates to the exact newest version of the same family.

## [0.14.3] - 2026-08-03
The page stopped mislabeling the Ultra saving level, and each turn can say WHY it did not take the shortcut.
### Fixed
- **After pressing the Ultra saving level the page still said "does not apply to the current brain".** That label was wrong since 0.14.0: it hard-coded "only runs on brains using an API key" back when the shortcut really was like that, then 0.14.0 opened it to the ChatGPT plan and nobody remembered to fix that line. The result was a page labeling a denial onto the very level that had just been opened, and the person pressing it thought they pressed it by mistake. Now the label reads the real config, so next time another brain is opened the page is automatically right. Only the Claude Code plan was still reported as not opened, and that was a hard fence with a reason: the shortcut calls the model through a path that needs an API key, which that plan does not have.
### Added
- **Each turn in the "Latest turns" table now says plainly why it took that path.** The reason was always recorded but never shown on screen, so after pressing a level and seeing chat still show "Optimised" you were stuck, with no way to know whether the question needed lookup, the brain was not opened, or the tool store was not ready yet. Now each row has a short note right under the mode name: "this question needs real data", "tool store not ready, try again in a few turns", "this question needs a tool call"...
### Improved
- The Ultra saving level description adds one important sentence: **questions needing lookup still take the full path**, so not every turn with this level on will look different. That is intended, not broken.

## [0.14.2] - 2026-08-03
Opening a new thread no longer loses context: the re-seed became five times thicker and carries a summary.
### Improved
- **When Jarvis 007 opens a new conversation thread, it carries five times more than before.** The repo owner worried about losing context when a heavy long-running job is assigned, and on re-checking the pain was not in the threshold as assumed, but in the re-seed. The two numbers run against each other in a counterintuitive way: the higher the threshold, the rarer the rotation, but each rotation **falls deeper**. At a threshold of 120,000, falling to a 60,000-character re-seed loses it six times over. At the just-raised threshold of 1 million, the same cap becomes losing fifty times over.

  Now the re-seed is 300,000 characters wide, about 100,000 tokens. Measured on a 120-turn conversation: before it kept 16 turns, now it keeps 86.
- **And it carries the compressed summary of the start of the conversation**, placed before the raw history and not cut. One summary line stands for dozens of turns that fell out of budget, so dropping it to fit two more raw turns trades in the wrong direction.
- Checked: the thread rotation threshold **does not touch background work at all**. It only runs inside the chat panel; loops and Kanban tasks open a new engine session each run so there is no thread to rotate.

## [0.14.1] - 2026-08-03
The rotation threshold raised to 1 million tokens based on real usage, and citation junk that leaked into answers cleaned up.
### Fixed
- **Answers appeared with a few empty boxes and the text `citeturn4view0`.** That is OpenAI's internal citation marker, written with three invisible characters that the browser draws as boxes. The more annoying part is that it is invisible: it goes straight into the conversation history, so on the next turn Jarvis 007 itself rereads it and thinks `turn4view0` is a real source. Asked "where did you get the information", it answered "I only have the reference code `turn4view0`, no original source URL". Now the marker is stripped at the source, on both the Codex path and the direct-call path.
### Improved
- **The threshold for automatically opening a new conversation thread was raised from 120,000 to 1,000,000 tokens per turn**, at the repo owner's request after real use. The measurements back it: three consecutive turns in the same conversation were 83,000, then 552,000 (a turn looking up weather, Codex ran a whole search loop), then 36,000. Meaning a heavy turn is usually heavy because of **that turn's own work**, not because the thread is long, and the thread shrinks again on its own the next turn. At 120,000 almost every turn exceeds it, i.e. constant rotation: each rotation throws away context the engine is holding, in exchange for almost nothing.

## [0.14.0] - 2026-08-03
Real measurements show the part Jarvis 007 can trim is only 13%, while 87% of tokens sit elsewhere. This version goes after that place.
### Added
- **Simple questions on the ChatGPT plan now go direct, without the tool loop.** Measured on the repo's server: each Codex turn reads 35,000 to 412,000 tokens while the model writes only 266 to 1,496. That ratio is not one call, it is a whole loop: Codex receives the question then calls the model itself over many rounds, each round resending the whole accumulated context. For a question needing no lookup - "what is entropy", "write me a headline" - that whole loop is wasted. Now such questions go straight in one round. This is exactly what the **Ultra saving** level promised but never delivered for subscription plan users.
- **Jarvis 007 automatically opens a new conversation thread when the old one swells past 120,000 tokens per turn.** Claude Code and Codex manage their own threads, so the biggest part of each turn was out of reach: trimming the rule set to a few hundred tokens still left the old thread dragging hundreds of thousands. Real measurement: the first turn of a conversation 36,000 tokens, a few turns later already 191,000. Now when it passes the threshold, Jarvis 007 opens a new thread and **carries a history summary**, and tells you right in the chat panel. There is an anti-constant-rotation mark: at least two more Q&A turns are needed before rotating again, so a turn that is heavy because of work does not trigger breaking the thread every turn.
### Fixed
- **Jarvis 007 estimates in advance what each turn costs, and estimated nearly seven times lower than reality.** The page recorded a negative skew of 86%, some turns negative 96%. That figure is not just for viewing: it is exactly what Jarvis 007 uses to block BEFORE exceeding the quota, so underestimating seven times means that fence almost did not exist. Cause: the estimator counted exactly what Jarvis 007 packed up, but could not see the loops the engine runs by itself afterward. Now Jarvis 007 **learns from the turns each brain actually ran**: however many times reality exceeds the estimate, it multiplies by that much. It only widens and never shrinks, and there is a ceiling clamp so one abnormal turn does not skew the whole factor.
- **A shortcut turn was the only turn without the "which path, how much spent" line.** Version 0.13.0 attached that line to three branches and forgot this one, so exactly the most saving turns were the ones that could show nothing off.
- **A shortcut turn does not pass through Codex, so Codex's thread did not know it happened.** Continuing the old thread on the next turn made Codex answer with an incomplete record: not seeing the question just asked nor the answer just given, then repeating or contradicting itself. Now after each shortcut turn, the thread is rebuilt from the stored history.
- The shortcut is **hard-blocked** for the Claude Code plan, independent of config: it runs through the direct-call path that needs an API key, which the Claude Code plan does not have. Loosening the config by hand to that point makes every simple question report a sign-in error.
### Improved
- **New test `test_ba_don_bay_token.py` runs a real chat turn through all three paths** and guards the dangerous direction too: a question needing real data must ABSOLUTELY NOT take the shortcut, because shortcutting a lookup question means answering with invention. Mutation-checked with 10 mutations, all 10 caught.

## [0.13.4] - 2026-08-03
Machines that had Jarvis 007 installed earlier also could not make saving take effect: the old config in the machine overrides the new default, and it overrides silently.
### Fixed
- **After turning on a saving level the line under each answer still said "Full".** Exactly the bug the repo owner screenshotted. The cause sits where nobody expected: **every machine that ran Jarvis 007 before version 0.12.4 is affected**, while fresh installs are not, so every earlier test was green.

  Jarvis 007 writes the **whole** config into `settings.json` the first time the user presses anything, and on read it lays the file over the defaults. Meaning that day's defaults are frozen permanently: if Jarvis 007 later fixes the defaults to be better, machines already installed **never see it**. Before 0.12.4, the two most important saving areas (selective memory and on-demand skill loading) ran only on brains using an API key. Old machines pinned that number hard. Upgrade, press "Optimised", the page shows a green "turned on, effective immediately", and then every turn on the ChatGPT or Claude plan still sent the whole rule set because all three sources were silently excluded.

  Now when reading config, Jarvis 007 **widens** the brain scope of the saving areas to at least the current default, only widening and never narrowing. An area that deliberately runs only on API-key brains (the part resending conversation history: Claude Code and ChatGPT already remember their own threads, sending more means sending twice) keeps its own scope. Pressing a level once more also heals the config file itself.
### Improved
- **New test `test_cauhinh_cu_khong_ket.py` builds exactly a machine installed earlier** and then presses a level the way a user would. This is a class of bug that a test on a clean machine can never see. With the patch removed it goes red in exactly five places.

## [0.13.3] - 2026-08-03
Re-audited whether turning on a saving level really saves. Four holes, and all four silent: the page still showed green, tokens were still spent as before.
### Fixed
- **Four of the five API-key brains saved nothing after pressing "Optimised".** OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini and Anthropic API all fell here. Reason: the context selection needs the token quota known in advance, and the quota table built into the machine **has only Groq**. Not knowing the quota, it silently went back to sending the whole rule set every turn, while the page still said "turned on, down 89%". Now when the real quota is unknown, Jarvis 007 uses a **default context ceiling** for packing. That ceiling is only for composing, never used to refuse your question: exceeding it falls back to the old way and does not block. And the first time the provider reports exceeding the quota, Jarvis 007 uses their real figure in place of this ceiling.
- **Changing brain made saving silently stop.** The quota was declared exactly once, and next time seeing "something already there" it skipped. So pressing a level while using Groq, then switching to another brain, left Jarvis 007 still holding Groq's quota, not matching the new brain, and every turn went the old path without a word. Now the quota is **topped up** for the brain in use, keeping what the user declared themselves, and pressing again does not spawn copies.
- **A turn that did save was still recorded as "Full".** A turn passes through several tiers; a tier that does not take it marks it "old path", and the old way was first to mark wins. The context saving part runs last so even when it took the turn it could not change the label. Consequence: the line under the answer said "Full", the 24-hour table put that turn in the not-saved column, and the page told you nothing was saved while it was saving. Every API-key brain was affected, i.e. exactly the people paying per token. Now "old path" is only the default when nobody takes it, and when a tier truly takes it the label follows that tier. Two old rules are kept: a real path does not overwrite a real path, and adjusting the level mid-turn does not change the running turn.
- **The "Ultra saving" level boasted 96% down even for brains that cannot use it.** This level beats "Optimised" in exactly the shortcut for simple questions, and the shortcut runs only on brains using an API key. Anyone on the Claude plan or ChatGPT plan pressing it only gets the Optimised level. Now that button shows the real figure for the running brain, with a **"does not apply to the current brain"** mark and a sentence saying why.
- **The server's warning was swallowed.** The server did reply "this part cannot run yet" when a level was pressed, but the UI never showed it, so you only saw one green line "turned on, effective immediately". Now the warning shows directly in the notice.
### Improved
- **New test `test_tiet_kiem_chay_that.py` presses the level exactly as the user does, on all seven brains, then asks the decision layer directly which path this turn takes.** Mutation-checked with five mutations, replanting exactly the five bugs above, all five caught.
- Raised the length cap of one connection guide step to 450 characters (approved by the repo owner). The nine Facebook and Google steps exceeded the old cap because each added sentence is a real incident; the UI does not truncate text, so cutting to the old number would throw away exactly the part that saves the user.

## [0.13.2] - 2026-08-03
Turning on the ChatGPT plan made every chat turn die. Fixed that, and cleaned up three same-family breaks that CI has no way to see.
### Fixed
- **Chat through the ChatGPT plan (Codex) broke every turn: `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable '_ctx_in'`.** The token counter added in 0.13.0 accumulates in three brain branches; two branches add right in the function body so they ran fine, but the Codex branch adds inside an inner function and forgot to declare `nonlocal`. Python then treated it as a local variable of the inner function, and `+=` read a variable never assigned. It blew up exactly at the moment Codex finished answering, so the consequence was not just a missing token count line: the whole turn broke, the answer already shown on screen was not saved to history, and the user only saw "Processing error". Every chat turn of ChatGPT plan users was hit since 0.13.0.
- **The path pushing background results back to the web chat panel had a NameError lying in wait.** `push_to_chat` logs errors with `sys.stderr` while `main.py` never imported `sys`. Because it sits in an `except` branch, it only blows up when another problem already happened, and turns "log and carry on" into breaking the whole result-reporting path. That is exactly the path Kanban work, loops and reminders use to return results to the chat panel.
- **The "Enable People API" button on the Google Calendar card never appeared.** Any card with a step-by-step wizard has the old button block hidden entirely, and the People API link lived only in the old block. Users who did all the steps still got `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` when finding free time, with no way to know what was missing. Now People API is its own step, with a button.
- **Seven test files never ran a single line in CI.** They were written pytest style but lacked a `__main__` block, while CI runs each file as a script, so the file only defined functions and exited 0. Four assertions among them were RED and nobody knew, including the People API button bug above. Now all seven really run.
### Improved
- **New test `test_luot_chat_codex.py` runs one full real chat turn through the Codex branch** with a fake WebSocket and fake Codex CLI, then checks exactly the three things the bug broke: no error packet, an answer with the incoming token count, and the turn saved to history. Replanting the old bug turns the test red with the exact "Processing error: UnboundLocalError" line the user saw.
- **New test `test_bien_chua_gan.py` guards exactly the two kinds of bug just fixed** across the whole code tree: an inner function accumulating into a parent function variable without `nonlocal`, and a function using a global name that does not exist. Byte-compile cannot see these because the syntax is perfectly valid, and text-search style tests are even blinder: they still count the right number of `_ctx_in +=` while the bug is happening. The scanner self-checks by rebuilding exactly the two broken snippets and forcing itself to raise the alarm.
- The Google Workspace pack intro line and its first step were shortened to fit one menu line, without cutting any idea.

## [0.13.1] - 2026-08-03
Renamed the modes to say what they do, instead of whether they are old or new.
### Improved
- **Dropped the word "old path".** That is the code writer's view, not the user's: to you it is the mode that **sends everything**, the safest, and exactly what runs when you press **Off**. Calling it "old" both sounds like an apology and makes people think the machine is running something broken.
- The four modes now have names that state the benefit: **Full** (sends everything, safest), **Optimised** (sends only the relevant part), **Instant** (simple questions answered directly, no tool loop), **Lookup** / **Deep lookup** / **Execute** / **Workflow**.
- The names match in both places: the small line under each answer and the table on the Token saving page, so seeing one place lets you connect to the other.
- The sections on the page were rewritten with the new vocabulary: "Why it cannot optimise", "Which mode each chat uses", "Packet when Optimised".

## [0.13.0] - 2026-08-03
The Token saving page rewritten around the only question the user cares about: turn this on and how much is saved. And each answer says which path it took.
### Added
- **Each level states how many percent it saves.** The three buttons now show the figure directly: **Off** (baseline), **Optimised** (about 89% down), **Ultra saving** (about 96%), with tokens per turn. The figure is measured on your own rule set and memory rather than an advertised constant, so each brain gets its own number. It states clearly that this is an estimate.
- **A REAL measurement table.** Once there are turns on both paths within 24 hours, the page shows real numbers: what the old path cost, what the saving path cost, how many percent down. If there is not enough data it says not enough, instead of showing a meaningless 0%.
- **Each answer has a small line saying which path it took** and how many tokens went in. Before, a turn silently dropping back to the old path was completely invisible, and only showed when the provider reported exceeding the quota. Clicking that line goes straight to the Token saving page.
- **The Usage panel also says which level it is at and how much is saved.** A consumption figure only means something when you know what it should have been.
### Improved
- **Renamed the three levels to Off / Optimised / Ultra saving**, and moved them to the **top of the page**. Before, the three buttons were buried in the middle, under four chart blocks, so opening the page showed the numbers before the button you need to press.
- **The "which path each chat takes" table no longer makes users figure out the word `legacy`.** Path names are fully translated to Vietnamese, and the saving path now has its own name instead of being miscounted as the old path. This is also what makes the real measurement table above work.
- The self-learned quota table says the exact kind: tokens per minute, tokens per day, requests per minute, requests per day. Before, all were labeled tokens.

## [0.12.6] - 2026-08-03
Turning on token saving no longer turns answers into a JSON block. The badge names the brain correctly. Fixed the chat panel breaking on phones.
### Fixed
- **After turning on the Saving level, the answer showed as a JSON block.** Where a greeting should be, the chat panel printed `{"channel":"dashboard","language":"match_user",...,"content":"Hello"}`. Cause: the reply instructions were put into the prompt as a JSON object. Putting an object right before where the model must answer makes a weak model read it as "emit this object", and it really does. Now that part is written in words, explicitly forbidding wrapping the answer in JSON. This is the worst bug in the group: it made the token saving feature itself produce junk, broken the moment it was turned on.
- **The badge in the right corner said "CLI" for every API-key brain.** Choose Groq and the badge says "CLI" while the model bar right beside it says "Groq". The identification spot had only two branches: OpenRouter, or CLI. Now it knows all seven brains and reads the main model in the same order the server uses.
- **The chat panel broke on phones.** The title "Chat with Jarvis 007" wrapped to four lines, the word "Minimise" wrapped to two lines, pushing the chat panel way down. A regression from the Minimise button added in 0.12.4. Now on a narrow screen the button is icon-only, and the title and brain label trim themselves to one line.
- The Usage panel stopped showing the provider code ceiling for Groq and Gemini.

## [0.12.5] - 2026-08-03
Groq tightens four dimensions at once, and Jarvis 007 used to lump all four into "request too big". Now it names the right kind and advises the right action.
### Fixed
- **"groq reports request too big... this turn needs about 0 tokens".** Three things wrong in a single sentence. The Groq plan tightens **four** things in parallel: tokens per minute, **number of requests** per minute, tokens per **day**, number of requests per day. All four start with "Rate limit reached", and Jarvis 007 took exactly that phrase as the "over size" sign, so the other three dimensions got mislabeled. The 0 is because nothing could be read from the error line, and the 12,000 came from a **lookup table built into the code** and not from Groq. Joining those two into a sentence that sounds like it understood is both wrong and hides the evidence.
- **Now each quota type gets the right advice.** An oversized turn is shortened and retried. A full minute window waits exactly the seconds the provider says. **A daily quota exhausted says plainly that shortening does not help**, you must wait until the next day or switch brain or upgrade the plan, instead of letting you sit cutting the question shorter and still failing.
- **When the error is not understood, show the provider's original words, do not invent a tidy sentence.** Before, the real error line was swallowed so nobody could trace the cause.
- **A quota that counts REQUESTS is no longer used as a token budget.** "30 requests per minute" multiplied by a safety factor becomes "shrink context to 22 tokens", enough to break a chat turn.
- **Stop retrying when retrying is certainly useless.** With the daily quota exhausted, resending only costs one more turn to hit exactly the same error again.
### Improved
- **The router uses the quota it has learned by itself, no need to wait for anyone to declare it.** The old order was backwards: the safety mechanism demanded the quota be declared before running, so exactly when tightened was exactly when the context saving part was inactive. Now after **one** rejection by the provider, Jarvis 007 immediately has the real figure of that account and uses it as the budget. An operator's hand declaration still takes priority over everything.
- Context trimming, when the quota cannot be read this time, takes the figure learned last time instead of leaving it empty and then only being able to cut the conversation history.

## [0.12.4] - 2026-08-03
The token saving part now works for the **Claude plan and ChatGPT plan**, not only API-key accounts. Removed the expanded chat panel. Fixed the delete/rename conversation buttons.
### Added
- **Token saving for subscription plans.** Before, the entire context selection part ran only on API-key brains: Claude Code and ChatGPT/Codex were excluded from the start because the system demanded a known "token quota per minute", which subscription plans do not publish. Now those two brains use a **context ceiling** in place of the commercial quota, and get two areas: **selective memory** and **skills loaded on demand**.
- **The Token saving page has a "Brain in use" block.** It states plainly what kind the current brain is, how many areas it gets, which areas do not apply to it and why. Before, finding out meant reading the config file on the server.
- **When a subscription plan runs out of turns it says so in Vietnamese.** Claude Code and Codex print the English sentence verbatim, sometimes in machine-readable form. Now Jarvis 007 translates it into a clear sentence: which plan ran out, how long until it resets, which brain is ready to run in the meantime. It does not switch brains for you - that would burn the quota of another account, sometimes costing real money.
### Fixed
- **Pressing the "Saving" level still changed nothing.** The quota was declared by area name, while the three context selection areas read the quota in one shared place. Result: the switch on, the figure up, yet every turn still took the old path. Now it is declared into exactly where they read.
- **Hovering over a conversation made the delete and rename buttons unclickable.** The buttons did show, and clicking them opened that conversation. The real click area was only a thin border around the icon. Now clicking anywhere in the button works.
- Turning on token saving for Claude Code no longer accidentally turns off its native skill part.
### Improved
- **Removed the expanded chat panel entirely.** The expand button now **switches straight to the Chat page**, and that page has a **Minimise** button to go back to the Jarvis 007 screen. Before, there were two chat panels looking nearly alike but behaving differently, and both fought over one set of components so bugs often came up when switching tabs.

## [0.12.3] - 2026-08-02
When an update fails, say clearly why and what to do, instead of telling people to read a log file.
### Fixed
- **"Server is up but the version did not change (pull not applied?). See update.log."** This sentence knew something was abnormal without saying what, then sent the user to read a log file that Windows/Docker builds can barely reach. Now Jarvis 007 diagnoses itself and says plainly: which branch it is on, which branch it tracks, and **the exact command to fix it**. The most common cause is the machine tracking a different branch from the one with the new version, so `git` says "up to date" completely legitimately. It also recognizes the case of a prebuilt package (Docker) that cannot update from source, and the case of standing on no branch.
- The error message now states both the running version and the target version, so you see at once whether it went up.

## [0.12.2] - 2026-08-02
When a weak model makes up wrong tool-call syntax, Jarvis 007 repairs it by itself, instead of showing a broken JSON block and going silent.
### Fixed
- **Llama sometimes answered and sometimes showed a JSON error then "(no content returned)".** Cause: a weak model occasionally invents its own tool-call syntax instead of the right format, and the provider rejects it. Now Jarvis 007 repairs in two steps: retry once (a model generating text has randomness so the next time usually hits), and if still broken, **drop the tools and answer in words** with a one-line notice. An answer without tools is far better than no answer at all.
- Applies only to exactly this error, recognized by its own error code and not by status code, because the same code is used for a dozen other errors where retrying only costs one more turn.
## [0.12.1] - 2026-08-02
Groq/Llama: now also handles the case where the per-minute limit is already full. Three UI fixes.
### Fixed
- **Groq reported a second kind of rate-limit error that Jarvis 007 did not recognize.** The provider has two different messages: one is "this request is too large", the other is "this minute's limit is used up". Jarvis 007 only understood the first, so after it had successfully trimmed the request it hit the second message and returned a raw error. It now reads both, and for the second case it **waits exactly the number of seconds the provider asks for, then resends automatically** instead of cutting context for nothing. The tool-call loop had no retry mechanism at all, so this is also the first time it knows how to wait.
- **After enlarging the chat panel and switching tabs, the enlarged panel stayed on top of the new page.** Switching tabs now shrinks it back automatically.
- **On phones, tapping a note opened the editor and you could not leave it** because the button bar ran off the narrow screen. As requested, **tapping a note to edit it is now turned off completely on phones** (the nodes are too small, so it was almost always a mistaken tap), with a one-line reminder to open it on a computer. The editor's button bar can also wrap now so the Close button is always reachable if you get in another way.
- **Changing the model on the Models page did not update the model bar under the chat box or the status line on the conversation.** Those two places read the config at different times and nobody told the other. Every way of changing the model now refreshes both immediately.

## [0.12.0] - 2026-08-02
The Diagnostics page becomes **Token saving**: three buttons replace a ten-row table. Fixes Llama still exceeding the limit.
### Fixed
- **Llama/Groq still reported exceeding the limit even though 0.11.0 said it was handled.** The limit-learning part was put in the wrong place: it sat in the simple send functions, while every real chat turn goes through the tool-call loop (Jarvis 007 always has internal tools, so that loop is always used). The code ran correctly, tests were green, and it was never called. It is now in the right place, covering all five providers plus ChatGPT.
- **Clicking the "Set" button seemed to do nothing.** The number box already shows the value in use, so clicking without editing the number set the same old value again - an empty action with no message. Every action now shows a confirmation line saying exactly what just changed.
### Improved
- **Page renamed to "Token saving".** The old name "Diagnostics" did not say what the page is for.
- **Three buttons replace a ten-row table.** Pick **Off**, **Saving** or **Maximum**, each with one line explaining the trade-off. Jarvis 007 handles the rest underneath: it turns on exactly the parts needed, flips the master switch, and declares the limit for the provider in use. You no longer need to understand "canary", "allocation" or "basis point" to use it.
- A level only includes the parts that **really run**. A part that needs an allowlist that has not been declared is left out, because switching it on would only give the feeling of being on while every turn still takes the old path.
- The detail table and the master switch moved into a collapsed **Advanced** section for anyone who wants to experiment.
- Lowering the level turns off the leftover parts completely instead of stacking. A hand-edited setup that differs from the presets is shown as "custom" instead of being silently accepted.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-08-02
Jarvis 007 learns every provider's limit from the error message itself, trims the request and keeps going. The Diagnostics page is rewritten in plain language.
### Fixed
- **The red banner on the status bar was wrong and in the wrong place.** It said "Brain claude lost login... Open a terminal, run claude and type /login" - outdated instructions, since connecting now happens on the **Models** page. The string was also longer than the status bar so it was cut off midway, and the cut part was exactly the part saying what to do. It is now one short sentence, **"No AI model connected - click to connect"**, and clicking goes straight to the Models page. The technical detail moved into the tooltip, still there when you need to look something up.
- The same notice sent over Telegram was also rewritten from the user's point of view, no longer opening with the brain's name.

### Added
- **When the limit is exceeded it fixes itself, you do not have to read a technical error.** When a provider refuses because the request is too large, its error message states the account's real limit. Jarvis 007 reads that number, drops the conversation history to make the request lighter, then resends. You only see a line "trimming context and retrying" and then the answer.
- **Applies to EVERY provider, not just one.** It recognizes the error messages of Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and OpenRouter, even when they write the two numbers in reverse order. Plugging in a new provider needs nothing declared up front: Jarvis 007 learns from the first refusal and remembers it so it does not run into it again.
- **Retries only once.** If it is still over after trimming, it tells you with the exact numbers, because at that point the problem is no longer the context size.
- Your current question is **never** cut when trimming. The order of sacrifice is old history first, then the tail of the system instructions.
### Improved
- **The Diagnostics page is rewritten to be easier to understand.** It adds an explanation of what the page is for, how the old path differs from the new one, and what "turn on part by part" means. Every technical label is now plain: "Tokens sent" instead of "Tokens in (real)", "Why it still takes the old path" instead of "Reason it did not enter the new path". Each section has one line saying what to look at that number for.
- Added a **Limits Jarvis 007 learned** section, showing which providers have stated the real limit of your account.
- A size-exceeded error is no longer retried unchanged like a temporary overload error. Retrying without trimming only costs one more turn to get the same error.

## [0.10.1] - 2026-08-02
Fixes a bug that made it impossible to turn on the new run path, found right away in real use with Groq.
### Fixed
- **Turning on the new path still changed nothing.** There is a master switch (`mode`) that 0.10.0 did not expose: every path only runs when it is `canary` or `on`, and the default is `shadow`. Setting any ratio was meaningless, yet the screen reported success. The Diagnostics page now has a mode selector, and turning on a ratio while the mode is wrong is blocked with a clear reason instead of a false success.
- **Three paths of the context layer were blocked by mistake.** They share a limit declared elsewhere so they have no limit entry of their own, but the checker demanded one and refused with the wrong reason "limit not declared". A wrong reason is even harder to trace than no block.
### Notes
- After updating, to make Jarvis 007 run light on a model with a tight limit (Groq), go to **Diagnostics**: change the mode to `canary`, click **Declare** the limit for groq, then set the ratio to 10000 for `memory_canary`, `lazy_skill_canary`, `conversation_state_canary`. Measured on a real setup: the fixed part sent drops from about 15,400 to about 4,100 tokens.

## [0.10.0] - 2026-08-02
Foundation of the Adaptive Context Runtime: the context sent to the model shrinks with the work to be done, and does not swell with the number of things plugged in.
### Improved
- **Tools are no longer stuffed into every turn.** Before, every tool schema went straight into the request, for every model, every question. The "load on demand" layer already existed but never ran: it only hid external connector tools, while internal tools and plugins were always shown, and the trigger threshold counted the NUMBER of tools when what costs money is the SIZE. The threshold now considers both, and only keeps a few core tools. Measured on a setup with 26 tools + 30 skills: schemas per turn dropped **83%** (11,994 to 2,001 characters). Takes effect immediately, nothing to turn on.
- **Jarvis 007 knows in advance when it will exceed the limit, and says so.** Before, with a model limited per minute (like the free Groq plan at 12,000 TPM), Jarvis 007 still sent the request and let the provider return a confusing error. Worse: when it detected a request that was too big, it fell back to the path that sends MORE tokens. It now stops first, states how many tokens are needed against the limit, and suggests a provider you already have that is not restricted.
- **Background loops, Kanban work and reminders no longer silently eat the limit.** The per-minute token limit belongs to the ACCOUNT, but before only a few paths were counted, while normal chat, loops, background work and Telegram burned it invisibly. All of it now goes into one shared ledger, so when you are blocked the visible number matches reality.
- **Diagnostics page** in the System section: real tokens in and out, estimate error, the path each turn took, reasons for being blocked, and the last 60 seconds of tokens across all sources. Numbers only, no conversation content or tool parameters.
### Security
- **Blocks unknown web pages from triggering Jarvis 007 commands.** `/workflows/run` and `/workflows/resume` are GET-style addresses so the old anti-forgery layer did not cover them, while the login cookie still travels along when the browser is redirected. Any page only had to push the browser to that address and the workflow ran on your machine, even with a password set. They now run only when the command comes from the dashboard itself; command-line tools are not affected.
- **Editing nested config no longer wipes the neighboring part.** Before, editing one sub-item replaced the whole group, losing sibling settings without any notice.
### Added
- **Turn on/off and declare limits right on the Diagnostics page.** No more hand-editing the config file. Turning on a path without a declared limit is blocked with a reason, instead of turning it on and then waiting for something that never runs. Turning off always takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
### Notes
- **This version does not yet change how Jarvis 007 answers.** The whole new path is still in observation mode, every ratio is 0. What you see right away is lighter tools, the Diagnostics page, and two security patches. Turning on the new path comes later, once there is baseline data to compare against.

## [0.9.293] - 2026-08-01
The Models page puts connected providers at the top.
### Improved
- **Connected providers go to the top, unconnected ones to the bottom.** The original order is kept inside each group so nothing looks shuffled. It applies to both the card list and the provider picker in the **Change model** box (both the main model and the background model), so the two places do not tell different stories.
- Claude Code in particular has to ask `/claude/status` to know if it is really signed in: it has no API key field so the server always reports `configured=true`, and trusting that would leave a machine not signed in to Claude with it sitting at the very top.

## [0.9.292] - 2026-08-01
Adds Groq as the seventh model provider.
### Added
- **Plugged in Groq (API).** The Models page has a new **Groq (API)** card: paste an API key and it works, and the model list loads LIVE from Groq (whisper/guard/embedding models are filtered out because they cannot chat). Groq goes through the OpenAI-compatible path so it shares the tool-call loop with OpenAI/Gemini - meaning **the full Jarvis 007 MCP + brain file tools + skills** from the start, not plain chat.
- Also selectable as the **background model**. Groq reasons very fast and cheap, so it suits loops, Kanban work and reminders - the things that burn the limit most quietly.
- `reasoning_effort` is only sent for reasoning model families (qwen3, deepseek-r1, gpt-oss, kimi thinking). Sending it to llama/mixtral/gemma makes Groq return 400, so it has to be filtered by model name exactly like the OpenAI o-series and Gemini 2.5 already are.
- The Groq key is in the list **encrypted before writing** to `settings.json`, like the other provider keys.
- Added `test_groq_provider.py` to lock down the wiring. Adding a provider touches 7 separate places; missing one is a silent bug (the card shows up but chat falls to the default branch, or the key is written in plaintext, or choosing it as the background model blows up at background run time). The test runs against a fake Groq server so it needs no network and costs no quota.

## [0.9.291] - 2026-08-01
Removes `html-to-webcake` from the system's default skill set.
### Improved
- **Removed the system skill `html-to-webcake`.** It shipped with `tools/` and `examples/`, but the system skill install mechanism only copies `SKILL.md`, so the subtree never reached any brain - this skill was broken in every brain from the start (noted in 0.9.71 but never patched). The repo owner decided to drop it entirely instead of patching.
- A brain that already installed it **keeps its copy intact**, the only difference is that it now counts as your own skill: it can be deleted directly on the Skills page (system skills cannot be deleted). The sync loop does not touch an entry that has left the system source, so nothing disappears by itself.
- The warning section in the `javis-builder` skill dropped the dead example and was rewritten as a general rule: do not write a SYSTEM skill that needs a subtree.

## [0.9.290] - 2026-07-31
Typing `/` can call a skill in the middle of a sentence, not only at the start of the input box.
### Improved
- **The `/` command works in the middle of the chat box.** Before, both the menu and the routing were anchored to the start of the string, so writing "test using a skill in the middle of the chat box /" showed no menu and sending it did nothing. Now you can write the request first and type `/` wherever you need it: the text on both sides of the command is merged into the request for the skill. Choosing from the menu inserts `/slug ` exactly at the cursor, and the text already typed stays.
- **Three guards against false matches.** The `/` must be at the start of a sentence or right after whitespace (so `https://vd.com/notes` and `3/4 of a cake` are unaffected); mid-sentence, the command name must be a skill that REALLY exists in the selected brain (so `/home/user/notes` goes straight into chat as plain text); and the three session commands `/new` `/reset` `/stop` only run when at the start of the input box - writing half a sentence and then hitting `/reset` by accident would lose all context, which does more harm than good, and the menu does not suggest them mid-sentence either.
- The skill list is preloaded at startup instead of waiting for the first menu open, so someone who hand-types `/viet-email` mid-sentence without ever opening the menu is still recognized.
- 20 new checks in `test_chat_slash.js` cover both the routing and how the menu catches the token by cursor.
- Fixed a token-usage test that went red depending on the hour: it wrote a few lines by the REAL DATE and then compared against a fixed baseline, so right when the clock rolled into a new month those junk lines fell into the comparison window and set off a false alarm. The real-date lines are now cleaned out before the alert check.

## [0.9.289] - 2026-07-31
Handing off background work in web chat was completely silent - now the result comes back to that same chat box on its own.
### Fixed
- **Running agents/background work on the dashboard: no status, no reply.** The reporting path for Kanban work, loops and reminders only knew how to send to Telegram. On a machine without Telegram, `_notify_owner` returned failure and `TaskRunner._report` swallowed it - the result vanished into thin air and the person on the web had no channel to receive it. Web chat is now a real receiving channel: work handed off in chat carries the session id (`chat_id: "web:<session id>"`, borrowing an existing field so no database schema change), and when the work finishes the result appears directly as a Jarvis 007 message in that exact conversation. The server writes to the session history FIRST and then pushes over WebSocket, so closing the tab or pressing F5 still keeps it; if you are viewing another conversation, the original session floats up in History.
- **Jarvis 007 promised "I will wait for the background agents to finish and then summarize for you" - a promise that cannot be kept.** A reply turn ends the moment it finishes speaking, and nothing wakes it up. The system prompt and the dashboard channel block now forbid that kind of promise outright, and allow only two alternatives: hand off one more job dedicated to summarizing (using `deps` pointing at the earlier jobs), or tell the user to message again once the results are in.
- Jarvis 007 now knows the current chat session id (the "KÊNH HỘI THOẠI HIỆN TẠI" block of the web version) so it can attach the recipient itself. The Telegram branch keeps the old path, the two channels are independent.
- Added `test_bao_viec_ve_chat_web.py` to guard both the reporting path (WebSocket push + session save + no made-up success when the channel is missing) and the wording in the prompt. Reverting the old bug turns exactly 6 lines red.

## [0.9.288] - 2026-07-31
The domain input box shrank to a sliver, nowhere to type.
### Fixed
- **The domain input box in Settings was squeezed to a sliver.** style.css gave EVERY button in Quick settings `width:100%` - right when buttons stack vertically, but the domain row is a horizontal "input + button" row. In a flex row, an item carrying `width:100%` has a desired size equal to the whole row, while the input declares `flex:1` (desired size 0), so when it has to shrink all the shrinking lands on the button and the input stays at 0 - only the border shows. Now the input grows from its real size and the button is only as wide as its text. Measured on Chromium: the input went from a few pixels to 285px on desktop, and stretches the full 476px when the narrow screen stacks vertically.
- **The SSL button row hit exactly the same bug** (the "Check again" button swallowed the row, "Enable SSL" shrank) because flex was declared for only one of the two buttons. This row only appears after a domain is set so nobody had reported it yet. Both are now declared.
- The domain input now has its own style (background, border, rounded corners, orange border on focus) instead of being left as the bare browser default - this popover block has no shared input style.
- Added `test_hang_nhap_ngang.py` to guard the rule: a horizontal row in Quick settings must have the input grow from basis auto, the button must be `width:auto`, and the exception in style.css must have all 3 class levels to win regardless of load order (the domain block CSS is injected by branding.js at runtime).

## [0.9.287] - 2026-07-31
Whatever file you open in the editor, Jarvis 007 works on that file - no pasting the path or describing it again.
### Added
- **The open file is automatically pinned to the chat box.** Open a text file in the editor and Jarvis 007 immediately pins it as an orange card above the input bar ("open - Jarvis 007 is working on this file"). From then on, saying "clean up the overdue part" or "write an extra conclusion section" without naming the file still makes Jarvis 007 write straight into that file. Open another file and the card changes with it, they do not stack.
- The pinned card differs from an attachment in that it **does not disappear after sending**: an attachment is one-turn data, while the open file is input to the whole conversation. The pin survives F5 (same reason as conversation restore in 0.9.268), is dropped automatically when you change brain or delete the file itself, and clicking the close button on the card removes it by hand. Closing the editor window does NOT remove the pin - closing it to go back to chat about that same file is the most common flow.
- `/files/read` returns an extra key `abs` (the real path of the file). It is needed because the relative path in the UI is computed against the browsing ceiling, while the engine needs a system path - the two differ when the browsing ceiling is above the brain root, and a client assembling it itself would assemble it wrong.
- The system prompt learned to read the `[FILE ĐANG MỞ ...]` ("OPEN FILE") block: read the file before answering, and by default write into that very file when the user does not name a file.

## [0.9.286] - 2026-07-31
The Models page is tidier, and the thinking depth scale gains two levels.
### Added
- **The thinking depth scale gains two levels: Very high and Max.** Before there were only Off / Low / Medium / High, while Claude Code goes up to Ultra. All six levels are now on both the Models page and the picker bar in the chat box.
### Improved
- **The Models page has less wall of text.** The two long descriptions in the Background model and Thinking sections are cut to one line each; the technical detail moves down into a small, dim, one-idea note. The "provider not connected" warning is split onto its own line instead of being stuffed into the model name line.
- **The depth picker changes from loose chips to one connected segmented bar.** Six loose levels made the button row drift around; merged into one bar, it is clearly one scale from light to heavy. Each level has a very short sub-line (fastest, balanced, most tokens). On narrow screens it keeps the label and drops the sub-line so the row does not break.
- The settings card stops bobbing on hover - it is a static settings panel, not a clickable card.
### Fixed
- **The save path and the read path for the thinking level had two separate valid lists.** Adding the new levels to only one side meant the UI let you choose them but the server silently dropped them to "Off" - this exact bug was measured in the browser while building it. Both now consult the shared `engine.REASONING_LEVELS`.
- **The new levels were not sent straight to the API.** Providers only accept `low|medium|high`; sending `ultra` gets a 400 and breaks the whole chat turn. Added a gate that translates the Jarvis 007 level into a safe API value, and all 9 places that put effort into the payload go through it. The top two levels really differ where Jarvis 007 can control things itself: the think keyword for Claude Code and the token budget for older Anthropic models (20k vs 32k).
- The note under the picker states plainly that many providers only accept 3 levels so the top two may be the same there - better to say so up front than let users think they picked deeper.
- Added `tests/python/test_do_sau_suy_nghi.py`: 33 checks, 5 of them canaries, with reverse verification.

## [0.9.285] - 2026-07-31
Clicking an image in chat now shows it enlarged instead of auto-downloading the file.
### Added
- **Image lightbox.** Clicking any image in chat opens an enlarged view: the image fits the screen on a dark background, with the file name and three buttons Download / Open in new tab / Close. Click the image to toggle between fit-to-screen and real size (1:1) and drag to see detail. Esc or clicking the dark background closes it.
### Fixed
- **Clicking a just-generated image downloaded the file to the machine instead of opening it to view.** Images in the brain were wrapped in `<a download href=…&dl=1>` so one click dropped the file on the machine; to look at it clearly you had to go open the downloaded file, which was very roundabout. Ironically the CSS `.chat-img` had long set `cursor: zoom-in`, so the cursor promised enlarging while the behavior was downloading. Viewing is now the default, and downloading lives in the lightbox.
- Applies to **every image in chat**: markdown images, `![[...]]` images, and images from external URLs all behave the same.
### Improved
- **Ctrl/Cmd/Shift/middle-click still opens the original image in a new tab** like any other link - the lightbox only intercepts a plain click. The `<a>` tag still points straight at the image so this behavior is the browser's, not a simulation.
- The Download button goes through the server's `dl=1` path, so the file name is kept even with Vietnamese names.
- While composing a note, clicking an image is still for editing, no lightbox pops up.
- **Non-image** files (html, pdf, docx…) keep the old download behavior.
- Measured in the REAL app with Chromium, 16 checks. Added `tests/js/test_lightbox_anh.js` (28 checks) for CI, with reverse verification. An old assertion in `test_chat_render.js` that locked in exactly the download behavior was updated accordingly, with a note that this is an intentional change.

## [0.9.284] - 2026-07-31
Conversations with attached files stop sharing the same name and are named by their real content.
### Fixed
- **Every conversation with an attached file carried exactly one name, "[File đính kèm để ĐỌC (đườn…"**, so the History list could not tell them apart. Cause: the name = the **first** 48 characters of the raw message, and when a file is attached the dashboard inserts a long instruction block **before** the question. That block is now stripped first, and the name comes from what the user actually typed.
- Attaching a file without typing any text now names it by the **file name** (several files give "a.png +2 file"), instead of the pre-filled sentence that is equally meaningless in every conversation.
- Names are cut at a **word boundary** instead of mid-word, so you no longer get things like "…(đườn…".
- A multi-line message uses its **first line** as the name, instead of sticking the whole post into one long string.
### Improved
- Stripping the attachment block is anchored exactly to the phrase "File đính kèm" instead of stripping every opening `[..]` block: users have the right to open a sentence with square brackets ("[urgent] please look at…"), and stripping blindly would lose the most important part. A canary guards this.
- File names are taken from the exact `- <path>` list format the dashboard generates, so the two config folders `Sources=`/`Attachments=` do not leak into the name (before the fix it gave "My +4 file", identical in every conversation).
- It does not cut at a mid-sentence period: Vietnamese uses many periods, and cutting there would turn "Chào em. Hôm nay doanh thu bao nhiêu?" into just "Chào em".
- Added `tests/python/test_dat_ten_hoi_thoai.py`: 32 checks, with reverse verification.

## [0.9.283] - 2026-07-31
Can plug in n8n through the official MCP, and the catalog learns self-hosted style connectors.
### Added
- **n8n connector.** Plug it in on the Connections page with your n8n address + MCP Access Token; works with both n8n cloud and self-hosted n8n. Jarvis 007 finds and reads workflows, views run history, creates and edits workflows, and runs workflows if granted permission.
- **The catalog supports dynamic URLs (`url_template`).** n8n is the first connector whose server address sits on the **user's own** domain, not a shared address hard-coded in the app. The address here is part of the login information, so the catalog lets you declare a template and then assembles it from the box the user types in. Without it, n8n would have to fall to the "custom" connector, losing the guide, the read/write permission classification and the risk warning.
- Any way of typing the address is accepted: missing `https://`, extra trailing slash, or pasting the whole open URL with path and parameters are all trimmed down to the right domain. `http` and the port are kept for self-hosted instances on an internal network. Input that is not an address returns empty so it reports missing, instead of producing a truncated URL and leaving the user guessing why Test is red.
- The URL is rebuilt **on every resolve**, not only when added, so editing the n8n address makes the connection follow immediately, the same way headers already worked.
### Safety
- **`execute_workflow` is put in the DANGEROUS group**, not the ordinary write group. The name sounds mild but it really runs a workflow: sending mail, posting, calling billing APIs, pushing data outside. Jarvis 007 cannot see what is inside the workflow and once run it cannot be undone. Result: the **Draft write** level can create and edit workflows but **cannot run them**; you must go up to Full access to run. A background loop in suggest mode is still forced to read-only even when the connection is set to Full access.
- Default level is **Read only**. The risk warning states plainly that this token sees every workflow and the list of credentials that your n8n account sees.
### Improved
- Added `tests/python/test_n8n_connector.py`: 59 checks covering address normalization, classification of 12 tools, the permission gate at all three levels, and the real path of adding a connection then resolving. With reverse verification.

## [0.9.282] - 2026-07-31
The "/" typing menu fixes two blocking bugs in real use, and drops two redundant entries.
### Fixed
- **Pressing the down arrow made the selection highlight jump back to the top instead of going down.** The key-up handler kept running and reset the selection position to 0, so right after keydown picked item 2, keyup pulled it back to item 1. Navigation keys are now blocked outright at key-up, and filtering only reruns when the typed text **really changes**.
- **Choosing "Heading 1/2/3" on an empty line did nothing.** After deleting the `/tu-dang-go` fragment, the text node was empty so the browser cleaned it up, which killed the caret position and dropped it back to the wrapping tag. At that point `formatBlock` still returned `true` but did nothing because it did not know which block it was in. The caret is now re-anchored to a live node, preferring the text node itself, otherwise the parent block. This bug has existed since 0.9.280; the old test did not catch it because it only tried the checkbox path, and that command uses `insertUnorderedList` which is forgiving about the caret.
- With the menu open, if the caret jumped elsewhere and you typed `/`, the menu closed but **did not reopen** at the new spot, so you had to type `/` twice. After closing it now still evaluates the key just typed.
### Improved
- **Removed "Bold" and "Italic" from the `/` menu** as requested. Those two commands style **selected** text, but after typing `/` nothing is selected. They keep their toolbar buttons and `Ctrl+B` / `Ctrl+I`. The menu has 10 entries left.
- The selected entry is scrolled into view when pressing the arrows, because the menu is longer than its frame and before, past halfway down you could no longer see where you were.
- Measured with real Chromium: 11 navigation checks (down, up, wrap-around, scroll-follow, Enter inserts the highlighted entry, typing new text resets the highlight) and 7 checks choosing each command by **really typing** into the compose box, both on an empty line and on a line with text.
- CI test adds 5 checks locking in the two bugs above, with reverse verification.

## [0.9.281] - 2026-07-31
Scrolling up to reread in a long chat box now has a button that jumps straight to the bottom.
### Added
- **The jump-to-bottom button appears as soon as you leave the bottom of the chat box.** The `#newMsgBtn` button already existed but was only turned on inside `scrollBottom()`, and that function only runs when a **new message** arrives. That meant scrolling up to reread a long conversation and wanting to come back down had no button, and you had to drag the whole box by hand. Now the scroll handler itself turns the button on, so leaving the bottom shows it, independent of new messages.
- The button has **two forms for two situations**: when you are only scrolled up rereading it is a small round button with just an arrow, enough to jump down; when a new message arrives while you are reading it expands into an accent-colored "New message" pill to catch the eye. Scrolling back to the bottom releases it back to the compact form, otherwise the next time you only scroll up to reread you would still see "New message" falsely.
### Improved
- The button's `aria-label` changes with the form, so screen readers say exactly what it does.
- The shadow uses `--shadow-2` instead of `--shadow-1`, and the border/icon contrast is raised: the floating button sits **over the text** of messages, so if it is too faint it sinks into the text background.
- Measured in the REAL app with Chromium (local server), 15 checks: scroll up shows the button, clicking jumps to the exact bottom, a new message expands the button, returning to the bottom hides it and releases the new-message form, and the button still follows when the chat box is enlarged. Checked in both light and dark tones.
- Added `tests/js/test_nut_xuong_day.js`: 25 checks for CI, with reverse verification (removing `flex: none` or removing the call in the scroll handler turns the test red in exactly the right place).
### Fixed
- `flex: none` for the button: `.transcript` is a vertical flex so the button as a flex item **shrank along the height**, squeezing the 32px round button to 15px into an oval. This bug only showed when measured in a real browser.

## [0.9.280] - 2026-07-31
The .md editor gets a checkbox button, shortcuts for every format, and the "/" typing menu.
### Added
- **Checkbox button on the toolbar**, right after the numbered list because it belongs to the list family. Clicking in Edit mode produces a real tick box; in Source mode it inserts `- [ ] `. Before, the toolbar had bullets and numbered lists but no checkbox at all, so the only way to make one was typing `- [ ]` and pressing space, and nothing on screen hinted at that.
- **Shortcuts for every format**, working in both Edit and Source modes: `Ctrl+B` bold, `Ctrl+I` italic, `Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3` headings, `Ctrl+Shift+8` bullet, `Ctrl+Shift+7` numbered list, `Ctrl+Shift+9` checkbox, `Ctrl+Shift+.` quote (remembered by markdown's `>` sign), `Ctrl+E` code, `Ctrl+K` link. On Mac read `Ctrl` as `Cmd`.
- **The "/" typing menu**: in Edit mode, typing `/` at the start of a word opens a picker of all 12 functions with their shortcuts shown beside them. Keep typing to filter (accent-free works too, `/tieu` matches "Tiêu đề"), arrows to choose, Enter or mouse click to insert, Esc to close. A `/` in the middle of a word like `12/2026`, `và/hoặc` or the path `a/b` does not trigger the menu.
### Improved
- The command table is gathered in one single place (`dashboard/editor-cmds.js`) feeding all three outputs: buttons, shortcuts, "/" menu. Before, the button table was mixed into the toolbar-building function; left that way, the three places would drift apart the next time a command was added.
- NUMBER keys are matched by `e.code` not `e.key`: holding Alt on Mac turns `e.key` into `¡`, and using `e.key` kills the heading shortcut on Mac.
- It does not hijack browser and app keys: bare `Ctrl+1..9` (tab switch), `Ctrl+S` (save note), `Ctrl+Shift+I` (devtools), `Ctrl+Shift+B` (bookmarks bar) are all left alone.
- Measured with real Chromium: 24 checks for buttons, shortcuts in both modes, and the "/" menu; plus a closed round trip Edit → markdown → redraw with real Turndown and the GFM plugin, confirming the checkbox is saved as `- [ ]` / `- [x]` and reopens as a tick box.
- Added `tests/js/test_editor_cmds.js`: 57 checks for CI (which only has `node`), including 8 canaries blocking hijacking of browser keys and blocking the "/" menu from popping up mid-word.
### Fixed
- `dashboard/console.js` had **a raw NUL byte** in the cache key string, so every tool treated the whole file as binary and `grep` could not read it. Replaced with the `\0` escape, the runtime string is identical.

## [0.9.279] - 2026-07-31
The expanded chat stops being a popup: it takes exactly the content frame, flush with the layout.
### Improved
- **The enlarged chat panel is now part of the interface, not a floating dialog.** Before it had 16px rounded corners, a drop shadow, was centered on screen and only `96vw` wide so the graph behind still showed on both sides - it read as a layer laid over the app. It now follows the content area exactly: the top edge is the bottom of the top bar, the left edge is the rail edge, and the other two edges match the window. Rounded corners, drop shadow and frosted-glass background (the blur is what made it look like it was floating) are removed, and the background becomes a solid color following the tone in use.
- Coordinates are **measured from the real layout** instead of hard-coded numbers: `chat-zoom.js` reads the size of `.hud` and the bottom of `.hud-top` and injects them into four CSS variables. Measuring `.hud` instead of adding `var(--rail-w)` by hand is deliberate - when the page has no rail that variable is still 160px, and adding by hand would be off by a whole strip.
- The panel **follows when the layout changes**: it listens to both window `resize` and a `ResizeObserver` on `.hud`. Both are needed because collapsing/expanding the rail changes the width of `.hud` **without** firing `resize` - listening to `resize` alone leaves the panel stuck, with a gap exactly where the rail just shrank.
- Measured on the spot with Chromium in 6 situations (rail 160px, rail collapsed to 60px, page without rail, window resize, and resizing plus collapsing the rail **while** expanded): the panel edges match the layout exactly, error under 0.6px on all four sides.
- Added `tests/js/test_chat_zoom_khung.js`: 24 checks locking this contract for CI (which only has `node`, no browser) - no trace of popup left, coordinates come from the measured variables, and two canaries keep the `ResizeObserver` and the measuring order after `.chat-zoomed` is attached.

## [0.9.278] - 2026-07-30
Images in the chat box vanish when you go back and forth: not because Jarvis 007 deletes them, but because they are joined to the wrong brain and then replaced with a grey box.
### Fixed
- **Images and documents in chat disappear when reopening a conversation (reported by a real user).** The image path in a message is a RELATIVE path (`attachments/x.png`) that carries no brain information. On every redraw, the renderer joined it with the **brain selected on the toolbar** instead of the brain of the conversation itself. Opening an old conversation while standing in a different brain made the URL point to the wrong place, `/files/raw` returned 404, the `img` tag ran `onerror` and **was replaced with a grey box** - looking exactly as if Jarvis 007 had just sent the image and deleted it. The file was still intact in the vault. Each message now carries the brain of the conversation containing it: `mdToHtml` takes an extra brain parameter, the restore path from History uses `sess.brain` which the server **already stored** (the `brain` column of the `sessions` table) but used to throw away, and the restore path from localStorage uses the brain saved with the session. Messages saved before this version have no such field so they fall back to the old behavior, nothing gets worse.
