- **The grey box wrongly blamed "expired".** It said "Image expired" for EVERY load error, even when the image was intact and only the path was joined wrong, so users went looking in the wrong direction. It now says something neutral with the file name, noting the two possibilities: the file was really deleted, or the conversation belongs to a different brain than the one selected.
### Improved
- Added `tests/js/test_chat_anh_theo_brain.js`: 11 checks locking that all three path syntaxes in the vault (markdown image, `![[...]]` image, document link) follow the conversation's brain, that external URLs are untouched, and two leak canaries - the brain of the previous render must not stick to the next, even when the middle render throws an error.
### Not fixed
- Files **the user attached themselves** are still lost when reopening a conversation from History: that restore path hard-codes an empty attachment list because the session database has no place to store per-message attachments yet. It can be fixed but needs added storage structure, left for the repo owner to decide first.

## [0.9.277] - 2026-07-30
Long chats often got cut off by "Claude not responding 180s": silence while loading context is not a hang.
### Fixed
- **The longer the conversation, the more likely to hit "Claude not responding 180s - stopped to avoid hanging the server" (reported by a real user).** The anti-hang watchdog had two ceilings: 180 seconds for when the model is silent, and 3600 seconds for when waiting on a tool to run (because render/build being silent for an hour is normal). It missed exactly a third case: the silence **before the first word**. In a long conversation the first turn has to reload the entire context, the model thinks before emitting text, and sometimes even compacts the history itself - silence then is normal, but it was counted as a hang and cut off. A third ceiling `JAVIS_CLAUDE_FIRST_TIMEOUT` (default 600 seconds) is now split out and applies only to the wait for the first word; silence AFTER words have arrived still cuts at 180 seconds as before, so the anti-hang effect stays. Applies to BOTH the Claude and ChatGPT/Codex brains.
- **The error message now points only to exits ordinary people can take.** The old sentence only said to raise an environment variable, which most users do not know where to set. The new one says clearly that it is common when the conversation is already very long and **opening a new conversation usually fixes it right away**, with the environment variable still mentioned for anyone who wants to tune it. The three cut-off situations now have three different messages, so reading one tells you which problem you hit.
### Improved
- Added `test_watchdog_treo.py` locking the relationship of the three ceilings in both engines (wait for first word > mid-stream silence, tool wait is the longest), that the marker flag is really flipped, and the content of the three messages.
- `test_sdk_engine.py` replaced the old verification case with four cases that really run through a fake engine: a long-running tool stays alive, silence after words arrived cuts at IDLE, waiting for the first word longer than IDLE but under FIRST stays alive, and silence beyond FIRST still cuts. The last case matters most: relaxing the ceiling without guarding it trades this bug for an infinite-hang bug.

## [0.9.276] - 2026-07-30
Errors returned by a service in the middle of a tool call are now diagnosed on the spot by Jarvis 007, instead of leaving the model to guess and guess wrong.
### Fixed
- **The Google error diagnoser was only wired into the Test button, not into the real tool-call path.** That is where 99% of users meet the error, and there `_guard` returned Google's original English text. The consequence was real: Google returned `The caller does not have permission` on `list_calendars` and `create_event`, and Jarvis 007 read it and concluded that **the Jarvis 007 hub was blocking permission** and asked to go fix the permission layer. Completely wrong: the connection was at Full access so `allowed()` passed it from the first line, and when Jarvis 007 really blocks, it says so in Vietnamese with the word "bị chặn" (blocked), never as an English sentence. Now every tool error passing through the hub is inspected, and when it recognizes a familiar error family it **appends** a `[Jarvis 007 chẩn đoán]` ("diagnosis") line right below the original error text. Appended, not replaced, so the original text stays to trace clues.
- **Added recognition of 403 PERMISSION_DENIED without a scope word.** With Google's MCP server, this error family is almost always that the Developer Preview was not enrolled for the exact signed-in account, or the project has not enabled the separate MCP API. The message states three things the user needs to know: this is not Jarvis 007 blocking, enrollment is counted per Google ACCOUNT so as soon as the account changes you must enroll again, and email on a custom domain also needs the domain administrator's permission. A missing-scope error also carries the status `PERMISSION_DENIED`, so the new branch is placed AFTER the scope branch, with a test guarding exactly that order.
### Improved
- Split `chan_doan_loi()` out of `_friendly_tool_error()`: the recognizer returns empty when it does not recognize, and the caller decides what to say. The Test button keeps its old behavior (not recognized still gives the sentence "Key is wrong or lacks permission" with the original text), while the tool-call path stays silent when unsure instead of making up a diagnosis.
- `test_loi_ket_noi_google.py` adds 10 checks: the content of the new message, the order of the scope branch against the permission branch, the canary "an unfamiliar error must stay silent", and a check that `_guard` really appends the diagnosis while keeping the original text.

## [0.9.275] - 2026-07-30
Changed the Google account yet Jarvis 007 still ran on the old one: changing the login field now discards the old token.
### Fixed
- **Signed in again with a different email yet every tool still returned the old account (reported by a real user).** The user deleted the connection and signed in again with `hi@minhquy.vn`, but the Google tools still reported the account `blogminhquy@gmail.com`. The cause follows directly from 0.9.274: `workspace-mcp` caches tokens by email, and the "Your Google email" field only SELECTS which credential to use, it does not force a new sign-in. The old token sat intact on disk so it kept picking the old one. Now changing any login field (email, Client ID, Client Secret) on a source that keeps its own token makes Jarvis 007 discard the old account's token store, and the next tool call must sign in again. Re-entering exactly the same value, or only changing the reminder name, does NOT touch anything - nobody is made to sign in again for no reason.
### Improved
- `test_cred_dir_rieng.py` adds 7 checks, 4 of which REALLY run `update_connection` on a fake store and then inspect the token folder on disk: re-entering the same keeps, renaming keeps, changing email discards, changing Client ID discards. This kind of bug cannot be seen by reading the source, it only shows when run.

## [0.9.274] - 2026-07-30
This is the real broken spot behind "Calendar reports missing permission, deleting and reinstalling a dozen times changes nothing": the Google Workspace connection keeps its token outside Jarvis 007, so deleting the connection cleans up nothing.
### Fixed
- **Deleting and re-adding the Google Workspace (and Google Tasks) connection does NOT sign in again.** These two cards run `workspace-mcp`, a server that handles its OWN OAuth flow and caches the token to `~/.google_workspace_mcp/credentials` - out of Jarvis 007's reach. Deleting the connection in Jarvis 007 only deletes Jarvis 007's record; adding it again makes the child process read the very same old token file, without reopening the Google sign-in screen. A token issued with missing permission is missing forever, and reinstalling any number of times is useless. This is exactly the loop that version 0.9.271 did NOT touch: that version fixed the permission scope list of the separate **Google Calendar** and **Gmail** cards (the OAuth type where Jarvis 007 keeps the token itself), not the combined Workspace card. Anyone going through the Workspace card had to wait for exactly this version.
- **One token store per account.** Before, every connection of those two cards shared one default folder, so two Google accounts stepped on each other. Jarvis 007 now points each connection at its own `connector-cred/<connector>-<slug>` through the variable `WORKSPACE_MCP_CREDENTIALS_DIR`, and **deleting the connection deletes the token too** - from this version, "delete and reinstall" does what the user thought it did.
### Added
- **A "Sign in to Google again (clear old permissions)" button** in each account's menu, shown only for sources that keep their own token like this. It discards the token while KEEPING the connection, permissions, name and the blocked-tool list; on the next tool call the server opens the browser by itself to ask for permission again with the current set. Before, the "Reconnect" button only saved the Client ID/Secret so it never touched the token, and users pressed it endlessly while Google never showed the permission tick boxes again.
### Improved
- Added `test_cred_dir_rieng.py`: 27 checks locking the whole chain - the catalog declares the token store, two accounts give two different folders, delete really deletes, `delete_connection` cleans up too, the sign-in-again endpoint does not accidentally delete the connection, the button only appears on sources with their own store, and a canary that a source which does not declare it spawns no extra folder.
- **After updating, anyone using Google Workspace or Google Tasks must sign in to Google once more** (the token store moved). On the first tool call the browser opens by itself on the machine running Jarvis 007.

## [0.9.273] - 2026-07-30
Signed in to Google again but saw no permission tick boxes: tells the user this is normal and how to make Google ask again.
### Improved
- **"Re-auth but it does not show the permission checkboxes" (reported by a real user) is not a bug, it is how Google works.** The screen with a tick per permission only turns on for permissions NOT yet granted, and only when the app asks for two or more permissions; permissions already granted pass straight through. The version before 0.9.271 asked for just one scope `auth/calendar`, so there was never a tick box to show. After this version Jarvis 007 asks for 5 Calendar scopes, 4 of which were never granted so the tick screen will appear.
- **Always points out the exit when you still see no tick boxes**: remove Jarvis 007 from the permissions page of the Google account and then click Reconnect, at which point Google asks again from the start. This sentence is attached in all three places users will read: the last step in the Calendar and Gmail card guide (with a button opening the revoke page directly), the missing-permission error message at tool call time, and the status line in the health check loop.
- `test_scope_google.py` adds 6 checks guarding all three paths, so this instruction does not fall out in a later edit.

## [0.9.272] - 2026-07-30
The Google Workspace setup guide is rewritten so it can be followed, and a missing environment variable that kept sign-in from ever finishing is patched.
### Fixed
- **Missing `OAUTHLIB_INSECURE_TRANSPORT=1` meant that plugging in Google Workspace/Google Tasks still could not sign in even after clicking agree.** These two connectors run `workspace-mcp`, which takes a Client ID + Secret so it goes through the confidential OAuth flow, and where it catches the result is `http://localhost:8000/oauth2callback` - bare HTTP. The oauthlib library throws `InsecureTransportError` on http by default, and the upstream README declares this variable mandatory. Jarvis 007 never set it, and not a word in the guide could save it. It is now declared in the static `env` block of both connectors, so the user does not have to know about it. It is safe because the callback only runs on that machine's own loopback.
- **The guide said to enable exactly 4 APIs while the card promises more.** The `core` tier of workspace-mcp serves Sheets, Slides, Forms, Tasks and Contacts too - the card description lists those but following the guide exactly leaves them silently dead, and nobody understands why. The API enabling step is now split into two groups: the four basics and the ones to enable additionally if needed, with a sentence stating that forgetting one only breaks that tool group, not the whole connection.
- **The warning "you must have a machine with a screen" was at the LAST step.** Someone installing on a VPS read that far after already spending 10 minutes creating a project, enabling APIs and creating an OAuth client, only to learn this route cannot work. It is now the FIRST step, and points straight to the two Google Calendar/Gmail cards that sign in neatly inside the dashboard.
### Improved
- **All 8 steps of the Google Workspace card are rewritten** (and the Google Tasks card on the same mold): it states clearly that a client of type "Desktop app" does NOT need a redirect URI declared - quite different from the Calendar/Gmail card so anyone who did that card first goes looking for that field; it separates the key-pasting step from the Connect-clicking step; it adds a step advising to get past the "app not verified" warning screen via Advanced > Continue and to tick all the permission boxes - the place where users often freeze and give up.
- **The Google email field label changes from "optional" to "recommended"**, with the reason: left empty, on every tool call the server asks back which account to use. Still not mandatory, it just states the real consequence.
- The MCP docs page is updated too, adding a reminder to declare the full permission scopes for the Calendar/Gmail card.
- Added `test_google_workspace_setup.py`: 33 checks locking the environment variable (including checking that `build_env` really pushes down to the child process), the order where the warning step must come before the get-to-work step, the full API list, the email field label, and the rule "every connector running workspace-mcp must have both of those" so next time half a bug is not patched.

## [0.9.271] - 2026-07-30
Google Calendar kept reporting "missing permission" no matter how many times it was deleted and reinstalled: the permission list Jarvis 007 asks for was the wrong part.
### Fixed
- **Google Calendar returned `ACCESS_TOKEN_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT` at the free-time search step, however many times it was reinstalled (reported by a real user).** Jarvis 007 only asked for the single combined scope `auth/calendar`, but Google's official MCP server demands the FINE-GRAINED scopes: `calendar.calendarlist.readonly`, `calendar.events.readonly` and above all `calendar.events.freebusy` for `suggest_time`. Without freebusy, sign-in still shows green, `list_calendars` still works, and it only dies at the free/busy check - so deleting the connection and recreating it changed nothing, asking again for the same missing permission set every time. The Calendar connector now asks for all 5 scopes (keeping both `calendar` + `calendar.events` for the write tool group); Gmail asks additionally for `gmail.readonly`, `gmail.compose`, `gmail.labels` for the same reason (these three are inside `gmail.modify` so permission is not widened). **Anyone connected to Calendar/Gmail must click Sign in again once** - the old token only carries the permissions asked in the previous version.
- **The Test button showed green while the connection lacked permission.** Calendar's validate tool is `list_calendars`, which only needs the calendar-list scope, so it ran fine and both the Connections page and the health check loop reported OK. Jarvis 007 now SAVES the list of scopes really granted (read from the token response, both at sign-in and at refresh) and compares it with the scopes the catalog is asking for: missing ones turn red immediately, naming the missing permission, with a Reconnect button. A token saved by an old version has no such information so it counts as "unknown" and stays silent, not making anyone sign in again for no reason.
- **The missing-permission error at tool call time now says exactly which permission is missing** and says plainly that deleting and recreating the connection does not cure it, you must Sign in again after updating - instead of the generic "tick all the permissions" sentence that made users re-check the consent screen and see nothing wrong.
- **Tools hidden by the permission level are now LISTED instead of silently disappearing.** The Calendar connection defaults to Read only so `create_event` is not in the tool list, the model looked and did not find it, then wrongly concluded the connection was broken (exactly the trail of the user asking "create a calendar event tomorrow 9am"). `javis_connections` now returns an extra `tool_bi_an_do_quyen` ("tools hidden by permission") + how to open them, and `javis_search_tools` adds a note when the source just found still has tools being masked - so Jarvis 007 says the right sentence "the connection is at Read only, if you raise it to Draft write I can create it", rather than raising permission itself.
### Improved
- The Calendar/Gmail setup guide adds two often-missed steps: enable the **People API** (the MCP server uses it when searching free time with attendees) and declare the full scopes on the **Data Access** page of the Google Auth Platform, with buttons opening those two pages directly. The guide also says outright why all 5 scopes are needed and reminds you to TICK ALL the boxes on the consent screen.
- Added `test_scope_google.py`: 33 checks locking the scope list in the catalog, the comparison of granted scopes (including the Google trap of returning `email` as the URL `userinfo.email`), the canary "unknown must not be guessed as missing", the content of the three error paths, and a check that validate/health really go through the scope checker.

## [0.9.270] - 2026-07-30
Jarvis 007 stops leaning toward Claude: every brain has equal capability, and the red banner demanding Claude login no longer bothers a machine running OpenRouter.
### Fixed
- **The red banner "Brain claude lost login" hung on a machine that never installed Claude.** The brain indicator kept its state in RAM and nobody cleaned it, so a light switched on back when Claude was the Main Model hung forever after the user switched to OpenRouter - exactly the bug a customer hit. The light now only counts the brain the user REALLY chose (Main Model, plus the background model when a provider is set explicitly), cleans itself in the scan loop and filters right when returning `/connect/health`, so changing provider turns the banner off immediately, no waiting 10 minutes. API providers (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic API) have no light because they run on an API key, with no login session to lose.
- **The Connections page wrongly reported "Google Gemini does not yet support tool calling".** Gemini was left out of the `MCP_PROVIDERS` list in the UI even though `_api_stream_mcp` on the server had served it for a long time. All five providers now show a green card; the yellow line is only left to block unknown providers.
### Improved
- **Jarvis 007 now describes its own capability correctly.** The system prompt used to say "in addition supports plain chat through OpenRouter / OpenAI / Anthropic API", so when a customer asked, Jarvis 007 answered "without Claude Code it can only chat for fun, it cannot orchestrate or do tasks" - wrong. The Nature section is rewritten: Jarvis 007 is an agentic AI with a SWAPPABLE BRAIN, six providers sharing one toolkit through the MCP Hub (the Connections store, brain file tools, skills, Kanban work, agents/workflows/loops/reminders), and the only difference is that two CLI engines can also run machine commands. With a ban on claiming "only chat" / "must install Claude Code to do it".
- **The labels in the UI now tell the truth.** The type label of the four API providers changes from **chat** to **MCP Jarvis 007**. The Main Model line changes from "Direct API call - plain chat (no MCP)" to "Direct API call - MCP Jarvis 007 + skills + loops (no machine commands)", and there is an extra line just for Codex. The OpenRouter card in the wizard, the Engine section on the Overview page, and the description of Telegram's `/cli` `/or` commands are fixed accordingly. The Engine section on Overview used to read the old `model.engine` field so a machine running Gemini/OpenAI was still labeled "Claude CLI" - it now reads `model.main` like the Models page.
- **The intro documents shift axis.** README, `docs/README.md`, `docs/01-bat-dau-thiet-lap.md` and `docs/10-models-va-engine.md` are rewritten toward "an agentic AI with a swappable brain" instead of "built on Claude's CLI": the engine comparison table gets a separate machine-command column, and notes like "this line is outdated, do not trust the label on screen" are removed because the label is now correct.
- Added `test_engine_ngang_quyen.py` guarding both sides: the brain indicator logic by the brain in use, and the rule that nowhere (system prompt, UI, docs) may say an API provider "only chats, no MCP". The list of MCP-capable providers in the UI is checked directly against the real list in `main.py` so next time a provider is added and the UI forgotten, the test goes red immediately.

## [0.9.269] - 2026-07-30
The input box on the Chat tab showed a dark grey strip, and secondary buttons on the Model page lost their text on hover.
### Fixed
- **The input box on the Chat tab was not the same color as the input box on the Jarvis 007 screen.** The tab's CSS hard-coded `background: rgba(24,24,34,.6)` instead of using the background token, so the light tone showed a dark grey strip in the middle of the white paper background, while the dark tone was slightly off from the original. It now uses `var(--bg2)` and 18px rounded corners exactly like the input bar on the Jarvis 007 screen. The chat enlarge layer is adjusted too, so all three places that host chat (cockpit, Chat tab, enlarge layer) look as one. While at it, the last two hard-coded spots in the same block were changed: the history column background uses `var(--surface-1)`, and the mobile drawer shadow uses `var(--shadow-veil)`.
- **Secondary buttons on the Model page lost their text on hover, in both dark and light tones.** Five buttons (Via browser, Disconnect x3, Check again) wrote `style="background:transparent"` right on the tag. Inline style beats every `:hover` rule, so on hover only half the effect ran: the background stayed transparent while the text changed to `var(--on-accent)` - which is the color meant for text PLACED ON a solid orange background. In the dark tone `--on-accent` is near black on a dark background, in the light tone it is white on white: both invisible. All five moved to the existing class `.gcard-btn.ghost`, where hover gives a faint background + bolder text.
### Improved
- A `disabled` button no longer turns orange on hover (turning orange and then changing the text color while the opacity drops makes it unreadable) - it keeps its normal look.
- Added `test_theme_tokens.py` guarding two rules: no hard-coded colors in the dynamically injected CSS of the Chat tab, and no `style="background:transparent"` on a button with `:hover`. This kind of bug only shows when flipping the tone or hovering, and the eye skimming the code does not see it.

## [0.9.268] - 2026-07-30
Reloading the page or opening another tab now returns to the conversation in progress.
### Improved
- **Reloading the page no longer throws you into a new conversation.** Version 0.9.88 changed the default so every page load opens an empty box; in real use every F5 and every extra tab lost the thread of what was being discussed, and you had to go into History and click again. It now goes back to restoring the conversation in progress. To get an empty box, click the + button as before. Restore reads from localStorage so it shows instantly and keeps both the attached images and the answer-choice chips - things a reload from the server does not have. The session id comes back too, so a turn running in the background keeps streaming into the right box after the reload.

## [0.9.267] - 2026-07-30
The error bubble in chat printed a raw svg tag, and Jarvis 007 did not recognize Codex losing its login.
### Fixed
- **Error messages in chat showed a raw `<svg ...>` and the text was escaped twice.** The fourth leak of the switch to Lucide icons, with a mechanism quite different from the previous three: `appendJavisMessage` runs the content through `markdownToHtml`, and the renderer escapes HTML so the icon tag became text. Worse, the caller had already run `escapeHtml` before passing it in so the text was escaped a second time and the user read `&quot;` in the middle of the log sentence. Split out a separate `appendJavisError`: the text still goes through the markdown path like every other message, and the icon is attached to the bubble as real HTML.
- **Codex lost its login but the brain indicator did not light.** Codex CLI reports "Your access token could not be refreshed because your refresh token was already used. Please log out and sign in again." The pattern set only knew Claude's phrasing ("OAuth session expired", "failed to authenticate") so none matched: the user asked three times and got three confusing error bubbles, with no one telling them to sign in again - exactly what the brain indicator feature was created to avoid. Added three Codex phrasings to the pattern set.
### Improved
- The icon scanner guards a fourth path: a helper function that takes a parameter and passes it through an **escape or markdown render** (`markdownToHtml`, `escapeHtml`, `esc`), not only `.textContent`. All four leak paths of the same bug now have a barrier.

## [0.9.266] - 2026-07-30
The Channels icon changes to a paper plane, and text in every input box is standardized.
### Improved
- **The Channels section changes its icon from an envelope to a paper plane.** This page is Telegram and chat channels, and an envelope reads as email so the meaning was wrong.
- **Every placeholder in input boxes now capitalizes the first letter and drops abbreviations.** Reviewed 96 strings in index.html, dashboard/*.js and system/mcp-catalog.json: "vd 123456789, 987654321" became "Ví dụ: 123456789, 987654321" ("Example: ..."), "dán API key Pancake POS..." became "Dán API key Pancake POS..." ("Paste the Pancake POS API key..."). Technical sample strings (keys, URLs, commands) cannot have their content capitalized because capitalizing would make the value wrong, so the prefix "Ví dụ: " ("Example: ") is added to both satisfy the rule and state clearly that it is a sample. A few places were rewritten to be tighter along the way: "để trống = không đặt mật khẩu" became "Để trống nếu không đặt mật khẩu" ("Leave empty if not setting a password"), "args cách nhau bằng dấu cách" became "các tham số cách nhau bằng dấu cách" ("parameters separated by spaces").
- Added `test_placeholder_ui.py` guarding this convention. Placeholders are scattered in three places and every new connector adds its own set of fields, so without a test it drifts again within weeks.

## [0.9.265] - 2026-07-30
A customer installing on a VPS and plugging in Facebook got "URL blocked" because the guide had no place to copy the callback address.
### Fixed
- **The Meta Ads / Facebook Page setup guide did not show the copy box for the Redirect URI.** The step 4 text says "paste the https address from the 'Copy' button below" but that step forgot to declare `"copy": "redirect"`, and when a connector has steps, the old setup block (which did have this box) is replaced entirely by the steps - so there was nowhere to copy from. The customer on a VPS guessed the callback path (wrong, since the real path is `/connect/oauth/callback`) and was then blocked by Facebook with "URL blocked". Both connectors now show a copy box that generates the EXACT address from each install's domain.
- **The "App Domains" step was missing too.** A customer who got past the redirect gate hit the next one "Cannot load URL - The domain of this URL is not included in the app's domains". Added a new step for VPS installs: paste the bare domain (no https, no /) into 'App settings > Basic > App Domains' - with a new copy box of type `copy: "domain"` that pre-generates the customer's domain. Both the wall-of-text guide and the docs page are updated, and these two errors are added to the Common problems section.
### Improved
- A new test barrier in the catalog lint: any step that promises a 'Copy' button or says to paste an address/domain "below" without declaring `copy` goes red immediately - tried on the old catalog and it caught exactly the two faulty steps. An unknown `copy` value (one the dashboard does not understand) is also caught.

## [0.9.264] - 2026-07-30
Adds a brain icon before the brain-picker dropdown on the top bar.
### Improved
- **The brain-picker group on the navbar now has a brain icon** standing before the dropdown, orange following the accent, with a caption for screen readers. The icon is inside the `.navbar-brain` block so when mobile moves this group into the rail the icon goes along, with no special handling.

## [0.9.263] - 2026-07-30
The fourth leak of the emoji-to-Lucide icon switch: page titles printed the icon name as text.
### Fixed
- **Sidebar page titles showed the text "brain Tự học", "bot Agents", "puzzle Skills"** instead of drawing the icon. The previous three times the icon leaked through the `.textContent` path in JS; this time it went through the HTML path: the page title binds the icon with Alpine's `x-text` (correct back when it was emoji), while `VIEW_META.icon` since 0.9.257 had changed to the Lucide icon NAME, so the name was printed straight on screen in the icon's orange. Changed to `x-html` and wrapped through `ic()` so the icon name becomes a real svg tag. The left rail bar was not hit because it used a prebuilt svg string from the start.
### Improved
- The icon scanner guards a fourth path: **binding an icon value with `x-text`** (scanning both index.html and the Alpine templates built in .js). Tried the new rule on the version before the fix: it caught exactly the faulty line.

## [0.9.262] - 2026-07-30
The third spot of the same bug: the activity chip in the chat box also printed a raw svg tag.
### Fixed
- **Every chat turn showed a `<svg ...>` block in the middle of the screen.** The activity chip ("Getting data - analyzing...", "Composing the answer...") is called through the `showActivity` function, which pours its parameter into `.textContent` while three callers passed an icon string in. This is the third leak of the emoji-to-Lucide icon switch, and the hardest to see: the caller and the assignment are three hundred lines apart. `showActivity` now accepts HTML, the three icon callers use `Icons.msg`, and the two callers passing text from the server are escaped first.
- While at it, a small hole is plugged: status text sent up by the engine used to go through `textContent` so it was harmless; switching to `innerHTML` without escaping would open a path to inject HTML from server data. There is now `escapeHtml`, and tried with the string `<img src=x onerror=...>` it shows correctly as text, producing no tag.
### Improved
- The icon scanner guards a third path: **a helper function that takes a parameter and then pours it into `.textContent`**. The test traces from where the function is declared to every call of it in the same file, and only reports when a call really passes an icon string into exactly that parameter position. The three leaks in two days were all the same bug going three different ways, and now all three ways have a barrier.

## [0.9.261] - 2026-07-30
Two UI bugs slipped in from the emoji cleanup version: clicking the model chip showed no menu, and the .md editing toolbar showed a raw svg tag.
### Fixed
- **Clicking the model chip did not show the change-model menu.** Version 0.9.257 added `overflow: hidden` to the model row so the long SYSTEM/MCP strip would not stretch the chat column. But the change-model menu is an `position:absolute` child lying ENTIRELY above that row, and the row is its containing block, so it was cut off completely: the menu still opened correctly in the DOM, there just was not a single pixel drawn. The overflow clip on the model row is removed and the anti-stretch work moves to exactly where it is needed: the SYSTEM strip cuts its own excess as before, and the model chip gets a width cap so a long model name cannot push the row either.
- **The .md editing toolbar showed a raw `<svg ...>` as text.** The same version changed the Quote and Link buttons from emoji to Lucide icons, but the button label was still assigned with `textContent` so the SVG string was printed as text, taking two big lines in the middle of the toolbar. The label is now built with `innerHTML`, and plain text is escaped first so the `</>` button is not swallowed by the browser.
- Two new test barriers for exactly the two bugs above, since both are the kind a human reviewer does not see: the icon scanner can now trace the icon path through a DATA TABLE and then destructured into a variable (`BTNS.forEach(([label]) => ...textContent = label)`), not only a variable assigned directly; and the model bar layout test changed from "must have `overflow: hidden`" to "overflow clipping is FORBIDDEN on the model row" - the old test line was itself locking the bug in place.

## [0.9.260] - 2026-07-30
Scheduled jobs now SAY clearly when they run, can be edited, and are not created when conditions are not met.
### Fixed
- **Looking at a reminder card you could not tell when it runs.** The cron card only printed the raw expression `cron 0 7 * * *` and nothing else. It now reads it in words (`7:00 every day`) with the next run and how long until then (`next tomorrow 07:00 (in 14 hours)`), the raw expression is still kept alongside for whoever needs it. The recurring-work card also states the date instead of only a bare time, and says plainly "it is off so there is no next run yet" instead of leaving it blank.
- **Cron schedules could not be edited or deleted.** Once a reminder was created it was immovable: only Cancel and Switch brain, and to change the time you had to delete and recreate. Added an **Edit** button (change name, content, type, and time - after editing cron the next run is recalculated immediately) and a **Delete** button (gone completely, unlike Cancel which keeps it in history). Two new endpoints `POST /reminders/update` and `POST /reminders/delete`; the `javis_schedule` tool adds `op=update` so it can be edited through chat too.
- **Jarvis 007 created crons too easily, creating them even when conditions were missing and then staying silent.** A customer set up a job "every morning report email + calendar via Telegram" while Telegram was not even connected: the job ran on time, the result fell into nothing, and no one told them what was missing. The server now blocks at creation, says clearly what is missing and where to fix it; the user still has the right to click "Create anyway". The Scheduled page shows a warning at the top when there is no reporting channel, and any card whose previous run failed shows that error directly. Script jobs are not blocked - that kind is deliberately silent.
- **The "Self-improvement loop" grew back after every deletion.** The old migration rebuilt the legacy loop on every startup if the `Javis/loops` folder was empty - and deleting the last one really leaves it empty, so deleting any number of times was useless. Added three barriers: stamping migrated-already into `loop_config.json` (run once and done forever); an empty config has nothing to migrate, so a clean fork no longer sprouts a blank loop by itself; and an old vault recorded in the config but no longer on the machine is skipped, instead of pushing the old loop onto the default brain - that was exactly the path by which a strange "Self-improvement loop" entered Brain Default on a customer's machine. Old data with real content and a vault still intact is still moved over fully.
- The Scheduled page also reports when **a channel is connected but really failing** (revoked token, 409 duplicate poll): the work still runs but the message does not arrive. This kind of error does not block creating new work because it may be momentary, but it must be said.
### Improved
- **Opening the app lands on the Jarvis 007 screen**, even on a narrow screen or with the brain cavity off. Version 0.9.182 made lite-mode jump to Chat by itself; in real use it was more confusing because every reload landed on a different page. The Jarvis 007 screen already has a chat box, the only difference is that it does not draw the brain cavity. Resizing the window across the mobile threshold also no longer pushes you to another page by itself.
- The rule **"only create a schedule when conditions are met"** goes into CLAUDE.md + the channel instructions + the tool description: before creating, Jarvis 007 must check for itself whether the data sources are connected and whether there is a place to report the result; if something is missing, say so plainly and ask, do not create just to be done.

## [0.9.259] - 2026-07-30
Cleans up two long-standing red tests, now all 93 tests are green.
### Fixed
- **`/brains/<name>/<path>` called the `/files/raw` handler directly like an ordinary Python function.** It worked so nobody noticed, but the handler's default parameter is a `Query` object, not a string, so the day someone calls it missing an argument it would blow up in the old-link compatibility route, not at the spot just edited. Split out the pure core `raw_file_response()` the same way `zip_dir_response()` already went, and both handlers call into it.
### Testing
- **The lite-mode contract in `test_settings_consolidation.py` was written against the intention so it was red from birth (0.9.182).** Version 0.9.182 deliberately sent narrow screens straight to Chat because the Overview page was removed, but the test demanded "must not jump to Chat". The test is fixed to follow the decided behavior, and it also guards that nowhere still points back to the deleted Overview page.

## [0.9.258] - 2026-07-30
Fixes several places that showed raw `<svg ...>` code as text on screen - the aftermath of the emoji-to-Lucide icon switch.
### Fixed
- **Channels page: the Telegram status line printed the raw tag `<svg class="ic ic-fill ic-ok" ...>`** instead of the green light. Cause: that line's content contains an icon (which is HTML) but was still assigned through `textContent`, and `textContent` treats everything as inert text. Changed to `innerHTML`. The same bug was in the "Send test" result line, in the password status and the Telegram test send button in the Quick settings box, and in the button row of the file viewer frame (rename / delete / enlarge / close - before, each button was a long piece of code).
- While at it, two places that joined a server error string straight into HTML were plugged too (Telegram's 409 error and the error when sending a test): they are now escaped through `esc()`, and `r.sent`/`r.total` are forced to numbers.
- The Telegram status in the Quick settings box when OFF still used the `●` character, it now uses an icon like the other three branches so all are drawn the same way.
### Improved
- **`tests/python/test_icons.py` guards this kind of bug too**: it scans the source for places assigning an icon string to `.textContent`, tracing intermediate variables as well (`line = ic(...)` then `st.textContent = line` - exactly the case that slipped through). It is a bug a human reviewer hardly sees because in code it looks just like a normal line of text.

## [0.9.257] - 2026-07-30
Removed all emoji from the interface, replaced with the stroke-drawn Lucide icon set. Emoji are drawn by the system font so every machine shows a different picture, and being fixed in color they hurt the eyes in the LIGHT tone; stroke icons look the same on every machine and follow the text color automatically.
### Improved
- **392 emoji spots in the dashboard changed to Lucide icons**, spread over 18 files. Icons are drawn with `stroke="currentColor"` so they change color automatically with the LIGHT/DARK tone and with the text color where they stand - something emoji could not do. Icon size is `1em` so it shrinks with the font size of the containing block, not a hard number.
- **Vendored a trimmed set of 115 icons, 20.7KB** (`dashboard/vendor/lucide-icons.js`) instead of the full 414KB for ~2000 icons. It makes no network call at runtime so it works even when the machine has no internet. Regenerate with `python tools/gen_icons.py` after adding names to `dashboard/icons.manifest.json`.
- **Replaced 24 hand-drawn SVG icons** in the navigation bar with Lucide, and merged duplicate declarations: before, each page declared its icon twice (`ICON` + `VIEW_META`) so they really drifted - Tasks (Kanban) had the same icon as Files, Account the same as Settings. Both now read from a single `VIEW_ICON` table.
- **The brain picker uses `<optgroup>`**: the `<option>` tag only accepts text so an SVG cannot be put in it. External folders now go into the group `Thư mục ngoài` ("External folders") - the native HTML way, keeping all the information the folder icon was carrying, shown correctly on every machine.
- Icons also work inside CSS `content:` (the tick at workflow steps, the bullet of the update log) through a mask + `--ic-*` variables generated by the script, so they still follow `currentColor` rather than a hard color.
### Security
- `Icons.msg()` / `Icons.warn()` / `Icons.ok()` escape the text part by themselves. The icon change forced dozens of places to switch from `textContent` to `innerHTML`, and many of those join server error strings straight in - that is the path that opens an XSS hole in exactly the places that used to be safe. These three functions close that path outright, with a test guarding it.
### Fixed
- A local variable named `ic` in `iconInner()` hid the global function `ic()`, renamed to avoid the conflict.
- `chip()` escapes its content by itself so it takes an icon NAME instead of HTML, and cannot accidentally let raw HTML in through this path.
### Kept on purpose
- Obsidian Tasks syntax (`due date`, `priority`, `done date`...) in `.md` files stays emoji because it is a DATA FORMAT, and changing it makes Obsidian unable to read it. The display of those milestones in the interface already uses icons. Emoji in Telegram messages are also kept because Telegram renders them uniformly on every device.
### Verification
- `tests/python/test_icons.py`: scans the source and reports an error if emoji creep back (a short exception list, with the reason written for each line), and cross-checks every icon name called in the source against the vendored set - blocking the bug of a mistyped name becoming an invisible icon.
- `tests/js/test_icons.mjs`: really runs `ic()` / `Icons.msg()` in a minimal DOM, including the XSS barrier.
- Checked on the running app: 17/17 pages render icons, none left behind, no wrong icon name, no console error, icons the right size and aligned with the text line in both tones.

## [0.9.256] - 2026-07-30
Webcake gets an easier way to connect: click Connect and sign in, no pasting a JWT, no Node.js needed.
### Added
- **Webcake Landing (web sign-in)**: a new connector pointing at the hosted server `https://mcp.toolvn.io.vn/mcp`. This server publishes OAuth to the standard (RFC 9728 discovery + RFC 7591 dynamic client registration, PKCE S256, scopes `landing:read` and `landing:write`), so Jarvis 007 registers the app itself and the user only needs to click Connect, just like Higgsfield. The two ways of connecting Webcake are gathered into the SAME card in the connection store, each with a one-line description to choose by.
- The card states the trade-off plainly: the web way goes through an intermediary server run by the tool's author (Pancake links to it in its docs but it is not Pancake's own infrastructure), so access to the Webcake account sits at that server; the on-machine way keeps the token on the machine and goes straight to Webcake.
### Security
- **Does NOT use the link-with-token style that the Webcake docs suggest** (`...?jwt=<token>`). `mcp_store` saves `url` UNENCRYPTED and `_public()` returns `url` as-is to the frontend, only headers/env/secrets are masked, so a token put into the URL falls straight out onto the dashboard and logs. OAuth is used instead.
- `test_webcake_env.py` adds an invariant for the WHOLE catalog: no connector may put `jwt=`, `token=`, `api_key=`, `secret=`, `password=`, `access_token=` into `url`, with a canary proving this rule really inspects.
### Testing
- Checked with real curl: the hosted endpoint returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate` pointing to `.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, and the metadata has a `registration_endpoint`. The browser sign-in step must be clicked by the user themselves so the connector stays `status: beta`.
- The test forces the two Webcake ways to have the SAME `tool_meta`, the SAME validate tool and the SAME `default_perm`, to avoid one path letting through what the other blocks.

## [0.9.255] - 2026-07-30
Connecting Webcake in Jarvis 007 broke right away: every tool that creates, edits or publishes a page returned `missing_env WEBCAKE_API_BASE`, because the catalog never supplied the API base URL.
### Fixed
- **The Webcake connector lacked the API base URL**: the package `webcake-landing-mcp` resolves the base in the order `WEBCAKE_API_BASE` > the preset of `WEBCAKE_ENV` > the `auth.json` file written by the `login` command. The Jarvis 007 catalog only mapped `WEBCAKE_JWT` and `WEBCAKE_ORG_ID` from the login fields so it supplied nothing on those three paths, killing all 9 storage tools (`list_organizations`, `create_page`, `list_pages`, `find_pages`, `get_page`, `update_page`, `add_section`, `patch_page`, `publish_page`) right away. The validate tool is in that group too so the connection card was red from the moment it was connected. The catalog now supplies `WEBCAKE_ENV=prod`: paste the JWT and it runs, no need to make the user type the `login` command outside Jarvis 007.
### Added
- **A connector-level static `env` block in the catalog**: the place to declare technical constants that are NOT secrets (base URL, environment preset) so no extra input field is spawned that makes the user type a URL. Precedence: env the user sets on the connection > login fields > catalog static env, so a staging or self-hosted build can still override with its own `WEBCAKE_API_BASE`. A preset is used instead of hard-coding the URL so that if Webcake changes its domain the package handles it.
### Testing
- `test_webcake_env.py`: pasting the JWT is enough to resolve the base, no input field may be spawned for the technical URL, the validate tool must be in the group that needs the base, the precedence of static env against the login fields and connection env, with a canary proving the check reads the real catalog and is not always green.

## [0.9.254] - 2026-07-29
Notes in the 3D graph were still faint and blurry, unreadable. Two bugs, and the simulator in the previous version hid both.
### Fixed
- **Particle size was hard-coded in world units, when it must be PROPORTIONAL to the cloud size**: particles were fixed at 3.2-20 units, but however wide the physics force spreads the cloud, the particles shrink by the same amount. On a real machine the cloud spreads much wider than assumed so the particles were left as a few faint dots. Particle size is now a ratio of the measured cloud radius: a lone note 0.030R, a hub at most 0.115R - whatever the cloud size, the visible ratio is kept. Checked at radius 70 and 210 with real three.js, the ratio held.
- **The particle color ramp was too sharp**: solid up to 9% of the radius then dropping immediately, so at real screen size that solid core was smaller than a pixel and only a faint halo remained. It is now a SOLID DISC with a soft edge (solid to 34% before fading) so a particle is always a real dot, not a blurry streak.
- Links in the light tone were lowered from 0.26 to 0.16 because they were overpowering the notes; fog was lowered further to 0.13 (dark) and 0.10 (light).
### Testing
- The simulator in the previous version used a fixed cloud size so it accidentally hid exactly this proportion bug. It can now stretch/shrink the whole cloud and computes particle size by radius, and every option must be checked at two sizes 2.5 times apart to be approved.
- `test_graph3d_nebula.js` adds a locking point: a cloud 3 times bigger must have particles 3 times bigger, measured on the real sprite rather than copying the formula.

## [0.9.253] - 2026-07-29
The previous version fixed the 3D graph but made it worse: both dark and light became one fog, no notes visible. This time a simulator was built to SEE it before tuning.
### Fixed
- **Three layers of glow stacked in the middle of the brain cavity**: the CSS background, the starfield's halo, and the bright core added in 0.9.252. The core alone had a diameter of 2.5 times the cloud radius so it covered the whole graph. The core is now pulled back to 0.38 (compact inside the cloud, reading as a "heart" not a "blindness"), and the background halo is kept UNTOUCHED because it is shared with the 2D graph.
- **Notes sank under the links**: links were at opacity 0.20 while notes were only 0.52, giving a grey spiderweb with no notes seen - the exact reverse of the important order. Notes now go to 0.90 (dark) / 0.97 (light), and links down to 0.12 (dark).
- **Note particles smeared into streaks**: the color ramp was too gentle so each note was a faint cloud, not a point. It is now tight, almost solid to 9% of the radius then fading fast - each note is a readable POINT.
- Fog was lowered from 0.26 to 0.17 (dark) and 0.30 to 0.13 (light); the rim dust was lowered from 620 particles to 260 and made half as faint. Both were helping to blur instead of creating depth.
- The particle size floor was raised from 2.4 to 3.2: below that, a note with few links is so small it counts as nonexistent.
### Improved
- **The core carries the warmth of Jarvis 007**: changed from white-violet to an orange brand ember bleeding into violet. The light tone becomes a faint peach-lavender blush, reading like the place where ink soaks deepest in the middle of the page.
### Testing
- Built a PIL-rendered simulator that stacks layers in the right order and with the app's exact blend mode, so it can be compared by eye before fixing code. Checked at 150, 220 and 400 notes - color kept, not flattened at dense counts.
- `test_graph3d_nebula.js` changed from locking constants to locking RELATIONSHIPS (fog inversely proportional to radius, a size range with floor and ceiling) so aesthetics can still be tuned without the test breaking for nothing.

## [0.9.252] - 2026-07-29
The 3D graph was until now a grey-white speckled sphere, flat and characterless. The cause has been measured, it is not a matter of taste.
### Fixed
- **Folder colors in the 3D graph washed out to grey**: each particle had a WHITE dot at the center before reaching the category color. Measuring the center pixel of a single particle: indigo `#8b93ff` gave `rgb(177,178,190)`, green `#3fdc9a` gave `rgb(171,184,181)`, orange `#f0a24a` gave `rgb(186,179,174)` - that is about **90% of the color lost before any layering**. Add a few hundred additively-blended particles stacked and the whole cloud turns pale white. The particle color ramp now has only ONE hue from center to edge: the three colors above come out as `rgb(125,132,230)`, `rgb(57,197,139)`, `rgb(215,145,68)` - under 11% lost.
- Lowered the particle base opacity to 0.52 (before 0.62): simulating additive blending showed that above 0.6, only 16 overlapping particles are enough to push to white, so color only survived at the rim.
### Added
- **A bright core at the center of the nebula**: something every good reference has and the old version completely lacked. It breathes with the voice, and is not affected by fog because it is a light source. The light tone becomes a lavender-peach blush, reading like ink soaked thick in the middle of the page.
- **Depth fog**: far particles fade toward the background color so the cloud has volume instead of looking flat like a pasted picture. Thickness is derived from the measured cloud radius, so a big or small brain both fit.
- **A rim dust layer**: 620 very fine particles around the outside, drifting the opposite way very slowly to create parallax - the eye reads a real 3D volume instead of a rotating picture.
### Improved
- **Dense core, sparse rim**: the pull toward the center is now proportional to the number of links, so notes with many links are pulled to the middle while lone notes drift to the edge. Better looking than an evenly round sphere, and meaningful too - what matters sits in the middle.
- **A wider and smoother particle size range**: lone notes become small dust particles, hubs many times bigger. Before, all particles were nearly the same size so it looked like an even scatter of dots.
- Links were raised from 0.11 to 0.20 opacity so the network structure shows, and they fade with depth along with the particles.
### Testing
- `test_graph3d_nebula.js` locks 20 points: particles must have no white stop, the light tone must change its layering style, fog is derived from the radius, the core/dust are in the right draw order and do not duplicate on rebuild. Every API used was checked against real three.js r159.

## [0.9.251] - 2026-07-30
Zalo is pulled back to exactly one MCP path: after linking the account you find chats and send directly, with no need to turn on listening or choose a watch list.
### Improved
- **Sending Zalo directly through the upstream MCP**: Jarvis 007 uses `zalo_search_threads` to find the right person/group and then calls `zalo_send_message`; the gate that depended on the list of chats being listened to is removed, and so is the `javis_zalo_send` tool.
- **Removed the whole "Continuous listening" menu**: no more choosing a listening account, watched chats, Telegram alerts by keyword, or quiet hours.
- **A single Zalo process**: removed the sidecar listener, webhook, per-chat rules and the two old Zalo plugins; uses `zalo-agent-cli` 1.6.2 directly over stdio with all 7 MCP tools.
- The Zalo connection card has a link opening the guide document on GitHub.

## [0.9.250] - 2026-07-29
The tone button used to only flip from black to grey, not a truly light interface. Now there is a real light tone, and the brain cavity is redrawn to suit the paper background.
### Added
- **A truly LIGHT tone**: warm ivory white background `#FBF9F7`, white cards, near-black text, brand orange accent. The tone button now flips directly DARK ↔ LIGHT (a moon/sun icon shows the tone in use); the old "soft dark" tone is removed, and anyone using it automatically goes back to the dark tone.
- **The brain cavity redrawn in the "ink on paper" style**: a paper background with a very faint lavender-peach halo in the middle, nodes and links drawn in dark ink in the same tone as the old category colors, stars become paper dust specks, and the dark vignette becomes a gradual darkening in the paper's own color. The category color palette has its own ink version, in the same color order so each folder keeps its own "identity color" when the tone changes.
- Changing tone **does not reload the graph**: nodes keep their positions, the lit-up cluster and the hovered node remain - only the colors change in place.
### Improved
- Gathered **62 color variables** into a single token set at the top of `style.css`, declared in full for both tones. Three techniques that a light background does not have (frosted white glass, black drop shadow for layering, glow halos) get their own separate tokens so the light tone replaces them with equivalent techniques: a light tint, a very faint brown shadow, a ring border.
- Declared `color-scheme` for each tone, so the system scrollbar, the text caret, the calendar, and the browser's yellow autofill background also follow instead of being stuck at the dark default.
- Code blocks are also light (with their own syntax palette for the paper background) instead of leaving a black patch in the middle of the page.
### Fixed
- Every text in the light tone reaches at least 4.5:1 per WCAG AA. Brand orange is split into two roles: `--accent` keeps its full vividness for dots/borders/underlines, while a solid orange button carrying white text uses a darker version - because contrast is symmetric, one color that both stands out on white and holds up white text is impossible.
## [0.9.249] - 2026-07-29
Wanting to give Jarvis 007 one more fanpage by pressing Reconnect, but Facebook asks nothing.
### Fixed
- **Reconnecting Facebook now shows the Page selection screen again**: once permission has been granted, Facebook takes the "Continue as X" shortcut and skips the "Choose what you allow" screen, so there is nowhere to tick a new fanpage - users were stuck with the same set of Pages picked the first time, and deleting the account and connecting again did the same. The Meta sign-in link now always carries `auth_type=rerequest` (the parameter Meta documents for asking again), so every Reconnect shows the full permission dialog and more Pages can be ticked. Applies to both Facebook Pages and Meta Ads (re-picking the ad account).
- Note when ticking: **keep the old Pages ticked**, unticking a Page makes Jarvis 007 lose access to it. The guide in the Connect box and the Common problems section now mention this step.
### Tests
- `test_meta_graph.py` locks in that Meta's authorize link must carry `auth_type=rerequest`, so nobody removes the parameter by accident while tidying up later.

## [0.9.248] - 2026-07-29
Cleaned up the last media bloat path missed in the previous version, and it turned out to be the biggest one.
### Improved
- **Temp staging folder now cleans itself**: the place where files dropped into the chat box land had no cleanup before, and on the dev machine it had piled up to 114MB across 62 files, the oldest 27 days old. It now expires after 3 days, adjustable via `media.staging_days` in `settings.json`. The limit is shorter than the brain cache area because this is a hand-off spot for one chat turn that nobody reopens; for the same reason a stray `.md` file in there is cleaned up too instead of being spared as it is in the brain.

## [0.9.247] - 2026-07-29
Images and files sent in no longer sit permanently in the brain. They are passing material: once read and distilled into a note, that is enough.
### Improved
- **Media no longer goes into git**: `attachments/` and `inbox/` now live outside the brain's git. Before, every image was a blob kept forever in history, deleting the file later never gave the space back, and the mirror doubled it. Brains that had already committed them get them removed from the index once; the history already written is kept as is, not rewritten.

Adjustable through the `media` key in `settings.json`; set `enabled: false` to stop cleaning. Stray `.md` notes in those two folders are spared.

## [0.9.246] - 2026-07-29
Wiring Telegram into the session store in 0.9.244 exposed the opposite problem: nothing stops a Telegram session from growing forever.
### Improved
- **Telegram sessions now ROTATE.** On the dashboard users press "＋ New conversation" themselves so a session never grows forever; on Telegram almost NOBODY types `/reset`, so a Chat ID stuck to one session means that session grows endlessly until the server restarts. Opening it pulled in thousands of messages, because `openStoredSession` draws ALL of `sess.messages` with no paging - the sidebar "Show more" button only pages the conversation LIST, not the messages inside one conversation. Now `_tg_conv_sid` moves to a new session after 12 hours idle or at 200 messages (`/reset`, switching brain and restart already opened a new session since 0.9.244).
- **Rotation only rotates the RECORD, not the engine context.** `sess['cli']`, the Codex thread and `sess['or']` (which already has `compact_mem` managing the window) are all kept, so Telegram users never see Jarvis 007 forget anything; only the dashboard sees the conversation split into readable chunks. This is why the approach is acceptable, and a dedicated test locks that constraint.
- **Nothing to change on the reading side.** Rotation turns one endless session into many finite ones, so what grows is the NUMBER of conversations - exactly what the sidebar "Show more" button already handles. `app.js` is untouched.
### Added
- **`channel` column in the `sessions` table** (`web` by default, auto-migrated for old DBs through the existing ALTER loop) + a **TG** label in the conversation list, to tell conversations coming from the bot apart from those opened on the dashboard. Without it, rotation would only fill the sidebar with conversations of unclear origin.
- **`SessionStore.archive_stale(channel, before_ts)`**: Telegram sessions cold for over 30 days are archived automatically so the sidebar does not slowly flood. It runs on the rotation beat (every few days) rather than every turn. Archived, not deleted - still findable through `search` and `include_archived`.
### Tests
- **`test_telegram_sessions.py`**: 38 assertions. The `channel` column including old-DB migration; `archive_stale` right channel, right coldness, still searchable after archiving; the REAL rotation rule in `_tg_conv_sid` rather than a re-simulation (keep the session while hot, rotate after a long idle / at the message ceiling / when the session was deleted on the dashboard, two chats never share a session); and the rotate-without-touching-the-engine constraint.
- The one-turn SAVE part is still covered by `test_luu_luot_chat.py` (0.9.244); this test does not step on it.

## [0.9.245] - 2026-07-29
Closed the last seven places where the two engine dispatch copies had drifted apart. The spec appendix list is now empty.
### Fixed
- **Telegram lost all context when the old Codex session no longer existed on the machine**: Codex's rollout lives on the machine, and if it was cleaned up or lost after an upgrade the turn died outright with nothing rebuilt. Now the exact resume failure is caught, a new thread is opened and context is reloaded from the saved history, and later turns resume the new thread. This is fixable thanks to 0.9.244 giving Telegram a session store to rebuild from.
- **Switching model and coming back to Codex left it blind to the turns in between**: switch to Claude, chat a few lines, return to ChatGPT, and Codex still resumed the old thread that had never seen those lines. Now when another provider takes a turn, the Codex thread link is cleared, and the next Codex turn rebuilds context from the session store.
- **A minor mid-turn error killed the whole answer on Telegram**: one broken tool made Jarvis 007 return only a "⚠" line, while the normal stream kept going and still produced a decent answer. Now a mid-turn error is non-fatal: if there is an answer, the answer is sent with a line at the end noting there was an error; with no new text, the error is reported as before. This is how the dashboard already handled it.
- **The web chat bubble hung forever when the stream broke midway**: the `response` frame of the Claude branch sat inside the `final` handling branch, so if the engine died before emitting `final`, the client got no `response` at all even though text had already appeared. Now the `response` frame sits outside the loop and falls back to the text streamed so far. The Telegram branch too.
- **Long Telegram sessions had to wait for summarizing to finish before showing the answer**: `compact_mem` is one more LLM request but ran directly in the request path. Now it runs in the background, and applies its result only if history has not changed since compaction started (if a turn slipped in and it overwrote, that turn would be swallowed).
- **Files written by Codex were not sent along**: the Codex branch passed an empty list to the file collector, so a file only reached the user if its path happened to be mentioned in the answer. Codex has no normalized `file_path` field like Claude - paths are scattered across `changes[]`, `arguments`, or mixed into shell commands depending on the kind of job. Now `CodexCLI` pushes up the raw payload and the new collector walks the whole payload picking up anything that looks like a path; collecting broadly is harmless because the filter behind it only keeps files that really exist and changed during the turn.
- **Model was forced to a valid one with nobody told**: choosing `gpt-4o` for a ChatGPT account makes Codex unable to run, Jarvis 007 silently switched to another model and the user kept thinking the chosen model was running. Now the right model is written back into Settings and reported right in the answer. Reported in the answer, not the status line, because the status line gets replaced by the answer so nobody could read it.
### Changed
- **`_tg_ket`** wraps the Telegram answer (system warning on top, mid-turn error at the bottom) and **`_tg_compact_bg`** moves the compaction loop to the background. The dispatch flows are still NOT merged: each bug is fixed in place, as the spec recommends.
- **`channel_context.candidate_paths_from_tool`**: the path collector for tool call payloads, deliberately broad because the filter layer behind it is already tight.
- **`CodexCLI` now emits an extra `item` event** for unfamiliar items (e.g. a file patch). It does not show as "calling tool" to avoid noise, but callers can still dig out the path of the file just written.
### Tests
- **`test_dispatch_hai_kenh.py`**: 27 assertions, six Telegram bugs tested by calling the real `_tg_answer` directly with a fake engine (measuring behavior, not code shape) - does a broken resume really rebuild context, does a mid-turn error swallow the answer, does compaction block the request path, does a file written by Codex reach the user. The hung-bubble bug lives in a function nested inside the WebSocket handler so it cannot be called directly; it is tested via AST on exactly the two things that make up the bug.
- 90/90 green.

## [0.9.244] - 2026-07-29
Telegram conversations are now SAVED and LEARNED from like web conversations, Telegram tokens are counted in the Usage table, and the button-block stopped leaking into the session store.
### Fixed
- **Telegram conversations were saved nowhere**: not in `/sessions`, not in `brain/Memory/conversations`, not in the self-learning loop. No matter how long you chatted with Jarvis 007 over Telegram, the History page was empty and the brain never grew at all. Now each Telegram turn opens/matches a session in the store like the dashboard, saves both the question and the answer, auto-titles it, writes the conversation log into the Memory of the brain in use, and pushes it into the self-learning queue.
- **Telegram tokens were not counted unless running through Codex**: the Claude Code branch and the API branch (OpenRouter/OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini) both lacked `usage_store.record`, so the Usage table under-reported every Telegram conversation. The API branch now also uses the REAL model reported by the `meta` event, not the model set in Settings (OpenRouter bills by the real model).
- **The raw button block leaked into the session store and the conversation log**: the dashboard wrote `<!-- JAVIS_ASK ... -->` straight into SQLite and `brain/Memory/conversations`, i.e. junk in the very corpus used for self-learning. Now the block is stripped before saving on BOTH channels. Buttons still draw normally because the dashboard builds them from the live WebSocket event, while history never rebuilt buttons anyway.
- **A 9th place calling a route handler like a plain function**: `bench_hotpath.py` called `asyncio.run(main.list_brains())`. The net built in 0.9.243 missed it because it only looked at `main.py` + `routes/` and only caught bare calls, not the `module.handler()` form.
### Changed
- **`_persist_turn(...)` - the one-turn save path, shared by all channels**: strips the control block, then `append_message` + `auto_title` + `log_conversation` + `learn.enqueue`. This is the ONLY shared piece extracted; the 4-branch engine flow is still kept as two copies, as the spec recommends fixing each bug first and only then considering a merge.
- **Telegram split shell from core**: `_tg_answer` (shell - session + save) and `_tg_answer_engine` (4-branch core, kept verbatim). The shell decides the engine label then passes it down to the core, so no session ever gets labeled `cli` while the real turn ran through OpenRouter. Convention: the core returns a **dict = a real answer (worth saving)**, and a **string = an error message (not saved)**.
- `/reset` and `/brain` on Telegram now open a new session in the store instead of continuing the old thread.
- **`learn.enqueue` changed from `asyncio.create_task` to a direct `await`**: it only reads config + increments a counter under a lock (the real learning batch runs in `tick`), cheaper than the log file write right above it. An orphan task nobody waits on swallows errors silently, not worth it.
### Tests
- **`test_luu_luot_chat.py`**: calls the REAL `_tg_answer` DIRECTLY with a fake engine so it measures behavior, not code shape - covers both the Claude CLI branch and the API branch, asserts that Usage is recorded with the right provider/tokens/real model, that both question and answer are saved into the SAME session, that several turns do not spawn new sessions, that two different chats produce two different sessions, and that the saved copy / log / self-learning corpus are all free of the control block.
- **`test_handler_khong_goi_truc_tiep` now scans all of `server/`** and catches the `module.handler()` form too, distinguished per module so `skill_router.list_skills()` (a plain function sharing a name with a handler) does not raise a false alarm.
- 89/89 green.
