## [0.9.242] - 2026-07-29
Separated tests from source code. `server/` went from 126 `.py` files down to 50 pure source files.
### Changed
- **76 Python test files moved to `tests/python/`, 11 JS test files to `tests/js/`**. Before, tests sat interleaved alphabetically with the 50 source modules in one flat folder, so every search in `server/` was noisy and "which files are source" could not be answered by eye.
- **Tests no longer depend on the working directory.** Before, they had to be run from exactly `server/`: 62 files loaded `sys.path` from the script folder, 35 `__file__` expressions probed the way to the source, 15 places opened source files by cwd-relative paths. Running from the wrong place meant mass red tests because `import main` did not see the module, or worse, quietly reading the wrong file. Now everything goes through `tests/python/_paths.py` (`ROOT`, `SERVER`, and importing it also loads `server/` into `sys.path`), so it runs from anywhere and next time it moves only one file needs fixing.
- **JS tests are no longer served publicly**: they sat in `dashboard/`, which is statically mounted, so `/static/test_chat_render.js` was reachable from outside. Moving to `tests/js/` ends that.
### Added
- **`tests/run.py`**: runs everything or filters by name (`python tests/run.py zalo`), with `--js` / `--py` / `-v`. It finds `.venv` itself so it does not run the system python by mistake (missing fastapi/yaml). It prints progress with `flush` so running in the background or through a pipe can still be followed, instead of staying silent until the end.
- **`tests/python/conftest.py`**: lets `pytest` run the files already converted to pytest style. The main runner is still the per-file loop, because 61 of 76 files call `sys.exit()` at module level so pytest's collect step would abort the whole run.
### Tests
- **7 JS tests that had never run now run.** CI used to list 4 files by hand (`test_chat_ask`, `test_chat_render`, `test_chat_slash`, `test_wikilink`), missing the other 7. Now it scans the whole folder so adding a new test makes it run automatically. All 11 are green.
- CI dropped `cd server` and runs `tests/python/test_*.py` and `tests/js/test_*` directly. 87/87 green.
- `tests/` added to `.dockerignore`: the image does not run tests. Before 0.9.242 this could not be excluded because tests were scattered in `server/` and `dashboard/`, and excluding them would have hit the source code too.

## [0.9.241] - 2026-07-28
Plugged a secrets leak into the Docker image, and fixed three bugs in the test suite itself - one of which made two performance tests always green whether the code was right or wrong.
### Security
- **`.dockerignore` let secret keys into the image**: `Dockerfile:64` is `COPY . .` so this is the ONLY barrier, and it had drifted into an older and much weaker copy of `.gitignore`. Four files were being baked straight into the image: `server/.secret_key`, `server/.hub_token`, `server/.oauth_mcp.json`, `server/usage_index.db`. The GHCR build runs from a clean checkout so it was not affected, which is why this bug lived long unnoticed; only people running `docker build` locally were hit.
- **`.dockerignore` syntax trap**: patterns match from the context ROOT, and do NOT automatically match at every depth like `.gitignore`. So a bare `.staging/` line never excluded `server/.staging` (114MB), and likewise `brains-backup` (1.4GB). To match at every depth you must write `**/`, exactly like the `**/__pycache__` line already in the file. After the fix, **the build context went from 1,239 MB down to 6 MB**.
### Fixed
- **The event-loop latency measurement in tests was meaningless**: `test_brains_dem` and `test_kanban_snapshot` (added in 0.9.239-240) cancelled the heartbeat task RIGHT after calling the function. A synchronous function has no point that yields the loop, so the heartbeat was cancelled before it could record the delay - the result was that both the synchronous path and the thread path reported 16ms, meaning the test was always green whether the code was right or wrong. Now it yields to the loop before cancelling, and each test has an extra mandatory CROSS-CHECK step requiring the synchronous path to be clearly worse. Real numbers after the fix: synchronous `/brains` blocks the loop for 456ms versus 21ms through a thread; Kanban snapshot 221ms versus 35ms.
- **`test_khoi_dong_nhe` falsely failed on a loaded machine**: it used an absolute ceiling of 3000ms, but on a machine running a virus scan `import fastapi` alone takes 2.9-6.3 seconds and an empty interpreter takes 500ms, so `import main` jumped to 7.6 seconds though no line of code changed. A millisecond ceiling measures the MACHINE's speed, not the thing to measure. Now it measures by RATIO against the cost of loading `fastapi`: currently 1.93, if someone adds `edge_tts` back at the top of the file it is 3.66, and the 3.0 threshold separates them cleanly and is immune to machine speed.
### Cleanup
- **`.gitignore` now covers 7 artifacts that were previously neither tracked nor ignored**: `kanban.sqlite3`, `tg_brain.json`, `update_state.json`, `logs/`, `brain-trash/`, `_selfupdate.bat`, `videos/`. Before, a single `git add -A` would commit runtime data and deploy state straight into the repo.
- **Removed the `/agents` and `/workflows` lines from `.gitignore`**: they were created to hide two 28-byte junk files (fragments of a broken redirect), but the effect was to permanently block creating REAL `agents/` or `workflows/` folders at the root. The two junk files were deleted outright, along with two empty folders `memory/` and `server/utf-8/`.
- **`test_brains_dem` from 27 seconds down to 9.5 seconds**: dropped creating 3000 real files in favor of simulating a slow disk - both faster and closer to the real situation to guard against (large vault, network drive, I/O-choked VPS).
### Not done (deliberate)
- **Did NOT move `server/brains-backup/` (1.4GB) and `server/.staging/` (114MB) out of the repo** as the original spec said. On inspection neither is junk: `brains-backup` is the git working copy of the brain backup-to-GitHub feature (`main.py:1474`) and HAS uncommitted changes; `.staging` holds files users really uploaded. Both are content of `JAVIS_STATE_DIR`, and `STATE_DIR` defaults to `server/` itself, so "moving out" is really changing `STATE_DIR` - exactly what the spec forbids in item 3 because it is a trap that loses accounts and connectors. `server/tmp/` is also in use by `claude_sdk_engine.py:254`.
### Tests
- New `test_ignore_files.py`: checks that 28 secret/state/heavy-data paths are all excluded by both git and Docker, and that source code and system layers are NOT excluded. The git part uses `git check-ignore` itself so it is ground truth; the Docker part uses a simulation of the matching rules that self-checks 5 cases before concluding, and its main value is hard-locking the `**/` trap.
- 76/76 tests green.

## [0.9.240] - 2026-07-28
Phase 1 of the restructuring: removed all the cheapest event-loop blockers. Each chat turn went from 150.8ms to 37.2ms, startup from 2,263ms to ~1,400ms. No behavior changed except the note count (see below).
### Improved
- **YAML read with the C loader (libyaml)**: `yaml.safe_load` picked the pure-Python version though the venv already had libyaml. On real SKILL.md frontmatter the C version is 6.2 times faster, and YAML accounts for 64% of the cost of `build_system_prompt` - the function that runs every chat turn, every Kanban task, every reminder that fires, every loop tick. `fastyaml.safe_load` replaced it in all 9 places; if the C loader rejects the input it retries with the Python loader so it cannot be a step backward. **150.8 -> 52.6ms.**
- **Skill tree scanned once instead of twice per turn**: `_javis_capability_summary` called `list_skills` while `_skill_router_block` called `list_enabled_meta` (which is `list_skills` filtered again). **52.6 -> 43.5ms.**
- **Cache plugin manifest + state by mtime**: `describe()` re-read and re-parsed every plugin's `plugin.yaml` on each call, and also re-read `plugins.json` for EACH bundled plugin. Also found: `plugins.json` does not exist on most installs, so each call threw `FileNotFoundError` once per plugin. After the fix, the second call reads 0 files (it was 9). **43.5 -> 33.7ms.**
- **Lazy-load `edge_tts`**: it took 944ms of the 2,263ms startup (41%) and pulled the whole aiohttp chain into the boot path, though TTS is an optional feature. On a VPS, slow startup eats straight into the healthcheck window at deploy. **2,263 -> ~1,400ms.**
- **Cache the token price table**: `estimate_cost` linearly scanned the whole price table for EACH row - 321,009 prefix comparisons for 3 report rounds, though there are only 11 distinct models and 6 price keys. Scans per `summary()` went from 53,496 down to 54. Honest about the gain: it cuts only 9% of total time, because the function is still called the same number of times as `_group` reruns over the same rows for 15 dimensions.
### Fixed
- **Four event-loop blockers**: `/usage/summary` and `/usage/insights` ran sqlite queries directly on the loop (46-65ms) though `refresh()` on the line above had already offloaded properly; `GET /brains` scanned `rglob("*.md")` over the whole tree of each brain (136ms) and the dashboard calls it at BOOT; the Kanban snapshot ran synchronously in 10 route handlers. On a uvicorn process without `--workers`, every block piles up in the same place and one day they add up enough to fail the 4-second healthcheck, Traefik drops the route, and you get 404 - exactly the disease already seen.
- **Usage store lacked WAL**: after moving to run in a thread, `summary`/`insights` read IN PARALLEL with `refresh()` writing. The default journal mode made the two lock each other and throw "database is locked" exactly when the user opens the Usage page. `sessions.py` and `task_store.py` did this right long ago, only this store had not.
- **Kanban snapshot N+1**: it fetched `list_tasks(limit=5000)` then called `list_events` for EACH task. Added `list_events_bulk` using one `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY task_id)` query: a 120-task snapshot went from 120 queries to 1. Plus a per-brain asyncio lock, because pushing to a thread and forgetting the lock creates a new bug - two parallel snapshots both write a valid file but the OLDER one can land after the NEWER one and leave a stale mirror.
### Changed
- **Note count on the brain picker dropdown is lower** (e.g. 623 -> 579): it now counts with `_count_md` so it skips system folders. The difference equals the number of files in `.claude/` - the skill mirror generated by Jarvis 007 ITSELF, not user notes. The new number is more correct than the old. When the count hits the ceiling the label shows a "+" so it does not falsely claim to be exact.
### Tests
- 6 new test files, all of which lock the silently fragile parts, not just the easily measured parts: `test_fastyaml` cross-checks 295 REAL frontmatters in the repo plus 14 tricky corner cases where the two loaders tend to differ; `test_prompt_scan_once` COUNTS that scans equal exactly 1 and compares the generated content to be identical to the old path; `test_plugins_cache` checks both "stale" and "dirty" (a dict modified in place by the caller then written back to the file); `test_usage_hotpath` cross-checks 27 models x 4 token levels against the original algorithm because the risk is silently returning the wrong MONEY, and really runs 200 writes in parallel with 60 reads; `test_brains_dem` and `test_kanban_snapshot` MEASURE THE EVENT LOOP HEARTBEAT LATENCY, not just the function time.
- `test_brains_dem.py` has a guard asserting that `BRAINS_DIR` points to a temp folder before writing. This guard was born from a real accident while writing it: a wrong environment variable name dropped 3,019 junk files into the real `brains/`, which were cleaned up and the 4 real brains confirmed intact.

## [0.9.236] - 2026-07-28
CI is green again after several red versions in a row. Two independent bugs, neither an app logic error.
### Fixed
- **`test_graph_watch.py` segfaulted on Linux**: the test printed "ALL PASS" and only then `Segmentation fault (core dumped)`, so the CI loop got a nonzero exit code and the whole suite counted as red though no assertion failed. The cause is that watchfiles' `awatch` runs on a Rust (notify) thread; when the socket closes, the `finally` block of `/ws/graph` only `.cancel()`s the tasks without `await`ing, so that thread was still alive when the interpreter finalized and touched freed objects. Now the test sleeps 0.5 seconds for the watcher to see `stop_event` and then exits with `os._exit`, skipping the finalize step entirely. Verified the exit code is still right: 0 on pass, 1 when an assertion is deliberately broken. No effect on production because the server runs continuously and never exits, but `/ws/graph` cancelling without await should still be cleaned up separately.
- **`test_catalog_guides` caught 2 guides over the 200 characters/line ceiling**: `meta-ads-graph` had lines of 291 and 441 characters at line 291 and 441, `facebook-pages` had a line at 442. Line breaks were INSERTED at sentence boundaries, NOT changing a single word; verified by removing all whitespace and comparing the JSON tree, which matched the old version exactly. Fixed by string replacement in the raw text so the diff is exactly 2 lines (writing back with `json.dump` would expand compact arrays, bloating the file from 1012 to 1633 lines).
### Notes
- Chronically red CI since 0.9.231 means for the last 5 versions nobody could see the test signal. The real import step added in 0.9.235 is only valuable when CI is green at baseline, so these two patches came together.

On a small brain of 101 files `build_system_prompt` is only 39.6ms, a nearly 4x gap, so every acceptance mark must state which brain it was measured on.
### Tests
- **CI adds a real `main` import step**: byte-compile does not run code so it cannot see a broken import cycle, and the server has 3 cycles being broken by in-function imports plus 8 more modules relying on that trick. Mistakenly lifting one import to the top of the file kills the app at startup rather than at build, and the old CI stayed green then auto-deployed to the VPS. The new step closes exactly that gap.
### Docs
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-tai-cau-truc-server-design.md`: the 5-phase restructuring spec. Measuring before designing let it refute 3 assumptions: hermes-agent is NOT more compact (`gateway/run.py` 18,911 lines, 12 source files larger than `main.py`, 200 routes hanging off `@app.*` in a 14k-line file); Python file length costs 0 runtime (compile 155ms once then `.pyc` loads in 1.7ms, route scan 0.13-0.64ms and `include_router` merges to the same result); the app hanging comes from blocking the event loop on a single uvicorn process without `--workers`, not from the folder structure.

## [0.9.234] - 2026-07-28
Fixed the bug that hung the whole server when browsing folders, wiped the Tasks board clean, and graph tooltips no longer stick to other pages.
### Fixed
- **`/browse` no longer deadlocks the whole server** (the VPS incident returning 404 on the whole site): the function was declared `async def` but scanned the disk synchronously inside, and the `glob.glob(..., recursive=True)[:500]` only looked like it had a ceiling - the slice is applied to the RESULT so glob still walked the whole directory tree before cutting. On the VPS `/home` holds both the brains and other projects, so one folder-browse request hard-locked the event loop; the healthcheck was starved, Docker marked it unhealthy, Traefik dropped the route and the whole site became 404 though the app was alive. The log proves it: healthcheck 200 every 30 seconds then total silence right after the line `GET /browse?path=/home`. Now `_browse_sync` is split out and runs through `asyncio.to_thread`, and `_count_md` counts with `os.scandir` with a REAL ceiling (stop on reaching it), a depth ceiling, no following symlinks (a symlink pointing back to a parent makes recursive glob loop forever), and a permission error in one branch does not kill the whole count.
- **Graph node tooltips no longer stick when switching pages** (fixed by Codex, I reviewed and merged): the real cause is that View Transition captures the old frame with the hovered tooltip, so hiding it in `pause()` is already too late. Now it is hidden at the very start of `navigateTo` before capturing, `hideTooltip()` added for both 2D and 3D graphs, and a final guard with CSS `body.in-console .graph-tooltip { display: none }`.
### Added
- **`TaskStore.clear_board` + `POST /kanban/clear`**: WIPE the Tasks board of a brain clean, keeping only tasks a worker is currently holding (deleting a task while a worker runs would leave an orphan worker writing to a task that no longer exists).
### Tests
- New `test_browse_khong_treo.py` (9 cases): the counting ceiling stops in the right place, does not follow looping symlinks, skips permission-denied folders, a 2,400-file tree still answers in under 3 seconds, and the most important guard is that the event loop keeps breathing during the scan.
- `test_tasks_autonomous.py` adds a case for `clear_board`; `test_graph_tooltip_cleanup.js` runs with node for the tooltip part.

## [0.9.233] - 2026-07-28
Jarvis 007 stops creating tasks by itself: it only creates a task when told directly, plus a board cleanup button.
### Changed
- **The learning loop NO LONGER auto-creates background tasks** (`capabilities.task` defaults to `false`). Reason from real data: of 33 tasks across 4 boards, all 33 were inferred by the machine from conversations, none directly assigned by the owner, and most died young because the headless worker could not do them. From now on tasks only appear when TOLD DIRECTLY in chat (`POST /kanban/task`) - exactly level 2 of the orchestration scale. The switch is still in Settings for anyone who wants it back on.
- **Migration `task_autocreate_off`**: changing the default is not enough because `read_config` lets a saved value override the default, so running machines keep `task: true`. Now there is a migration mechanism that runs EXACTLY ONCE then writes a `_migrations` flag, so it both lowers the old config and does not turn the switch into a dead button when the owner turns it on again.
### Added
- **`TaskStore.purge_terminal` + `POST /kanban/purge`**: FULLY clear finished tasks from the store (with events/runs/dependencies), unlike `archive_old_terminal` which only hides them from the board. By default it only touches archived + cancelled; `include_done=1` also clears done. A hard `_PURGEABLE` whitelist so a call with a wrong parameter cannot sweep away tasks that are waiting or running.
### Tests
- `test_learn_task_gate.py` adds 3 cases: task auto-creation off by default, an old config that is on is lowered exactly once and written to disk, and the owner turning it back on by hand is respected.
- `test_tasks_autonomous.py` adds 3 cases for purge: deletes exactly archived/cancelled with their events, does not spill into another brain, does not touch live tasks even when a bogus status is passed.

## [0.9.232] - 2026-07-28
Background jobs report concisely and stop spawning junk tasks: blocks at the door what a headless worker cannot do.
### Fixed
- **Telegram notifications for background jobs are no longer a wall of text**: `_query` collected the narration lines (`text`) TOGETHER with the closing sentence (`final`) so `result` = the whole stream of the worker's thoughts ("I will trace...", "The shell command was just blocked..."); `_report` pasted `result[:1200]` and then pasted `block_reason[:500]` which was also cut from that very same string - one message repeating itself twice. Now if there is a `final`, `final` IS the result (text is only an escape for engines that do not emit final), a blocked task reports only a short REASON, a finished task reports the first few lines, closing with "See details on the Tasks page". Messages dropped below 400 characters.
- **The block reason now takes exactly the point being asked**: `_needs_input_reason` cut 1000 characters from the START of the string so it always caught the opening ramble. Now it takes the last meaningful line (where the worker actually states what is missing), at most 200 characters, one line.
### Improved
- **Gatekeeper for tasks learn creates by itself** (`learn.task_infeasible`): the main brain's Kanban board had 28 tasks, 100% auto-created by learn, and the groups "update Facebook cookie", "send Drive link to Zalo group", "watch Substack post approval", "fix IPN of ShortMason repo" all ended archived/cancelled/blocked - the background worker is headless, with only files in the brain + MCP reads, no owner's hands, no logged-in browser, not allowed to send outside, cannot see repos outside the brain. Those four groups are now rejected RIGHT at the door with a Vietnamese reason (before, they slipped through and were only blocked at run time: wasting a worker turn, wasting quota, adding one more annoying notification). The learn prompt is also tightened: only propose a task when all three conditions are met (user clearly asked, worker can finish it alone, there is a verifiable result), better to miss one than spawn a junk backlog.
### Tests
- New `test_learn_task_gate.py` (7 cases): 4 groups of infeasible tasks rejected, tasks that manipulate files in the brain and tasks that read MCP still pass (the gate is not overzealous), and the returned reason is a short Vietnamese sentence.
- `test_tasks_autonomous.py` adds 5 cases: `_query` takes final and drops narration, with no final it keeps text, the block reason is one short point, blocked/done notifications are both under 400 characters and do not repeat.

Switching brain switches the conversation: no more "thought I lost my chat, had to reload the page".

Now the page remembers the session being viewed for EACH brain in page memory: switching to another brain gives a clean blank pane (new conversation), returning to the old brain automatically reopens the exact in-progress session from the server, including a session still answering in the background (the live bubble reattaches). ## [0.9.228] - 2026-07-28
Background-job router: a multi-link fallback chain, whose last link is the strongest free OpenRouter model.

When the earlier link dies at run time (out of quota, CLI error, silent stream, not ready), the next link takes over the whole task; only when the whole chain dies is a real error reported. Now even when CLAUDE runs out of quota the background job stays alive on a free model.

The chosen model is saved in the setting `model.fallback_openrouter_model` - the user can view/change it later; if this field is preset the router respects it and no longer picks by itself.

## [0.9.223] - 2026-07-28
The realtime graph runs on operating system file events: when the vault does not change, the server stays idle.
### Improved
- **`/ws/graph` drops periodic polling entirely and moves to watchfiles** (inotify on Linux / FSEvents on macOS / ReadDirectoryChangesW on Windows - a lib already shipped with `uvicorn[standard]`, works on both Docker VPS and Mac): nodes sprout the INSTANT a .md file is written instead of waiting for the 4-second scan beat, and nothing changing costs no CPU (the old poll answered "nothing new" 99% of scans). Measured server background CPU is ~2% versus ~18% in 0.9.222 and a whole core in the version before that.
- **Safety net of a sparse scan every 5 minutes** (in to_thread): catches changes events do not cover - a vault on an NFS/SMB network drive fires no events, or events dropped in too large a burst. Without watchfiles it falls back to the sparse scan only, so the feature does not die.
- Files in hidden folders (`.git`, `.obsidian`, `.trash`...) are filtered on both the event path and the scan path; on disconnect the watcher + background task of that socket are cleaned up completely.
### Tests
- New `test_graph_watch.py` (10 cases, running REAL file events through the TestClient websocket): creating a new file produces `graph_add` immediately with `isNew=true` + correct wikilink extraction, editing an existing file produces `isNew=false`, files in hidden folders do not get through, disconnect does not raise an exception.

## [0.9.222] - 2026-07-28
Faster page load: no more event loop clogging from vault scanning, long-term asset cache, self-hosted libraries.
### Fixed
- **The server no longer "freezes" in 0.3-1.4 second bursts**: the realtime graph watch loop (`/ws/graph`) scanned all the vault's .md files EVERY 1.5 seconds with sync code right on the event loop - on a big vault every request (static files and API alike) queued up, measured P50 ~500ms for a few-KB JS file and the server ate a whole CPU core 24/7. Now the scan goes through `asyncio.to_thread`, the poll beat is relaxed 1.5s → 4s, and scanning uses `os.walk` pruning hidden folders while walking (the old glob still crawled into `.git`/`.obsidian` and only then filtered). `GET /graph` (source `all` measured ~10 seconds sync) also moved to to_thread.
### Improved
- **Auth/CSRF middleware about 10 times cheaper**: `read_settings()` is cached by mtime+size of `settings.json` (before, EVERY request read the file + decrypted Fernet 2 times, ~10-16ms just to check login; now ~1ms). When the file changes the cache rereads by itself, returning a copy so a caller's edits do not dirty the cache.
- **Static assets with `?v=` are cached for 1 year immutable** (changing the version changes the URL so it is safe): the next page open does not have to re-ask for ~27 JS/CSS files.
- **Self-host Alpine.js + force-graph** in `dashboard/vendor/` instead of loading from unpkg (measured 2.1s + 0.7s on the boot path, dependent on the outside network, UI dies offline). three.js/3d-force-graph (only used when 3D is on) are still lazy from the CDN.
- Results measured on the dev machine: home page TTFB 572ms → 35ms, DOMContentLoaded 2936ms → 1114ms, static file P95 from ~700ms → ~24ms, server background CPU from ~100% of a core → ~18%.

## [0.9.218] - 2026-07-28
Dataview much faster on large vaults: incremental cache, ETag 304, FROM scoping.
### Improved
- **Incremental server-side index cache by mtime**: `/files/mdindex` no longer reads + re-parses all notes on every call; only files that changed (mtime/size differ from last time) are re-parsed, the rest come from RAM. A vault of a few thousand notes drops from about a second to a few dozen ms from the second call. Deleted files are cleaned from the cache on a whole-brain scan.
- **ETag / If-None-Match**: if no note changed the server returns an empty 304 instead of resending the whole index JSON blob; dataview.js keeps the old copy in RAM and reuses it. After the 15-second TTL it costs just an almost-free "anything new?" request.
- **Scan scoping by FROM**: a query where every OR branch has a positive folder (e.g. `FROM "01 - Daily Log" OR "02 - Weekly Log"`) makes the client request only the index of exactly those branches (`?path=A&path=B`, the endpoint accepts multiple paths), and the server walks only those folders. A branch with only a #tag still scans the whole brain because tags are scattered. The result is a superset, and matchFrom still filters precisely on the client.
- Index ceiling raised from 3,000 to **20,000 notes** (safe thanks to the incremental cache).
### Tests
- `test_dataview_tasks.py` adds 9 cases: counting parse runs (second call = 0, editing 1 file parses only 1), 304 in the right scope, accepting a path list + compatibility with a string path, new/deleted files enter and leave the index correctly. Plus real HTTP verification through the TestClient: multiple `?path=` gather into the right list, 304 by the right scope.
- `test_dataview.js` adds 4 fromScope cases: merging folders, a tag-only branch returns null, ignoring negation, no FROM gives null.

Images created by Jarvis 007 automatically carry the javisos.com author label.
### Added
- **Author label on images**: every image generated with `javis_generate_image` now gets metadata written in: `Software = Jarvis 007`, `Source = https://javisos.com` and the creation time, as a standard PNG tEXt chunk. Anyone opening the file with a metadata viewer will see the image was made by Jarvis 007.
- Labeling **only ADDS a chunk, removes nothing**: the Content Credentials (C2PA) part that the image provider embeds stays intact in the file, and pixels are not touched. A file that is not a valid PNG is returned untouched and the image is not damaged.
### Tests
- `test_image_gen.py` adds 8 cases, including one that locks the behavior "do NOT remove the existing C2PA chunk" so nobody later quietly turns it into stripping the origin and overwriting with their own name.

## [0.9.213] - 2026-07-28
Jarvis 007 can delete posts on a Page, so changing the image of a published post can now be fully done by words.
### Added
- **Tool `fb_page_delete`**: permanently delete a post published on a Page by words ("delete this post for me"). Before, Jarvis 007 could post and edit text but not delete, so the most common situation, wanting to CHANGE THE IMAGE of a published post, got stuck: Meta does not allow replacing the image of an old post, you must post a new one then delete the old one, and the delete step had to be done by hand. Now it goes all the way through.
- The tool runs at the **Full access** level, declared in the dangerous group. Before deleting, Jarvis 007 **re-reads the post** to be sure it is the right one and to keep the content: if the post cannot be read it stops, NOT deleting blindly by a wrong id; after deleting it returns the content just deleted for cross-checking (and something to paste back if it was a slip).
- **The risk warning of the Facebook Pages connector** rewritten to match the true blast radius: it says plainly that Full access can delete posts and deleting is NOT undoable, Pages have no recycle bin.
### Fixed
- **The Page plugin declaration was missing 4 tools**: `plugin.yaml` listed only 5 tools while the plugin registers 9 (missing image, album, video, edit post). Now all 10 are declared.
### Tests
- `test_meta_pages.py` adds 5 cases for `fb_page_delete`, including the guard case "a post that cannot be read must NOT trigger DELETE", and a case that the connector warning must state clearly that deletion is not undoable.

## [0.9.212] - 2026-07-28
Corrected: the "Invalid Scopes" screen does NOT block sign-in, do not make users take a detour.
### Fixed
- **Downgraded "Invalid Scopes" from a blocking error to a skippable warning**: version 0.9.211 described this screen as a mandatory error where you had to add permissions before connecting. Wrong. Meta's own message says "This message is only shown to developers" and the sign-in flow keeps going; with the app in Development mode and the clicker being an Administrator, Facebook still grants full permissions (verified in practice: the token obtained has `pages_show_list`, `pages_read_engagement`, `pages_manage_posts`, `pages_manage_engagement`, no permission denied). The guides of the Facebook Pages and Meta Ads connectors now say to press OK and continue, and only when after connecting no Page/ad account is seen should you go back and add permissions.
- **Added a self-verification method** in the docs: after connecting, ask Jarvis 007 "list my Pages", and if all show up you are done, no need to dig into app configuration.

## [0.9.211] - 2026-07-27
The guide for connecting Pages and Ads adds a step to enable permissions for the app, ending the "Invalid Scopes" error.
### Fixed
- **Added the step of enabling permissions for the app - the real cause of the "Invalid Scopes" error**: in Meta's new app interface, permissions are locked by use case. An app created with the use case "Authenticate and request data from users" only has `email` + `public_profile`, so pressing Connect makes Facebook return "Invalid Scopes: pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_posts, pages_manage_engagement" and stop. The guide of the **Facebook Pages** connector now has a dedicated permission step (Add use case > "Manage everything on your Page" > Customize > Permissions), with a warning to recognize the exact error message so users do not go hunting through App ID and Secret.
- **The Meta Ads (Graph API) connector gets a similar warning** for `ads_read` and `business_management`, because it is the same mechanism.
- **The Facebook Pages guide updates two leftover points**: recognizing the old/new interface, and the redirect URI field only needing to be filled when running on a VPS/own domain (skip it on a personal machine).
- **Troubleshooting** adds an "Invalid Scopes" entry with separate fixes for Page permissions, ad permissions and the old interface.

## [0.9.210] - 2026-07-27
Fixed a wrong step in the Meta Ads guide: the personal-machine version does NOT need a redirect URI.
### Fixed
- **No more making users fill in what Meta does not let them fill**: the old guide said to paste `http://localhost:7777/connect/oauth/callback` into the "Valid OAuth Redirect URIs" field, but when the app is in Development mode Meta AUTOMATICALLY allows redirecting to localhost and deliberately blocks adding it by hand (with a note right next to the field). People installing on a personal machine following the old guide got stuck at exactly this step. The guide in the Connect dialog and the docs now separate clearly: a personal-machine install SKIPS that field, an install on a VPS/own domain MUST fill in the https address.
- **Troubleshooting states the right cause**: the entry "Facebook refuses / redirect_uri" is split by where it is installed, and stresses that for a localhost install it is KEEPING the app in Development mode that makes localhost accepted. Added a separate entry for the case "cannot enter localhost in that field".

## [0.9.209] - 2026-07-27
The Meta Ads connection guide now works on both of Meta's app interfaces, ending the "cannot find the Products section" situation.
### Improved
- **The guide to creating a Facebook App recognizes 2 interfaces**: Meta is moving the app management page from the old version (a "Products" menu) to the new version (a "Use cases" menu), so each person opens it and sees a different style, and anyone on the new version could not find the step "add the Facebook Login product". The guide in the Connect dialog and the docs now opens with how to recognize which version you are on, then splits a separate path for each (new version: Use cases > Customize > Settings).
- **States clearly that skipping verification and review is allowed**: the app's "To do" list lures people into ticking both "Business verification" and "App review", while Jarvis 007's way of connecting (app kept in Development mode, self as Admin) needs neither step. The guide now says plainly to skip them, avoiding days of useless waiting for approval.
- **Callback address for the VPS version**: before it only guided `localhost`, and anyone installing on a VPS/own domain had to guess. Now both cases are written out, with a reminder that outside localhost Meta requires https.
- **Troubleshooting** adds 2 entries: not seeing the "Products" menu (because on the new interface), and not seeing "Facebook Login for Business" (only exists on apps created with the Business type, but Jarvis 007 uses the normal version so it is not needed).

## [0.9.208] - 2026-07-27
The "Update now" button works on Mac (and Linux without systemd).
### Fixed
- **Mac is no longer blocked from updating**: before, the updater on a non-Windows machine required a systemd service 'javis', while Mac has no systemd at all so pressing update stopped immediately with the error "No systemd service 'javis' to restart automatically". Now the updater has 3 restart modes: Windows (bat/vbs), Linux systemd (systemctl), and nohup for Mac or Linux installed without systemd - it stops the right server process by itself (the server passes its PID to the updater, with a fallback port probe) then restarts uvicorn in the background just like install.sh. Automatic rollback is intact.
- **Platform label tells the truth**: a Mac was labeled "Linux (systemd)" in the Update section because the frontend hardcoded it by mode. `/version` now also reports the real platform (windows/mac/linux) and the UI shows "macOS" or "Linux" correctly.
- **update.sh also restarts by itself without systemd**: instead of only printing "please restart manually", the script now stops the process holding the port by itself then restarts in the background with nohup.
### Tests
- `test_update.py` adds 8 cases: the 3 modes of service_mode, the updater no longer has the systemd-blocking branch, dry-run accepts --server-pid, /version has platform, console.js no longer hardcodes the label and main.py passes --server-pid.

## [0.9.207] - 2026-07-27
Fully removed the "Personal Facebook (cookie)" connection - the mbasic path is dead and cannot be saved.
### Removed
- **Deleted the `facebook-personal` connector and the `fb-personal` plugin** along with its 11 tools (`fb_feed_read`, `fb_personal_post`, `fb_personal_comment`, `fb_personal_comments`, `fb_personal_comment_reply`, `fb_personal_delete`, `fb_personal_react`, `fb_personal_share`, `fb_messages_read`, `fb_message_thread`, `fb_message_send`). Reason: Facebook has retired mbasic so the plugin can no longer read or write even with a good cookie, and the approach itself violates Facebook's terms, with a real risk of account lock. Replaced with nothing - another direction will be considered later.
- The remaining Facebook connections are NOT affected: `meta-ads-graph` (ads), `facebook-pages` (Pages), `facebook-monitor` (monitoring public Pages/Groups through Apify), `meta-ads`.
### Tests
- Deleted `test_fb_personal.py`; `test_canh_bao_rui_ro.py` removes `facebook-personal` from the list of connectors required to carry a risk warning.

## [0.9.206] - 2026-07-27
Abandoned OAuth connections no longer show up as real accounts and do not regrow after deletion.
### Fixed
- **No more the OAuth connection "deleted then appears again"**: pressing the sign-in button of an OAuth connector creates the connection FIRST and only then goes to ask for sign-in; when asking fails (e.g. Meta Ads MCP is in beta and open only by list) the no-token shell stayed on the Connections page like a real account, regrowing every time you tried. Now when sign-in fails the server deletes the connection just created by itself and returns a clear error.
- **Leftover OAuth shells show an honest red dot**: an OAuth connection that never had a token (abandoned sign-in) is marked red by the health loop with the message "Sign-in not completed - press Reconnect", with a fix button right on the card - applies to virtual connectors like Meta Ads Graph that were previously falsely reported green.
### Tests
- `test_connect_health.py` adds a case: an abandoned oauth shell reports red with the right reason and does not dial the server.

## [0.9.205] - 2026-07-27
Pasting very long text into the chat box automatically becomes an attached .txt file, Claude style.
### Added
- **Long paste becomes a file**: pasting over 1500 characters or over 25 lines into the chat box, instead of stuffing it all into the input box, Jarvis 007 turns that passage into an attached file van-ban-dan-*.txt as a compact chip. The conversation becomes much easier to read, Jarvis 007 still reads the full content when answering, and follow-up questions on that document are fine. Applies only to the chat box - pasting into other fields (Connect form, naming...) is unchanged; short passages pasted into chat are also unchanged.

## [0.9.204] - 2026-07-27
Images and videos pasted into the chat box can be posted straight to Facebook without copying into the vault first.
### Fixed
- **The Facebook posting tool accepts files from the chat's file-receiving area**: images and videos pasted into the dashboard chat box land in a temp area outside the vault, and the posting tool refused with the error "cannot determine vault" though the file was just sent by the owner. The media sandbox now has two roots: the working vault and the chat's file-receiving area; files sent through Telegram already land in the inbox inside the vault so those worked before. Files outside these two roots are still refused as before - arbitrary files on the machine cannot be posted.
### Tests
- `test_meta_pages.py` adds 3 cases: an absolute path inside the staging area can be posted, a relative path computed from staging can be posted, a file in STATE_DIR but outside staging is still blocked.

## [0.9.203] - 2026-07-27
Facebook Pages can post multi-image albums and edit published posts.
### Added
- **Tool fb_page_album**: posts 2 to 10 images grouped into ONE post with a shared caption. Images accept files in the vault or URLs, mixed is fine; each image is uploaded unpublished then grouped in one go so it lands on the Page as one neat album. Over 10 images reports Meta's ceiling clearly; one image should go to fb_page_photo.
- **Tool fb_page_edit**: edits the text of a published post by post_id, deriving the Page from the post id. States Meta's limit clearly: only the text can be changed, not the attached image or video.
- Both are ranked at the Full access level and declared danger in the catalog like the other posting tools.
### Tests
- `test_meta_pages.py` adds 11 cases: album uploads each image with published=false, the last post has the full attached_media, mixing URLs with vault files, the 10-image ceiling, a comma-separated string is still understood, editing a post with the right Page token, a missing parameter reports an error.

## [0.9.202] - 2026-07-27
Facebook Pages can post both images and videos.
### Added
- **Tool fb_page_photo**: posts an image to the Page with a caption. Accepts an image file path in the vault (e.g. attachments/anh.jpg) or an http(s) URL.
- **Tool fb_page_video**: posts a video to the Page with a title and description, accepts a file in the vault (up to about 1GB) or a URL. The upload goes to Meta's separate video host; Facebook processes in the background for a few minutes and then the post appears.
- Both are REAL public actions so they are ranked at the Full access level like text posting: suggest mode and safe-auto mode never post by themselves. The file MUST be INSIDE the vault, the same sandbox as the file tools - an arbitrary file outside the vault cannot be posted to the internet.
### Tests
- `test_meta_pages.py` adds 10 cases: posting an image by URL and by file, blocking a file outside the vault, a missing vault reports clearly, video goes to the right graph-video host, a missing parameter reports an error, and the catalog danger list declares all 4 write tools.

## [0.9.201] - 2026-07-27
OAuth sign-in on an https VPS is no longer blocked by Meta with "not using a secure connection".
### Fixed
- **Server-side OAuth redirect follows the user's real https**: running behind a reverse proxy (Hostinger VPS...), the server sees the request as internal http so it built redirect_uri as http://... and sent it to Meta/Google - Meta blocked it outright with the message that the app is "not using a secure connection". Now the server prefers the X-Forwarded-Proto/Host headers set by the proxy when building the return address. This value is used only for redirect_uri so it does not affect permission decisions based on the client address.
### Tests
- `test_security.py` adds 5 external_base cases: takes proto/host from the proxy, stacked proxies take the first value, no proxy leaves it unchanged, and locks that this function must not get mixed into the auth guard.

## [0.9.200] - 2026-07-27
Redirect URI follows the domain actually opened, and the Facebook guide rewritten to match the Vietnamese interface.
### Fixed
- **Redirect URI no longer hardcodes localhost**: people running Jarvis 007 on a VPS (e.g. Hostinger) opening the Facebook form saw the copy box showing http://localhost:7777 - pasting that into Meta made sign-in return to the wrong place, breaking the whole flow. Now this box takes the address actually opened (https://domain/connect/oauth/callback); only 127.0.0.1 is still forced to localhost because Meta only exempts HTTP for the host localhost.
### Improved
- **The Facebook guide becomes a step-by-step wizard matching Meta's Vietnamese interface**: points to the exact menu 'Facebook Login > Settings' and the field 'Valid OAuth Redirect URIs', with a warning not to stray into 'App settings > Advanced' (where users get lost most). Facebook Pages states clearly that the Meta Ads app can be reused.
### Tests
- `test_connect_group.py` extended: the schema checks EVERY connector with steps by itself, a BYO connector must have exactly one step that copies the Redirect URI, and when steps replace the old setup block every link must reappear in steps.

## [0.9.199] - 2026-07-27
The drag-and-drop box for the JSON key file no longer grows by mistake onto the Facebook form.

## [0.9.198] - 2026-07-27
The Notifications button on tablet is as tidy as the mobile version.
### Improved
- **The tablet-size (861-1180px) Notifications button uses exactly the mobile style**: the unread count floats at the top corner of the button instead of squeezing with the bell inside a 34px pill - before, the two squeezing together looked very messy.

## [0.9.197] - 2026-07-27
The brain indicator light no longer shows an empty shell on the status bar when the brain is healthy.
### Fixed
- **The brain indicator light hides exactly when healthy**: the light's display rule overrode the browser's default hidden attribute so an empty light showed permanently next to the Notifications bell though the brain was normal. Added an explicit hide rule; the light now shows only when the brain has truly lost sign-in.

## [0.9.196] - 2026-07-27
Cancelling a schedule in natural language is understood too, cancelling the wrong one is harder, and reminder messages no longer leak machine instructions.
### Fixed
- **"Cancel the schedule Working at the cafe" now enters the right cancel gate**: before, you had to say cron, reminder or "nhắc hẹn" for the cancel gate to catch it, and saying it in short natural style slipped outside so the model guessed how to delete (it might edit reminders.json directly and cancel the wrong one). Now the standalone word "schedule" is enough, but schedules outside Jarvis 007 (Google Calendar, meetings, events) are still left to the Calendar tool.
- **Telegram messages of do-it-yourself reminders send only the result**: before, the internal prompt (role, procedure, paths) was stitched into the message - both messy and leaking machine instructions like the Coach "Mục Tiêu & Kỷ Luật" case. Now only the finished work is sent; on error it reports briefly, also without leaking the prompt.
### Improved
- **Safe cancel rule for agents**: when the javis_schedule tool fails, the channel guide says clearly that the only fallback is POST /reminders/cancel with form-data using the real id taken from the list; calling DELETE is forbidden, guessing the JSON body is forbidden, editing the reminders.json file directly is forbidden.
### Tests
- New `test_reminder_delivery.py`: a task sends only the result, an error does not leak the prompt, a normal notify stays unchanged. `test_tool_reliability.py` and `test_channel_reminder_brain.py` add cases for natural cancel sentences, a Google schedule not being hijacked, and the fallback recipe hitting the right endpoint.

## [0.9.195] - 2026-07-27
Brain indicator light: when the brain loses sign-in the dashboard says so immediately, plus a tidier status bar.
### Added
- **Brain indicator light**: when the Claude brain's sign-in session runs out, the status bar shows a red strip saying clearly what happened and how to fix it (run claude then type /login), with ONE Telegram message - no re-spamming every round, only a new alert after it revives and dies again. Two signal sources: the server checks token expiry periodically in the existing health loop, and any engine run that returns a sign-in error turns the light on immediately. Lesson from the 2026-07-27 incident: the brain died silently, 3 background jobs ran out as junk and nobody knew - a dead brain cannot report itself, so there must be an outside light.
### Improved
- **Status bar tidied**: removed the Jarvis 007 text and the weekday-date line at the owner's request - the bar was overloaded; the workspace name still shows in Settings. The space is left for the Notifications bell and the brain indicator light.
### Tests
- `test_connect_health.py` adds 5 indicator tests: the light turns on with a real error string, does not turn on with a normal result, Telegram is notified exactly once per death period, the probe does not override a red light set by a real run, reading token expiry covers all branches.

## [0.9.194] - 2026-07-27
The Connections page has less technical wording, is tidier and easier to read on a phone.
### Improved
- **The two built-in connection areas of Claude Code and Codex merged into one, collapsed by default**: users usually do not need to see them, and pressing opens them. The list loads only when opened so the Connections page shows much faster (before, it called the ambient health check as soon as you entered the page).
- **The word MCP leaves all main text**: the sign-in method label on store cards changes to plain language (Paste key, Scan QR, Sign in to account, One tap and done); technical terms remain only in the Add your own (advanced) section.
- **Mobile**: the connection store drops to 1 column, long account chips trim themselves and do not overflow the frame.

## [0.9.193] - 2026-07-27
All Google services gathered into one door, with a step-by-step wizard, drag-and-drop key file and a reuse-key button.
### Added
- **One-door Google card in the Connection Store**: 6 Google services (Calendar, Gmail, Tasks, Workspace, Sheets, Keep) gathered into ONE card. Clicking it shows a service picker screen: each line is one sentence saying what the service can do and how to sign in, with a label for how many accounts are connected. Users no longer have to understand the technical differences between the connection routes.
- **Step-by-step wizard replaces the wall of text**: the guide to creating a Google key is now numbered steps, each step with a button opening exactly the page needed on Google Cloud (create project, enable API, consent screen, create client) and a one-tap copy box for the Redirect URI right at the step where it must be pasted. The Redirect URI is taken from the address being opened so it works correctly on a VPS with a domain too.
- **Drag-and-drop JSON key file**: after downloading the client file from Google, drag it straight into the form (or click to choose the file), and Jarvis 007 extracts the Client ID and Secret by itself, accepting both the Web application and Desktop types. No more copying with missing characters by mistake.
- **Reuse a key between Google services**: once a key has been created for one service, the next service only needs a press of "Reuse this key" - the server copies it internally, and the key never passes through the browser.
### Tests
- New `test_connect_group.py`: full group members, the wizard step schema, the Redirect URI step, reusing a key does not overwrite a hand-entered value and does not copy a key outside the target connector list.

## [0.9.192] - 2026-07-27
The Connections page can check its own health: a colored dot on each account and a one-tap Reconnect button.
### Added
- **Constant connection health**: the server has a background check loop (once every 10 minutes) that pings each enabled account through the session pool, without calling a real tool so no quota is spent. Each account chip on the Connections page shows a colored dot: green is alive, red is an error, yellow is not yet checked; hovering shows the cause and check time. The status refreshes itself every minute while the page is open.
- **Errors in plain language**: technical errors are classified at the server into sign-in session expired, service not responding, connector cannot be started on the machine - instead of a raw error string. Lesson from the Google Workspace false-suspicion incident: vague messages made a whole series of wrong diagnoses.
- **One-tap reconnect**: an account that died from an expired sign-in session shows a Reconnect button right on the card - an OAuth account reopens the original sign-in flow, a paste-key account opens a new paste-key box that overwrites; keeping the name, permissions, settings, with no need to delete and re-add. The account menu also adds this item to change a key proactively at any time.
### Tests
- New `test_connect_health.py`: error classification covers all branches, virtual connectors do not report a false red, one failing connection does not kill the whole sweep, the snapshot returns a copy.

## [0.9.191] - 2026-07-27
The Tasks board cleans itself: finished one-off tasks no longer linger on the board.
### Added
- **Auto-archive finished tasks**: tasks done or cancelled for over 3 days move to archive automatically in the orchestrator's periodic cleanup loop. The Tasks board keeps only live tasks and recently finished ones; history is not lost and can still be looked up in the archive area. Before, there was no cleanup mechanism so one-time assigned tasks stayed on the board forever.
### Tests
- `test_tasks_autonomous.py` adds an auto-archive test: cleans exactly the old tasks, keeps recently finished tasks and waiting tasks, running again does not clean twice.

## [0.9.190] - 2026-07-27
When a background session has a tool blocked, the error message states the real reason so the agent does not misdiagnose.
### Improved
- **The background session's tool-block message no longer misleads**: before, an MCP tool refused by the permission fence only showed "user cancelled MCP tool call", and the agent read that as the connector being dead and proposed signing in to OAuth again (the Google Workspace false suspicion in 0.9.189). Now the message says clearly that this is the background session's safety permission fence, the connection is not broken, do not try to re-auth, and a job that needs broader permission should report back to whoever assigned it.

## [0.9.189] - 2026-07-27
Background jobs can use data sources (MCP) again: fixed a wrong block that made tasks and loops report "connector broken" though the connection was alive.
### Fixed
- **Kanban tasks and background loops can call MCP tools again**: the background session's permission gate compared tool names with fnmatch, while the allow list wrote `mcp__javis` in Claude CLI's prefix style, so it matched no tool - every call through the hub was refused ("user cancelled MCP tool call") and the agent wrongly concluded the connector was dead, leaving a whole series of background jobs hung in the blocked state. The permission gate now understands the prefix style too: a bare `mcp__<server>` allows every tool of that server, and still does not over-match onto a server with a similar name. With a test reproducing the exact failure case.
### Tests
- `test_sdk_engine.py` adds a group of prefix tests for the background session permission gate: matches hub tools, blocks another server, blocks a server with a similar name.

## [0.9.188] - 2026-07-27
Removed buttons that do nothing on image-only messages.
### Fixed
- **Image-only messages no longer have dead buttons**: a message sent with an image but no text has no text to resend, so the resend and edit buttons are hidden entirely instead of doing nothing when pressed. Jarvis 007's answer to such a message also hides the resend button accordingly. A message with both text and image keeps all buttons and resends the text part as before.

## [0.9.187] - 2026-07-27
Each message in the chat pane gets a small row of buttons underneath: send time, resend, edit and copy.
### Added
- **Button row under each message**: hover over a message (or tap a message on a phone) to show the send time with the resend, edit and copy buttons. The button row always reserves its space so showing it does not make the chat pane jump.
- **Send time for each message**: shown as `HH:mm`, hover to see the full weekday and date. A conversation reopened from History takes the exact time saved in SQLite; old messages saved before this version have no timestamp so the time part is hidden instead of guessing.
- **Resend and edit**: resend turns the exact old question into a new turn at the end of the conversation, deleting nothing from the previous turn; on a Jarvis 007 message this button reruns the question right above it. Edit pours the old sentence into the input box to edit then presses send by itself. While a turn is running the resend button is locked.
### Improved
- The old copy button on Jarvis 007 messages is merged into the shared button row so both sides are consistent.
### Tests
- Added `dashboard/test_chat_acts.js` covering time formatting, messages missing a timestamp, button row components per side and walking back up to the nearest question.

## [0.9.186] - 2026-07-27
A web chat turn keeps running on the server when the page is closed or reloaded, and you can still come back to see progress and stop the exact turn.
### Fixed
- **Closing the web no longer cancels the request**: the lifecycle of the chat job is split from the WebSocket; losing the connection only removes the display channel, it does not `cancel()` the task being processed.
- **Reopening shows the running job**: the server sends a snapshot of the sessions being processed and the content already streamed so History shows the state, and opening the right conversation continues watching live.
- **Stop stays accurate after reconnect**: a registry by `session_id` holds the task and subprocess tag, so the Stop button or the `/stop` endpoint cancels only the chosen turn, even one started from an old connection.
### Tests
- Added tests for the job lifecycle, reconnect/snapshot, Stop by session, and the situation where the WebSocket closes right after sending but the result is still fully saved into SQLite.

## [0.9.185] - 2026-07-26
Cleaned up the Environment form when installing Docker, leaving only the fields users truly need.
### Improved
- **Hostinger has only 3 fields left**: `DOMAIN_NAME`, `JAVIS_ADMIN_USER`, `JAVIS_ADMIN_PASSWORD`; the technical variables about port, state, brain and working folder were removed from the form.
- **No internal configuration lost**: technical defaults keep coming from the Docker image; the Hostinger target is attached in the run command instead of being exposed as an Environment field.
- **Tidier VPS/build compose**: removed declarations duplicated with the Dockerfile, production VPS keeps only the token that must be shared with Watchtower.
- **Clear install docs**: README, DEPLOY and the `.env` guide state exactly the three fields to fill on Hostinger.
### Tests
- Added a regression contract reading YAML to stop technical variables from returning to the Environment form in later versions.

## [0.9.184] - 2026-07-26
Friendlier voice names and domain setup becomes a clear wizard right in the UI.

- **Renamed the display of Edge voices**: HoaiMy to **Ngọc Thu**, NamMinh to **Nam Minh**; the Microsoft voice code behind is unchanged so saved choices and the voice quality do not change.
- **Three-step domain wizard**: saving the domain, checking/pointing DNS and turning on HTTPS are shown by state, with a button to copy records and a link to open the domain when done.

## [0.9.183] - 2026-07-26
Synced all usage guides with the new navigation structure after removing the Overview page.
### Improved

## [0.9.180] - 2026-07-26
Images generated by ChatGPT/Codex or OpenRouter models in Telegram are sent as real images instead of showing the raw Markdown path.
### Fixed
- **Accept paths with spaces**: the file collector used to match only `attachments/x.png`, so it missed real paths like `99 - Attachments/claude-workforce-vietnamese-4x5.png`; the new parser supports paths with spaces, the `<path>` form and absolute paths inside the brain.
- **ChatGPT on Telegram sends real media**: the Codex OAuth branch resolves Markdown images to the right file in the brain, queues `sendPhoto` and removes the `![...](...)` line from the text once the file is picked up.
- **OpenRouter/API has the same capability**: the gateway now collects files created by MCP for every API provider, and no longer assumes an API engine can only return text.
- **No empty message before the image**: if the reply contains only an embedded image, Telegram drops the `(không có nội dung)` (no content) message and sends the image directly.
### Security
- **No expansion outside the brain**: web URLs, `data:`, ordinary links and `../` paths that escape the vault are not treated as local files; only a Markdown image that matches a queued file is hidden from the text.
### Tests
- Added regressions for the exact `99 - Attachments` case from the bug screenshot, `<>`-wrapped paths, keeping URLs/ordinary links, blocking brain escape, and confirming a file-only reply still goes to the right Telegram chat.

## [0.9.175] - 2026-07-26
Deleting crons/reminders directly from chat now works consistently with ChatGPT/Codex and every OpenRouter model, and no longer pushes the user to delete from the UI.
### Fixed
- **Recognizes the word "delete" (xoá)**: the intent router used to have only `huỷ/tắt` (cancel/turn off), so a sentence like "xoá cron..." (delete cron) was not forced to call `javis_schedule`; added all delete/cancel/stop variants and blocked misrouting to the read-only path (`server/engine.py`).
- **Schedule-delete gateway does not depend on the model's function-calling**: Jarvis 007 itself calls `op=list`, matches, and calls `op=cancel` only when exactly one item matches for sure. Several similar items return the real list to ask back; an empty store reports truthfully that it is empty, and never guesses or fakes a delete confirmation.
- **ChatGPT on Telegram has MCP like the dashboard**: the OpenAI OAuth branch moved from plain-chat Responses to Codex CLI with native MCP, in the right brain and keeping a separate session per chat (`server/main.py`).
- **OpenRouter no longer calls itself "no MCP"**: schedule deletion goes through the shared gateway, so even models without function-calling can delete a surely matching item; other tool actions keep using the existing multi-model MCP loop.
- **Clear channel rule for every provider**: creating/editing/deleting/cancelling/turning off a schedule must use `javis_schedule`; a delete without an ID must list first, and must not tell the user to go to the Recurring work page themselves (`server/channel_context.py`).
### Tests
- Added regressions for the "delete cron" intent, unique name match, no wrong delete when ambiguous, an empty store, the ChatGPT Telegram route and the OpenRouter label. Ran an integration with two real crons in the test brain: the gateway deleted the right brainstorm cron, kept the remaining medicine cron and stored the deleted item with `cancelled` status.

## [0.9.174] - 2026-07-25
Patch for the AI queue: Codex runs normally again, failed tasks are recovered in a controlled way and the Kanban detail view is fully usable.
### Fixed
- **Codex CLI no longer blocks tasks in bulk**: the global flags `--sandbox`, `--ask-for-approval`, model, profile and config are placed before the `exec` subcommand, compatible with the Codex syntax installed on the VPS (`server/claude_cli.py`).
- **Correct auto-recovery of the group of tasks with the argument error**: on startup after an upgrade, Jarvis 007 requeues exactly once the tasks blocked by the `unexpected argument '--ask-for-approval'` error; other exceptions are left as they are so nothing runs by mistake (`server/task_store.py`, `server/tasks.py`).

## [0.9.173] - 2026-07-25
Kanban becomes an operations queue for AI, instead of a Trello-style board where a person has to press run on each card.
### Added
- **SQLite-durable task kernel**: added boards, tasks, dependencies, runs and an event log; task claim uses compare-and-set in a transaction, with worker lease, heartbeat, timeout, retry, idempotency key and per-run history (`server/task_store.py`).
- **AI specifier before execution**: a new goal goes through a triage layer where a background model normalizes the intent and picks lane `files`, `research`, `mcp-read`, `code` or `external-write` before entering the run queue. Outward actions without `full` permission are blocked by `capability` type, never run recklessly (`server/tasks.py`).
- **New Operations console**: the Work page focuses on running workers, the queue, exceptions to handle, 24-hour throughput and a run/event drawer; it auto-refreshes every 3 seconds. The six horizontal columns and the Run button on each card are no longer the main flow (`dashboard/console.js`).
### Fixed
- **Dispatcher scans every brain**: no longer hardcodes `tick(["brain"])`, which made other boards show auto but never run.
- **Runs exactly the selected task**: the run/retry endpoint claims the exact task id in a transaction, instead of moving it to ready and accidentally picking an older task with higher priority.
- **Background tasks do not block cron and the medicine schedule**: the dispatcher has its own loop, each worker is an independent asyncio task; the 30-second scheduler only wakes the dispatcher and returns immediately.
- **Learn tasks no longer stop for bulk manual review**: internal tasks complete automatically by default; only missing input, missing capability, an outside action or an explicit approval flag needs a person.
### Compatibility
- The old `Javis/kanban.json` is imported exactly once, and `running` tasks from the old process are reclaimed back to `ready`. SQLite is the main lifecycle source but Jarvis 007 still exports a JSON snapshot for brain backup and for older versions to read.
- Workers keep going through `aux_engine`, so Claude Code, Codex/ChatGPT and OpenAI/OpenRouter API use the same queue, brain context and existing MCP policy.
### Tests
- Added `server/test_tasks_autonomous.py`: covers JSON migration, atomic claim, dependency promotion, multi-brain dispatcher and running the selected task.

## [0.9.172] - 2026-07-25
ChatGPT remembers the conversation thread correctly, and every model reads cron/medicine schedules from real data instead of guessing from memory.
### Fixed
- **ChatGPT/Codex no longer forgets context between turns**: each conversation stores its own `codex_thread_id` and uses `codex exec resume`; if an old session lost its rollout, the thread is rebuilt from SQLite history. When switching to another provider, the old Codex link is cleared to avoid resuming a stale conversation branch (`server/claude_cli.py`, `server/sessions.py`, `server/compaction.py`, `server/main.py`).
- **Codex reads cron in the brain being chatted in**: the MCP hub receives `X-Javis-Vault` per Codex process and passes it down to plugins. Before, Codex saw `javis_schedule` but the context lacked `vault_root`, so the tool stopped at the error "cannot determine the working brain" (`server/mcp_hub.py`, `server/main.py`, `server/aux_engine.py`).
- **OpenRouter no longer says "no tool" or guesses schedules from memory**: questions that only view cron/reminders/medicine schedules make the server call `javis_schedule(op=list)` directly before the model answers, so it still works when `openrouter/free` routes to a model without function calling. Creating/editing/cancelling schedules still requires the tool call; if the model skips it twice, Jarvis 007 blocks the answer that risks being made up (`server/engine.py`).
### Improved
- **One real-data principle for every provider and every channel**: Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenAI-compatible and OpenRouter are all reminded to call a tool when the user asks about running status or outside account data; tool errors must be reported truthfully, not replaced by old memory (`server/channel_context.py`).
- **Internal plugins are still available on Codex when no outside connector is attached**: the hub profile is no longer removed just because the outside MCP list is empty; system tools like `javis_schedule` and `datetime-vn` remain usable.
### Tests
- Added `server/test_codex_context.py` and `server/test_tool_reliability.py`; the regression suites for Codex context, lazy MCP, schedule/cron, background-work provider, channel reminder, Claude SDK and session brain pass.

## [0.9.171] - 2026-07-25
Trimmed the fixed head of every chat turn, WITHOUT touching memory.
### Improved
- **Skill descriptions in the mirror are forced to the 150-character ceiling**: Claude Code loads natively by reading the frontmatter in `.claude/skills`, and that skill list sits in the FIXED head of every chat turn. Measured on a real brain: 14/30 skills exceeded the project's own 150 ceiling (longest 1,018 characters), total descriptions 10,095 characters; after forcing, 3,844 remain, down 62%. The canonical copy in `skills/` **keeps the user's wording as is** - the mirror is a derivative anyway. No capability lost: descriptions are only for routing, and the router has always cut at 150, so the excess was already being lost silently; the skill body still loads in full when invoked. Handles multi-line YAML (`>`, `>-`, `|`) too - the two longest descriptions in the real brain were both written that way (`server/system_sync.py`).
- **The memory index has a CEILING, stepping down gradually**: `JAVIS_MEMORY_INDEX_MAX` defaults to 20,000 characters. Over the ceiling, descriptions shrink to 100 characters, then 60, then just the title with a link - **dropping the line entirely is the LAST step**, and when it must drop, it says clearly how many memories remain and how to keep reading. Shortening descriptions does not lose memory: titles and file paths remain, and full details stay in `Memory/facts/`. Nothing is cut today (18,363 < 20,000) - this blocks the slope before it becomes a problem, exactly the illness the curator just had (`server/main.py`).
- **CLAUDE.md no longer carries long file templates**: the frontmatter templates for loop, agent, workflow, skill and even `plugin.yaml`/`plugin.py` already live in the `javis-builder` skill, loaded on demand when actually creating one. Removed the duplicate from the system prompt while **keeping every safety rule and behavior rule intact** (default `mode: suggest` + `enabled: false`, plugin env gate, 150-character ceiling, mandatory `group`, `owner_chat`, `notify: false`). Added `tools_profile` and `notify` to `javis-builder` so no information is missing.
### Measured
- The head of each chat turn shrinks by about **9,328 characters (~2.9k tokens)**: the Jarvis 007 system prompt from 46,056 to 42,979, skill descriptions from 10,095 to 3,844.
- **Memory is not cut**, and that was a measured decision: MEMORY.md takes only 5.7k of the 85k prefix (7%); trying to shorten descriptions to 60 characters saves only 1.4k tokens, and trading memory for that is a loss.
### Tests
- `server/test_prefix_slim.py`: cuts all 4 description writing styles (plain, double-quoted, folded `>-`, block `|`) while the skill body and `group` stay intact; canonical is untouched; the memory index keeps all memories across several ceiling levels and drops lines only at the last step with a pointer; CLAUDE.md has the templates removed but still has all 8 rules, and `javis-builder` covers all 10 fields that moved.

## [0.9.170] - 2026-07-25
The curator inspects only the wiki parts that actually changed, and stops rescanning the whole store every day.
### Improved
- **Curator cost follows the AMOUNT OF CHANGE, no longer the brain's size**: before, every curator round rescanned the entire wiki as if never seen. Measured on a real brain: early July cost 2.46M/round, late July already 5.22M/round - double in three weeks - while the number of turns grew only 16% (37 to 43); each turn's context swelled because every round re-read the whole store. That means the more the Second Brain grows, the more expensive background work gets, with no ceiling. Now the curator compares against the last scan mark and decides: if no wiki note changed it **skips the round entirely, no agent spawned**; if some changed, the prompt lists exactly those notes and forbids rescanning the whole wiki (`server/learn.py`).
- **Measured after the fix**: one round with 10/174 notes changed (a week's backlog) cost **1.62M**, versus 5.22M for a full-scan round - about 69% cheaper. And in practice 7 of the last 14 days had no wiki note changed, so those days now cost 0.
- **Full scan still runs periodically**: default once every 30 days (`curator.full_every_days`, set 0 to turn off) because inspecting only changes cannot see cross-page problems that build up over time. Also, deleting or renaming a note forces a full scan that round, because they create broken wikilinks on pages that did NOT change - something mtime cannot see. Adding a new note does not force it, that is routine and the new note is already in the changed list.
- **Skipping a round keeps the old mark**: if a skipped round also moved the mark up to now, notes edited earlier but not yet inspected would fall out of the window forever, silently never linted.
### Tests
- `server/test_curator_scope.py`: covers first run, no change, change, delete, rename, add note, full-scan due, periodic scan off, empty wiki, and pins the trap of keeping the mark when a round is skipped.

Now the filter text is kept and reapplied after every draw.

## [0.9.167] - 2026-07-25
Background work can run on models OUTSIDE Claude, and the curator stops scanning abandoned brains.
### Added
- **Choose the provider for the background model**: the "Auxiliary" field on the Models page used to be hard-locked to the `anthropic-cli` list (console.js read `providers.find(id==="anthropic-cli").models` directly), so all background work - loops, Kanban tasks, reminders, self-learning, source digestion - ate Claude quota with no way to change. Now this field lists EVERY connected provider (signed in or with a key), grouped by provider; whichever you pick, background work runs on that provider's plan/key (`server/aux_engine.py`).
- **Three kinds of background engine, differing in tools**: Claude Code stays as before (native file tools + Bash + MCP, blocked by per-call allowlist). Codex CLI is also a real agent (reads/writes files + MCP through the javis profile) and now receives `--sandbox` mapped from the loop's mode - suggest becomes `read-only`, auto becomes `workspace-write`, full keeps full access; before, Codex always ran with the sandbox bypassed so it could not be used for background work with a permission level (`server/claude_cli.py`). API models (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic API) have no native tools but use the hub's vault tools (`javis_read_file` / `javis_write_file` / `javis_use_skill` + MCP), and `javis_write_file` already blocks itself when the mode is suggest - so a read-only loop stays read-only on every engine.
- **Guard rail for broken configuration**: choosing a provider with no key or without Codex CLI installed makes background work SILENTLY fall back to Claude with a log line giving the reason, instead of dying midway. An unknown provider sent to `/settings` is forced to `anthropic-cli`.
### Improved
- **The curator stops scanning abandoned brains**: the `learn_config['brains']` list only APPENDS each time a new brain is chatted in and never shrinks - yet every curator round is a full Wiki LINT session for EACH brain. Measured: in July it ran 22 times and used 97M tokens across 4 brains, of which 1 was a nonexistent path and 2 were brains the user had abandoned for almost 3 weeks. Now the curator skips brains whose folder no longer exists, and brains silent for more than `curator.stale_days` (default 14 days), with a log stating which one is skipped and why (`server/learn.py`).
- **Freshness is measured by Memory/conversations, NOT by folder mtime**: the curator itself writes `Javis/learn-log` every round, so using the folder mtime would make every brain look "just active" and the curator would keep feeding its own reason to run on a dead brain.
### Tests
- `server/test_aux_engine.py`: default and old config (missing `provider`) still yield the Claude engine; switching to API inherits system_prompt/vault/mode; a missing key or unknown provider keeps Claude; mode maps correctly to the Codex sandbox and the sandbox really lands in the command line; the API engine gathers multiple text chunks into exactly one `final` event.
- `server/test_curator_targets.py`: skips a brain whose folder is gone, skips a cold brain, keeps a recently chatted brain, and pins that a fresh learn-log does NOT rescue a cold brain.

## [0.9.166] - 2026-07-25
Fully removed the BUSINESS METRICS card board. To see numbers, just ask directly and Jarvis 007 calls MCP to fetch them.

- **The metrics card board in the left column**: this board was already removed from the UI earlier (replaced by the Vault explorer), but all the machinery behind it still ran to feed a hidden stub nobody could see - every dashboard open was a full Claude session with MCP. Now removed completely: the `/metrics` endpoint and the cache layer just added in 0.9.165 (`server/main.py`), the entire card-building part in `dashboard/app.js` (`loadMetrics`, `renderMetrics`, `agenticFallbackCards`, `extractMetrics`, `pushMetricsToPanel`, the `savedMetrics` variable and its per-session save/restore), the hidden stub in `index.html`, and the `.metric-*` classes in `style.css`.

The control-block stripper for plain-text channels is KEPT and still strips every `JAVIS_*` alike - old memories in the brain still mention this block name, so it stays to be safe against leaking as-is into Telegram.
### Improved
- **`goal: business` loops fetch numbers via MCP themselves**: before, this loop was primed with metrics from the dashboard card job itself, and with no numbers it skipped the whole round with a reminder to "press ⟳ to load metrics" - the button no longer exists. Now the first step of each round is the loop calling MCP itself to fetch 3-6 metrics in priority order POS → channels → ads → other sources, and the report must state the number with its source.
