## [0.9.165] - 2026-07-25
Stopped a silent token drain: opening the dashboard no longer spawns a new agent every few minutes.
### Fixed
- **Dashboard metric cards burned quota with nobody using them**: measured on real session logs of the VPS build, the project "app" used 22M tokens, of which 402/502 sessions were exactly one repeated job - "create BUSINESS METRICS cards for the dashboard" (~16k tokens each, adding up to ~6.5M). The root was in `/metrics`: the cache was only 180 seconds, only in RAM, did not remember failures and did not merge duplicate requests, so almost every dashboard OPEN was a full Claude session with MCP. Now the cache defaults to 15 minutes (`METRICS_TTL`), is **written to disk** so restarts or auto-updates do not lose it, **remembers failed results too** for 2 minutes (`METRICS_ERR_TTL`) so a broken MCP does not respawn on every F5, and **merges duplicate requests** with one shared lock - opening the dashboard on phone and computer at the same time counts once (`server/main.py`).
- **The Token page named the project wrongly**: every Claude engine runs with `cwd` = the project root, not the brain folder, and Claude Code's raw log records only `cwd`, so Telegram chats, background work and dashboard jobs were all lumped into one project ("Javis-OS" when running on a machine, "app" in Docker) - it looked like coding on Jarvis 007 when in fact it was the owner's conversations on another brain. Now the engine records which session belongs to which brain (`server/session_brain.py`) and the token indexer uses the brain name as the label, so the numbers go to "My Bullet Journal", "Brain Default"... `cwd` is not touched because changing it would break `.claude/skills` discovery and the plugin's `vault_root`. Only effective for sessions run from this version on; old sessions keep their previous label.
### Tests
- Added `server/test_metrics_cache.py`: covers long/short TTL by result quality, a cache that survives restart, recompute on expiry, and the per-brain project label (including the case where the brain cannot be looked up and the old label is kept).

## [0.9.164] - 2026-07-25
Switching the Claude model now takes a LIVE LIST from Anthropic, so a new release shows up immediately.
### Improved
- **The "Anthropic OAuth (Claude Code)" provider lists models dynamically**: before, this provider could not query the API so the picker fell back to 4 static aliases in the code (opus/sonnet/haiku/fable) and was missing Opus 4.8, 4.7, 4.6, Sonnet 4.6... Now Jarvis 007 borrows the very OAuth access token Claude Code already saved (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` variable) to call `GET /v1/models`, so when Anthropic releases a new model the list appears on its own, with no code change (`server/claude_models.py`).
- **Aliases derived from the live list**: the 4 "always latest" names at the top of the picker are extracted from the model rows the API returns, so when a new model line appears its alias appears automatically.
- **Remembers the latest list in the catalog**: after each successful live fetch, `/provider/models` writes it back to `settings.json` (up to 50 entries). When offline or the OAuth token has expired, the fallback is still the NEWEST list ever seen, not a drop back to the old hardcoded aliases.
- Does not auto-refresh the OAuth token (to avoid rotating the `refresh_token` and logging the user's Claude Code out): an expired token quietly uses the fallback, and running Claude Code once makes it fresh again.

## [0.9.163] - 2026-07-24
Connections page: pinned the "Add your own (advanced)" card to the TOP of the store with a ⭐ icon, right followed by Composio.
### Improved
- **The "Add your own (advanced)" card moves to the top of the Connections store, icon changed from 🧩 to ⭐**: it used to sit at the end of the grid, so anyone wanting to enter their own URL/command had to scroll through the whole store to find it; the old icon also clashed with the newly added Composio.

## [0.9.162] - 2026-07-24
Added the Composio connector: ONE connection opens more than 500 apps that already have MCP (Gmail, Notion, Sheets, GitHub, Linear...), so Jarvis 007 does not have to write a separate connector for each app.
### Added
- **Composio connector (new "App store" group)**: connects connect.composio.dev/mcp with an API key (header x-consumer-api-key), goes through the hub and is subject to permissions like every other connector. 7 tools explicitly classified: finding and viewing tool descriptions is Read-only; connecting a new app (COMPOSIO_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS - Composio gives a link, the user logs in themselves) is Draft write; COMPOSIO_MULTI_EXECUTE_TOOL plus the 2 remote bash/workbench tools are classed DANGEROUS because every real app action (even read commands) runs through ONE shared tool, so Jarvis 007 cannot separate read from write inside it - to let Jarvis 007 act for real, you must deliberately raise the connection to Full access, and the guide and risk warning say this clearly. Background loops are still capped by mode as usual (suggest forces Read-only, auto forces Draft write).

## [0.9.161] - 2026-07-24
Google Keep has an oauth_token fallback when Google rejects the App Password (BadAuthentication).
### Fixed
- **Connecting Google Keep says 'Google rejected the login' even though the App Password is right**: Google is gradually tightening the route of exchanging an App Password for a master token (perform_master_login returns BadAuthentication depending on the account, even on a personal machine). Added the standard gkeepapi community fallback: a new oauth_token field in the form - the user opens accounts.google.com/EmbeddedSetup in an incognito tab (with a button to open it directly), signs in, takes the oauth_token cookie and pastes it in, and Jarvis 007 exchanges it via gpsoauth.exchange_token into a master token. The cookie is single-use, dropped without being stored and not mapped to env. The BadAuthentication message now lists only 3 possible causes along with this fallback, and the guide has step-by-step instructions to get the cookie.
### Improved
- **cred_exchange.run allows optional inputs to be left blank**: an input declared optional in auth.fields is no longer blocked as "Missing" from outside - the handler checks the combination itself (Keep needs an App Password OR an oauth_token, not both).
### Tests
- `test_cred_exchange.py` adds 9 checks: the oauth_token route exchanging via exchange_token (fake gpsoauth, no network), a BadAuthentication error must point to the fallback, an optional input reaches the handler, the oauth_token field is not mapped to env and is in the drop list, the EmbeddedSetup button. `test_google_keep.py` updated to count 5 input fields.

## [0.9.160] - 2026-07-24
Fixed "Cannot connect (ValueError)" when connecting Google Workspace: a tools/list response larger than 64KB blew asyncio's default line limit.
### Fixed
- **Connecting the Google Workspace connector says "Cannot connect (ValueError)"**: the tools/list of the workspace-mcp server is ONE NDJSON line of a few hundred KB (dozens of tools, long descriptions), exceeding the default 64KB/line StreamReader limit of asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, so readline() blew up with LimitOverrunError disguised as ValueError. Raised the limit to 16MB for every stdio MCP session. Other stdio connectors were unaffected only because their responses are still under 64KB.
- **Connection error messages include the real error content**: before, only the error type name was shown (e.g. "ValueError") so there was no clue to trace; now it includes a shortened message too.
### Tests
- Added `test_stdio_big_line.py`: a fake MCP server returns tools/list as one ~200KB line, which must be read fully without blowing up, with a canary proving the scenario really exceeds the 64KB limit.

## [0.9.159] - 2026-07-24
Connecting Google Calendar/Gmail no longer ends up "connected but without permission": the guide adds 2 mandatory Google requirements, and the Test button reports the right cause.
### Fixed
- **Google Calendar/Gmail OAuth done but still "no permission" (reported by a real user)**: Google's hosted MCP servers (calendarmcp/gmailmcp.googleapis.com) require 2 things the old guide did not mention: enrolling in the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program (free) and enabling a SEPARATE MCP API (Google Calendar MCP API / Gmail MCP API) next to the regular API. Without them Google blocks with 403 even though sign-in succeeds, easy to misread because the "connected" status stays green (Google's tools/list needs no token, only tools/call does). The guides for the 2 connectors are rewritten with all 6 steps, adding buttons that open the enrollment page and the API enabling page directly. Not a brain/model error: the Test button runs entirely server-side, not through the engine.
- **The Test button translates Google errors into the right advice**: replaces the generic sentence "Key is wrong or lacks permission" with recognition of 3 error families: API not enabled in the project (with the exact enabling link taken from Google's message, reminding to enroll in the preview if it is a *mcp.googleapis.com server), token missing scope because a box was unticked at consent (advises signing in again and ticking everything), broken/expired token (advises signing in again). Unknown errors keep the old behavior.
### Tests
- Added `test_loi_ket_noi_google.py`: 15 checks for the error translator (API not enabled with/without an MCP server, missing scope, broken token, fallback + canary, UI strings with Vietnamese diacritics, and a check that validate_connection really goes through the translator).

## [0.9.158] - 2026-07-23
The connection store adds Google Tasks, along with a fix to permission classification of Google Workspace's combined manage_* tools.
### Added
- **Google Tasks connector**: read and manage to-dos in Google Tasks (view lists, add tasks, set due dates, mark done). Runs on the same `workspace-mcp` server as the Google Workspace connector but loads only the tasks service at the complete tier - because `list_task_lists` (looking up the task list ID, which every other tasks tool needs) exists only at the complete tier, and the core-tier Google Workspace connector using Tasks would hit a dead end. Asks only for Google Tasks permission, not touching Gmail/Drive/Calendar; if you already have a Google Workspace OAuth client it can be reused, you only need to additionally enable the Google Tasks API. Considered and did NOT choose gtasks-mcp (zcaceres): that server breaks the credential path on Windows (`new URL(...).pathname` gives `\D:\...`), its token does not auto-refresh (dies after ~1 hour and must be re-authed by hand), it is not on npm so you must clone and build it yourself, and it forces running an auth command manually - against the principle of connecting through the UI.
### Security
- **Fixed a classification hole for Google Workspace `manage_*` tools**: `manage_task`, `manage_event`, `manage_gmail_label`... matched no write/danger pattern and the word "manage" was not in the heuristic either, so they were wrongly classed as "read" - a connection set to Read-only (or a suggest loop) still let Jarvis 007 edit/delete real calendar events and tasks. Added a `*manage*` pattern to the write group and stated it clearly in the risk warning.

## [0.9.157] - 2026-07-23
ChatGPT (Codex) can use its own native MCP store, on par with how the Claude engine uses Claude Code's native MCP.
### Added
- **The Connections page gets a new "MCP from Codex (ChatGPT)" section**: lists the servers in the native MCP store of Codex CLI (what you registered yourself with `codex mcp add`, kept in Codex's native config), alongside the existing "MCP from Claude Code" section. The ChatGPT engine already loaded this store itself when running (the javis profile only layers Jarvis 007's MCP ON TOP of the native config, not overriding it), but before, Jarvis 007 could not see or manage it so users hardly knew what tools ChatGPT had. The `/mcp/ambient` endpoint also returns `codex_servers`; also supports older codex versions without `mcp list --json` (reads the text table).
- **OAuth-type MCP servers now register for BOTH CLIs**: OAuth servers cannot go through the hub (the CLI must hold the token itself), so before, adding one in the "Add your own (advanced)" form registered only into Claude Code (`claude mcp add`) - the ChatGPT engine did not see this group at all. Now Jarvis 007 also registers into Codex's native store (best-effort, skipped if codex is not installed, without blocking the flow), and deleting a server removes it from both. Authenticate once with `codex mcp login <name>`; the `/mcp/oauth-auth` endpoint accepts `{"engine":"codex","name":...}` to open a terminal with that command ready (local machine with a screen), and `/mcp/native-status` accepts `engine=codex` to check login status.
### Tests
- Added `test_codex_native_mcp.py`: parses `codex mcp list --json` output (3 different JSON shapes across codex versions + disabled/needs-login states), the text table fallback, and builds the `codex mcp add` argv (HTTP, bearer env, stdio). All parse functions are pure so the test does not need Codex installed.

## [0.9.156] - 2026-07-22
Reports the right cause when Facebook retires mbasic (instead of wrongly blaming the cookie).
### Fixed
- **Distinguish "mbasic no longer served" from "cookie broken"**: Facebook is retiring `mbasic.facebook.com`, which redirects (302) to `m.facebook.com` even though the cookie is still logged in fine. Before, the tool wrongly reported "cookie rejected", sending users to fetch the cookie again for nothing. Now `_fetch` notices when it is kicked off the mbasic host and returns the right message: mbasic may have been discontinued by Facebook, the cookie is not the cause, and reading the feed/personal actions needs a real browser or a switch to a supported source (Pages via Graph API, public tracking via Apify).

Now the overwrite is removed, wikilinks in the editor also call this existing bridge, and a warning comment was added right at the function to prevent a repeat.

Fixed broken-cookie detection in the personal Facebook plugin.

## [0.9.152] - 2026-07-22
Wikipedia-style navigation in the vault: .md file paths in chat are clickable to open for reading/editing right away, and wikilinks [[..]] are clickable when reading a note to jump to the target note.
### Added
- **File paths in chat are clickable**: when Jarvis 007 mentions a file like `Javis/loops/x.md` in the chat (as inline code), clicking it now opens a read/edit panel in the middle of the screen, with no need to hunt in the Files page. ## [0.9.150] - 2026-07-21
Fixed Jarvis 007 (running on Claude) reporting that sources connected to the Claude account (Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar...) were "not connected" while lean tool mode is on, even though they could actually be called.
### Fixed
- **Claude account MCP not seen when lean (lazy) tools is on**: connectors attached directly to the Claude account (Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar... synced from claude.ai) are native tools of the Claude engine and do NOT go through the Jarvis 007 hub. But the source listing (javis_connections) and the tool search box of lean tool mode knew only the sources managed by Jarvis 007 (POS, Substack...), so Jarvis 007 looked up the list, saw "only POS and Substack" and wrongly concluded "Drive not connected" even though the user had connected it. Now the hub reads the Claude account's MCP list itself (the ones "Connected") and attaches it to both javis_connections and the tool search results, stating clearly that these are tools called DIRECTLY (mcp__<name>__...), not wrapped by the hub's run tool. Jarvis 007 no longer denies a source already connected in the account.
### Improved
- The Claude account source list is read in a background thread and cached because the listing command is a bit slow, so it does not slow down answers. Only the Claude engine gets this hint (Codex and API engines have no such native tools so they do not get it, to avoid pointing at a tool that does not exist). Can be turned off in settings `mcp.ambient_hint` if not wanted.
### Tests
- Added tests for reading the account MCP list (taking only those "Connected"), matching sources by name/prefix, attaching correctly to javis_connections and the tool search box, and pinning that the API engine (in-process path) is not wrongly given the account hint.

## [0.9.149] - 2026-07-21
Fixed a repeating task with no declared goal being wrongly run as business analysis, and removed the default repeating task "Self-improve Jarvis 007" from the app.
### Fixed
- **A repeating task missing a declared goal was wrongly run as a business report**: a repeating task (loop) whose definition file did not state a goal line defaulted to "improve business metrics", so it ignored the content written for the task and went off reading sales numbers. For example a "remind to take medicine" task read POS revenue and discussed orders instead of reminding about medicine. Now the default is to run exactly the content written in the file; for a repeating task to inject business numbers every round, a business goal must be declared explicitly. The two paths to create a repeating task (via chat and via the Work page) already set it correctly; only the file re-read step was off, which is how it slipped through.
### Improved
- **Removed the default repeating task "Self-improve Jarvis 007"**: dropped the self-improvement system loop from the app entirely; it is no longer installed into any brain. A brain that already has the old copy only needs to delete it once on the Work page, and from this version it will not grow back.
### Tests
- Added a test pinning the repeating task goal default to run exactly the file content (not falling back to business), and a test confirming that with no system loop left in the app the sync mechanism still works correctly.

## [0.9.148] - 2026-07-21
Fixed reminders created via chat while using another brain (e.g. My Bullet Journal) landing in Brain Default.
### Fixed
- **Reminders landed in Brain Default even when chatting in another brain**: when setting a reminder from Telegram or the dashboard, Jarvis 007 often used the sample curl command in the guide to call the reminder store, and that sample command did NOT include the selected brain. The curl command runs from the sandbox so it carries no login session, and the brain can travel only inside the command content; without it the reminder store silently uses Brain Default. Result: with the brain My Bullet Journal selected, a reminder was set but it ended up in Default. Now the sample command automatically includes the session's brain, and calling the javis_schedule tool directly (which always attaches the right brain) is preferred. The reminder store also logs when it receives a reminder missing a brain so it is easier to inspect if it recurs.

## [0.9.147] - 2026-07-21
Added the /notes command on Telegram to quickly save a message (with image) into the brain's Sources, like the web chat.
### Added
- **/notes command on Telegram**: before, only the web chat had /notes to quickly capture a note into the Second Brain, and it was not in the Telegram command menu. Now /notes is in the Telegram command menu (type "/" to see it), saves the message verbatim into Sources and then distills it up to the wiki if worthwhile, same as the web version.
- **Send an image with /notes**: sending a photo with the caption "/notes ..." is now correctly recognized as the command, and the image is downloaded and attached to the note. Before, the command caption was buried in the attachment description text so it did not run as a command, even though this is the most common use case: photograph something and save it straight into the brain.
### Tests
- Added tests for the Telegram command list and for extracting the command from an image caption (keeping the image path for the skill to use).

## [0.9.146] - 2026-07-21
Added a "lean tools" mode for MCP: when many sources are connected, Jarvis 007 no longer preloads hundreds of tools into every message and instead opens exactly the tools needed when the context calls for it, saving a lot of tokens.
### Added
- **Lean tools (lazy tools) mode for MCP**: before, every question, even one unrelated to sales or ads, had to carry the full tool descriptions of EVERY connected source (POS, Meta Ads, Systeme.io, Webcake...), costing a lot of tokens even when unused. Now when the total tool count passes a threshold, Jarvis 007 gives the model only a compact menu listing which sources exist, plus two mechanical tools: one to FIND tools by need, one to CALL the tool found. The model decides each message whether any source is needed and only then opens exactly that tool group. Chit-chat, translation and writing cost almost no tool tokens; a question needing numbers opens the right source on its own. No manual on/off needed.
### Improved
- This mode turns on automatically when there are many tools (default above 40) and off when few; adjustable in settings `mcp.lazy_tools` (auto/on/off), `mcp.lazy_threshold` (tool count threshold), `mcp.lazy_top_k` (number of tools returned per search). Small, frequently used internal tools (read/write files, image generation, reminders, Zalo sending...) still show directly as before; only the crowded group of outside-source tools is gathered behind the menu.
- The permission layer, logging and rate limiting are unchanged because every tool call still goes through the same old path. Added tests for tool search ranking, hiding/showing the right group, and the error branches when calling.

## [0.9.145] - 2026-07-21
Fixed the tick selecting a watched chat on Zalo disappearing after a page reload or server restart.
### Fixed
- **The watch tick disappeared on reload**: the chat list in the panel was drawn only from an in-memory scratch ledger (rebuilt from incoming messages), and this ledger is empty every time the server restarts. The watch rules were still intact on disk but there was no row to show, so the tick vanished even though watching was actually still on. Now the panel draws from the UNION of the scratch ledger and the enabled rules, and the server reloads the ledger from the rules right at startup, so a watched chat always shows and can be ticked right away, without waiting for a new message to pass through.
- **Two chats with the same name overwrote each other's rules**: the rule file used to be named by the chat NAME, while the system deliberately gives the same name to groups with unknown names. Two different groups with the same name wrote to one file, and saving the later one erased the earlier one's rule, so its tick disappeared on reload. Now the file name embeds the chat ID directly so they cannot collide.
- **Saving an empty list wiped out all watching**: the old web build sent the old data shape, which was misread as "drop everything", turning off every active watch rule. Now watching is dropped only when the owner clearly sends a new list.
- **Groups shown as individuals after restart**: rules now record whether the chat is a group or a customer, so after a restart the group label is still built correctly and messages are sent in the right group style, no more mix-ups.
- Cleaned up old stray config keys (threads, dm_only, keywords) left in settings, so they do not leak back into the interface's keyword box and flip a watched chat into keyword filtering.
### Note
- If the server is running an old version you must RESTART the server and reload the page (Ctrl+F5) for this fix to take effect. The old version could not write the tick to disk, so reloading loses it.

## [0.9.144] - 2026-07-21
Fixed the Zalo listening panel always showing "Disconnected, retrying" even though it was actually listening normally.
### Fixed
- **Stuck in the "Disconnected" state even though the connection was alive**: whenever the network blinked, the Zalo library reconnected right away underneath WITHOUT printing any notice line, so the control panel had nothing to tell it had reconnected and stayed at "retrying" forever. Also, the line announcing a successful reconnect in the re-login branch carried the text "events:" and was swallowed by the startup line filter. The result: a single network drop left the red label sitting there, temporarily clearing only when a new message arrived within three minutes, even though the listening process was alive and messages kept coming.
- Now Jarvis 007 recognizes the recovery lines correctly and pulls the status back to listening. For the silent reconnect case (no line printed), if the listening process is still alive and a quiet period has passed with no new drop line, it counts as reconnected. A real drop makes the library print drop lines regularly so it still correctly reports retrying; and a process that died completely is still left to the rebuild mechanism, not misrecognized.
- Added tests pinning both recovery paths and the silent reconnect case.

## [0.9.143] - 2026-07-21
Fully removed the feature where Jarvis 007 auto-replies to customers on Zalo. Now Jarvis 007 only reads and reports, and every outgoing message is directly requested by the owner.
### Improved
- **Zalo is read and report only, no more auto-reply**: removed the "Auto-reply" (chatbot) mode along with the entire sandbox engine part that composed automatic messages for customers. The listener now only listens then reports to Telegram by each chat's rule, with the four modes kept: silent, report all, report by keyword, and remind when too long without anyone replying. To send a message to someone, the owner tells it directly in chat and Jarvis 007 uses the safe sending tool javis_zalo_send.
- The "Continuous listening" panel is simpler: each chat now has only a watch tick for read and report, removing the two-option mode selector and the confirmation dialog for self-messaging.
- Cleaned up the Zalo code: removed the bot's message composing function, the sandbox constants, the hourly message limit, and the auxiliary model dependency that only the auto-reply mode needed.
### Safety
- There is no path left for Jarvis 007 to send messages to customers on its own when it reads their messages. Old rule files with chatbot mode are automatically lowered to silent on read, so after updating no group auto-replies.

## [0.9.142] - 2026-07-21
Fixed a serious bug: telling Jarvis 007 to send a Zalo message to one person made it message someone else not on the watch list.
### Fixed
- **Sending a Zalo message via chat could go to the wrong account and the wrong person**: when listening on an account is turned on, the listener turns off that account's connector, so when the owner asked to send a message the engine quietly fell to another Zalo account that was on, looked up the recipient name in the wrong account's contacts and sent from the wrong account. There was no confirmation step so the message flew out immediately and could not be recalled. This was the result of the connector auto-off mechanism plus the engine being free to send without being sure of the right person.
- Added a dedicated safe Zalo sending tool, hard-locked to the listening account and able to send only to a chat in the watched list, so structurally it cannot send to the wrong account or person. If a name matches several, the tool refuses and makes you ask back, no guessing. If it is not in the watch list, it refuses.
- Told Jarvis 007 in the system guide to use this safe tool when asked to send a message, and never to use the raw tool.
### Safety
- The sending tool is at the safe permission level, so a background loop running in read-only mode cannot send messages on its own. It sends only when the owner asks directly in chat.

## [0.9.141] - 2026-07-20
Fixed images that Jarvis 007 created during a Telegram chat always going to the first Telegram account instead of the person asking.
### Fixed
- **Image went to the bot owner when two people chat**: when Jarvis 007 creates an image, it is saved into the brain's attachments folder and embedded in the answer with a relative path like `![](attachments/anh.png)`. The auto-attach-files-to-Telegram mechanism used to accept only ABSOLUTE paths or files written with the Write tool, so created images were not auto-attached. The engine had to send the image with a curl command, and this command lacked the recipient ID so it fell to the first Telegram account in the list. The result: the second person chatting still saw their image fly to the first person's device.
- Now the auto-attach mechanism also understands relative paths in the vault (e.g. `attachments/...`), resolves them against the brain root of the session actually chatting and sends directly to the person asking, with no curl needed. It blocks vault escape (no `../` going outside) and ignores web links. The gateway also reminds the engine that a just-created image only needs to be embedded, no curl (curl easily sends to the bot owner by mistake).
- Added tests pinning file collection: a relative embedded image is caught correctly, absolute paths still work, a URL is not mistaken for a file, vault escape is blocked, and old files are not resent.

## [0.9.140] - 2026-07-20
Fixed pressing Start listening showing Enabled and then immediately reverting to Start listening with nothing happening.
### Fixed
- **The Start listening button threw a silent error and then reset itself**: version 0.9.136 renamed a variable in the interface but missed one place using the old name, so when clicking Start listening the code building the data to send referenced a variable that no longer exists and threw an error. The button is programmed to always re-enable itself so it went back to Start listening, and the command never reached the server. There was no message so it looked like no reaction.
- Fixed that missed spot, and also updated the description and panel layout to the two-state Read-only and Auto-reply design that 0.9.136 applied incompletely.
- Added a pinning test so this kind of missed-rename bug does not slip through again.

## [0.9.139] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the root bug that made every interface change in several recent versions invisible to the browser.
### Fixed
- **The browser kept the old interface in its cache forever**: each javascript and css file was version-numbered by hand in the home page, and the console.js number stood still for dozens of versions. Because the load address did not change, the browser kept using the old copy in its cache, the server really updated but the interface froze. This is why changes like the two-state design, buttons no longer sinking, and timeouts were all on the server but users never saw them.
- Now the home page automatically attaches the app version to every javascript and css file when serving, so every update makes the browser reload everything, with no hand-bumping of numbers and no way to forget.

## [0.9.138] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the Start listening button sinking forever after a click, neither turning on nor resetting.
### Fixed
- **The start listening endpoint blocked the whole event loop**: it wrote config, decrypted the connection and waited for the old thread to stop, all done synchronously inside the async function, so during that time the server could serve nothing else and the button hung. Now the heavy part runs in its own thread, so the loop is not clogged.
- **Waiting too long for the old thread**: when re-enabling right after turning off, it used to wait up to fifteen seconds. Now it kills the child process first and waits only four seconds, because once stopped it exits right away.
- **The button did not reset when the request failed**: the step to re-enable the button was missing in every case, so a slow or failed request left the button stuck permanently. Now the button is always re-enabled, and the call has a thirty-second timeout, past which it says the server is not responding instead of sinking forever.

## [0.9.137] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the report of no Zalo account selected while the selector clearly showed an account name.
### Fixed
- **The account selector showed a name but it was never saved**: that value was written only when pressing Start listening, while pressing Save watching did not send it, so the config stayed empty and the message, though confusing, was correct. Now saving watching also writes the selected account, and changing the account in the selector saves immediately.
- **An old error message sat on screen**: since 0.9.132 the interface shows errors even when off, but the stop command did not clear the old error, so one failed start from some time ago kept showing and made it look broken. Now stopping listening clears it.

## [0.9.136] - 2026-07-20
Each Zalo chat now has only two easy-to-understand states, and Jarvis 007 decides for itself when to speak up.
### Changed
- **Two states replace five modes**: each chat in the list has a selector with two options, Read-only and Auto-reply. Much simpler than the old way, and anything more sophisticated is just told directly in chat.
### Added
- **Jarvis 007 is allowed to stay silent**: in auto-reply mode it decides whether to speak up instead of answering every message. When people are talking among themselves, chatting, or about something unrelated, it stays quiet. Before, the bot always had to produce a reply, and a bot that interjects in every conversation in a group is more annoying than no bot.
- **Free to phrase things by context** instead of sticking to existing wording, and to speak in each group's own style if the owner specified it in the rule.
- **Turning on auto-reply needs confirmation once**, because a sent message cannot be recalled.
### Security
- The sandbox is kept as is: the bot has no tools, sees no business data, and only produces text, while where it is sent is decided by Jarvis 007 code.
- Kept one hard barrier even when the owner allows creative freedom: it must not make up prices, stock, delivery times or commitments to customers. One wrong sentence there costs real money, so when it comes up it asks the owner back.

## [0.9.135] - 2026-07-20
Jarvis 007 cleans up the pile of noisy rules produced by its own broken default, instead of making the owner fix each one by hand.
### Fixed
- **Changing the default did not rescue rules already created**: version 0.9.131 switched the default to silent but applied it only to new rules, while chats already ticked since 0.9.130 still carried the report-every-message mode and so still flooded Telegram. Three times before, Jarvis 007 only told the owner to press Save again, pushing the cleanup of the consequences onto the user. Now at startup Jarvis 007 switches them to silent exactly once, and tells the owner what it fixed.
- It touches only report-all rules with no keywords, because that is precisely the trace of the broken default. Rules with keywords, remind-on-no-reply rules, and rules letting Jarvis 007 auto-reply are all deliberately set by the owner so they are kept.
- The cleanup runs exactly once, and later startups do not overwrite rules the owner set again.

## [0.9.134] - 2026-07-20
No more red duplicate-session warnings after an update, and no more having to delete the connection and rescan the QR code.
### Fixed
- **The listener was not closed properly when the app shut down**: during an update the process was stopped abruptly before it could close the connection, so Zalo's side still treated the old session as alive and blocked the new listener. Now when the server shuts down it closes the listener first, sending a gentle stop signal so the tool can disconnect cleanly.
- **A duplicate session was treated as a hard error from the first time**: right after a restart a duplicate session is normal and clears on its own after a few dozen seconds, but the listener stopped completely and made the owner delete the connection and rescan the QR code unfairly. Now it patiently retries five times with growing wait intervals, saying clearly that it is waiting for the old session to drop and that this is normal after an update. Only after patience runs out does it conclude, with the number of tries.
- **Cleaning up old processes also interrupts gently first**: they are the ones holding the Zalo session, and killing them outright leaves the session hanging, exactly the vicious circle just removed.

## [0.9.133] - 2026-07-20
Jarvis 007 now knows to set Zalo rules when told in words, instead of only writing it into memory and stopping.
### Fixed
- **A verbal instruction was only remembered, not turned into action**: the owner said to just reply freely with this account, Jarvis 007 answered that it had remembered and created a preference file in memory, but created no rule so behavior did not change. The cause is that the system guide did not mention Zalo at all, so Jarvis 007 did not know there was a rule-setting tool to use and fell back to its default habit of recording a preference.
- Added setting Zalo rules to the list of ways to handle requests received via chat, with a choosing rule stating plainly that remembering does not change behavior, there must be a rule file for the listener to really stay silent, report, or auto-reply.
- The tool description was rewritten using the exact sentences users tend to say, for example stop reporting, just be silent, report all messages of this group, remind me if no one replies in thirty minutes, just reply freely with this account.

## [0.9.132] - 2026-07-20
Fixed Zalo rules set by words in chat that the listener never applied.
### Fixed
- **Written in one place, read from another**: when the owner gave an instruction in words, the tool wrote the rule file into the open brain, for example My Bullet Journal. But the listener is a background service so it read only the default brain, Brain Default. A rule set by words landed where nobody reads it, so telling it to stop reporting still got reports. Now the listener gathers rules from every brain, removing this whole class of bug.
- When the same chat has rules in two different brains, the most recently edited copy is taken, instead of picking one at random.
### Notes
- Old rules created in version 0.9.130 are still report-all, because the default change in 0.9.131 applies only to newly created rules. To be silent, press Save watching once more with the keyword box left empty, or tell Jarvis 007 in chat.

## [0.9.131] - 2026-07-20
By default Jarvis 007 stays silent when watching a Zalo chat, no longer flooding Telegram with every message.
### Changed
- **The watch tick now defaults to silent**: it only records the chat and does not report to Telegram. Before, ticking meant reporting every message, and watching a few busy groups made the phone explode until nobody read it anymore. Listening is for Jarvis 007 to know what is going on, while reporting must be something the owner actively asks for per group.
- **To be notified, say so clearly**: enter keywords in the box below to be notified only when a message contains those words, or tell Jarvis 007 in chat per group, for example report all messages of this group, or remind me when thirty minutes pass with no reply.
- The confirmation line after saving states clearly whether it is silent or reporting by which keywords, to avoid misunderstanding that you will be notified.

## [0.9.130] - 2026-07-20
Fixed ticking a chat to watch that saved nothing, and added a save button with a visible confirmation.
### Fixed
- **Ticking saved nothing at all**: since moving to per-chat rules, the interface still sent the list in the old config shape, while the config writer accepted only fields still in the default shape so the list was silently thrown away. This was an architecture migration bug where the interface was never reconnected. Now ticking writes a real rule file in the brain.
- **The tick box showed the wrong state**: it read from the dropped config field, so rules set via chat did not show up and vice versa. Now it takes directly from the active rules, and redraws itself when rules change.
### Added
- **Save watching button with a confirmation line**: press it and immediately see how many chats were saved and in what way. Before, saving was hidden so there was no way to know whether it took effect. The keyword box and quiet hours are saved together too; before, those two boxes were written only on toggle on/off, so an edit without toggling was lost.
### Security
- **One tick must not erase hard work**: for chatbot-mode or remind-when-no-reply rules the owner carefully set via chat, ticking only turns them on or off and never overwrites the mode and script. Unticking also only turns the rule off without deleting the file, so the written script stays intact.

## [0.9.129] - 2026-07-20
Zalo groups can now be told apart in the chat list, instead of all showing the sender's name.
### Fixed
- **Groups showed the sender's name rather than the group name**: the incoming message data does not include the group name at all. The previous version guessed the field name without being able to verify, so in practice it still fell back to the sender's name, and two different groups with the same person messaging looked identical.
### Added
- **Distinguishable at once**: a group with no real name yet shows the last four digits of the group ID, so no two rows are the same.
- **Fetch group names button**: asks Zalo for the real names of all groups in one call and attaches them to the list. It is a manual button and not run silently in the background, because each call opens a short connection that makes the listener reconnect for a beat.
- The result reader accepts many different formats and never errors on unfamiliar data, because the tool's output format cannot be verified without a real logged-in account.

## [0.9.128] - 2026-07-20
Fixed reporting a lost connection while it was actually listening normally and messages kept arriving.
### Fixed
- **A declaration line misread as an incident**: the tool prints a notice line that auto-reconnect is enabled, right after the line announcing it started listening. The log reader matched strings too crudely and read that declaration as losing connection, overwriting the correct status and getting stuck there. Now it accepts only real incident lines, and ignores lines listing capabilities, events or the webhook address.
- **Added a source of truth more reliable than the log**: if a message arrived within the last three minutes the connection is certainly alive, so the status reports listening regardless of what the log suggests. Inferring status from the log is fragile because the tool's wording can change at any time. Hard errors like a duplicate session are not masked, because those must be fixed by a person and then re-enabled.

## [0.9.127] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the blindness of the Zalo process detector on the server: it always reported finding nothing, even when a process was actually holding the connection.
### Fixed
- **The process detector could not run in Docker**: it called the pgrep command, while the Docker image installs only ca-certificates, curl, git, ripgrep, ffmpeg and tini, with no package containing pgrep. The command threw an error, swallowed, so the status page always reported no stray process while the listener kept being kicked out. A false zero is worse than no number because it leads to ruling out the real cause. Now it reads the system's process directory directly, which is always there with no package to install.
- **Missed the QR login session**: the cleaner used to look only for the listening process and the connector's process, while a QR login session that has not exited also holds a connection for the same account. Now it scans all three kinds.
- **No longer kills its own child process**: excluded by process group, avoiding turning off right after turning on.
### Improved
- The process directory path is split into a constant so tests can run on both Windows and Linux. Before, the Linux branch was never tested, which is exactly why the blindness slipped through.

## [0.9.126] - 2026-07-20
Settled Zalo duplicate sessions for good: the listener automatically turns off that account's own connector when enabled, and cleans up the connector's process, not just the listening process.
### Fixed
- **The Zalo connector was the thing kicking the listener**: it holds a long-lived connection for the same account, while Zalo allows only one connection per account. The previous version only changed the message sending path, while the connector itself stayed on and kept competing for the slot. Now enabling listening makes Jarvis 007 turn off the connector of exactly that account, and stopping listening turns it back on as before, and it tells the owner plainly instead of silently losing the tool.
- **The old process cleaner missed some**: the previous version looked only for the listening process and did not touch the connector's process, so the thing holding the connection stayed alive. Now it scans both.
### Notes
- Since version 0.9.124 the listener does not need the connector anymore, handling both listening and sending itself, so temporarily turning off the connector loses no function.

## [0.9.125] - 2026-07-20
Automatically cleans up leftover old listening processes, and adds a way to completely delete the Zalo login session when a duplicate session occurs and logging out does not help.
### Added
- **Enabling listening cleans up before starting**: orphaned listening processes from earlier versions keep a live connection and kick the new listener out right away. Logging out elsewhere cannot kill it because an already open connection simply stays alive. Now every time it is enabled, Jarvis 007 finds and cleans them first, so the owner does not need to hunt for processes on the server.
- **Delete login session button**: shown only during a duplicate session. Needed because the tool's logout command deliberately keeps the login info to log back in automatically next time, so logging out cannot remove a stuck session. After deleting, scan the QR again and it is clean.
- **States clearly how many old processes were found** instead of leaving the owner to guess why the session is duplicated.
### Security
- **Blocked a destructive bug before release**: the first version of the process detector filtered by command line, but the query itself contained the very words being searched so it caught itself, and the cleanup command killed the whole process tree. Now it inspects only node processes and excludes the probe query itself. A test pins this.
- **Session deletion is fenced inside the connector's own session folder**, so a tampered connection ID cannot make Jarvis 007 delete another folder.

## [0.9.124] - 2026-07-20
Handled the one-connection-per-Zalo-account collision, which was noted as unverified from the first version and has now really happened on the server.
### Fixed
- **The listener was kicked out repeatedly**: the real log said another connection was opened so this one was closed, every few minutes. The cause is that the message sending path went through the Zalo connector, and the connector holds a long-lived connection for the same account so it kicked the listener, then the listener reconnected and kicked it back. Now messages are sent with a one-shot command that opens the connection for only an instant and exits.
- **No more pointless looping**: the Zalo library's error string in this case was not in the hard-error recognizer, so the listener thought it was an ordinary network drop and kept retrying forever. Now it recognizes it properly, stops and says clearly what to check: whether the Zalo connector is turned off, whether Zalo Web is open, whether any old listener is still running.
- **Log no longer has junk characters**: strips color codes before display, ending the sight of fragments like ESC bracket 31m ERROR.
- **Groups show the right group name**: before, the chat ledger used the sender's name as the group name so two different groups showed one name and could not be told apart. Now the group name takes priority, and a later sender does not overwrite a name already known.

## [0.9.123] - 2026-07-20
Zalo moves from one shared notification filter to a separate policy per chat, set by words via chat. Added a mode where Jarvis 007 replies to customers like a chatbot, running in a sandbox.
### Added
- **One rule per chat**, written to `Javis/zalo/<slug>.md` in the brain so it has git, and can be reviewed and edited by hand. Five modes: record only, report every message, report by keyword, remind when N minutes pass with no reply, and auto-reply to customers by script.
- **Set rules by words**: the `javis_zalo_rule` tool lets you say it directly in chat or Telegram, for example for this group if no one replies in 30 minutes, remind me. The interface only displays rules, with no input form. If the group name matches more than one, the tool refuses with a list and does not guess, because attaching a script to the wrong group means the bot replies to another group's customers.
- **Remind when a reply is forgotten**: if a customer messages and N minutes pass with no answer, it reports to Telegram exactly once. This works because Jarvis 007 has its own Zalo account, so the owner replying with their own account is another member of the group and the owner's messages come in fully.
- **Chatbot mode**: Jarvis 007 replies to customers by each group's own script, with a per-hour message cap, and escalates to the owner on its own when something is outside the script.
### Security
- **Sandbox for the chatbot**: the engine runs with no tools, sees no MCP, and carries no memory or brain. The model only produces text, while where it is sent is decided by Jarvis 007 code and always goes back to the exact chat that produced the message, so even if fully tricked it cannot message anyone else.
- **Patched a dangerous trap in the engine layer**: the tool list check condition allowed an empty list to be treated as nothing set, so the most intuitive way to build a sandbox actually opened full permission and also loaded the machine's existing MCP, right when content composed by strangers enters the engine. Now it passes a nonexistent tool name so the permission gate really turns on, and a test pins this.
- The other four modes still do not touch the engine, keeping the previous version's barriers.
- Chatbot mode is always created in the off state, and the owner must enable it separately after hearing the script again.

## [0.9.122] - 2026-07-20
Zalo groups now appear to be selected, the chat list withstands hundreds of groups, and the orphaned child process bug is finally cleaned up.
### Fixed
- **Group messages never appeared**: the listening tool by default sends only two event types, messages and friends, with the group type missing. Now all four types are declared. Also the chat ledger used to record only message events, so right after adding the account to a group with nobody messaging yet, the group did not appear. Now every event that has a chat is recorded, so adding to a group shows it right away.
- **Orphaned child processes**: npx is only a shell, and the node inside is what holds the connection. The old stop command killed only the shell so node kept running and kept pushing messages, causing the interface to report the process not running while messages kept flowing. Now the whole process tree is cleaned up, with taskkill on Windows and killpg on Linux.
- **Re-enabling while the old thread was mid-stop**: before, it returned "already running" without building a new thread, the stop flag stayed on so the old thread exited and left the off state while the config said on. Now it waits for the old thread to fully exit and only then builds the new one.
- **No flood of old messages on reconnect**: excludes events that replay history and mark as seen, avoiding a bulk dump of old messages into Telegram every reconnect.
### Improved
- **The chat list is usable with hundreds of groups**: added a search box, shows only the 8 most recent chats by default and has a show more button. A chat being watched is always pinned to the top and never cut, so it can always be unticked. The memory cap was raised from 60 to 300.
- **Broader message recognition**: also accepts event name variants such as group message, because the tool's event names have no final documentation.
- **Added an event type counter** on the status page, so next time something that should appear does not, you can see the truth instead of guessing.

## [0.9.121] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the Zalo listener still showing "Off" after pressing On and receiving no messages. This was a fully blocking bug: in earlier versions the listener NEVER managed to start, it was not that it ran and then broke.
### Fixed
- **Took the login session folder from the wrong source**: the place that looks up the session folder read through mcp_store.get_connection, and that function returns a copy with secrets masked and the config field stripped, so the path was always empty and every enable failed right at the check step. Switched to reading from mcp_store.resolved, which is also where the home folder is computed for isolated connectors, so the listener and connector no longer diverge.
- **A failed enable was still recorded as enabled**: the enable endpoint wrote the enabled flag first and only then checked, and when the check failed it did not roll back, leaving the exact sight of an "Off" label sitting next to an "Off" button while the list said it was listening. Now it enables only after the check passes.
- **The error reason was wiped after 5 seconds**: the status polling overwrote the error line that had just appeared, so the owner could not read it in time. Now the reason is kept in the background process and shown even when off.
- **Error messages now include the concrete path** instead of just saying generally that it is not logged in.
### Improved
- **The background thread no longer dies silently**: every unexpected error is turned into a readable status instead of leaving the status standing at its old value and the interface reporting wrongly.
- **Distinguishes a hard failure from a network drop**: a sidecar that starts and exits immediately 3 times is stopped for good and the tool's log is exposed, instead of looping endlessly while still showing "retrying".
- **Shows the sidecar's raw log in the interface** when something is wrong, so no more guessing.
- **The status label names the actual problem**: enabled but the process not running says exactly that, and does not show "Off".
### Verified
- Actually ran `zalo-agent-cli --help` and `listen --help`: the listen command is real, and the webhook, filter and no-self flags are all correct. Also noted that filter accepts only user, group or all; the value "dm" used in 0.9.118 was wrong, replaced with "all" since 0.9.119.
- Ran listen with an empty folder: the tool prints "Not logged in" and exits with code 1, matching the existing error recognizer.
- Checked on real data: the Zalo connection returns a home path that exists.

## [0.9.120] - 2026-07-20
Fixed the "Watched chats" box being completely blank with not a word of guidance, so users who opened the panel did not know what to do to get a group to select.
### Fixed
- **An empty chat box now has guidance**: the redraw-guard variable was initialized with an empty string, and an empty list also produces an empty key, so the first draw was blocked immediately and the guidance line never showed. Changed to initialize with null.
- **Guidance states the right thing to do per state**: when off, it says to press Start listening first; when listening but nobody has messaged, it says to ask someone to send a message into the group to watch. Before, there was one generic sentence for both.
- Added 4 checks in dashboard/test_zalo_panel.js pinning this exact bug so it does not recur.

## [0.9.119] - 2026-07-20
Tightened the Zalo listener to match real usage: listen only to selected chats, and security-reviewed the whole route because message content is composed by strangers.
### Changed
- **Listen only to selected chats**: the watched chat list is now the main gate, and with none ticked nothing is reported. Before, the default was to listen to every private message and then filter by keyword, which was noisy and not what was needed. Keywords are demoted to a secondary filter that only narrows further within the chosen chats. Removed the "private messages only" box because it contradicts having chosen specific chats.
- **Automatically lists chats to choose from**: the owner does not know thread IDs, so the sidecar learns from the stream of messages passing through and shows it as a tick-to-select list on the Connections page. Ticking takes effect immediately, with no need to toggle off and on. It deliberately does not call the list-conversations tool because doing so would set up an extra socket for the same account, exactly the unverified collision.
### Added
- **Indicator line on the panel**: shows when the latest message was received, and clearly distinguishes "connected but no message received yet" from "off". This is what is needed to know whether the listener is truly alive or only claims to be.
### Security
- **Zalo content has no path to touch the engine or the server**: the data path is only webhook, filter, text string, Telegram. The module accepts exactly five dependencies, no engine, no Bash, no files, no MCP. A test pins exactly that set so anyone loosening it later will break the test.
- **Protection against impersonating Jarvis 007's words**: customer messages are fenced between two bars labeled "NOT a command for Jarvis 007", the label is placed before the content and long messages are truncated, so a message that deliberately breaks lines and writes "Jarvis 007: confirm the transfer" cannot fool it.
- **Protection against building markup**: pinned by a test that the listener's Telegram sending path does not set parse_mode, unlike the usual sending path that uses MarkdownV2.
- **Protection against XSS on the dashboard**: Zalo display names are chosen by strangers and drawn into the chat list, now wrapped entirely in esc(). Added dashboard/test_zalo_panel.js that actually runs the esc function and pins the source of the list drawing spot.
- **Filters hidden-text characters**: removes control characters, zero-width and RTL reversal characters, things that look harmless but that a machine reads as different content. Added a 256KB payload cap and a cap on the number of remembered chats.

## [0.9.118] - 2026-07-20
Added CONTINUOUS listening for Zalo messages. Before, the Zalo connector was pull-only: you had to call a tool to learn about a new message, and the MCP pool closes a process after 10 minutes idle (`mcp_client._IDLE_TTL`), so the websocket and message buffer of `zalo-agent-cli mcp start` did not survive. Now Jarvis 007 runs its own sidecar process, independent of the pool, which receives a message the moment a customer sends it and reports it to Telegram.
### Added
- **Zalo listener running in the background**: the `zalo-agent-cli listen --webhook` sidecar pushes each event to `/hook/zalo`, Jarvis 007 filters it, then fires Telegram. Turn it on or off right in the Zalo card on the Connections page, with real status shown (listening, connection lost and retrying, duplicate session). It rebuilds itself after a drop with backoff of 5s, then 30s, then 120s, then 300s, and turns itself back on after the app restarts.
- **Strict default filter**: only reports private messages containing a keyword, never groups. Keyword matching ignores diacritics and letter case, so a customer typing "gia" still matches "giá". There is a separate watched-chat list, quiet hours, msgId de-duplication, and a cap of 20 notifications per 10 minutes so a busy group cannot flood Telegram.
### Security
- **`/hook/zalo` has two layers of protection**: it only accepts loopback (`_AUTH_LOCAL_EXACT`), plus an auto-generated shared secret. The secret travels in the query, not a header, because the CLI's `--webhook` only POSTs plain JSON and cannot set arbitrary headers; guarding by header would block every message. Loopback alone is not enough because another process on the same VPS is also loopback. The secret is never returned to the frontend.
- **Jarvis 007 still does not reply to customers by itself**: the listener only reads and reports. Sending a Zalo message still has to be requested directly by the owner in chat.
### Known issues
- Zalo allows only ONE socket per account, so the `zalo` connector and the sidecar can kick each other off if they share an account. This is not yet verified, so the design makes the clash visible: it catches the duplicate-session sequence in the log, pushes it to the UI, and stops completely instead of looping uselessly.

## [0.9.117] - 2026-07-20
Fixed a false "Codex CLI not installed" message that blocked chatting with the ChatGPT plan even after a successful sign-in. Cause: the codex binary is not in PATH, so Jarvis 007 has to look for it in the home folder, and home was taken only from the USERPROFILE environment variable; when the server is restarted by auto-update or a background task this variable can be empty, home becomes empty, so every ~/.codex/... path turns relative and fails to match, even though the binary is still in the same place.
### Fixed
- **Codex CLI detection no longer depends only on USERPROFILE**: added fallbacks in turn: HOME, HOMEDRIVE plus HOMEPATH, then Path.home(). Checked by unsetting all three environment variables one after another; the correct binary is still found.
- **Added the JAVIS_CODEX_BIN variable**: points straight at the codex file if the machine installed it somewhere unusual; a wrong path is ignored and detection continues as normal.

## [0.9.116] - 2026-07-20
Reviewed every risk warning of the 23 connectors. Nobody had re-checked them since they were written, and they were not shown in the UI (fixed in 0.9.115), so errors piled up unseen. Found three connectors with dangerous tools and not a word of warning, one contradictory classification, and one description milder than reality.
### Security
- **Three connectors with dangerous tools and NO warning now have one**: `pancake-pos` (create orders, record cash-flow transactions, edit debts, issue e-invoices, run ads, create vouchers), `botcake` (send real messages to customers through the chatbot), `webcake-landing` (publish public pages, and it defaults to the Draft writes level).
- **Tightened `*share*` of `google-sheets` from Write to DANGEROUS**: this connector defaults to Draft writes level, meaning that before, Jarvis 007 could share a spreadsheet holding business numbers with outsiders right from the default. It now follows one standard with `google-keep` (which already ranks `add_note_collaborator` as dangerous): pushing data out to outsiders is always Full access.
### Fixed
- **`google-workspace` described itself as milder than reality**: the warning said the Draft writes level "only drafts, creates events, creates documents", while the list also has `*modify*` and `*move*`, so editing existing documents and moving Drive files are possible too. Rewritten accurately.
- **`zalo` is the ONLY connector that defaults to Full access** (17 Read-only, 5 Draft, 1 Full access) and the old warning did not say so clearly. The default level stays because Zalo is mostly connected to send messages, but the warning now states plainly that message sending is switched on and how to lower it.
### Improved
- **Rewrote all 20 warnings to one template, with paragraph breaks**: before, each was one long run-on paragraph with no line breaks, the same problem as the guide text fixed in 0.9.111. Now each permission level gets one paragraph, with the heaviest warning first.
### Added
- Added 5 rules to `server/test_canh_bao_rui_ro.py`: a connector with a dangerous tool must have a warning; a data-sharing tool must not be ranked Write; a long warning must break lines with no line over 200 characters; a warning must not use wording that understates the real permission level; a connector that defaults to Full access must say so and how to lower it.
### Notes
- The three remaining connectors without a warning (`google-search-console`, `google-ads`, `tiktok-ads`) declare no dangerous tools and default to Read-only, so they correctly need none yet.

## [0.9.115] - 2026-07-20
Fixed a serious presentation hole: **15 of the 16 connectors that have a risk warning never showed the warning when you pressed Connect**. The `risk` field was only drawn in the QR flow (Zalo) and in the permission-change dialog, so the strongest warning was missing at exactly the moment the user decides.
### Fixed
- **The risk warning now shows in ALL three connection flows**: `openApikeyFlow` and `openOauthFlow` now draw the `conn-risk` block as `openQrFlow` already did, placed RIGHT ABOVE the instructions so it is read first. Affects 15 connectors, including `facebook-personal` (paste the cookie of a real account), `google-workspace`, `slack`, `gmail`, `google-keep`.
### Improved
- **The `google-keep` card description speaks plainly about the blast radius**: Keep has no official API so it needs a master token with FULL access to the Google account, very different from `gmail` / `google-calendar` / `google-ads` which ask for exactly one scope. Jarvis 007 can only touch notes, but the token opens the whole account if leaked. Said right on the card so it is seen before clicking in.
### Added
- Test `server/test_canh_bao_rui_ro.py` (12 checks, no network): cuts out each JS function body to confirm all three flows draw `conn-risk` and only draw it when a warning really exists; checks the Keep card description states the risk; checks `google-keep` still declares only Keep tools and does not spread to Gmail/Drive. Includes a canary proving the function-body cut inspects exactly one function.
### Notes
- Kept the name "Google Keep" because it is correct for the CAPABILITY (the server exposes only 23 Keep tools, counted with a real MCP handshake). The problem is in the CREDENTIAL, not the capability, so it is handled with a warning instead of a rename.
- Did NOT expand `google-keep` into a Workspace-style connector. Jarvis 007 already has `gmail`, `google-calendar`, `google-workspace` using scoped OAuth, which is much safer. The master token should be locked into the one place with no alternative.

## [0.9.114] - 2026-07-20
Connecting **Google Ads** no longer requires running commands either. Before, you had to install the Google Cloud CLI, run `gcloud auth application-default login` with a very long scope string, then hunt for a JSON file in `%APPDATA%` and paste it in. Now you fill in Client ID/Secret and press sign in like Gmail and Calendar, and Jarvis 007 builds the login file itself.
### Added
- **`oauth_mcp.credentials_file(conn_id, fmt)`**: builds the credential file content for a STDIO connector that signs in with OAuth. Combines the refresh_token in the oauth store with the client_id/secret in `mcp_store` into exactly the ADC shape gcloud produces (`{type: authorized_user, client_id, client_secret, refresh_token}`). Synchronous, no network call.
- **`oauth_file` in the catalog**: a connector that declares `{format, env, ext}` makes `mcp_store.resolved()` write a 0600 file into `connector-files/` and point the environment variable at it. Reuses the existing pattern of the `file` field.
- Test `server/test_google_ads_oauth.py` (26 checks, no network): catalog declaration, ADC content building, and an END-TO-END check that `resolved()` writes a real file to disk with the right content. Includes a canary proving the function really reads the token store and does not invent a file.
### Fixed
- **`openOauthFlow` could not render multi-line fields**: it forced every field into a single-line input, so the box for pasting an ADC file (fallback) would be unusable. Now a field declared `multiline` becomes a textarea, same as the apikey flow.
### Improved
- **Dropped the Google Cloud CLI requirement** from `google-ads`. Only Git is still needed (already in the Docker image) because uvx downloads the server from GitHub.
- **Kept the manual ADC paste box as a fallback** for anyone who already ran gcloud, and the fallback WINS: once pasted by hand, OAuth does not overwrite it.
### Notes
- The `oauth_mcp` import in `mcp_store` must be LAZY (called inside a function) because `oauth_mcp` already imports `mcp_store` at module level. A direct import is a cycle.
- Did NOT touch `args` of google-ads: it still downloads from `git+https://...` because the PyPI version is only 0.0.1 (10/2025), and switching would add needless risk.
- Not yet verified with a real Google Ads account (needs a developer token + ad account), so the sign-in step must be tried on the spot.

## [0.9.113] - 2026-07-20
Dropped the step that forced users to open a terminal to connect **Google Keep**. Before, you had to run a long command to swap an App Password for a master token and paste it in; now you paste the App Password straight into Jarvis 007 and the server swaps it. The two remaining steps (turn on 2-step verification, create the App Password) are Google's own UI and cannot be automated, but there is now a button that opens them directly.
### Added
- **Credential exchange step declared from the catalog** (`server/cred_exchange.py`): a connector declares `auth.exchange` with `handler` / `inputs` / `output` / `drop`; when connecting, Jarvis 007 does the exchange and then DELETES the fields in `drop` before saving. Built generically instead of hardcoded for Keep, because `google-ads` will need exactly this mechanism.
- **`google_master_token` handler**: calls `gpsoauth.perform_master_login`, strips spaces from the App Password (Google shows it as 4 groups of 4 characters), checks for 16 characters, and translates Google error codes into Vietnamese (wrong password, 2-step not enabled, browser verification demanded, blocked for running on a VPS).
- **Button to open an external page for apikey-type connectors**: `openApikeyFlow` now calls `oauthWizard(con)` so every connector that declares `auth.setup.links` can show the button, not just the OAuth flow. Google Keep has a "Create App Password" button.
- Test `server/test_cred_exchange.py` (25 checks, no network): covers exchange success/failure, skipping when a token is already pasted, missing inputs, unknown handler, and an END-TO-END check that the App Password reaches neither disk nor env. Includes a canary proving the delete check is real.
### Security
- **The App Password is NEVER stored**: it is deleted whether the exchange succeeds or fails, is not mapped to an environment variable, and does not appear in error messages. Checked by reading the `mcp_servers.json` file on disk directly for the secret string.
- **Kept the fallback of pasting the master token by hand**: important because Google often blocks sign-in from data center IPs, so the VPS build still has a way through.
### Notes
- Added `gpsoauth` to `requirements.txt` (pulls in pycryptodomex, requests, urllib3). Checked with `pip install --dry-run`: it does not touch the `fastapi`/`starlette` pins.
- Not yet tried with a real App Password (needs a real Google account), so the token exchange step must still be verified on the spot.
- Surveyed `google-ads`: it CAN be moved to the UI, details in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-doi-credential-tren-ui-design.md`.

## [0.9.112] - 2026-07-20
Corrected a WRONG claim in version 0.9.110 and removed the extra Dockerfile line that came with it.
### Fixed
- **Removed the redundant `pip install uv` from `Dockerfile`**: version 0.9.110 added this line along with the claim "the image lacks uv so the 4 other uvx connectors (google-sheets, google-search-console, google-ads, tiktok-ads) are broken on the VPS". That claim was WRONG. `uv>=0.5` has been in `requirements.txt` since v0.9.0 (commit 856cb19) and the `Dockerfile` still runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`, so the image ALWAYS has `uv`. The other four connectors were never broken for this reason.
- Cause of the mistake: only grepped `Dockerfile` for the word `uv`, found nothing and concluded it was missing, even though the `pip install -r requirements.txt` line was right there and `requirements.txt` was never opened.
### Improved
- **Recorded the reason in `requirements.txt`**: the `uv>=0.5` line now has a comment saying it is not a library the app imports but the runner for connectors that declare `command: uvx`, with a warning not to remove it.
- Corrected the `CHANGELOG` of 0.9.110 and the design file `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-google-keep-connector-design.md` to match the facts, keeping the analysis of what went wrong so it is not repeated.

## [0.9.111] - 2026-07-20
Rewrote the sign-in guides of ALL 23 connectors to be easier to read, and fixed the guide box overflowing sideways. Before, all 23 guides were ONE run-on paragraph with no line breaks, with steps (1)(2)(3) wedged mid-sentence; a long string with no spaces (a shell command, a callback URL) pushed the box out of the modal so you had to scroll sideways to read it all.
### Fixed
- **The guide box no longer overflows sideways**: added `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to `.conn-guide` and `.conn-risk`, so long shell commands or callback URLs wrap instead of overflowing. Measured on a real 520px modal: `scrollWidth == clientWidth`, no horizontal scrollbar.

### Improved
- **23/23 guides rewritten to one template**: a "Cần trước:" (Needed first:) line for what must be installed, then "Làm 1 lần:" (Do once:) with one numbered step per line, and finally notes and warnings in their own paragraphs. The facts stay the same, only the presentation changed.

### Added

Includes a canary proving the rule catches the old-style string.

## [0.9.110] - 2026-07-20
Added the **Google Keep** connector so Jarvis 007 can read and work with Keep notes. Google Keep has no official API for ordinary gmail accounts, so this connector goes through an unofficial library and demands a Google master token, a kind of token with FULL access to the Google account, not scoped like OAuth. This risk is written straight into the connector's warning.

> **Correction (0.9.112):** version 0.9.110 originally also added `pip install uv` to the `Dockerfile` with the claim "the image lacks uv so the 4 other uvx connectors are broken on the VPS". That claim was WRONG: `uv>=0.5` has been in `requirements.txt` since v0.9.0 and the Dockerfile still runs `pip install -r requirements.txt`, so the image always has `uv`. The extra line was removed in 0.9.112.
### Added
- **`google-keep` connector** (apikey, 3 fields: `google_email`, `master_token`, `unsafe_mode`): runs locally through `uvx` with the community server `keep-mcp`. Covers 23 tools: search/read notes, create notes and checklists, edit, label, pin, archive, trash, delete, share. Declared in `system/mcp-catalog.json`, default `readonly`.
- **`UNSAFE_MODE` is opt-in, default OFF**: left empty, Jarvis 007 can only edit notes it created itself (labeled `keep-mcp`); typing `true` allows touching notes the user wrote by hand. Keeps the fork clean, following the principle that a capability touching personal data must be switched on by the user.
- **Deliberate permission classification**: `restore_note` is at Draft writes level but `trash_note` is at Full access, so the Draft writes level can always bring back a note trashed by mistake without being able to trash one itself. The two collaborator tools are ranked dangerous because they share a note with other people, different in kind from editing content in-house.
- Test `server/test_google_keep.py` (40 checks, no network, no token needed): env mapping, the opt-in rule of `UNSAFE_MODE`, the blocking layer by 3 permission levels and the mode ceiling, with a canary proving the blocking layer has real power.
### Notes
- **keep-mcp entry point trap**: this package declares a console script named `mcp`, the SAME name as the CLI of the MCP SDK, which is its dependency. So `uvx keep-mcp` errors, while `uvx --from keep-mcp mcp` runs the SDK's CLI by mistake with NO error at all. The correct way is `uvx --from keep-mcp python -m server`, verified with a real MCP handshake (returns exactly 23 tools). There is an `_args_doc` note in the catalog so that no one "tidies" it up later.
- Not yet verified on real Docker (the dev machine has no Docker) and no tool touching real Keep has been called (needs a master token). See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-google-keep-connector-design.md`, section "CHƯA kiểm chứng được" (NOT yet verified).

## [0.9.109] - 2026-07-20
Added the **Facebook Monitor (Apify)** connector and the `fb-monitor-apify` plugin: watch PUBLIC Pages and Groups to find viral posts (many shares) through the Apify scraping service, instead of scraping with a personal cookie. It does not touch the user's Facebook account so there is no lockout worry, runs fine on a 24/7 VPS, and returns share/react/comment counts to filter hot posts. This is the right direction for the need "watch groups/pages to find posts with many shares" that a personal cookie cannot handle 24/7.
### Added
- **`facebook-monitor` connector** (apikey, field `apify_token`): paste an Apify Personal API token (sign up free at apify.com). Read-only, costs Apify per run (~2.6 USD/1000 posts). Declared in `system/mcp-catalog.json`.
- **`fb-monitor-apify` plugin** (bundled) - tool `fb_monitor(urls, limit, min_shares)`: takes a list of public Page/Group links, picks the Apify actor by URL (`/groups/` → `apify/facebook-groups-scraper`, otherwise → `apify/facebook-posts-scraper`), runs synchronously through `run-sync-get-dataset-items`, normalizes posts (share/react/comment/link/author), filters by `min_shares` and sorts by shares descending. readonly, does not use a personal account.
- Test `server/test_fb_monitor.py` (17 checks, no network): valid catalog, actor routing, extracting the share count from many field names, filter + sort, merging errors.

### Notes
- V1 covers only PUBLIC Pages + Groups (the official Apify actor cannot enter closed groups). CLOSED groups are a later step: they need an actor that accepts a cookie + the cookie of an account that is a member, still with some lockout risk.
### Improved
- **ChatGPT sign-in through the browser reports a clear error when the backend is not ready**: if the server is running an old build (without the browser OAuth route), the "Via browser" button used to open a blank tab (about:blank) with no explanation. Now it says plainly "The server does not have this feature yet - restart Jarvis 007 and reload the page" instead of opening a blank tab.

Added a second way to sign in to ChatGPT through the browser (OAuth Authorization Code + PKCE), for Workspace accounts that block device-code authentication. Before, Jarvis 007 had only one way, device-code (enter a code at auth.openai.com/codex/device); a Workspace that turns off device-code could not sign in.
