## [0.9.106] - 2026-07-19
Fixed the Usage page (tokens & cost) showing all zeros on some installs (typically Docker VPS). Cause: the Claude/ChatGPT figures are built FROM raw logs (~/.claude/projects, ~/.codex/sessions); an install without or unable to read those raw logs loses everything, even though each turn already wrote real token counts to usage-events.jsonl (a source that used to be ignored for cli/codex).
### Fixed
- **The Usage page uses usage-events as a fallback source**: the indexer now also loads cli (Claude SDK) and codex/ChatGPT turns from usage-events.jsonl when raw logs are missing, so the report has numbers instead of 0. Double-count guard: on any day already covered by raw logs, event-derived rows for that day are dropped, so raw logs always win.
- **One-time history backfill**: after this version, the indexer re-reads usage-events.jsonl from the start exactly once to rebuild the cli/codex token history written before (old rows are deleted first so the API branch is not double counted).

## [0.9.105] - 2026-07-19
Fixed the Recurring page saying "could not load the task list" on a heavy VPS. Cause: /viec/all counted the notes of every brain (scanning the whole file tree) on each open, which takes a few seconds on a large vault and the reverse proxy cut it off midway. A light VPS finishes in time and still shows it, a heavy VPS errors.
### Fixed
- **/viec/all no longer counts notes**: the Work page does not need the note count, so the whole file-tree scan (rglob) is gone - 4-6 times faster (measured on the spot, 2.06s down to 0.3s). This was the root of the customer VPS failing to load the list.
- **Automatic retry once**: when /viec/all errors or briefly jams, the dashboard retries after 1.5s before reporting an error + a Retry button, saving a manual click when the network is briefly slow.

## [0.9.104] - 2026-07-19
The Recurring page no longer has the problem of creating by hand with an empty Brain box, and now you can add reminders right in the form, not only loops. A loop created through chat shows up whichever brain it lands in.
### Added
- **Add a reminder right in the Recurring form**: the "+ Add task" button lets you choose "Repeating job" or "Reminder". A reminder accepts flexible timing ("in 30 minutes", "8:30", cron "0 7 * * *", or a full date and time) and the type "Remind only" or "Do it, then report", saved straight into the reminder store of the chosen brain.
### Fixed
- **Empty Brain picker when creating a task by hand**: the Brain box used to be filled only after /viec/all (scans notes of every brain, slow on a VPS) finished loading, so clicking early gave an empty box that never refilled. Now it fills independently from /brains so there are always choices even while the task list is still loading.
- **A loop created through chat ran but did not show in the Work tab**: /viec/all now also merges brains registered with the scheduler that sit outside the brains folder, so a loop running in the background in an outside brain shows up too. When /viec/all errors or is too slow it now says so clearly with a Retry button instead of silently showing "no tasks yet".

## [0.9.101] - 2026-07-19
Personal Facebook: correctly recognize the mbasic SIGN-IN page returned when the cookie is rejected, instead of misreading the login page as a feed. Earlier the User-Agent fix (0.9.99) cleared the "not supported" error, but if the cookie is expired/blocked by Facebook, mbasic returns the sign-in page (the URL is still mbasic, no redirect) so it was not caught.

## [0.9.95] - 2026-07-19
Added the **Facebook Personal (cookie - experimental)** connector and the `fb-personal` plugin: automate a PERSONAL Facebook account using a session cookie (Facebook has closed the personal API) - browse/read the feed, post to the wall, comment. Goes the cookie + mbasic route with httpx so it runs on a headless VPS, no Chromium needed. WARNING: violates Facebook's terms, risk of account lockout; OFF by default, cookie encrypted at rest. This is step 2 following the Pages connector (0.9.90) for the need to browse a personal feed.
### Added
- **`facebook-personal` connector** (apikey, encrypted `cookie` field): paste the Facebook session cookie (with a guide to take it safely from DevTools). Read-only by default; posting/commenting runs only when raised to Full access. Declared in `system/mcp-catalog.json`.

The engine calls `mbasic.facebook.com` with httpx + cookie, extracts `fb_dtsg` itself and finds the post/comment form (best-effort, adjust selectors when Facebook changes). Clearly blocks when the cookie is pushed back to login/checkpoint.

### Notes
- The personal Facebook automation is EXPERIMENTAL and can only be verified by running for real with a real cookie on the target machine; mbasic may be changed/closed by Facebook so the form finder is best-effort and needs tuning when connected for real.

## [0.9.80] - 2026-07-18
The "Update now" button is hardened across the board: a health check after updating, the git build (Windows/native) AUTOMATICALLY ROLLS BACK to the old version on failure, a step-by-step progress bar and a "what's new" preview before pressing; the Docker build gets clear rollback instructions. **Server restart required** (the update flow changed + an endpoint was added). Spec + plan at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-update-triet-de-design.md` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-18-update-triet-de.md`.
### Added
- **Cross-platform updater with automatic rollback (git build)**: added `server/updater.py` that runs detached, using only the standard library (so it still runs even if the new version breaks a dependency). Sequence: stop the server -> (git stash if the tree is dirty) -> `git pull` -> `pip install` -> restart -> wait on `/health` for about 90 seconds. If the new version does not come up, `git reset --hard` back to the old commit + reinstall libs + restart (automatic rollback). Every step writes state to `update_state.json` (survives restarts).
- **Progress bar + preview of the new version in the Version panel**: the dashboard shows the changelog of the new version before pressing, and during the update shows the steps Prepare -> Download code -> Install libraries -> Restart -> Health check -> Done; on failure it reports that it rolled back to the old version (git) or shows how to roll back (Docker), with a notice when local changes were put aside into git stash.
- **`GET /update/status` endpoint + `previous_version` in `/version`**: the UI follows progress through structured state + the tail of `update.log`, and knows the old version to go back to.
- **CI publishes version tags to GHCR**: the image gets an extra `:x.y.z` tag (read from VERSION) next to `:latest` and `:<sha>`, so there is always a fixed old build to pin when rolling back on Docker.
### Fixed
- **The Windows build skipped the library install step when updating**: the old updater only ran `git pull` then started again, with no `pip install`, so a new version that added a library crashed the app. Now every git build installs libs when updating.
- **`git pull` died when the working tree was dirty**: a local change to a tracked file made pull abort silently, the update failed with no clear reason. Now it runs `git stash` automatically (kept, not lost, never auto-popped to avoid conflicts) before pulling and tells the user.
### Security
- **Guard against a double-click spawning 2 updaters**: `POST /update` claims the state right after the guard (no await in between) and only blocks when an unfinished update STARTED recently, so clicking twice does not create two overlapping update processes, and it also does not get stuck "updating" forever if an update was interrupted.

### Added

For `.md` and text files it shows an editable `<textarea>` (for `.md` only, a "Source / View" toggle, the View rendered with the existing `mdToHtml`); images/PDF preview; other files offer download. Now it catches a balanced pair of parentheses one level deep and allows spaces, and also strips the optional markdown title (`( "title" )`). So clicking opens the right file.

## [0.9.77] - 2026-07-18
Deleting a brain now SPREADS to every synced machine (no more "resurrection"), and keeps a copy in a local trash for 30 days. **Server restart required** (the sync flow + delete endpoint changed); the UI reloads itself thanks to the `?v=7` bump. Brainstorm + spec + plan at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-brain-delete-sync-propagation-design.md` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-18-brain-delete-sync-propagation.md`.
### Added
- **Synced death notice (tombstone) to spread a brain deletion**: when deleting 1 brain (after typing the confirming name correctly), Jarvis 007 writes a small file `<BRAINS_DIR>/.javis-tombstones/<name>.json` synced with the repo. The new `_apply_tombstones` step in sync reads the tombstone and definitively deletes that brain on every machine, overriding the policy "a deletion does not beat a surviving copy" - BUT only for a deliberate deletion. There is a time guard: a brain created/edited again after the deletion is not killed unfairly (the tombstone removes itself, and recreating a brain of the same name through `/brains/new` also removes the tombstone). The default brain is immune.
- **30-day local trash**: deleting a brain now MOVES the data into `<STATE_DIR>/brain-trash/<name>__<time>/` (outside the sync area, one trash per machine) instead of a hard delete; entries older than 30 days are cleaned at the start of each sync. The confirmation when deleting says this clearly. Restore by hand (move the folder from the trash back to `brains/`). The delete endpoint is atomic: if writing the tombstone fails, the move to trash is undone.
### Fixed
- **A deleted brain "resurrected" on sync/update**: the old sync policy deliberately did not let a deletion beat a surviving copy (to prevent data loss), so a brain deleted on this machine was pushed back by another machine/remote. Now a deliberate deletion spreads through the tombstone; the general data-loss shield stays intact for every case WITHOUT a tombstone (a folder vanishing because a volume is not mounted, an engine half-writing... is restored by `_restore_missing_brains`, not spread as a deletion).

## [0.9.76] - 2026-07-18
Spread out the header bar so it stops bunching up, and added a button to switch between a deep-dark and a soft-dark tone. Brainstorm + spec at `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-header-theme-toggle-design.md`.
### Added
- **UI tone switch button at the right of the header**: flips between deep-dark (default, background `#0e0e16`) and soft-dark (gray background `#282a37`, gentler text to be less glaring). There is NO white-background light mode - the whole app stays dark so the 3D cockpit is not broken. The choice is remembered through `localStorage["javis.theme"]`, with an inline script at the top of `<head>` applying it before painting so there is no flash.
### Improved
- **Header no longer "crammed", spread evenly over 3 columns**: `.hud-top` (grid `1fr auto 1fr`) used to have 4 flat children; on management pages `.brand` + `.hud-actions` are hidden so the 2 remaining children bunch into columns 1-2, leaving column 3 (~414px) empty. Now they are wrapped into 3 column-fixed groups: left (brand + brain picker + figures), middle (name + date), right (theme button + cockpit button group). A hidden child just shrinks itself while the group keeps its column, so it is balanced on BOTH home and management pages; the theme button is a direct child of the right group so it always shows, filling the right column that used to be empty.

## [0.9.75] - 2026-07-18
Fixed the brain picker dropdown keeping "external folders" (📁) that were deleted from the disk or duplicate a real brain - they survived folder deletion, brain deletion, and updating to a new version. **Server restart required** to get the `/path/exists` endpoint; the UI reloads itself thanks to the `?v=6` bump.
### Fixed
- **The brain picker menu showed an old deleted brain again**: the dropdown merges options from 2 INDEPENDENT sources. The 🧠 kind (`data-brain`) is loaded fresh by `brains-ui.js` from `GET /brains` (reads the real disk) so deleting a folder/brain makes it vanish on reload. But the 📁 kind (`data-custom`) is loaded by `app.js` from `localStorage["javis.brains"]` (an external folder chosen through the browse button) and was NEVER checked for existence, never cleaned, with no remove button. `localStorage` lives per browser origin so it survived folder deletion, brain deletion and app updates - exactly the symptom. The trash button on a selected 📁 even said "an external folder is just removed from the list" but offered no way to remove it → the entry was stuck forever.
- **`brains-ui.js` now cleans the 📁 list on every load**: after getting the real brain list, the `pruneCustomBrains` function removes from `localStorage` entries whose path DUPLICATES a real brain (to avoid showing twice) and entries whose path is NO LONGER a directory (deleted from disk), KEEPING valid external folders with a different path. It cleans the `localStorage` source right away so the next `app.js` render is still correct and does not "come back to life" through an update. Runs BEFORE the selection restore step so it does not restore to a dead path.
- **The trash button can remove an external 📁 folder**: selecting a 📁 then pressing delete now asks for confirmation and removes it from the menu + `localStorage` (does NOT touch data on disk), instead of only reporting an error and giving up as before.
### Added
- **`GET /path/exists?path=` endpoint** (read-only, only `os.path`, lightweight): returns `{exists, is_dir}` for an absolute path. Used so the dropdown can check whether an external folder still exists. FAIL-SAFE: an access error returns `exists=null` → the frontend reads it as "undetermined" and KEEPS the entry, cleaning only when the server clearly confirms the path is gone (a missing/404 endpoint because the server has not restarted, or a network error, never lose a valid entry). Comes with the test `server/test_path_exists.py` + `dashboard/test_brains_ui.mjs` (mock DOM, runs the cleanup logic straight on the real bug scenario).

- **Narrowed the rail width 172→160px** in expanded mode to cut spare area; measured that no item is text-clipped (including "Recurring").

## [0.9.71] - 2026-07-17
Version 0.9.70 shipped the `javis_schedule` tool in a state where it was NOT really usable - an independent review (running code, not guessing) found 2 Critical bugs, 3 Important bugs and 1 piece of technical debt. This version patches all of them. Thanks to the review for pointing out exactly: "both halves of the tool fail to do what it promises".
### Fixed
- **[Critical] SYNCHRONOUS `httpx` calling back into the very server running it → hangs the WHOLE SERVER**: the `javis_schedule` handler (`plugin.py`) is a plain `def`, and the 3 functions `_post_reminder`/`_get_reminders`/`_cancel_reminder` call `httpx.post`/`httpx.get` SYNCHRONOUSLY to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/reminders`. `plugins_host._make_call` calls the plugin handler with `res = handler(args, ctx)` and only then `await`s - NOT wrapped in `asyncio.to_thread` - so the `httpx.post` call blocks the WHOLE uvicorn event loop (a single worker, `main.py:5037`) while it waits for THAT SAME request to be answered → deadlock, `ReadTimeout` after ~5-10s, and meanwhile the server cannot answer ANYONE (every user, every tool). Worse: the reminder is still really created (it entered the queue before the hang), the tool returns an error so the model retries → creates 1 MORE duplicate reminder + hangs once more. Fix: all 4 functions switched to `async def` + `httpx.AsyncClient`, following the pattern of `system/plugins/meta-ads-graph/plugin.py` (`_get()`) and `system/plugins/image-chatgpt/plugin.py` (`_gen()`) - the other 2 bundled plugins already did it right from the start, `javis-schedule` was the only exception breaking the convention.
- **[Critical] A loop created through the tool NEVER does what the user asked**: `_create_loop_file` wrote frontmatter that lacked the `goal` field entirely. `self_improve.py:250` `goal = fm.get("goal", "business")` defaults to `"business"` when missing, and the `goal == "business"` branch (`self_improve.py:546`) does not read a word of `loop["body"]` (the file body - exactly where the prompt the user just typed in chat sits). Two ways to break: with no business-data MCP connected → `skip_reason` makes the loop skip FOREVER every round; with POS/ads → the loop silently runs "business metrics analysis" (the default task) instead of what the user really asked, then still reports to Telegram as if it did the right job. The web form for creating loops does it right (`self_improve.py:914` `goal = goal or (old["goal"] if old else "custom")`) - the tool was the ONLY wrong place. Fix: `_create_loop_file` hard-writes `goal: custom` into the frontmatter, with a comment explaining why this line is required so no one deletes it by accident.
- **`notify_only` had no effect - every reminder built the whole Claude engine + MCP to "do it for you"**: `_do_create` hard-coded `"mode": "task"` in the payload sent to `POST /reminders`, regardless of `notify_only`. Consequence: "remind me in 30 minutes to call the customer" (wanting just 1 reminder sentence) ran `reminders.py:418 _run_task` when due (building the CLI, reading MCP, `max_wall_s=300`) then sent "⏰ Nhắc hẹn (Jarvis 007 đã làm): ..." (Reminder (Jarvis 007 did it): ...) instead of the correct "⏰ Nhắc anh: ..." (Reminder for you: ...) (`reminders.py:342`) - the exact opposite of the tool's own description and of CLAUDE.md ("notify_only=true if it only reminds"). Fix: `"mode": "notify" if notify_only else "task"`.
- **Schedules "mỗi tuần"/"mỗi ngày"/"mỗi tháng"/"mỗi sáng" (every week/day/month/morning) were all read as running EVERY 5 MINUTES**: `_UNIT_ALT` previously only knew minutes/hours (VN + English abbreviations), with no day/week/month; these strings could not match number + unit so `_interval_min` fell to the hard floor of 5 minutes - "a weekly revenue recap job" ran every 5 minutes (plus the goal bug above = Telegram spam + burning real LLM cost). The worse case: "mỗi sáng 7h" (every morning at 7h) was read as "every 7 HOURS" (`interval_min=420`) because the regex only saw the number "7" + the unit "h", unable to tell it was a TIME OF DAY and not a repeat interval. Fixed in 3 layers: (1) added `ngay=1440`/`tuan=10080`/`thang=43200` to the conversion table, and let a unit stand alone implying quantity 1 ("mỗi ngày" = "mỗi 1 ngày"); (2) the new `_daily_cron` function detects a DAILY REPEAT signal (`mỗi` + morning/noon/afternoon/evening, or the word "ngày", or the phrase "hằng ngày") PLUS a clock time (`7h`, `07:00`) → routes to the reminders store as a 5-field cron instead of an interval loop; (3) **safety rule**: an ambiguous schedule from which no unit/time can be extracted (e.g. a bare "mỗi sáng", "mỗi khi rảnh" (whenever free)) → `_interval_min` returns `None`, `_create_loop_file` returns `"ERROR: ..."` asking for a clearer statement - it NEVER silently falls to 5 minutes in any case.
- **The `javis-builder` skill taught typing YAML by hand, beating even CLAUDE.md's "prefer calling the tool" instruction**: `CLAUDE.md` (section "Tự tạo năng lực" (Building capabilities)) says to use the `javis-builder` skill; this skill loads AFTER so being more specific it wins - and its Loop section (before this version) only had a YAML template to write the file yourself, not a word about `javis_schedule`, so the model still typed by hand even though the tool existed (and the template lacked `owner_chat` → a hand-written loop reported to the wrong person). Fix: the Loop section now teaches calling the `javis_schedule` tool (op=create) first, writing the file by hand only when EDITING an existing loop or needing an advanced field the tool does not accept yet (`quiet_hours`/`max_runs_per_day`/`workspace`/`ambient_mcp`/`goal` other than `custom`); the remaining YAML template gained `goal: custom` + `owner_chat` to match the standard the tool produces. Added the hash of the old version into `system_sync.py:LEGACY_HASHES["skills/javis-builder"]` so users' brains pick up this fix through sync (not treated as "hand-edited").
- **`apply_mcp` did not pass `brain` on a few UNGATED paths, so an in-process plugin could still be brain-blind**: the places that create a CLI with `allowed_tools=None` (ungated) all load in-process plugins (`claude_sdk_engine._plugins_server`, reading `cli.javis_vault`) - a missing `brain` repeats exactly the 0.9.70 bug just fixed on the chat path (`image-chatgpt` saved wrongly to `brains/Brain Default`). Fix: `self_improve._make_cli` takes an extra `brain` parameter, passing it down to all 3 `apply_mcp` calls inside (the `mode=full` branch, the `ambient_mcp` branch, and the default branch - this one is actually GATED so plugins do not load, but it is still passed for consistency/just in case); the 2 `_make_cli` call sites in `run_cycle`/verification now pass the `brain=brain` already in scope. Added an `else` for the ungated branch of `execute_workflow` (`main.py`, Studio "run with full permission") that sets `c.javis_vault = vault_root` directly - does NOT call `_apply_mcp()` here because this branch deliberately relies on `setting_sources` to inherit the machine's MCP like a real interactive `claude` session, and calling `_apply_mcp` would change behavior beyond the bug being fixed. **The 2 remaining paths CANNOT be fixed** because there is no brain/vault variable in scope to pass (no inventing variables): `/metrics` (`main.py:1451`) takes no brain parameter (an endpoint shared by every brain); `/ingest-upload` (`main.py:1733`) only takes already-resolved `staged`/`sources`/`attachments`, with no original brain.
### Tests
- `test_javis_schedule.py` gained 5 test groups blocking exactly the bugs above: (1) `inspect.iscoroutinefunction` on the handler + 3 HTTP functions - a regression net blocking a return to the sync way; (2) a REAL NET for the goal bug - passes the just-created loop through the REAL API `self_improve.LoopFeature.get_loop` (not only checking the text written to the file) and asserts `goal == "custom"` + the file body reaches where it will run; (3) monkeypatches `_post_reminder` to capture the payload, asserting `mode` changes correctly with `notify_only`; (4) `_interval_min` for day/week/month + cron at a fixed clock time + an ambiguous schedule must be `None`/`ERROR`; (5) the dispatcher with a wrong `op` and an empty `vault_root`. `test_loop_ambient.py` updated so the `_apply_mcp` stub takes an extra `brain=None` to match the new signature.

## [0.9.70] - 2026-07-17
### Added
- **`javis_schedule` tool - chat can set recurring jobs, no more typing YAML by hand**: before, to "create a job that scans orders every 2 hours" you had to type YAML frontmatter into `Javis/loops/<slug>.md` yourself, or shell out to `curl POST /reminders` (`reminders.py:17` documented exactly that). The second path also contradicted itself: a loop in suggest/auto mode is blocked from Bash (`self_improve.py:112`) so a loop could not set a reminder for itself. Now one chat sentence calls the tool directly, and `op=create` routes into 1 of 2 stores by the nature of the job: repeating + durable → a `.md` file (editable in Obsidian); reminder/cron/one-off → the reminders store (which already has 5-field cron: `cron_util.py`, computing the next run at `reminders.py:364`). `op=list` sees BOTH stores, `op=cancel` cancels a pending reminder. Safety keeps the CLAUDE.md rule: a loop created through chat is always `enabled: false` + `mode: suggest`, with no parameter to change it; a duplicate slug reports an error instead of spawning a parallel copy (identified by FILE NAME, `self_improve.py:321-327`).
- **Why a bundled plugin and not a tool in the hub**: the hub cannot reach every engine for this, blocked by two barriers. Barrier 1: `_builtin_tools` (`mcp_hub.py:211-212`) early-returns as soon as `vault_root` is empty - registering no tool that needs to know the brain - while the hub HTTP path (`tools/list`/`tools/call`, `mcp_hub.py:392,398`) always calls `discover_all` without a brain so `vault_root` is always `None` on that path. Barrier 2: `claude_config_path` (`mcp_hub.py:448-453`) returns `None` when no MCP connector is on yet, meaning Claude Code has never even seen the hub exist. The plugin goes through the IN-PROCESS MCP server of the SDK engine (`claude_sdk_engine.py:162-186`, the `_plugins_server` part), hitting neither barrier.
### Fixed
- **A plugin called from chat was always brain-blind, `javis_generate_image` silently saved images into Brain Default**: `_plugins_server` (`claude_sdk_engine.py`) used to infer the brain from `self.cwd`, but chat always runs with `cwd=CLAUDE_CWD` (`main.py:318`, the project root - with no `Javis/` folder) so this inference always missed to `None` on exactly the chat path, and every plugin called from Claude Code got `ctx.vault_root=None`. Concrete result: `image_gen._resolve_vault` fell back to `brains/Brain Default`, with no error reported. Building `javis_schedule` (which must write the open brain's correct `Javis/loops/`) exposed that the brain had never been passed explicitly through the SDK engine. Fix: `_apply_mcp` (`main.py`) takes an extra brain parameter and sets `cli.javis_vault` explicitly on both chat paths (dashboard websocket + Telegram, brain already in scope) - no longer inferred from cwd.
- **A job name containing YAML indicator characters silently killed the loop**: `_yaml_scalar` used to escape only `[:#'"\n]`, missing characters YAML treats as leading indicators (`- @ * ! % ? | & >`). A job name using these characters broke the written frontmatter, `yaml.safe_load` threw `ScannerError`/`ConstructorError`, and `self_improve.list_loops()` swallowed the error with try/except so the loop vanished from the Recurring tab even though the tool had just reported "created successfully". Fixed by always returning a JSON-style double-quoted string (`json.dumps`) instead of listing characters to escape - YAML 1.2 is a superset of JSON so a JSON double-quoted scalar is always valid. Applied to `owner_chat` too (before, joined by hand with no escape function).
- **`op=cancel` always got 401 on an instance with a password enabled**: `POST /reminders/cancel` was missing from `_AUTH_LOCAL_EXACT` (`main.py`), so when `gate_active()=True`, `javis_schedule` calling httpx from localhost (no cookie) was always blocked. `/reminders` (create reminder) had been exempted in the same group earlier; cancelling is a weaker action than creating so exempting it at the same level is only consistent.
### Improved
- **CLAUDE.md teaches exactly what was just built**: the "Orchestration" section, level 6 (Reminder) changed from `POST /reminders` to calling the `javis_schedule` tool; level 7 (Loop) gained a sentence preferring to call the tool over writing the file yourself. Why it had to be fixed in the same version as the tool: the tool description competes directly with the instruction in the system prompt, and the prompt usually wins - with a tool existing but documentation still teaching hand-typed YAML, the model still types by hand. The loop file format description stays below, still needed for EDITING an existing loop.

## [0.9.69] - 2026-07-17
### Security
- **`/automations/sync` was a security hole, deleted together with the whole fake feature it belonged to**: the route called `claude_engine(...)` without passing `allowed_tools`, so per `claude_sdk_engine.py:290-301` it ran with `permission_mode="bypassPermissions"` AND loaded `setting_sources=["user","project","local"]` - the least guarded engine call in the codebase. This route's "LIST ONLY" guarantee was just words in the prompt, with no real gate behind it. Deleted the route together with the whole `automations` registry.
### Improved
- **The "Schedule" tab was a fake feature, now fully removed**: `Javis/automations.json` never had any executor reading it - `_scheduler_loop` (`server/main.py`) ticks 6 jobs (loop, learn, kanban, reminders, backup, index) and no branch reads this file. Real check before deleting: 0 `automations.json` files exist on all 4 running brains, 0 tests cover it. What made it look real: a green "N running" badge for rows that never fire, and a schedule box that was free text no line of code parses - because the tab mostly projected the Loops themselves through two layers `_loops_as_routines` (main.py) and `pending_as_automations` (reminders.py), with the string "every N minutes" invented at GET time and read from nowhere. Both projection layers, 3 registry helpers and 5 `/automations*` routes are now deleted.
- **One "Work" page replaces the two pages Loop + Schedule**: the `selfimprove` rail item renamed "Loop" to "Recurring", with a merged "Pending reminders" block (reads `GET /reminders`, cancels through `POST /reminders/cancel`) - merging was mandatory because reminders used to appear ONLY in the Schedule tab just deleted. No new endpoint added: the page reads the existing `GET /loops` and `GET /reminders` directly.
- **The ROUTINES stat box deleted outright, not replaced by another box**: this box in `index.html` counted "running routines" by fetching `/automations` in `loadBrainStats()` (`app.js`) - the very route just deleted above, so after the route vanished, the displayed number would be 0 forever because the 404 error was silently swallowed by `.catch(() => ({}))`. This box was exactly the lying badge that cleaning the Schedule tab was meant to kill, only the original plan missed it because `app.js` was never grepped.
- **Cleaned 138 lines of the dead cluster of the old loop panel**: the panel `<div class="loop-box" style="display:none">` in `index.html` together with its serving cluster in `app.js` (`loadLoopConfig`, `saveLoopConfig`, `renderLoopStatus`, `loadLoopLog`, the `loopRunNow` listener with a poll loop, the `lintBtn` listener, the fetches of `/loop/config`, `/loop/log`, `/loop/run-now`) - the panel was hard-hidden by `display:none` and no line of code ever removed it, so the whole cluster behind it could no longer be reached. The backend `/loop/config` and `/lint` stay as is, only the dead UI side was cleaned.

## [0.9.68] - 2026-07-17
### Improved
- **Conversation history shows only 20 items, with a "Show 20 more" button**: the sidebar used to pour 100 conversations out in one go, and with lots of chatting the list was endless and needed endless scrolling. Now the default is 20 items, each press opens 20 more, and when the conversations run out the button hides itself. No server change needed: the `/sessions` endpoint already takes `limit` freely so the client just asks for exactly 1 extra item (`limit = shown + 1`) to know whether data remains behind.
- The number of open items is kept when the list auto-refreshes on a new message (otherwise someone viewing 60 items would be pulled back to 20), and resets to 20 only when the brain changes. Re-rendering also keeps the scroll position so pressing "Show more" does not jump to the top.
- **Search still scans ALL conversations** as before, untouched by this 20-item limit.

## [0.9.67] - 2026-07-17
### Fixed
- **Deleting a step LOST text being typed in the other steps**: the ✕ button called `steps.splice(i, 1)` directly then `render()` but forgot to call `captureSteps()` first (the "+ Step" button does call it), so `render()` painted over every input with the old values in the array. Edit a few steps, not yet Save, press delete on any step and it all vanishes, easy to think you typed wrong. Rebuilt exactly this scenario on both the old and new builds to compare: the old build returns the old text, the new build keeps the text just typed.
- **The "Verification" row broke into three lines**: the combined rule `.editor-box input { width: 100% }` has specificity (0,1,1), beating `.st-retries { width: 48px }` at only (0,1,0), so the retry-count box was stretched full-width and pushed the word "times" onto its own line. The original intent was for three things to sit neatly on one line but the CSS never worked that way. Now changed to `.editor-box .st-retries` (0,2,0). The verification agent picker is not hit by this because it has `flex: 1`.
### Improved
- **The Edit workflow form folds steps to show the whole picture**: an 11-step workflow used to spread at full size in a box 86vh high so only one and a half steps were visible at a time, and grasping the whole needed constant scrolling. Now each step is one compact line with the number, agent name and an excerpt of the task; click it to open and edit, open another step and the old one folds itself. The inputs stay in the DOM when folded (hidden only by CSS) so `captureSteps()` reads everything, and a folded step keeps its verification config on Save.
- **Added up/down buttons to reorder steps**: before, moving step 9 before step 4 meant copying back and forth by hand. The ↑ button on the first step and ↓ on the last fade out by themselves.

## [0.9.66] - 2026-07-17
### Improved
- **Workflow variables in the step box read as words instead of an ellipsis**: the old code replaced every `{{...}}` with `…`, so the first step of viral-video-production showed "Receive …, create project folder", which reads as cut-off. Now `{{input}}` becomes "input", `{{prev}}` becomes "result of the previous step", and an unknown variable shows its name instead of being swallowed. Handles the case with spaces inside the braces like `{{ input }}` correctly.

## [0.9.65] - 2026-07-17
### Fixed
- **The Workflows page showed steps as tall, empty columns**: the step strip used `flex: 1` splitting the width evenly, so an 11-step workflow (viral-video-production) squeezed each cell to about 35px, while the agent name `viral-video-director` has `white-space: nowrap` so it was cut off entirely, leaving only the step number. Now each cell is at least 150px wide and wraps when out of room, so text is always readable. Measured on a real 1720px screen: 10 cells in a row, the 11th drops to the next row; 1280px gets 7 cells; 900px gets 5; 600px gets 3; 380px gets 2. Cell width always stays within 152 to 173px at every size and no size overflows sideways.
- **Steps from the 10th on were numbered wrongly as `010`, `011`**: the code concatenated `0${i+1}` so it was only right for steps 1 to 9. Replaced with `padStart(2, "0")`.
- **Workflow cards were stuffed into a narrow column grid**: the Workflows panel shared the `.cards` grid (`auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr)`) with Agents and Schedule, but the pipeline is horizontal so the two fought, and with only one workflow the rest of the row sat empty. Now Workflows has its own `.wf-list` and `.wf-row`, one workflow per full-width row; Agents, Schedule, plugin and loop keep the old `.cards`/`.wf-card` so they are unaffected.
### Improved
- **The step box takes the task as the main text, the agent name drops to secondary text**: many workflows call the same agent at every step, so with the agent as the main text 11 cells show identical text and you cannot tell one step from another. The task content is cut to 2 lines, hover to see it in full.
- **The button group and step count moved up to the same row as the workflow name**, instead of sitting at the bottom, so scanning is faster when there are many workflows.

## [0.9.64] - 2026-07-17
### Fixed
- **Jarvis 007 spent up to ~52ms every chat turn just to sync skills, and it blocked the whole process**: the skill mirror function read and re-hashed the `SKILL.md` of EVERY skill (both source and destination) each time the system prompt was built, meaning every chat turn, every Telegram message, every Kanban task, every loop round, every reminder. Measured for real on 3 running brains, before the fix: My Bullet Journal (27 skills/41 files) 52.48ms/turn, Ngọc Thu Phạm (16 skills/30 files) 44.23ms/turn, Brain Default (6 skills/9 files) 11.62ms/turn - run synchronously on the event loop so it froze the other connections. Now replaced with a signature gate that uses only `stat` (reading no file content), copying for real only when the skill tree changed. Re-measured on exactly those 3 brains after the fix: down to 8.30ms, 6.05ms, 2.28ms/turn in the same order - about 5 to 7 times faster depending on the brain (5.1x / 6.3x / 7.3x), not a single fixed number. A pre-existing flaw, unknown until measured.
- **A side file in a skill changed content but the mirror never received it**: the old gate hashed only `SKILL.md`, so editing an image or a sibling document in the skill folder left the natively loaded Claude Code copy on the old version forever. The new signature covers every file (relative path, modification time, size) so this bug is gone.
### Added
- **A skill can carry `references/` and `scripts/` along**: the mirror to `.claude/skills` now copies the whole subtree, so a skill with separate documents or an accompanying script works on the Claude Code native-load path too, not only the router path. 10 skills in the existing brains already used `references/` before and until now still had not reached the native path; confirmed all 10 arrive after this version.
### Known issues (not fixed)
- **System skills still cannot ship a subtree**: `html-to-webcake` ships with `tools/` and `examples/` but the system skill install mechanism transfers only `SKILL.md`, so the subtree never reached any brain. This version does NOT fix that: it sits in the install layer, above the mirror layer.
- **A mirror broken from outside will not heal itself until restart**: the signature gate is computed on the source tree and remembered in memory, so if someone deletes a file in `.claude/skills` by hand without touching the original skill, Jarvis 007 will not notice. A deliberate trade-off for speed; toggling the skill off/on or restarting both bring it back right.

## [0.9.63] - 2026-07-17
### Fixed
- **Skills Jarvis 007 LEARNED BY ITSELF lost all frontmatter when the description had a colon**: `learn.py` wrote `description: <value>` without double quotes. Vietnamese descriptions very often have colons (version 0.9.62 itself had to double-quote 2 of 5 system skills, about 40%), and then PyYAML throws an error on the WHOLE frontmatter block, not just one line: `name`, `group`, `origin`, `status` are lost too, `split_frontmatter` swallows the error and returns empty, and that skill silently can never be routed. Now every model-generated value (`name`, `description`, `group`) goes through `_yaml_scalar` (double-quoted + correctly escaped), with a round-trip test calling the real code directly.
- **`learn.py` never enforced the 150-character cap**: version 0.9.62 only blocked it at `POST /skills`. The self-learning path still wrote an overlong description straight to disk and left the runtime to truncate it. Now `_promote_sync` calls `validate_description` and puts violations in the blocked list, in the same pattern as the existing secret scan and injection scan.
- **`javis-builder` still taught exactly the bug that 0.9.62 was born to kill**: the file template in that skill, under the heading "write EXACTLY as this", still wrote `description: <SHORT description clearly stating WHEN to activate - this is the trigger, write it carefully>` while the standard set just 14 lines below says the opposite. **The 0.9.62 CHANGELOG claiming "both" documents were fixed is WRONG**: `CLAUDE.md` was fixed, `javis-builder` was not. Because a skill written through chat writes straight to disk, no blocking layer catches it, and whoever writes following the template creates a skill that cannot be routed with no error reported. Now the template and a second spot of the same kind are fixed.
- **A usage-counter sidecar corrupted in DATA TYPE took down the whole Skills page**: `GET /skills` and `is_stale` cast numbers without defense, so a hand-edited corrupt record returns a 500 error for the whole page, against the very commitment "a corrupt sidecar must never break anything". Worse: it does not heal itself, because `bump` also stumbles at the same spot then swallows the error, so the corrupt record lives forever and the whole brain stops counting. Now all three places are defensive, and `bump` overwrites to self-heal on the next use.
### Added
- **Jarvis 007 knows which skills are ACTUALLY used**: each skill load through `javis_use_skill` is recorded into the brain's `Javis/skill-usage.json`. The Skills page shows "used N times, most recently ..." or "not seen used" for a skill old enough with no signal. **This is a ONE-WAY signal and must be understood correctly**: Claude Code also loads skills NATIVELY through the `.claude/skills` mirror, a path that does not go through the counter. So "used" is certain, while "not seen used" only means **no evidence yet**, NOT that the skill is useless. Nothing auto-disables, auto-archives or auto-cleans a skill based on this number; every decision is still the user's.
- **A skill-writing standard in the self-learning loop's prompt**: 9 required points (the 150 cap interpolated from a constant rather than hardcoded, no filler openings, double quotes when there is a colon, the order of body sections, no inventing flags and paths, a body length cap, no router-style skills), with `group` made a required field in the schema.
- **The sidecar does not leak into learning history**: `Javis/skill-usage.json` is runtime state so it was added to the brain's `.gitignore` and excluded from backups. An old brain never received `.gitignore` updates before (the repo init function returns early, and even the init branch skips if the file already exists); now missing lines are merged in at the next time self-learning is turned on or learn is pressed, keeping lines the user added. This creates a one-time `chore:` commit in the brain's repo, deliberately separate from the `learn:` prefix so it does not show on the Review page and is not undone by mistake.
### Known issues (not fixed)
- **The `html-to-webcake` system skill is broken in every brain**: it ships with `tools/` and `examples/`, the skill body tells the agent to run them, but the system skill install mechanism transfers only `SKILL.md` so the subtree never reached any brain. A pre-existing bug, not caused by this version.
- **`references/` and `scripts/` in a skill reach only the router path, not yet the `.claude/skills` mirror**: the mirror currently copies only top-level files. This limitation is written right in `javis-builder` so skill authors know beforehand. A recursive mirror was considered and DELIBERATELY DEFERRED after review found 6 real blockers (the costliest: it would scan and hash the whole skill tree every chat turn, and block the event loop). Details in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-skill-telemetry-authoring-design.md`.
- **The mirror does not receive a side file that changed content if `SKILL.md` did not change**: the skip gate hashes only `SKILL.md`. A pre-existing bug, the same profile as the two items above.
## [0.9.62] - 2026-07-16
### Fixed
- **Skill descriptions were silently truncated, so skills could not be routed**: Jarvis 007 cut a skill's `description` in THREE places with THREE different limits and nobody knew: 60 characters in the `javis_use_skill` tool description, 100 characters in the router block of the system prompt, 140 characters in the fallback path when the frontmatter has no `description`. A skill author had no way to know which ruler was used. Measured with `skill_router` itself on the running brain: **6 of 6 enabled skills were truncated**, losing 79 to 316 characters each, and the part thrown away was exactly the trigger examples, the thing that makes routing work. All three are now one constant, `skill_router.SKILL_DESC_MAX = 150`, and the two limits on how many skills are listed (15 in the system prompt, 20 in the hub) are merged into `SKILL_LIST_MAX = 20`.
- **The docs were teaching the wrong thing**: `CLAUDE.md` said `description` must "spell out the triggers" and `javis-builder` said "write it in detail", while the runtime truncates. Both now state the 150 cap WITH THE REASON (longer text is lost silently, the skill cannot be routed, count it yourself after writing) and say that the full trigger examples belong in the `## Khi nào dùng` (When to use) section in the body, which is not truncated. Architecture: the index is for FINDING, the body is for DOING.
- **`javis-builder` pointed to the wrong place to write skills**: the skill builder taught writing to `.claude/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md` in three places, but that is a derived MIRROR. The canonical path is `skills/<slug>/SKILL.md`. All three fixed.
### Added
- **Rewrote the descriptions of 5 system skills to fit the cap**: `html-to-webcake` (376 characters), `javis-builder` (333), `ingest-source` (266), `query-wiki` (249), `lint-wiki` (213) are now 69 to 110 characters. No information lost: every trigger example moved to the `## Khi nào dùng` (When to use) section in the body. Also dropped the empty opener "Kích hoạt khi người dùng muốn" ("Activates when the user wants to", 29 identical characters in every skill, burning nearly half the budget while telling skills apart not at all).
- **CI lint blocks the bug from coming back**: `server/test_skill_caps.py` scans every system skill and fails on a description over the cap, with boilerplate, empty, or with broken frontmatter. It lists EVERY offending skill in one run instead of stopping at the first.
- **`POST /skills` rejects a bad description at write time**: before, the endpoint only checked the slug, so a 400-character description was saved and then silently truncated. It now returns 400 with the reason, and checks BEFORE creating the folder, so a rejected request leaves no empty folder on disk.
- **Skill writing standard built into `javis-builder`**: 8 mandatory points (150 cap, no boilerplate, double quotes when the description has a colon, order of body sections, no invented flags or paths, body length cap, no router-style skills). It says plainly that a skill written to disk from chat goes through NO blocking layer and that CI lint only checks system skills, so counting it yourself is the only line of defense.

Clicking a button sends it as if typed, in the same session. Only the last message is clickable; scroll up into history and the chips are frozen.

## [0.9.60] - 2026-07-16
### Fixed
- **Background loops see claude.ai connectors (Gmail/Drive/calendar) again through the opt-in `ambient_mcp` flag**: since the engine switch to the Agent SDK (around v0.9.35-0.9.37), self-running loops no longer "saw" claude.ai connectors such as Gmail, Google Drive and Google Calendar, so loops like "read Gmail in the afternoon and summarize" stopped working even though they used to. Cause: loops run in a permission-locked background fork (each tool approved one by one, every tool outside the whitelist denied by default), and in that branch the SDK engine deliberately does NOT load machine config (`setting_sources`) so allow-rules in settings cannot hide the gate layer. A side effect is that claude.ai connectors (which only appear when machine config is loaded, as `claude -p` does) disappear from loops. The old Popen branch ran `--dangerously-skip-permissions` plus `--mcp-config` without `--strict`, so connectors were always merged in, which is why old loops could read Gmail. Chat (web and Telegram) is NOT affected because it runs the non-locked branch that reloads `setting_sources`. Fix: a new per-loop frontmatter flag `ambient_mcp: true`. When on, that loop runs the non-gated branch (machine config loaded, so claude.ai connectors reappear), Bash/WebFetch/WebSearch/Task stay hard-blocked, and money/order tools through the hub stay locked by mode. OFF BY DEFAULT so a fork starts clean and no loop touches anyone's Gmail/Drive on its own; turn it on only when the user clearly asks. The verification step always stays locked down even when the flag is on. Comes with a behavior test in `test_loop_ambient.py`.
### Security
- **No real identifier in config examples + git sweep**: `system/mcp-catalog.json` mistakenly used a real identifier as a suggested placeholder; it is now the fake number `1234567890` so a fork shows nobody's real information. Swept every git-tracked file: all connection data files (Connection store, hub config, settings, secret keys, tokens) are already in `.gitignore` and were never committed, so anyone forking gets a blank copy with no connection preinstalled.

- **3D graph glaring white + lost twinkling while "thinking"**: since v0.9.55 the 3D version was colored by category (rainbow palette) and pulled into a tight ball, but the 3D version renders with `AdditiveBlending` (light adds up), so many colors piled up in a tight cluster drifted to WHITE - burned-white cores that looked glaring. ## [0.9.53] - 2026-07-15
### Fixed
- **Substack connection reported "Substack 403: <!DOCTYPE html>..." on Test/cookie fetch**: the bridge `server/substack_mcp.py` called the Substack API with `httpx`, but Substack sits behind Cloudflare, which blocks Python clients by TLS fingerprint (returning 403 with a whole HTML page). So not only the Test button but also creating drafts and publishing were hit. Fix: moved all of the bridge's HTTP calls to `curl` (verified that curl reaches the Substack app, returning JSON / "Not authorized"; available on both Windows and the Docker image). Also filters error messages to be SHORT and clean (no long HTML dumped into chat and the Connection form). With a correct session token, Test now returns 200 and the connection succeeds.
- **The Connection form still overflowed/could not scroll even after the v0.9.49 patch**: the CSS patch (`.conn-form` scrollable) was in `console.css` but did NOT show up because `index.html` loaded `console.css?v=14` (cache-bust) that had not been bumped - the browser kept using the old cached CSS. Fix: bumped to `?v=15` so the browser fetches the new version. Added a CLEARLY VISIBLE scrollbar for `.conn-form` (accent color on hover) and capped the error message in the footer so it cannot grow too tall and push the Connect button out.

## [0.9.52] - 2026-07-15
### Fixed
- **Clicking "Open" on a file (video/image/document) Jarvis 007 attached in chat said "File not found" though the file exists**: links and images Jarvis 007 inserts in chat use paths relative to the VAULT ROOT (e.g. `videos/tin-tuc.mp4`, `attachments/anh.jpg`) as the CLAUDE.md convention says, but the file-serving endpoints (`/files/raw`, `/files/read`, `/files/download`) resolved paths against the File Manager's browse CEILING. On localhost (no login required) the browse ceiling reaches the WHOLE DISK, so `videos/tin-tuc.mp4` was read as `D:\videos\tin-tuc.mp4` and always returned 404. The bug only showed on localhost; the public/login build (ceiling = brain root) matches, so it was not affected. Fix: added the resolver `_safe_serve_path` for the READ-ONLY endpoints, accepting BOTH conventions - first relative to the ceiling (keeping File Manager behavior), and if not found, relative to the vault root (links/images in chat). Both branches stay locked inside the browse ceiling, and the vault branch is tightened inside the brain root, so access is not widened, and the write/delete/rename endpoints are untouched. Tested by calling the real server function directly: vault paths that used to 404 now serve the right file, File Manager style paths still work, and a `../` attempt out of the vault is not loosened. The Jarvis 007 server must be restarted for the patch to take effect.

## [0.9.51] - 2026-07-15
### Fixed
- **The helper that gets the Substack User ID did not work because Substack changed its Profile link format**: Substack dropped Profile URLs like `substack.com/profile/12345678-ten` (with a number) for `substack.com/@handle` (no number), so the old "Way A" (pull the number from the URL) was useless. Added backend endpoint `GET /connect/substack/resolve-uid` that takes a handle or Profile link, asks Substack's public API, and returns the User ID plus Publication URL suggestions. Because Substack sits behind Cloudflare (blocks httpx by TLS fingerprint, returns 403), the endpoint calls through `curl` (available on both Windows and the Docker image) - the handle is strictly validated and passed as argv so there is no SSRF/command injection risk; the endpoint is still behind the auth guard. The Docs page updates Way A: paste the `@handle` link and click "Get User ID" to get the number + a Copy button + a list of suggested Publication URLs to click to copy. Tested end to end on the backend (real curl) and the front end (mock fetch in the browser).

## [0.9.50] - 2026-07-15
### Fixed
- **CI and Docker build red on every push (library conflict in requirements.txt)**: GitHub Actions kept sending "Run failed" mail for both the CI and Build Docker workflows, failing right at the `pip install -r requirements.txt` step. The cause dates from v0.9.35 (unrelated to Substack): the commit that added the Agent SDK engine pinned `starlette<0.39`, but `fastapi==0.115.6` (bumped in the v0.9.12 security patch) requires `starlette>=0.40` - two constraints clashing so pip could not solve them. Version 0.115.6 was in fact never installed; the app still ran fastapi 0.115.0 + starlette 0.38.6. Fix: lowered the pin to `fastapi==0.115.0` to match `starlette<0.39` and what really runs. This exposed a second hidden conflict: `uvicorn==0.30.6` clashes with `mcp` (requires `uvicorn>=0.31.1`) - raised to `uvicorn==0.51.0` (the version the .venv uses). A trial resolve came out clean and the full local test suite ran (8/8 pass) before pushing. Added a note in requirements.txt that fastapi and starlette are locked as a pair so it does not recur.

## [0.9.47] - 2026-07-15
### Added

The publish tool creates then publishes (title+body) or publishes an existing draft (draft_id); there is a compact converter from markdown to Substack's body format (# headings, lists, quotes, **bold**, *italic*, [link], `code`). Publishing goes to the web only by default, NO email to subscribers; the send-mail flag turns on only when you say so clearly (once sent it cannot be undone). ## [0.9.45] - 2026-07-14
### Fixed
- **No more "CLINotFoundError: Claude Code not found at ...\_bundled\claude.exe" on heavy work (long system prompt)**: the Claude engine reported Claude Code not found even though it was installed and signed in. The culprit was NOT a missing Claude Code but the Windows command-line length limit (32767 characters): the Agent SDK library stuffed the whole Jarvis 007 system prompt into a command-line ARGUMENT when launching Claude, and with a brain full of notes/memory the system prompt passed the threshold, Windows refused to create the process, Python raised "file not found" and the SDK mislabeled it "Claude Code not found" (pointing at the bundled copy). The threshold was probed and reproduced: a ~32k prompt works, ~33k and above breaks. Fix: pass the system prompt through a FILE (`--append-system-prompt-file`) instead of the command line, so prompt length is no longer limited (verified running smoothly at 48k-60k characters). The temp file is cleaned up after each turn, with a sweep for leftover files if the process is killed midway. This bug affected every chat/edit task on a large brain, not just video work. Includes tests in `test_sdk_engine.py`.

## [0.9.44] - 2026-07-13
### Fixed
- **Telegram chat no longer loses context in long sessions (finishing the same class of bug as v0.9.43)**: version 0.9.43 only patched the dashboard chat path; the Telegram chat path still had the exact same bug of forgetting the start of the conversation in a long session or right after switching from the Claude engine (Claude Code) to an API engine. Cause: unlike the dashboard (which rebuilds history from the database every turn and then compacts), a Telegram session keeps history IN MEMORY (`sess["or"]` per chat_id) and after each turn only HARD-CUT it to the 12 latest messages - the older part was dropped SILENTLY with no summary so the model forgot the earlier thread entirely. The hard cut is now replaced by `compact_mem` - the in-memory version of the dashboard compaction mechanism: the older part that falls out of the window is SUMMARIZED (merged with the old summary) and inserted as a system message right after the head, the most recent part is kept verbatim, a summary is only made when long enough to be worth one compaction, and if the provider fails it falls back to a safe cut so the payload does not grow without bound. The summarizing logic is split out and shared with the dashboard path (`compaction._summarize`). Includes behavior tests in `test_compaction.py` (covering multi-round rolling compaction, short sessions kept verbatim, and the provider-failure case).

## [0.9.43] - 2026-07-13
### Fixed
- **API engine chat (OpenAI/OpenRouter/Gemini/Anthropic API) no longer loses context midway**: in a long session or right after switching from the Claude engine (Claude Code) to an API engine, Jarvis 007 often forgot the start of the conversation and answered off-purpose (e.g. while discussing video editing, asked to "rewrite the plan" it went and wrote a Jarvis 007 product plan). Cause: each API engine chat turn rebuilt history from the database and then hard-cut it to the 12 latest messages - the older part should have been replaced by a compacted summary, but that summary was ONLY created when earlier turns also ran on an API engine. If Claude Code was used before (that engine manages its own memory and makes no summary), the head was cut SILENTLY with no summary, the model had only the system prompt + the last question and made up content from the system prompt. The hard cut is now replaced by `prepare_history`: the older part ONLY leaves the payload once it is inside the compacted summary; if the uncompacted tail of the conversation is too long (engine switched midway, or background compaction has not caught up) it compacts SYNCHRONOUSLY one round before sending to fold the older part into the summary. This guarantees no message is ever dropped silently. Includes behavior tests in `test_compaction.py` (covering the Claude-to-API engine switch and the short session kept verbatim).

## [0.9.42] - 2026-07-13
### Fixed
- **Long tasks (video editing, rendering, background removal...) are no longer wrongly killed at second 180**: the anti-hang watchdog treated "engine silent for 180 seconds" as a hang and cut the session, but when Claude/Codex calls a long-running tool (an hour-long video render, background removal, a build), silence while the tool runs is NORMAL - so a long job in progress was stopped with the message "Claude did not respond for 180s". The watchdog now tells two states apart: while WAITING FOR A TOOL to run it has its own 1-hour ceiling (change with the variable `JAVIS_CLAUDE_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, see [Env configuration](docs/16-cau-hinh-env.md)), while silence with NO tool running (a real hang) is still cut at 180 seconds as before. Applies to both the Claude engine (Agent SDK) and Codex CLI. Comes with 2 behavior tests in `test_sdk_engine.py`.
- **No more silent "(không có nội dung trả về)" ("no content returned")**: when a Claude session ends in ERROR without any text (common on the turn right after the previous session was cut midway), the engine now states the kind of error and suggests how to get out (resend / open a new conversation) instead of leaving the chat box showing an empty line with no stated cause.

## [0.9.41] - 2026-07-13
### Fixed
- **Jarvis 007's voice is no longer recorded back into the chat box**: before, when Jarvis 007 read an answer aloud (TTS), the speech-recognition mic stayed open and heard Jarvis 007's own voice from the speaker, transcribed it, and after 1.5 seconds of silence sent it into the chat box as a user message (most common when hands-free mode is on and you press a key to send - the mic stays open while Jarvis 007 talks). Cause: the recognizer (SpeechRecognition) records on its own stream WITHOUT echo cancellation, and there was no mutual exclusion between listening and speaking. Fixed in 2 layers in voice.js: (1) when Jarvis 007 starts reading while the mic is listening, recognition is paused right away (even a half-heard part is dropped), and when all reading ends it reopens listening after a short beat with a fresh recognition session; (2) any recognition result that comes in while sound is playing is dropped (surely Jarvis 007's voice, not the user's). Voice interruption (barge-in) still works normally because it measures sound level through the echo-cancelled mic stream and does not rely on recognition. If the user turns the mic off on purpose (Esc/button) it is not reopened automatically.

## [0.9.39] - 2026-07-12
### Fixed
- **Meta Ads connection reports errors honestly, no more dead end of "manual client_id needed"**: after deep investigation (real probes of Meta's endpoint + cross-checking official docs and community reports), it was established that `mcp.facebook.com/ads` is Meta's official MCP in a LIMITED beta: the server accepts only a few applications pre-approved by Meta (the assistants of ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) and has TURNED OFF self-registration of applications (DCR) - so Jarvis 007, and other tools too, cannot self-serve connect yet. This is a limit on Meta's side, not a fault on the user's machine. The old error message ("Server does not support client self-registration (DCR) - manual client_id needed") misled people into thinking pasting a client_id would be enough; it is now replaced with a clear explanation + Meta's message shown verbatim. The Meta Ads connector description and guide were also rewritten to match reality (dropped the line "one-tap sign-in, no need to create an app").

## [0.9.38] - 2026-07-12
### Added
- **The Files page can browse outside the brain (even to the whole disk)**: before, File Manager was hard-locked inside the brain folder, and clicking "Up" at the brain root was the end - data outside the vault could not be read/edited. Now when running on a personal machine (localhost), the browse ceiling opens up to the disk holding the brain: it still opens in the brain folder by default as before, but clicking "Up" can go all the way to the disk root to read/edit/download any file. Added a "⌂ Brain" button to jump back to the brain folder, and the "Up" button hides itself at the root. Safety is unchanged when running public (VPS/with login): still locked inside the brain so the whole disk is not exposed to the web. Tune with the variable `JAVIS_FILES_ROOT` (see [Env configuration](docs/16-cau-hinh-env.md)): force the brain lock, open the whole disk, or just one specific folder. The brain folder and the disk root cannot be deleted.

## [0.9.37] - 2026-07-12
### Improved
- **Fully removed the old Claude engine branch (Popen) - closing the Agent SDK plan file**: the Claude engine now runs only through the official Agent SDK. Deleted ~220 lines of homemade process spawn/parse code in claude_cli.py (where bugs like WinError 206 came from); Codex CLI and the shared auth/process-interrupt part stay as they are. The variable `JAVIS_CLAUDE_ENGINE` no longer has any effect (setting `cli`/`sdk-loops` is ignored with a log line). A machine without claude-agent-sdk gets a clear install instruction from the engine instead of a confusing error. All 6 test suites + a live check through the factory pass; the completion log is in docs/dev/2026-07-ke-hoach-agent-sdk.md.

## [0.9.36] - 2026-07-12
### Added
- **The Claude engine runs the official Agent SDK BY DEFAULT (all 4 phases of the plan complete)**: after the spike and smoke passed in full, the Claude engine now runs through claude-agent-sdk by default. Users have nothing to do - sign in to Claude Code as before, and chat/loop/workflow/Telegram run exactly the same but on a platform maintained by Anthropic, with background forks permission-blocked per tool call plus audit. If something goes wrong set the environment variable `JAVIS_CLAUDE_ENGINE=cli` to return to the old way at once (kept for at least one release); there is also an in-between level `sdk-loops` (only background tasks use the SDK). Verified by real isolated runs across all 3 flows: a 2-turn chat with session memory, a workflow running the whole chain of steps, and a suggest-mode loop told to "create the file at all costs" still unable to create a file; the server log is clean with no errors and no fallback.
- **Plugins run directly inside the server process (in-process) on the SDK engine**: plugin tools (ChatGPT image generation, Vietnam date-time, user-written plugins) no longer detour through the HTTP hub - the engine calls the Python handler directly, faster, and plugins work even when NO MCP connection is set up yet. The hub drops the plugin group by itself when the engine already has the in-process copy (no more risk of the model seeing 2 tools doing the same thing); other engines (Codex, API) still use plugins through the hub as before. The plugin min_mode permission level is still honored according to suggest/auto/full mode.

## [0.9.35] - 2026-07-12
### Added
- **The Claude engine can run through the official Agent SDK (experimental, Phase 0-2 of the plan)**: the spike passed all 7 items (subscription auth with no API key, stream, resume, interrupt, MCP config, a 43k-character prompt with no WinError 206, and time to first token even FASTER than the old way, 3.6s vs 4.0s). Added the engine `claude_sdk_engine.py` with the same contract as the old CLI engine; turn it on to try with the environment variable `JAVIS_CLAUDE_ENGINE=sdk` and restart - the default is still `cli` as before, and if the SDK fails it falls back to the CLI by itself. The Stop button interrupts both kinds of engine.
- **Per-call permissions for background forks (the biggest safety upgrade of this batch)**: when running the SDK engine, safe background forks (suggest/auto loops, task, reminder, learn) block tools OUTSIDE the whitelist on EVERY CALL, including builtin Bash/Write - with a JSONL audit at `logs/sdk_tool_audit.jsonl` in the state folder. Real smoke test: a read-only fork told to "create the file by any means" still could not create a file. Before, it could only be limited by a static list at spawn time, with no audit of builtin tools.
### Fixed
- **Pinned starlette to avoid breaking the server when installing new dependencies**: the `mcp` package (a dependency of claude-agent-sdk) pulled starlette 1.x, which conflicts with fastapi 0.115; requirements.txt pins `starlette<0.39` + `sse-starlette<3` (pip check clean).

## [0.9.34] - 2026-07-12
### Added
- **API engine chat no longer "loses its memory" in long sessions (conversation compaction)**: before, a long chat session on an API engine (OpenRouter/OpenAI/Anthropic API/Gemini) kept only the 12 latest messages and the older part was cut off - ask about the start of the session and Jarvis 007 forgot it entirely. Now the older history that falls out of the window is SUMMARIZED automatically (runs in the background after each turn, merged cumulatively with the previous summary) and fed back to the head of the session - Jarvis 007 still remembers the earlier thread (decisions, numbers, unfinished work) without the payload growing. The summary is stored durably in SQLite per session, and old DBs migrate by themselves. Ports the idea of session_memory_compaction from the Anthropic cookbook. Comes with the test `test_compaction.py` running in CI.
### Improved
- **Workflows self-improve in a proper evaluator-optimizer way**: a step with `verify_agent` that is graded NOT PASSED now sees the PREVIOUS RESULT together with the feedback to keep fixing (keep the good part, fix what was criticized) instead of redoing it blind from scratch - fewer repeats of the same error, faster convergence. The workflow template in the system docs adds 2 optional keys `verify_agent`/`max_retries` so Jarvis 007 knows to use the verification loop when creating workflows through chat.
- **Plan to move the Claude engine to the official Agent SDK**: wrote a detailed plan at `docs/dev/2026-07-ke-hoach-agent-sdk.md` - why (the homemade Popen layer is a bug nest for WinError 206, static tool permissions), an adapter architecture that keeps the ClaudeCLI interface, mapping the 3 permission levels suggest/auto/full into the per-tool-call `can_use_tool` callback, a 4-phase roadmap + go/no-go spike, risks and success criteria. Not coded yet - awaiting approval.

## [0.9.33] - 2026-07-12
### Added
- **Prompt caching for API engines**: learned from Anthropic's official cookbook. The Anthropic API branch with MCP tools (the branch that runs the most requests - each tool-call round is a request carrying the whole ~26k-character system prompt + tool schema + conversation) now caches system + tools + conversation, and later rounds pay only ~10% of the input price for the cached part. The new marking approach does not mutate the original conversation, so there is no longer a risk of markers accumulating past the API's 4-breakpoint cap (the reason this branch used to have caching turned off). Claude models run through OpenRouter also get the system prompt cached. Comes with the new test `test_engine_cache.py` running in CI.
- **Second Brain: self-contained wiki pages (contextual retrieval)**: the `ingest-source` skill now requires every wiki page to open with 1-2 positioning sentences (what concept, which source/topic it belongs to, when to use it) and to declare `aliases` (other names, English terms) in the frontmatter - so that asking later with different words still hits the page in search, and reading a single page apart from its source is still understandable. The idea comes from Anthropic's contextual retrieval recipe, applied to file-style search with no vector DB.
- **javis-builder writes system prompts in the metaprompt frame**: when creating an agent through chat, Jarvis 007 now builds the system prompt in a 6-part frame drawn from Anthropic's metaprompt (role + goal, business context, numbered procedure, output format with examples, how to handle hard cases, specific prohibitions) instead of 1-2 generic sentences - the created agent works right away with less rework. Two system skills update themselves into every brain that has not been hand-edited (a brain that has been edited keeps its own copy).

## [0.9.32] - 2026-07-12
### Fixed
- **Meta Ads connection no longer reports "This server does not declare standard MCP OAuth"**: Meta declares an OAuth issuer with a path (`mcp.facebook.com/ads`) and places the metadata in the RFC 8414 inserted form (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/ads`), while Jarvis 007 only looked for the appended form and the domain root so it did not find it. The discovery step now tries both forms (inserted first, appended as fallback) for both the issuer and the MCP URL with a path - clicking Connect brings up the Facebook sign-in page as designed. Other OAuth connectors behave as before.

## [0.9.31] - 2026-07-11
### Fixed
- **Pasting a long article into chat no longer blows up with "Subprocess error: WinError 206"**: before, the message (plus system prompt) was passed to the CLI engine through the command line, and Windows caps the command line at 32767 characters - pasting a long article or a big block of text went over the ceiling and failed with "FileNotFoundError: The filename or extension is too long" before the engine could even run. The prompt is now fed through stdin (not through the command line) so any amount pasted works; applies to both the Claude Code and Codex engines. Tested for real with a prompt of over 40 thousand characters.

## [0.9.30] - 2026-07-11
### Added
- **The ElevenLabs key in Settings is shared for video editing**: Jarvis 007 now knows how to build and cut video through two outside toolkits (HyperFrames creates new video from HTML, video-use cuts dead air / inserts subtitles / color-corrects real footage - installed as a skill for the CLI engines). The transcription part of video-use needs an ElevenLabs key: just enter the key in one place at **Settings > Voice (ElevenLabs)** as always, and the server injects the `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` environment variable into the engine and child tools at startup and as soon as Settings are saved (no restart, no editing the .env file). The key is still encrypted at rest like other secrets.
### Fixed
- **Python child processes no longer crash on Unicode on Windows**: the server sets `PYTHONUTF8=1` for child processes (respecting a value the user already set), avoiding UnicodeEncodeError when tools like video-use print special characters to a cp1252 console.
- **The masked value "••••" can no longer overwrite the real ElevenLabs key**: an outside client that fetches settings from GET /settings (key shown masked) and POSTs the whole object back no longer loses the saved key.

## [0.9.29] - 2026-07-10
### Added
- **Voice on/off button right on the chat box**: added a speaker button next to the mic and attach buttons on the chat input bar (shown on both the 3D screen and the Chat tab). Click to turn Jarvis 007 reading answers aloud on or off without going to the top corner or into Settings. When off, the button turns red with a strike-through to be easy to see; state syncs both ways with the speaker button in the header and the "Read replies aloud" switch in quick Settings, and is remembered across reloads.

## [0.9.28] - 2026-07-09
### Added
- **Telegram shows an intermediate status while waiting**: before, messaging Jarvis 007 through Telegram meant waiting in silence until the answer came, easy to mistake for a hang. Now the bot sends a status message ("🤔 Jarvis 007 is processing…") and updates it with the real progress of the turn (which tool is being called, data received, composing the answer); when done it deletes the status message and sends the answer. Updates are throttled (~2.5s) so as not to spam or hit Telegram limits. Applies to both the Claude Code engine and the API engines.

## [0.9.27] - 2026-07-09
### Added
- **Clicking a node on the 3D graph opens a read/edit note popup**: before, clicking a node on the chart sent a question straight into the chat box (confusing). Now clicking a node opens a window showing the note content to read and edit directly then Save (read/write through the proper Files API), with a button to open in a new tab; press Esc or ✕ to close.
### Improved
- **Esc no longer stops the answer / cuts off Jarvis 007 while it is speaking**: before, pressing Esc both paused the voice and cut the running turn, easy to lose an answer by accident. Now Esc only exits hands-free mode, turns off the mic and closes the popup. To stop, use the Stop button (red box) or the mute toggle.

## [0.9.26] - 2026-07-09
### Added
- **Multiple conversations running in parallel (like Claude)**: clicking "New conversation" no longer stops the conversation that is answering. Each chat turn runs independently in the background, so you can open a new conversation and ask something else RIGHT while the old one is still generating - both run at the same time. The History list shows ⏳ on a conversation that is answering; click a conversation running in the background to watch the part being composed live, and every turn saves to its own session even when you are viewing somewhere else. The Stop button only interrupts the conversation you are viewing; other background conversations are unaffected.
### Improved
- **The chat core handles each turn as a background task**: the server no longer locks to one-connection-one-turn-at-a-time; each turn has its own engine and every packet carries a session_id so the interface routes to the right session (with a write lock so interleaved turns do not corrupt a packet). The whole stream, session, MCP/skill and voice flow is unchanged. Also, if the Claude Code CLI is not installed but you use an API/OpenRouter engine, the connection is no longer blocked as before (an error is reported per turn only if the CLI is truly needed).

## [0.9.25] - 2026-07-09
### Added
- **"Chat" tab - a dedicated, roomy chat screen**: added a new tab on the left bar (right under "Jarvis 007") that opens a full-screen Claude-style chat, far more convenient than the cramped chat box beside the 3D screen. The left column is the conversation history (new button, a search box across all conversations, grouped by Today / Past 7 days / Older, rename and delete, the open session highlighted); the middle is a large easy-to-read chat with a title and the real engine badge (e.g. "CLI · opus"); right above the input is the model + effort bar, and at the bottom is the typing box with mic and file-attach buttons. This tab does NOT rewrite the chat machinery but reuses the 3D screen's own chat box (borrowed then returned when you leave the tab), so the same conversation shows in both places, keeping WebSocket, stream, session, voice and attachments intact; leave the tab and the 3D screen chats normally. Entering the chat tab turns the 3D graphics off by itself to go easy on the machine. On narrow screens (phones) the history column collapses into a drawer, opened with the 🕘 button.
### Fixed
- **Prevent lost content when switching pages quickly**: each time a management page is switched, the content frame (`#cviewBody`) is replaced with a new region, so if a slow-loading page (Overview, Models, Connections...) returns its result LATE after you have moved to another page, that write lands in the abandoned old region and does not overwrite the page you are viewing. Before, switching very fast from a slow-loading page to the Chat tab could wipe out the chat box you had just opened; it is now safe, and the flicker of the old page's content when changing pages is gone too.

## [0.9.20] - 2026-07-09
### Added
- **Loops and Tasks report results back to the requester's Telegram by themselves**: now the default Jarvis 007 behavior - every time a background loop iteration finishes, and every task (Kanban task) completes, it messages the result to the Telegram of the very person who asked (with a summary, the verification line, and a warning if the loop paused itself). A loop or task created on the web build (owner unknown) reports to the first Telegram ID in the whitelist. A loop also stores `owner_chat` (the creator's chat_id) in its frontmatter; a task stores the matching `chat_id` - Jarvis 007 attaches it automatically when you create through chat. An iteration skipped for lack of data sends no message so as not to disturb; to make a loop stop reporting every iteration set `notify: false` in that loop's frontmatter.

- **The chat box renders faithfully like Claude and can view Artifacts**: AI answers now show in full like in the Claude chat box. When a self-contained HTML page, an SVG image, a mermaid diagram or a long code file is returned, Jarvis 007 shows a compact artifact card in the chat flow; clicking opens a right-side panel with Preview / Source tabs plus Copy and Download buttons. HTML runs in an isolated sandbox iframe (cannot touch the parent page), SVG renders with scripts disabled, mermaid draws as a diagram (offline it drops to showing the source with a note). Press Esc to close the panel without also collapsing an enlarged chat box.
### Improved
- **More complete markdown and code blocks**: added multi-level headings, numbered + nested lists + checkboxes, blockquote, horizontal rule, italics, strikethrough; code blocks have a language label and syntax coloring, keeping the Copy button. While streaming, an unclosed piece of code still shows neatly as a code block being typed instead of raw text. The renderer moved to its own file `dashboard/chat-render.js`, keeping the left-panel numbers, vault images and links as before.

## [0.9.18] - 2026-07-07
