- **The model + effort switch menu is also in the enlarged chat box**: before, the model picker bar showed only in the normal chat box; when you enlarged the conversation (the ⛶ button / Collapse with Esc) the bar was left behind and not visible. Now when entering full-screen mode, the model picker bar is moved along right above the input, opens the provider/model picker menu and changes effort normally; collapse it back and it returns to its old place.

## [0.9.17] - 2026-07-07
### Added
- **Switch model + effort right on the chat box**: added a small bar right above the dashboard chat box showing the running provider, model and "Thinking" level (effort). Click to open a combined menu: a model list grouped by 6 providers (Claude Code, ChatGPT, OpenRouter, Anthropic API, OpenAI API, Google Gemini), with a model search box and an effort row (Off/Low/Medium/High) at the bottom. A connected provider expands to pick a model (the list loads dynamically per account), an unconnected provider shows locked with a shortcut to the Models page to add a key. Picking a model or effort saves straight to config and takes effect on the next chat turn, and the engine badge updates itself. Everything reuses existing endpoints so the chat/engine flow does not change.

## [0.9.16] - 2026-07-07
### Added
- **Start with the computer (Windows)**: added a "Start with computer" item on the Overview page to turn Jarvis 007 auto-running at boot on or off. Turned on, Jarvis 007 runs hidden in the background right after you sign in to Windows (no black window, open `localhost:7777` to use), and stops the old copy before running so there is no duplicate. The mechanism uses a per-account registry key (`HKCU...\Run`, no admin rights needed) pointing to the existing `start-javis.vbs`; with 2 `/autostart` endpoints to see status and toggle, and a flag that notices when you move the install folder. This item hides itself on Docker/Linux builds.
- **Reminders from chat**: saying things like "remind me in 30 minutes...", "remind me at 8:30 tomorrow morning...", "every morning at 7 remind me to take medicine" makes Jarvis 007 set the schedule itself, and when the time comes it wakes up and fires the reminder through Telegram to the very person speaking. You can schedule by number of minutes, time of day, a specific date, or a recurring schedule using a cron expression; the server works out Vietnam time by itself so you only need to say it in words. Three modes: reminder only (notify), do the work and send the result back (task), or run a monitoring script that needs NO AI to be cheap (script, only runs a file you already put in `Javis/scripts`). Reminders also show on the Work/Schedule page, flip the switch to cancel.
- **Added Google Gemini provider**: plug in a Gemini API key and the 2.5 Flash/Pro and 2.0 Flash models work for chat, including agent mode using Jarvis 007's MCP just like OpenAI. It goes through the OpenAI-compatible endpoint so it reuses exactly the same stream + tool-calling flow; the model list loads dynamically per account, and turning on "Thinking" applies to 2.5 models and above.
- **HTML → Webcake (.pke) skill**: converts an HTML file or snippet into a Webcake file that opens and can be edited in the landing page builder - reads the HTML, rebuilds it as a `page_source` in the exact Webcake mold, then exports `.pke` to upload and keep editing.

## [0.9.15] - 2026-07-06
### Fixed
- **Favicon now matches the app logo**: the icon on the browser tab was still the old default image even though the link pointed correctly. Cause: the path `/favicon.ico` (which the browser ALWAYS calls itself) returned 404 so the browser kept the old cached icon. Added a route that returns the current logo directly (default `logo.png`, changing automatically with the image you upload). Browsers cache favicons stubbornly so close and reopen the tab to see the new icon.
- **Empty strip above the chat box**: the `.hud` grid declared one row too few so the attachment bar (when empty) took up a 70px row, leaving an empty strip across the full width right above the input. Added an `auto` row for the attachment bar so it shrinks to 0 when empty; the body now stretches all the way down to the chat box.
- **The "History" button overlapped header buttons**: the "History" button floated fixed in the right corner, covering the Settings / Read / Reset conversation buttons below. The button now sits in the same row as the header buttons so they no longer overlap.

## [0.9.14] - 2026-07-06
### Added
- **"Usage" panel - multi-provider token metering**: the sidebar now shows the amount of tokens Jarvis 007 **measures itself** through each provider/model during the day (in ↑ / out ↓ + a cost estimate where the provider returns it, e.g. Claude Code), plus a total. Uniform for every engine (Claude Code, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenRouter, OpenAI API, Anthropic API) because Jarvis 007 reads the usage in every response. Includes the **REAL OpenRouter balance** if a key is plugged in (the only provider that exposes a balance through its API). This is the amount Jarvis 007 used, NOT a subscription plan quota - most providers do not let you fetch an account quota through the API so check in their app.

## [0.9.13] - 2026-07-06
### Added
- **Share agents / skills / workflows through files**: each agent, skill, workflow now has a **⤓ Export** button to download a `.zip` package, and each page (Agents / Skills / Workflows) has a **⤒ Import** button to upload a package - swapping capabilities with others is easy. A workflow package automatically **includes the agents it uses + those agents' skills** (your skills, NOT system skills) so the receiver can run it at once; an agent package includes its skills. Import accepts `.zip`, single `.md` files (agent/workflow), and **even Claude's `.skill` skill package** (Jarvis 007 recognizes the `SKILL.md` in the package and puts it in the right skill folder). There are safety guards (anti zip-slip, size limit) and a duplicate name is skipped unless you choose overwrite.

## [0.9.12] - 2026-07-06
### Security
- **Patched 2 DoS vulnerabilities in base libraries** (CVE-2024-47874 Starlette, CVE-2024-53981 python-multipart): raised fastapi to 0.115.6 (pulling Starlette up to 0.41.3) and python-multipart to 0.0.18. Before, an attacker who was NOT signed in could send a malformed multipart form to a public endpoint (sign-in / setup) to overload a VPS server.
- **Blocked XSS in the dashboard**: the escape functions now also escape quotes (`"` and `'`), so content generated by AI/MCP (file names, task content...) cannot break out of an HTML attribute and run same-origin JavaScript that controls Jarvis 007. Also, external links (search results, auth URLs) are only rendered when they are http/https, blocking the `javascript:` scheme.

- **X (Twitter) in the Connection store** (X's official MCP, remote): search and read posts, view public profiles and metrics. Paste the App-only Bearer Token from the X Developer Portal; Read-only by default (an app-only token cannot post/message so it is safe). Posting on behalf of a user account needs OAuth - to be added when you need it.

- **Brand logos for connectors**: X, Higgsfield, TikTok Ads, Google Ads and Gmail now show real logos instead of emoji icons.

- **Higgsfield in the Connection store** (official MCP, remote): create and edit images/video with AI - image generation, video generation, upscale, expand the frame, remove background, cut out a character, motion control. One-tap Higgsfield sign-in: Jarvis 007 registers the application itself following the MCP OAuth standard (auto-probes metadata + DCR + PKCE, no need to create an app or paste a key), works on every engine. ## [0.9.9] - 2026-07-06
### Added
- **View images and open files right in chat + the Files page**: Jarvis 007 can embed images in an answer (shown directly in the chat box, click to open full in a new tab) and attach open/download links for files like PDF, DOCX, XLSX. The Files page previews images and PDFs inside the app; other files have an "Open" button to a new tab through a static path. Added the endpoint `/files/raw` that serves files inline (unlike `/files/download`, which always forces a download).
### Fixed
- **Images/files in chat could not be viewed on click; the Files page could not view images and could not open PDF/DOCX** (download only): because the chat box did not yet render markdown images/links and there was no URL serving files inline. It now shows images, opens PDFs in the app, and every file has a static path to open/download.

## [0.9.8] - 2026-07-06
### Added
- **Skills run on EVERY engine, no longer dependent on Claude's structure**: before, skills only worked well on Claude Code (read natively from `.claude/skills`), while ChatGPT/Codex could not call them. Jarvis 007 now has its own **skill router** shared by every engine: the skill list (name + description) is injected straight into the system prompt, with the `javis_use_skill` tool to load the skill content and follow it. Claude Code, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenRouter, OpenAI API and Anthropic API can now all use skills equally.
- **The skill storage place moved to `skills/` (flat, owned by Jarvis 007)**: in sync with `agents/`, `workflows/`, `memory/`. An old brain that kept skills in `.claude/skills` is **moved automatically to `skills/`** once (safe, no data lost, disabled skills kept as they are). Jarvis 007 still **mirrors** to `.claude/skills` so Claude Code loads it natively as a bonus - but the main router no longer depends on that folder.
### Improved
- **Skills Jarvis 007 learns by itself are now ON by default** (instead of left as a disabled draft awaiting approval), marked `origin: javis-learned` to recognize them; it still absolutely does NOT overwrite a skill you already have and does NOT revive a skill you deliberately turned off.
### Fixed
- **ChatGPT/Codex could not find skills**: the chat branch through Codex was not loaded with the Jarvis 007 system prompt and ran in the wrong working directory so it saw no skill. Codex now runs in the right brain folder and gets the full skill router, able to call skills the user created.
- **Editing a disabled skill showed empty content**: the Edit button used to read only skills in the enabled location so a disabled skill opened an empty form. It now reads skills in `.disabled` too; and Save when editing keeps the on/off state (does not turn on a disabled skill, does not leave an orphan draft).

## [0.9.7] - 2026-07-05
### Improved
- **Smoother voice, no more odd voice inserted, stops when you speak**: (1) the first audio plays FASTER - the first sentence is split into a small chunk to synthesize + load at once, less of the few-second stall after the text has shown; (2) when a read-aloud chunk fails on the network, Jarvis 007 retries in the correct Vietnamese voice and ABSOLUTELY does not fall back to the browser default voice (usually English) - no more "odd English voice inserted midway"; (3) interruption (barge-in) in hands-free: while reading, if it hears you speak clearly enough it stops by itself and starts listening at once, with mic echo/noise cancellation turned on so it hears itself less.
### Fixed
- A read-aloud chunk that failed used to be handled twice (Chrome fires both the error event and the play() rejection for the same audio), causing 2 reading streams overlapping and audio that could not be stopped; each failed chunk is now handled exactly once.

## [0.9.6] - 2026-07-04
### Improved
- **Cleaner, more sensible Settings page**: merged "Voice provider" into the same Voice group (before it sat apart at the very bottom, after the avatar and domain); removed the duplicate "Preview" button (kept a single one); hid the Edge voice list (HoaiMy/NamMinh) when the OpenAI/ElevenLabs provider is chosen because the voice is then picked right in the provider block; fixed a misleading title (dropped "Interface" because there is no such item); the preview button changed to an outline so the Save button stands out in its main role.
- **Clearer Docker update notice**: a Docker build without Watchtower now gives direct instructions to **Redeploy** to get the latest image (on Hostinger click the Redeploy button in Docker Manager; on a VPS run `docker compose up -d --pull always`), instead of saying "add a watchtower service yourself". The Version panel always shows this guidance when a new version exists but cannot update in place, no longer letting you click "Update now" and only then report an error.
### Fixed
- The "Update now" button used to count as able to self-update just because the `WATCHTOWER_TOKEN` variable was present in compose (even though Watchtower was not running); clicking it silently failed to trigger and then reported "version unchanged". It now **probes for a real Watchtower** (checks the port, sends no HTTP so as not to trigger an update by mistake) before deciding, avoiding false reports.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-07-04
### Added
- **The "Connections" page replaces the MCP page**: a store of preinstalled connectors (Pancake POS, personal Zalo, Webcake Landing, Botcake) - click Connect, paste a key (or scan a QR with Zalo) and you are done, no more typing the URL/transport/header yourself. Jarvis 007 checks the key and names the account by itself (taking the real shop name from POS). The old technical form is still in the "Add your own (advanced)" card.
- **Official multi-account**: one service connects MANY accounts (several POS shops, several Zalo numbers) - each account is a chip with a name + permission + default mark, add/disable/delete each one. Each Zalo account runs isolated (its own home) so several numbers run in parallel without stepping on each other.
- **MCP HUB**: every brain (Claude Code, ChatGPT/Codex, OpenRouter, OpenAI API, Anthropic API) connects through ONE point - Codex and the API engines can now use local MCP in stdio form (Zalo, Webcake) and not only http as before.
- **Anthropic API has a tool-call loop** - no more "plain chat with no MCP". API engines also gain tools to read/write files in the vault, `javis_use_skill` (activate a brain skill) and `javis_connections` - every engine is a real agent.
- **3 permission levels per connection** (Read-only / Draft writes / Full access) HARD-blocked at the hub on every call, understanding multi-action tools of the Pancake kind too (`action=list` passes, `action=create` is blocked). Background loops in suggest/auto mode have write/money-order actions blocked by the hub whatever the prompt says. Turning on Full access requires ticking a risk confirmation; Zalo has its own warning about the risk of account lock (unofficial API).
- **Tool-call log (audit)** viewable per connection, a re-Test button, and rate limiting against spam for Zalo.
- **Sign in to Zalo by scanning a QR right in the dashboard**: Jarvis 007 runs zalo-agent-cli by itself, shows the QR code in a modal, and creates the connection automatically after you scan (needs Node.js 20+).
- **MCP-standard OAuth** (PKCE + client self-registration): any server following the standard just needs Connect on the VPS, Jarvis 007 holds and refreshes the token by itself - no more opening a terminal to type /mcp.
- A self-written **Botcake** bridge through Public API v1 (13 tools: customers, tags, flows, send flow, keywords...) - nothing extra to install.
- **3 Google cards for business**: Google Sheets (dump revenue/stock reports into a spreadsheet - paste the service account JSON and it runs, no sign-in), Google Search Console (SEO metrics: what customers search to reach the website), Google Workspace (Gmail + Calendar + Drive + Docs in 1 connection, self-created OAuth with step-by-step guidance; Draft writes by default - can compose drafts but does NOT send mail/delete on its own, turning on Full access needs confirmation). The store supports file-type fields (paste JSON, Jarvis 007 handles the rest) and ships with uv/uvx to run Python connectors.
### Improved
- The MCP client has a **long-lived session pool** (keeps the connection between messages) + stdio/internal support: no more "each message reconnects MCP so it is a bit slow". The hub warms itself up at startup.
- The MCP registry moved to STATE_DIR (writable in Docker) and **migrates automatically** from the old version: old servers become connections, the original is backed up at `mcp_servers.v1.bak.json`, no data lost.
### Security
- Connection API keys/tokens are **encrypted at rest** (Fernet, a per-machine key). The audit log records only parameter NAMES, not values. The hub endpoint authenticates with its own internal token, not the dashboard session.

## [0.8.12] - 2026-07-03
### Added
- Telegram has the **`/brain`** command - view and switch the brain (vault) for your OWN session only: type `/brain` to open a button panel to pick from (the brain in use has a ✓), or type the name directly `/brain <name>` (a partial match works too). After switching, the conversation resets to load the right memory/skills of the new brain; other people sharing the bot and the dashboard are NOT affected. `/reset` keeps the chosen brain.
- Files sent to Telegram now land in `inbox/telegram` of the SENDER'S SESSION brain (before, always in the default brain).
- `/status` shows the brain the session is using.

## [0.8.11] - 2026-07-03
### Added
- Telegram **multi-session per account**: each chat ID now has its OWN conversation context, no longer mixed up when several people share 1 bot. Before, all users shared one session (the next person continued the previous person's thread, and only 1 person could be answered at a time). Now each account has its own Claude session (independent `--resume`), its own OpenRouter history, its own `/retry`.
- Accounts **run in parallel**: while A is being answered, B asking is still handled at once, with no queueing. Within the SAME account it is still sequential, 1 turn at a time (sending a new message while busy replies "still processing the previous message").
- `/reset` and `/stop` affect only **the typer's own session**: reset clears exactly their context, stop kills only their own Claude process (not touching others chatting). `/status` shows the session code.
- Files Jarvis 007 creates are sent to **the person who asked**: the endpoint `POST /telegram/send-file` accepts an extra `chat_id`, and the gateway reminds the engine to always attach the asker's chat_id to the send command (if missing it falls back to the bot owner as before). The whitelist still blocks unknown IDs.
### Fixed
- Web dashboard: the **Stop button no longer kills another person's turn** chatting in parallel. Each WebSocket connection now has its own session tag (the server sends it in the hello message, the frontend sends it along when POSTing `/stop`) - the web was already multi-session (each tab/connection one session, stored in SQLite and resumable), and this was the only remaining cross-hole.
- The **enlarged chat box (chat workspace) used NOT to show the status** "thinking / calling tool": the old status bar sat outside `#chatArea` so it was left behind when enlarged. Replaced with an activity chip inside the chat box.
### Improved
- **Activity chip in the chat box** (both normal and enlarged): a bouncing 3-dot bubble + a live status line ("Jarvis 007 is thinking...", "⚙ Calling: pos_statistics", "✍ Composing the answer...") + a seconds counter when waiting long (shown from the 3rd second). The chip shows AT ONCE when you press send, always sits at the very bottom even below a streaming bubble, and disappears by itself when the turn ends.

The whitelist blocks exactly by the list; group IDs (negative numbers) work too.
- The **Send test** button sends a test message to ALL IDs and says which ID failed (usually because that person has not pressed Start on the bot); background notifications (a loop pausing itself...) are also sent to all IDs; the status line shows the number of allowed IDs, with a clear warning when left empty (anyone can message). Files auto-sent to Telegram with no specific chat go to the FIRST ID (the bot owner).

## [0.8.8] - 2026-07-03
### Fixed
- Renamed the sample file `.env.example` → `env.example` (dropped the leading dot): Hostinger's Docker Manager scans `.env*` files in the repo when deploying from a URL and imports the whole content (including `#` comment lines) into the Environment box, causing a string of red "Invalid variable name" variables on every deploy. The Environment box on Hostinger now needs exactly 1 variable, `DOMAIN_NAME`. Anyone already hit: delete the lines with `#` in the Environment box once and it stays clean for good. Running locally changes nothing except the copy command: `cp env.example .env`.

## [0.8.7] - 2026-07-03
### Added
- **Telegram becomes a full work channel** (porting the idea of the hermes-agent gateway):
  - Jarvis 007 now **knows which channel it is answering through**: the gateway inserts a "Current conversation channel" block (Telegram DM/group with whom, chat_id, the connected platforms) into the system prompt every turn - ask "which channel are we chatting on" and it answers correctly, not by guessing.
  - **Auto-send files to Telegram**: files Jarvis 007 creates in the turn (Write tool) or files with an absolute path mentioned in the answer are attached and sent automatically right after the answer (up to 10 files per turn, each under 50MB; images are sent as a photo with preview, the rest as a document).
  - Internal endpoint `POST /telegram/send-file` (accepts ONLY from localhost - from outside through the proxy it is still blocked by login): the agent can proactively send any file on the machine mid-turn with curl.
  - **Receive files/images from Telegram**: send a file/image (with a caption) to the bot and Jarvis 007 downloads it to `inbox/telegram/` in the brain and reads it like a chat attachment (the bot API download ceiling is 20MB). Voice/video is not supported yet - Jarvis 007 will say so clearly.
  - Reply messages render in **MarkdownV2** (bold/italic/code/link shown nicely), falling back to plain text if Telegram refuses to parse - no message is lost.
### Improved
- The web dashboard also has its own channel block: Jarvis 007 tells whether it is talking through the web or Telegram, and knows how to push a file to Telegram when the user asks (if the bot is running).

The sidebar can be hidden/shown (state remembered); on narrow screens it turns into a floating drawer, and Esc closes the drawer first and only then collapses the chat. ## [0.8.5] - 2026-07-02
### Changed
- GitHub backup is upgraded to **2-WAY sync**: each turn both pushes changes from the machine up to the repo and pulls changes from other machines and merges them automatically. Several machines can share 1 repo (a home machine + a VPS working in turns, the machines matching up by themselves) - no more 2 machines force-pushing and overwriting each other's backup.
- A conflict on the same file edited in 2 places: the version with the NEWER edit wins, and the losing version is kept as a file `.conflict-<local|remote>-<time>` right beside it (not a single word silently lost); when one side edits and the other deletes, the edit wins. Pushing uses a normal push (force-push dropped); if another machine cuts in, it pulls, merges, and pushes again by itself.
- Restoring a new machine needs no manual git: paste the repo + token and click Sync now and the brain comes back in full. An empty brains folder is treated as RESTORE mode - it only receives, never pushes an "empty state" over the backup. Files missing locally (wipe/new volume) are patched back from the synced copy automatically.
### Fixed
- Sync transfers bytes verbatim between machines (git autocrlf turned off on the mirror) - no more the same file differing in CRLF/LF between Windows and a Linux VPS and never matching.
### Improved
- Self-learning page: the section renamed "⇅ Sync brain with GitHub (2-way)", and the "Sync now" button reports detailed results (how many files received, whether it pushed, the list of conflict files); the last status is saved with the report. If it cannot write back to the machine (file locked) it DEFERS the push to keep data safe, and tries again next time.

## [0.8.4] - 2026-07-02
### Changed
- Two layers split clearly: the **system layer** (Jarvis 007's default features - the skills javis-builder / ingest-source / query-wiki / lint-wiki + the self-improvement loop) now travels with the app source at `.claude/skills/` and `system/loops/`, updating with the version when the app updates; the **brain layer** is now only your data (memory, sources, wiki, self-created agents/skills/workflows/loops). Switching brain no longer loses default features.
- Sync with a manifest (`.javis/system-manifest.json` in each brain): when the app moves to a new version the system skill/loop copies in the brain are updated along, BUT a file you edited keeps your version (user override); loops keep the on/off state, mode and cycle you adjusted. If you delete a system file by mistake it is reinstalled (to stop using one, TURN OFF the skill - the off state is respected through every update).
- At startup it syncs for EVERY brain in the brains folder (before, only Brain Default was seeded at boot, and a brain created on an old version never received new skills); an outside brain chosen through `path:` is synced on the first use. The "Create structure" button (vault init) now seeds fully like a newly created brain.
- System skills are loaded NATIVELY for chat in every brain (the standard source sits in the app folder - the Claude Code engine reads it directly), no longer depending on a copy in the brain.
### Improved
- Skills page: system skills have a "system" label and cannot be deleted (only turned off/on or edited - editing makes it your own copy and stops auto-updating).

## [0.8.3] - 2026-07-02
### Added
- Jarvis 007 Index (`Javis/index.md`): an operations-layer index - lists EVERY agent/skill/workflow/loop/schedule in the brain, generated from files (not hand-edited), with an overview line + health flags (workflow pointing to a nonexistent agent, orphan agent, disabled skill, self-paused loop). Alongside wiki/index.md so any AI/engine reading one place understands what Jarvis 007 can do.
- A compact (live) version is inserted into the system prompt of every engine (Claude/Codex/OpenRouter) → solving the problem "switch model and lose awareness of skills", and helping avoid creating duplicate capabilities. Endpoint GET /javis/index. Rebuilt at startup + on the background beat (writes only when changed, no git churn).

## [0.8.2] - 2026-07-02
### Improved
- The Self-learning engine tightens 3 anti-fabrication disciplines (in sync with the vault schema): hard citation for every specific wiki sentence, labeling target-vs-actual (never turning a vision sentence into a firm claim), and keeping contradictions without overwriting. Self-generated wiki is now less but better, trustworthy to accumulate.
### Added
- 3 Second Brain operating skills (seeded into each brain, create-if-missing): **ingest-source** (digest a source, with 3-pass for long sources), **query-wiki** (answer with citations + save valuable results), **lint-wiki** (health-check 8 kinds of errors, returns a checklist only). Turns the 3 operations INGEST/QUERY/LINT from prose into self-triggering tools, consistent across engines.

## [0.8.1] - 2026-07-02
### Added
- The default brain is now a universal "compounding wiki" kit (no longer minimal): each brain seeds a schema doc itself (CLAUDE.md + AGENTS.md so both Claude Code and Codex load it themselves) + wiki navigation files (index.md, log.md, _open-questions.md) + _session-handoff.md (switching between models without losing the thread). It encodes the knowledge-accumulation pattern + 3 anti-fabrication disciplines (mandatory citation, target vs actual, contradictions kept visible) + the 3 operations INGEST/QUERY/LINT.
- Industry-neutral: does NOT seed marketing/Bullet Journal folders; the taxonomy grows with real sources, with industry packs reserved as opt-in. All create-if-missing (does not overwrite files you edited).

## [0.8.0] - 2026-07-02
### Changed
- GitHub backup now syncs the WHOLE brains folder (every brain) in ONE pass instead of brain by brain (fixing brains overwriting each other when auto-backing up into the same repo). Each brain is a subfolder in the repo; delete a brain from the machine and the next backup drops it too. It is recommended to keep every brain in the brains folder (a new brain created with the ➕ button goes there automatically) to make moving machines easy.
- The new mechanism uses a clean copy (mirror): it leaves out original conversations/logs/locks + each brain's raw git (avoiding the nested-repo bug), and the token does not leak into .git/config.
### Added
- Changed the default avatar/logo of Jarvis 007.

Created create-if-missing, not overwriting files you edited.

## [0.7.5] - 2026-07-02
### Added
- Back up the brain to GitHub: a new section in the Self-learning page, with a 3-step guide right on screen (create a private repo → create a fine-grained token → paste it in). A Check connection button + Back up now + a switch for periodic auto backup. Detailed docs: docs/18-sao-luu-github.md.

- The GitHub token is stored internally in settings.json (gitignored), is NOT pushed to the repo and is masked automatically in every error message; the push uses a temporary URL so the token is not in .git/config. ## [0.7.4] - 2026-07-02

## [0.7.3] - 2026-07-02

- A full-access loop still respects each MCP server's "block tool" setting (deny_tools); the self-verification step switches to checking "within the task scope" instead of forbidding actions. Jarvis 007 in chat NEVER sets a loop to full access by itself - only when the user asks clearly.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-07-02
### Added
- MULTI-LOOP: the "Self-improvement loop" is upgraded to a system of MANY loops. Each loop = 1 file `Javis/loops/<slug>.md` in the vault (editable in Obsidian/chat/Studio), with on/off, its own cycle, quiet hours (quiet_hours), a per-day round cap, workspace + tools_profile (vault-safe by default / code for code-fixing loops). Executed SEQUENTIALLY (1 round at a time), with runtime state kept separately in `Javis/loop-state.json`.
- Self-protection: a loop that errors/fails verification ✗ 3 times in a row PAUSES ITSELF (records the reason + log, notifies Telegram if there is a bot); turn it back on or Run now to continue.
- New API `/loops` (list/create/edit/toggle/delete/run-now/log filtered by loop). The old `/loop/*` stays as is, pointing to the legacy loop `vong-lap-goc`.
- The "Self-improvement" page becomes a LIST of loops: status, last run + verification result, next run, toggle - run now - edit - delete buttons, a full loop creation form, a log filtered by loop.
- The Schedule tab shows EVERY loop like a builtin routine (id `__loop__:<slug>`): toggle on/off right there; deleting must be done on the Self-improvement page.
- Jarvis 007 chat = ORCHESTRATOR: the system prompt adds a procedure for choosing the smallest tool that is enough to finish (answer → Kanban task → skill → agent → workflow → schedule → loop), checking for duplicates before creating, and loops created through chat default to suggest + off.
### Improved
- One-time migration: the old `loop_config.json` automatically generates `Javis/loops/vong-lap-goc.md` (keeping all of custom_goal), with the old json kept as a backup.
## [0.6.6] - 2026-07-02
### Added
- Wired the self-learning engine into Kanban: new "Work (Kanban)" capability. After each conversation, the learning engine proposes background tasks into the backlog (deduplicated by name, awaiting approval).
### Fixed
- The whole dashboard was dead (Enter did not send, stats empty, no graph) because app.js still hooked the old, removed learn button. Added a guard and retired the old client-side auto-learn.

## [0.6.5] - 2026-07-02
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml "would not install": removed `${DOMAIN_NAME:?...}` (a required variable, so deploy failed when it was missing). It now ALWAYS deploys: without DOMAIN_NAME it runs temporarily on :7777, with DOMAIN_NAME you get HTTPS. Port 7777 is published again as a fallback way in.

## [0.6.4] - 2026-07-02
### Fixed
- docker-compose.yml: Watchtower moved to the "update" profile (OFF by default), so deploying the base compose no longer shows "Partially running" (Watchtower needs the Docker socket, which Hostinger often blocks). Turn on auto-update when needed: docker compose --profile update up -d.
### Improved
- README: fixed the Hostinger install section to use docker-compose.hostinger.yml and set DOMAIN_NAME for a domain/HTTPS; removed the wrong claim that "Hostinger gives you an hstgr.cloud URL automatically".

## [0.6.3] - 2026-07-02
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml: changed ports "7777:7777" (fixed) to "7777" (random, like Hermes) so the Open button points straight to the Traefik HTTPS domain instead of http://<ip>:7777. Access via https://<DOMAIN_NAME>.

## [0.6.2] - 2026-07-02
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml: verified that Hostinger does NOT provide the TRAEFIK_HOST variable for hand-pasted compose files (the link came out truncated as "javis-os."). Host now REQUIRES DOMAIN_NAME (uses `${DOMAIN_NAME:?...}`): if missing, deploy shows a clear error instead of producing a broken link. The docs now say to set DOMAIN_NAME=javis.<vps-hostname>.hstgr.cloud in the Environment box.

## [0.6.1] - 2026-07-01
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml: Host now defaults to `${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.${TRAEFIK_HOST}` (the Hermes pattern) instead of a localhost value, so a Hostinger deploy AUTOMATICALLY gets a <project-name>.<vps-hostname>.hstgr.cloud link + HTTPS with no variables to set. To use your own domain, set DOMAIN_NAME (it overrides). Anyone deploying on their own VPS gets the right link.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-07-01
### Changed
- Finished syncing ALL internal infrastructure names to javis: JAVIS_* environment variables, javis-data/javis-brains volumes, javis service/container/user (/home/javis), javis codex profile, JAVIS_METRICS marker, and the javis.service / start-javis.vbs / stop-javis.bat files. The whole project now uses one single name.
- NOTE when redeploying: the volumes were renamed, so the new version starts EMPTY (recreate the admin and reload the brain), or copy the data yourself from the old volumes to javis-data/javis-brains. If you previously set the admin variables on Hostinger, change the prefix to JAVIS_ADMIN_USER / JAVIS_ADMIN_PASSWORD.

## [0.5.1] - 2026-07-01
### Changed
- Renamed the GitHub repo/image to javis-os (image ghcr.io/blogminhquy/javis-os, GITHUB_REPO, install links in README/DEPLOY).

## [0.5.0] - 2026-07-01
### Changed
- Changed the displayed branding to Jarvis 007 (interface, docs, README, system prompt).
### Added
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml uses `${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}` for the Traefik router/service names: you can run several Jarvis 007 copies on one VPS without them colliding (like Hermes's random -efxd suffix).

## [0.4.7] - 2026-07-01
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml now sets Traefik labels exactly like the Hermes app: REMOVED the networks/external traefik-proxy part (the very thing that made deploy report "network not found"). Hostinger's Traefik finds the container through the labels on its own.
### Added
- A default HTTPS link without buying a domain: set DOMAIN_NAME=javis.<vps-hostname>.hstgr.cloud (Hostinger has wildcard DNS and issues SSL automatically).

## [0.4.6] - 2026-07-01
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml could not deploy on Hostinger: removed the requirement for the external `traefik-proxy` network (it caused a "network not found" error). The new version is just 1 container publishing port 7777, so deploy and it runs; attaching a domain + HTTPS is an optional step (Hostinger UI or manual Traefik labels, instructions in the file).

## [0.4.5] - 2026-07-01
### Fixed
- docker-compose.hostinger.yml dropped Watchtower (it needs the Docker socket and often causes "Partially running" in Hostinger Docker Manager). The Hostinger version is now just 1 javis container + Traefik labels, updated by Redeploy.

## [0.4.4] - 2026-07-01

### Fixed
